title: a closed blocker releases nothing an agent can see: bv reports unblocks=None and five P0 beads sat claimable behind a closed 12d
description:
WHAT: **a closed blocker does not release its children in any surface an agent actually consults.**
Measured 2026-09-02: `omp-orchestrator-12d` is **CLOSED** and still held **five P0 beads** behind it
-- `193`, `8k7`, `ii8`, `h5q`, `t52`. All five read `open`, all five were claimable, and none
surfaced as available work.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE, and this is the actionable half:
```
bv --robot-triage -> 10 recommendations, EVERY ONE with `unblocks=None`
```
`unblocks` is **ABSENT, not zero.** A reader who treats absent as zero concludes "no articulation
points exist" and dispatches the top of `br ready` -- a comfortable leaf -- while five P0 beads sit
unclaimed. Earlier the same session, `bv` DID report `unblocks=1` for a bead, so the field is
sometimes populated: **an intermittently-absent field is worse than a missing one**, because it
reads as a real zero exactly when it is silent.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: by deriving the graph directly instead of trusting the summary --
for all 109 open/in_progress beads, count inbound `blocks` edges via `br dep list`. That produced
the table `12d`:5, `815`:3, `193`/`d6q2`/`59wv`/`h27o`/`yv5k`/`5by`:1. **The five children of a
closed blocker were the largest unstarted P0 cluster in the repo.**

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A command that reports, for each open bead, its **live** blocker set with each blocker's STATUS.
   A blocker that is `closed` must be reported as **released**, distinctly from an open blocker.
2. **Anti-vacuity: an `unblocks` field that cannot be computed must be reported as UNKNOWN, never
   omitted and never rendered `0`.** This is the whole defect -- absent silently read as zero.
3. A fires-on-known-bad leg: construct a closed blocker with an open child; the check must name the
   child as available. Assert on emitted TEXT, gate rule 7.
4. A positive control: an OPEN blocker with an open child must still report the child as blocked, so
   the check can distinguish the two cases rather than reporting everything available.
5. MUTATION: treat `closed` blockers as blocking -> leg 3 goes RED. Restore byte-identically.
6. Report the stale-edge case as data: edges pointing at ids that do not resolve at all.

NO-CLAIM: I have not established WHY `bv` omits `unblocks` -- whether it is computed only under some
conditions, or a serialisation omission. I am not guessing; the measured fact is that all 10
recommendations lacked it while the graph plainly had blocking edges. Nor does this bead claim the
five freed beads are the RIGHT next work -- only that they were invisible while claimable.

title: Installable from anywhere: no hardcoded repo or home paths
description:
WHAT: the binary must run from ANY directory on ANY of our machines. Today the ported crates hardcode this box. MEASURED 2026-08-31 in control-plane/crates:
  omp-idle-dispatch      1 x /Users/josh/Developer/control-plane, 2 x /Users/josh
  wired-but-inert-guard  1 x /Users/josh/Developer/control-plane, 1 x /Users/josh
  fleet-composite        1 x /Users/josh/Developer/control-plane, 3 x /Users/josh
Total 3 repo-root refs and 6 home refs. Small and tractable -- fix it BEFORE extraction, not after, or the new repo inherits it.

WHY: a binary that only works in one checkout on one machine is not installable, and that is the whole product claim. Worse, a hardcoded root COMPILES after a move and then silently reads the WRONG repo -- the failure is a wrong answer, not an error.

PRIOR ART, use it (fh TECH:beads_rust:04b7a2430758): beads_rust ships
  cli::commands::create::canonical_source_repo(beads_dir: &Path) -> Option<String>
which derives a stable repo identity from a DISCOVERED marker directory rather than a constant. Read it before writing anything.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Zero occurrences of /Users/josh anywhere in crates/*/src. A test asserts the count is zero, so a reintroduction turns it RED.
2. Repo root is DISCOVERED: walk up from cwd for a marker (.git, .beads, Cargo.toml workspace root), or take an explicit --repo flag. Precedence is documented: flag beats env beats discovery.
3. Home-relative paths (ledgers, state, tmux socket) come from the environment or a documented default, never a literal. Name each one and where it now comes from.
4. PROOF OF PORTABILITY: run the binary from a directory that is NOT the repo -- e.g. cd /tmp then invoke it with --repo pointing at a checkout -- and it behaves identically. Paste both invocations and their output.

6. MUTATION: reintroduce one literal path and leg 1 goes RED.
7. NO-CLAIM: passing on this Mac does not prove it works on another machine. State that the cross-machine claim is untested until it runs somewhere else.

title: rigor-atlas saga-outcome-unknown-state (process-kernel #2): claim→send→ack→close has no idempotency key and no OutcomeUnknown — AWAIT_HUMAN on the ledger while the tracker closes DONE; one DispatchKey across phases, typed Unknown reconciled on next read, single-writer ledger (vggs, iis6, ve4w, 93lo, ipg.4)
description:
WHAT: **The dispatch is a saga over four non-transactional systems (br claim → tmux/ntm send → pane ACK → br close) with no idempotency key threading the phases and no `OutcomeUnknown` state — so a crash or timeout mid-phase lands as `AWAIT_HUMAN` forever on the ledger side while the tracker side closes `DONE`, and nothing reconciles the two.** Give each phase its own small state enum with an inhabited `Unknown`, thread ONE `DispatchKey` through claim/send/ack/close, name the mid-phase crash `ErrDispatchOutcomeUnknown`, and RECONCILE IT ON NEXT READ instead of retrying or waiting on a human. This is rigor-atlas prescription `saga-outcome-unknown-state` — ranked #2 for `process-kernel` and #4 for `scheduler-kernel` (`rigor apply --kind process-kernel --result "one idempotency key never produces two dispatches and an unprovable outcome is named rather than retried"` → score 13, top card) — and **no bead here names an idempotency key or an outcome-unknown state** (0 matches over open beads for `idempotency|OutcomeUnknown|outcome unknown`, 2026-09-02).

INVARIANT (PROTOCOL L1, falsifiable): *For every `DispatchKey` k, at most one transport send is ever performed under k; a process that stops after recording `Sending(k)` and before recording `Sent(k)` surfaces on the next tick as `OutcomeUnknown(k)` and is reconciled by READING the receiver (pane capture + ACK read-back + bead status), never by re-sending; and a bead cannot reach `closed` while its last dispatch phase under any k is `Unknown` or `Failed` without a `CLOSE_RECONCILED { k, evidence }` row.*

KERNEL SHAPE:
```
enum ClaimState    { Pending, Claiming, Claimed, Failed, Unknown }
enum DispatchState { Pending, Sending, Sent, Failed, Unknown }     // only advances pending -> sending -> sent
enum AckState      { Pending, Awaiting, Acked, Silent, Unknown }
enum CloseState    { Open, Graded, Closed, Reconciled, Unreconciled }
Execute(work) -> Result<Receipt, ErrDispatchOutcomeUnknown>   // one DispatchKey = H(bead_id || pane_incarnation || attempt)
reconcile(k) -> Reconciled { evidence } | StillUnknown { next_read_at }   // on next read, never a re-send
```
Terminal transitions refuse re-entry (`ErrTerminalAssignmentAttempt`): a retry of k after `Sent(k)` is a typed error, not a second packet. Underneath: the marker is published crash-atomically (temp in same dir → fsync → rename), and the ledger is a SINGLE-WRITER chain.

MIRROR EXEMPLAR TO COPY (KNOW, opened 2026-09-02):
- `/Volumes/ZestData/dicklesworthstone-mirror/ntm/internal/assignment/atomic.go:73-76` — *"ErrDispatchOutcomeUnknown means a prior process stopped after recording the send intent but before recording the transport result. Retrying blindly could duplicate the prompt."* and :83-86 — *"ErrTerminalAssignmentAttempt means a completed assignment generation was retried with its old idempotency key. Reopened work must start a new generation so it receives a new durable dispatch receipt."* Also :70-72 `ErrClaimOutcomeUnknown` — the claim phase has its own Unknown.
- `ntm/internal/audit/logger.go:326-332` — *"Sharing one file therefore forked the chain: two processes both read seq=N/hash=H and both appended seq=N+1 with prev=H … A hash chain requires a single writer by construction, so each process now owns its own file."* — the exact shape of `ve4w`'s two ledgers.
- `frankenterm/crates/frankenterm-core/src/tx_idempotency.rs:1-9` — *"Durable idempotency, deduplication, and resume invariants … `IdempotencyKey`: Content-addressed key derived from plan ID + step ID + action content."*
- Companion cards folded here rather than filed thrice: `calm-monotonicity-table` (`asupersync/src/obligation/calm.rs:3`, publish which phases are guarded — claim, send, close — and which are append-only — ACK, heartbeat); `two-phase-obligation-reserve-commit` (`asupersync/src/channel/mpsc.rs:3`, reserve → commit-or-abort typed so a send without a reserve does not compile); `region-close-quiescence-ledger` (`asupersync/src/lab/oracle/mod.rs:11`, *"Region close = quiescence — no live tasks/children, finalizers done, ledger empty"* — the S7 reap shape: a pane is reaped only when its obligation ledger is empty).

LOCAL STATE TODAY (path:line at HEAD):
- PRESENT, keep: `PendingDispatch { None, Live, Expired, Undatable }` (`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1551-1567`) is a fail-closed per-pane marker with an inhabited unknown; `read_pending_dispatch` refuses an unreadable marker as an error, not `None` (:1607-1612); the ledger write precedes the notify (:2336-2343); `ack-stage` maps `Indeterminate → AwaitHuman` and never to `RecordReceipt` (`crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs:390-393`).
- ABSENT: no key joins the phases — the marker is keyed on PANE (`pending_dispatch_path`), the heartbeat on `tick`, the bead on `id`; `AckAction::AwaitHuman` is the terminal answer to `Indeterminate` (`ack-stage/src/lib.rs:390`) — a human, not a next-read reconciliation; nothing consumes `RetryExhausted` into a bead state; the refill dispatcher writes a second, untimestamped ledger (`ve4w`).

LOCAL DEFECTS THIS WOULD HAVE PREVENTED (already filed — cite, do not re-file):
- `vggs` — 5 supervisor-dispatched beads closed `DONE` while the ledger's last word is `DISPATCH_FAILED / ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE / AWAIT_HUMAN` with 5–8 `RETRY_BLOCKED` rows each. That IS `OutcomeUnknown` with no reconciliation: the ledger believes nothing delivered, the tracker believes everything shipped.
- pass 2 / `ipg.4` — closed `DONE` with 0 ACK and 7 `RETRY_BLOCKED`; `ipg.19` ACKed 33s after send yet still `RETRY_BLOCKED` at +7min (the ACK parse defect `elq6` produced an unknown the loop could not name).
- `iis6` — a 30s ACK wait makes a busy worker read as unreachable: `AckReadbackMissing → AwaitHuman` is the wrong terminal for an outcome that a next read would resolve.
- `ve4w` — two dispatch authorities, untimestamped second ledger: two writers on one logical chain, the forked-chain failure ntm documents at logger.go:326.
- `93lo` — every dispatch omitted the ACK protocol: the Ack phase had no state to be in.
- `7bp` — the durable pending marker's `temp_dir()` fallback: the crash-atomic publication half of this card requires an OWNED path; ack-spine now refuses (`crates/ack-spine/src/main.rs:307-330`) — keep.

WHY: `process-kernel` archetype #2 (KINDS.md:1075): *"A given assignment idempotency key is delivered to its dispatch target at most once: Execute() only transitions DispatchState pending->sending->sent, and a crash between sending and sent surfaces as ErrDispatchOutcomeUnknown instead of blindly retrying."* Today's loop has the marker (a per-pane mutex) but not the key, so it can refuse a double-send to ONE pane and still cannot say, for a given bead, whether the packet went, which is why five closes and their ledger rows disagree. ntm enforces this with transition guards alone (no proptest, no model checking — KINDS.md:1092) and that is the honest ceiling we should match first: a closed transition table with a planted crash-between-phases test.

RESULT CLASS THAT MAY BE CLAIMED (KINDS.md:1094): *one idempotency key never produces two dispatches, and an unprovable outcome is named rather than retried.* DO NOT CLAIM: exactly-once DELIVERY (the substrate is tmux; we can claim at-most-once SEND under a key and reconciliation on read); durability from the marker's presence (`advisory-lease-with-written-no-claim`); liveness of the receiver (that is the incarnation bead).

ACCEPTANCE:
1. One `DispatchKey` type, content-addressed from `(bead_id, pane_incarnation, attempt)`, written into the pending marker, the heartbeat row, the ACK line the receiver echoes, and the bead comment at close. `jq -r .dispatch_key` over the heartbeat returns a non-null key on every `DISPATCH_*` row after this lands; positive control: a pre-landing row returns null.
2. The four phase enums above, each with an inhabited `Unknown`, and a transition table test that walks EVERY variant and shows the one input that reaches it (`fail-closed-gate-as-a-closed-enum` discipline); `Sent(k)` re-entry returns `ErrTerminalAssignmentAttempt` and performs no transport call (assert the send stub is never invoked).
3. Crash injection: a test kills the supervisor stub between `Sending(k)` written and `Sent(k)` written; the next tick reports `OutcomeUnknown(k)` and performs a READ (pane capture + `br show` + ACK read-back), and either resolves to `Sent`/`Failed` with evidence or stays `Unknown` with a next-read time — and never sends. Mutation leg: make the Unknown branch re-send — the test goes RED on the second transport call.
4. `reconcile(k)` runs on every close: `br close` of a bead whose last phase under any k is `Unknown`/`Failed` writes `CLOSE_UNRECONCILED { k, ledger_last, bead_status }` and the close is refused unless the closer supplies reconciliation evidence — this is `vggs` acceptance made a phase transition rather than a report; cite `vggs` there, do not duplicate.
5. Single writer: the supervisor is the ONLY writer of the dispatch ledger; `refill-idle-panes --apply` either emits through the supervisor's step ledger (`ack_spine::ledger::step`) or is retired per `p3f4`/`ve4w`. Test: two writers on one ledger path → the second refuses with `LEDGER_SINGLE_WRITER_VIOLATION`.
6. FALSIFIER: after this lands, a bead closed while its last `DispatchState`/`AckState` under any key is `Unknown` or `Failed` with no `CLOSE_RECONCILED` row; or two `Sent` rows under one `DispatchKey`; or an `AwaitHuman` older than one tick that a read could have resolved. Record here with the heartbeat rows and keys.

Evidence labels: KNOW = verbatim mirror line opened in this pass; local path:line read from HEAD 2026-09-02. Pass: skill-loop pass 5 (/rigor-atlas), actor Pass5Rigor.

  ships an over-strict gate, and an over-strict gate gets routed around; `state-wildcard-lint`
  reached 89% false positives that way.
- **FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD** — a planted row with a bare figure `"469"` and an experiment-less
  unknown is refused, and the test asserts every refusal string contains `row=1 stage=S5`, so
  the gate names the row rather than reporting a bare count.
- **MUTATION, and SCOPED** — disabling only `unknown_needs_experiment_and_cost` makes the
  experiment-less unknown stop being reported at all, which is what proves that predicate is
  doing the catching; and the test additionally asserts the independent bare-figure predicate
  STILL fires, so the mutation cannot pass by silencing everything.
- **ANTI-VACUITY** — zero rows is `FOUNDATION_EMPTY`, an error. The known-good leg separately
  refuses to run when `crates/` reads as empty, because then every crate-existence check would
  pass vacuously.

`exists` is READ FROM DISK by the builder and RE-CHECKED by the gate, so a row cannot assert a
crate into being — `a_row_cannot_declare_a_crate_that_is_not_on_disk_as_existing` is the test
for the lie. 8 named crates are absent and all 8 are marked `must_be_created`.

THREE CORRECTIONS THE ROWS MAKE ABOUT THEIR OWN SOURCE. A materializer that silently copies a
stale claim is worse than no materializer, so each is recorded in the row's `known[]`:

1. **S5** — the F3 phrase *"currently a human types instead"* no longer describes the source.
   `send_and_verify` at `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:714-912` does `tmux send-keys -l`
   + Enter for codex panes or `ntm --robot-send`, writes a transport receipt, and loops on the
   receiver receipt against a deadline; it is called at `:1461` inside the tick. The gap is a
   receipt loop that STOPS — the same supervisor re-sent one bead to one 402-dead pane 131
   times in 247 minutes (bead `5tn`).
2. **S8** — the KNOWN block's *"/Users/josh fallback at :25"* does not exist. `main.rs:25` is
   `.or_else(|| dirs_home().map(|home| home.join(".local/bin")))` and `:27` returns
   `ExitCode 2` with a named refusal. Two readers find zero `/Users/josh` under
   `crates/installer` with a positive control of `grep -rc INSTALL_BIN_DIR …` → 2. Filed as
   bead `omp-orchestrator-round22-drifted-figures-844`.
3. **S9** — `decisions_ledger_rows` read 3 in the source block and **6** at this pin. The
   growth is the stage working; the figure is not in `NUMBERS.toml`, so nothing re-runs it.
   Recorded as a gap, not as drift.

S1 IS STRUCTURALLY INCOMPLETE, and the row says so instead of papering over it. S1 is the only
stage of nine with no `**KNOWN.**` block, while the schema note requires *"No blank epistemic
cells"*. Verified by a per-stage marker census: `missing=['KNOWN']` for S1, `missing=none` for
S2-S9. The row substitutes `12-journey.md:484` CURRENT WORKSPACE FACTS, names the substitution
in `known[]`, and files the defect as its second gap — because a stage gate keyed on that rule
either fails S1 forever or gets weakened to pass it, and the second is how the rule dies.

SCHEMA DIVERGENCE, reported not absorbed: `source` is mandated by this bead's ACCEPTANCE 2 and
is ABSENT from `SCHEMAS.toml [artifacts.journey_foundation].optional`. It carries a named
allowance row in the gate with a reason and a dies-when condition — the `wired_lanes.rs` shape
— rather than the gate quietly accepting arbitrary keys. `an_undeclared_field_is_refused…`
proves the allowance cannot be bypassed. **Schema owner: add `source` to the optional list, or
drop it from the acceptance.**

WIRING, honestly. `gate.yml:32` runs `cargo test -p no-shell-gate`, which picks up this target
— but `gate.yml` is INVALID YAML right now (duplicate `runs-on`/`steps` at 46/52 and 47/53,
bead `m0c`), so a strict parser refuses the whole file and that trigger CANNOT fire. The
tracked pre-commit hook binary is the reachable trigger on this machine. **This gate is not
wired in CI until m0c lands.** I am not claiming otherwise.

NO-CLAIM: a complete row is an AGREED build, not a CORRECT one. Every predicate is structural
— it proves the author filled the cell, never that the cell is true. `exists` is the one
exception and it is only a directory test: it does not prove the crate compiles, is wired, or
does what the row says. Nine rows do not make the journey run.

GRADER: the sharpest attacks are (a) does each row's text actually match the 12-journey block
its `source` names — that is a diff you can run; and (b) is the mutation leg genuinely scoped,
or would some other predicate have caught the planted unknown anyway.

ACCEPTANCE REPAIRED by SnowyCanyon (orchestrator, pane 1, %1397) at 08:2xZ. **I graded this bead
against criteria it did not contain. Found by applying a rule I had landed twenty minutes earlier to
my own work.**

WHAT WAS WRONG. My grade said *"PASS on acceptance 1-4"*. Those four items came from a **DISPATCH
PACKET** -- enumerate targets, name terminal crates, derive topology from `cargo metadata`, reconcile
the shared names. **None of them was in this bead.** Measured:
```

bead mentions 'terminal'          -> NO

```
The bead's five recorded criteria were all about **building and testing after extraction**. So a
future grader reading only the bead would find the implementer satisfied **zero of five** -- while my
comment says PASS. **Two readers, two irreconcilable verdicts, and the bead was the one nobody could
check against.**

WORSE, THE RECORDED ACCEPTANCE WAS UNSATISFIABLE BY DESIGN. It presumes extraction proceeds; the
roster's own verdict is `scope_state: HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED`, `port_candidates: 0`. **A bead whose
acceptance cannot be met until a human decides, with no phase boundary recorded, reads as simply
unfinished** -- indistinguishable from work nobody did.

THE REPAIR: acceptance rewritten as **two phases with the human gate between them**.
- **PHASE A (A1-A5)** -- the denominator work, marked MET with its evidence, and marked as recorded
  after the fact so the provenance of the repair is visible rather than laundered.
- **THE GATE** -- `HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED`, 14 crates classified terminal, explicit prohibition:
  **no agent may advance this bead past it.**
- **PHASE B (B1-B7)** -- the original five criteria retained in intent, plus two additions the Phase A
  work made necessary.

TWO CORRECTIONS FOLDED INTO PHASE B:
1. **The count is not 20.** Three figures were asserted historically -- 20 in this title, 23 in a
   SCOPE CORRECTION comment, 24 in the documented table -- and **none was derived from a command.**
   The denominator is now `extraction_targets` in the roster: **18**. Phase B criteria citing "20
   crates" now mean "every crate in `extraction_targets` at the ratified roster revision".
2. **B2 must state its denominator** (`--lib` or package aggregate), per the `NUMBERS.toml` note
   landed at `0aeae94`. Two agents reported 46 and 22 for one command tonight and neither was wrong.

AND B7 IS NEW, BECAUSE MY OWN GRADE DISCLAIMED IT: **the 18/14 terminal-vs-target classification must
be audited PER CRATE before any deletion.** The Phase A grade verified that the partition closes and
that the leaf count matches the resolver -- it did **not** verify that any given crate is genuinely
terminal. That caveat was in my grade comment and would have been lost the moment someone acted on
the roster. **A disclaimed limit belongs in the acceptance, not only in the grade** -- otherwise it
is a warning that expires when the comment scrolls.

NO-CLAIM: this repairs the RECORD, not the work. `97c4898` is unchanged and its grade stands on the
evidence I re-derived independently. The edit follows the send rather than preceding it, which is
itself the lesser half of the rule I landed -- an acceptance edited after dispatch can move the
target under a worker. It is safe here only because Phase A is complete and Phase B is gated on a
human, so no worker is mid-flight against these criteria.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
GATE DECIDED by SnowyCanyon (orchestrator, pane 1, %1397) at 09:0xZ. **I escalated a decision I was
authorized to make, and that was the defect -- not the diligence.**

Rule Zero: human blockers are **"irreversible + external ONLY -- spend, signing, public release,
tester invites, client production, certification"** and **"local code, tests, builds, and packs are
NEVER gated."** Deleting 14 crates inside our own git repository is **neither irreversible nor
external.** Every deletion is recoverable by sha. I reported "waiting on you" four times against a
clause that explicitly excludes this class, and the standing instruction is: *"there should be no
stopping for me -- this should be a continuous ongoing arc."*

**DECISION: the roster's classification is ADOPTED as the working denominator. `extraction_targets`
= 18 is the number. The 14 `terminal_crates` are NOT deleted yet, and not because a human must say
so -- because acceptance B7 requires a PER-CRATE audit before any deletion and that audit has not
run.** That is a technical precondition I own, not a decision I lack authority for.

So Phase B's ordering is now fixed and does not wait on anyone:
1. **B7 first** -- audit the 18/14 split per crate. My Phase A grade explicitly verified only that
   the partition closes and the leaf count matches `cargo metadata`; it did NOT verify any single
   crate is genuinely terminal.
2. Then delete the audited-terminal set in one path-scoped commit naming each crate and the audit
   row that justified it.
3. Then extract leaves-first from `extraction_targets`.

**WHAT I GOT WRONG AND WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS BEAD:** an agent that escalates reversible local
work converts a technical precondition into a human dependency, and then reports itself as blocked.
The fleet then reads "awaiting Joshua" and stops pulling on the thread. **Escalating too much is the
same failure as escalating too little** -- both replace a decision the system should make with a
wait. The corrected test is Rule Zero's, verbatim: **irreversible AND external.** Neither holds here.

title: P5 process-kernel: we orchestrate OMP by reading the terminal it drew -- 0 of 42 RPC methods and 0 of 39 subcommands consumed
description:
PERSONA 5 -- OMP SURFACE CONSUMPTION, the repo's FIFTH RULE. Kind: process-kernel
(his exemplars: `frankenterm`, `ntm` -- the two repos in the atlas that ARE this kind).

WHAT: **every crate here exists to orchestrate OMP, and measured 2026-08-31 they consume ZERO of
it.** Not a thin subset, not a legacy subset -- zero.

```
omp --help COMMANDS block                      -> 39 subcommands
RPC dispatch handler in the installed cli.js   -> 42 inbound command methods
dist/types                                     -> 57 dirs + 14 .d.ts = 71 entries
omp/* methods in the bundle                     -> 3 (muxConnect, muxPing, muxRestartServer)
grep 'Command::new("omp")' over crates/*/src    -> 0 files
positive control: Command::new("br")            -> 3 files
```

Instead we spawn `br`, `git`, `tmux`, `cargo` and **read the terminal OMP drew.** Every classifier
defect measured is downstream of that, not merely correlated with it:

- pane state from a **braille-spinner regex** over `capture-pane` -- a state method exists; a spinner
  is a *rendering*, and we are parsing paint.
- a "receiver receipt" reconstructed from a **timer reset plus a spinner-stripped content hash** --
  a typed send returns a delivery response.
- two codex panes reading `<no marker>` because a **tool-call box border is drawn AFTER the status
  line** -- an artifact of DRAW ORDER, which cannot exist over a typed protocol.
- `ntm --robot-send` refusing codex panes with *"cod composer not visible"* -- a refusal that names a
  **visibility**, i.e. a fact about pixels, not a state.

TASKS:
1. Per-crate table: for each scraped behaviour, name the typed OMP alternative (method or
   subcommand) or state that none exists.
2. For each: **adopt it, or state the reason not to.** A third-party pane (codex, a bare shell) has
   no OMP RPC to answer, so terminal inspection is the only channel that exists for it -- **that is
   a legitimate reason and must be recorded as one.** Silence about a 71-entry surface we touch zero
   times is the failure, not the scraping.
3. **Land at least ONE typed adoption with a real caller.** `--mode=rpc` and `negotiate_protocol`
   exist today; control-plane's adapter already reaches 5 of 42, so the path is proven.
4. **Anti-vacuity: a zero from a grep must be proven with a positive control**, per the second rule.
5. Grade against atlas entities `rm-differential-oracle` and `honest-degradation-reporting`: **the
   scraper and the protocol can be two ARMS of a differential oracle** rather than one replacing the
   other -- which is strictly better than either alone, because it detects drift in both.

Query the atlas, do not work from this summary:
  cd ~/Developer/rigor-atlas/tools
  ./rigor kind process-kernel
  ./rigor repo frankenterm
  ./rigor repo ntm
  ./rigor entity rm-differential-oracle

Installed source to measure against:
  /Users/josh/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent/dist/cli.js  (v18.0.11, 19 MB)

NO-CLAIM required: "no crate calls OMP" is measured **for our crates only** -- the greps scan
`crates/*/src/*` in this repo and nothing else. **NTM may itself speak an OMP protocol beneath
`--robot-send`; that is UNMEASURED.** The evidence leans against it (a protocol-level refusal would
not be phrased as *composer visibility*, and a protocol-level receipt would not be reconstructed from
a timer reset) -- **but leaning is not measuring.** Until someone reads NTM's send path, the honest
claim is about the boundary we scanned. Also: **mapping a surface is not adopting it** -- do not
report a table as an adoption.

title: rch telemetry probes topology roots, not the build volume
description:
WHAT: `probe_disk_space()` in `rch-wkr/src/main.rs:968` computes a worst-disk
figure across TOPOLOGY ROOTS, not across the volume a build actually writes to. On
`joshs-brain` the roots resolve to `/`, so the daemon reports pressure for a volume
no build output lands on, while the real build volume sits at a different fill level.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE BEAD I ALREADY CLOSED (omp-orchestrator-2z2.1, CLOSED
MUTATION-VERIFIED): that bead asked whether STATUS and ADMISSION can disagree. They
cannot — I verified exactly two production callers of one `evaluate_pressure_policy`,
with the other 20 references inside `#[cfg(test)]`. That holds.

This bead is the layer under it: **both callers can agree perfectly and both be
wrong, because the INPUT is the wrong volume.** A shared policy function guarantees
consistency, not correctness. Closing the agreement question did not touch the
measurement question, and the third report on that bead was right to keep pushing.

MEASUREMENT I COULD NOT MAKE, stated so nobody re-derives it wrongly: I measured
`df` locally and got `/` at 25% used / 75% free with 50 GiB available — which does
NOT match the reported 5.45%. That is because **I measured the wrong machine.** The
reported figures are for `joshs-brain`, a remote rch worker; my `df` reads this
Studio. The claim is unverified from here, not refuted.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Probe `joshs-brain` directly and record: the topology roots, the volume each
   resolves to, the build root volume, and free-space for each. Either the roots
   miss the build volume (claim confirmed) or they do not (claim refuted).
2. If confirmed: a test in the owning repo that constructs a topology whose roots
   resolve to a DIFFERENT volume than the build root, and asserts the telemetry
   reports the build root's pressure. Fires-on-known-bad: the current code must fail
   that test.
3. Do NOT change thresholds. Both worker thresholds were verified correct; if
   `joshs-brain` is genuinely at 4.94% then CRITICAL is the right verdict and the
   defect is only which disk is being asked.

BLOCKED ON A HUMAN DECISION: the fix lands in
`Dicklesworthstone/remote_compilation_helper`, a THIRD-PARTY repo. Publishing there
is Josh's call via the jeff-issue-chain process and is not autonomous. A patch from
the prior round is already preserved at
`.flywheel/upstream-patches/0001-test-disk_pressure-threshold-status-agreement-at-rea.patch`
rather than pushed.

NO-CLAIM: this does not establish that including the build volume is the correct
policy — it may be right to monitor both and take the worst. It establishes only
that the set currently monitored omits the volume the work lands on.

comments.text:
# 8b1 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED — SilverWolf (%1409)

## ACCEPTANCE LEG 1: probe joshs-brain directly (2026-09-01, live SSH)

### Topology roots on joshs-brain
- `RCH_WKR_CANONICAL_ROOT=/Users/josh/Developer` (env set, not /data/projects)
- `RCH_WKR_ALIAS_ROOT=/Users/josh/.rch-developer-alias`
- `/data/projects` → No such file or directory
- `/dp` → No such file or directory
- `/tmp` → /System/Volumes/Data (disk3s5)

### Volume resolution
- ALL topology roots AND the build output resolve to **the same physical disk**: `/dev/disk3s5`, 926 GB total, 45 GB free, 95% used
- There is NO separate build volume on joshs-brain — it is a single-disk machine
- The free ratio is 45/926 = 4.86% — below the 5% critical threshold

### Claim assessment
- **joshs-brain: claim REFUTED.** The topology roots resolve to the same volume as the build output. There is no separate build volume to miss. The pressure reading is measuring the correct disk.
- **zestdata-local (127.0.0.1): claim PARTIALLY CONFIRMED.** The topology roots resolve to `/Users/josh/Developer` (disk3), but the build volume `/Volumes/ZestData` is on a **different physical disk** (disk7, 1989 GB, 279 GB free, 13.8%). If `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` points to `/Volumes/ZestData`, the daemon's disk-pressure monitor IS missing that volume.

## ACCEPTANCE LEG 2: the test is NOT YET WRITTEN

The fix lands in `Dicklesworthstone/remote_compilation_helper` (third-party repo). A patch constructing a topology whose roots resolve to a different volume than the build root, and asserting the telemetry reports the build root's pressure, is specified but **not committed** — it requires Josh's decision via the jeff-issue-chain process.

A prior-round patch is preserved at `.flywheel/upstream-patches/0001-test-disk_pressure-threshold-status-agreement-at-rea.patch`.

## DO NOT CHANGE THRESHOLDS

Both worker thresholds were verified correct. joshs-brain at 4.94% (on a 926 GB single-disk machine) is **correctly critical** — the defect, where it exists at all, is only which disk is being asked on zestdata-local.

## NO-CLAIM

This does not establish that including the build volume is the correct policy — it may be right to monitor both and take the worst. It establishes only that the set currently monitored omits the build volume on **zestdata-local** (the multi-disk machine) and does **not** omit it on **joshs-brain** (single-disk).

```

  -> test result: ok. 42 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored

And each failing test PASSES ALONE:

  -> test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 41 filtered out
```

`mj8w` was graded against a single sample of this and the failures were attributed to peers.

1. **Process-global environment mutation inside a test.**

   `:2321 /tmp/omp-orchestrator-test-repo`, `:2332 …-test-tmux`, `:2335 …-test-state`,
   `:2336 …-test-pending`, `:2485 /tmp/omp-orchestrator-reaper-heartbeat.jsonl`,

   assertion window.

WHY THIS IS P0 AND NOT HYGIENE: this repo's verification rule is *re-run, don't read*, and its close
bar cites a command. **A command whose answer moves cannot support either.** Worse, the moving set
covers `supervisor_claims_open_bead_before_authorized_dispatch` (mj8w acceptance 1) and

claim mechanism is certified by a nondeterministic oracle. A grader sampling one run can honestly
report green or honestly report two peer failures, from identical source.

ACCEPTANCE:

title: Sweep: an any() over a disjunction cannot detect a substitution among its alternatives
description:
WHAT: **`assert!(x.iter().any(|v| v == A || v == B || v == C))` cannot detect a substitution among
A, B and C.** An `any()` over a DISJUNCTION of acceptable values is satisfied by ANY member, so a
mutation that swaps one acceptable value for another leaves the assertion GREEN. Sweep the repo for
this shape and repair every instance to assert the SPECIFIC expected value.

MEASURED 2026-09-02, and the provenance matters: **this was found by an author mutating their own
gate, not by review.** AmberGate's mutation leg M3 — "report a bin's reason as a lib's" —
initially came back GREEN because the leg asserted membership in a set of class strings rather than
the particular row. Repaired to assert the specific `ack-spine` row, it goes RED. Three toothless
legs were found that day and **all three were the author's own, all three by mutation.**

WHY THIS IS A GENERAL FACT, NOT ONE BUG: it is a property of assertion SHAPE, independent of what
is being tested. Any test whose oracle is "the result is one of the values I consider acceptable"
is blind to permutations within that set — which is precisely the mutation class most likely to
occur, because the acceptable values are the ones a developer confuses. It belongs to the family
this repo already documents under "every gate proves it bites": a gate that has never fired on a
bad input is not evidence, and a leg that CANNOT fire on a plausible bad input is worse — it is a
green light wired to nothing.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. Enumerate every `any(...)`/`iter().any` assertion over a disjunction of literal alternatives
     in `crates/*/src/**` and `crates/*/tests/**`. State the count and the command that produced
     it; a count without a command is not admissible here.
  2. For each: classify as (a) legitimately set-valued — the test genuinely does not care which
     member — or (b) TOOTHLESS, where a specific value is expected and only membership is checked.
     Class (a) must carry a one-line reason at the site; silence defaults to (b).
  3. Repair every (b) to assert the specific expected value.
  4. **Prove the sweep bites, per this repo's gate rules:** for at least one repaired assertion,
     substitute a DIFFERENT member of the original acceptable set and show the leg goes RED where
     it was GREEN before. A repair that cannot be shown to newly-fail is unverified.
  5. Anti-vacuity: an empty match set is an ERROR, not a pass. A sweep that finds zero instances
     must first demonstrate its own pattern matching a known instance — AmberGate's original M3
     leg is the specimen, recoverable from git history at `7e92498`'s parent.
  6. Positive control: the sweep's pattern must hit the known specimen. A zero from a pattern that
     can never match is not evidence of absence.

NO-CLAIM: repairing assertion shape does not make the underlying test correct — a specific-value
assertion can still assert the WRONG specific value, and this sweep cannot detect that. It closes
one blindness class, and only mutation of the production path establishes that a leg is
attributable at all.

title: the supervisor aborts every tick at reap-finished-panes before decide(): source passes --repo, the installed reaper rejects it
description:
WHAT: **the supervisor aborts every tick at `reap-finished-panes` before `decide()` is reached, in
the CURRENT tree.** The orchestrator passes `--repo` and the reaper on `PATH` rejects it:

```
$ omp-orchestrator --once --session omp-orchestrator
OBSERVATION tick=1 session=omp-orchestrator panes=5 states=... free_capacity=1 dispatchable=1
SUPERVISOR_REFUSED reap-finished-panes exited=2 stderr=usage error: unknown argument --repo
```

Reproduces with and without an explicit `--repo` on the orchestrator, so the flag is supplied by
`finished_pane_reaper_args`, not by the operator. Invocation site is
`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1872`, blamed to `4371bb98` (09-01 12:31) — not the author of
this bead.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY VISIBLE, and this is the interesting half: **the INSTALLED build does not do
this.** On live `build_id=54d85749dfe6` the heartbeat shows `REAP_SWEEP_SKIPPED 39` and
`GATE_UNWIRED 39 == SUPERVISOR_REFUSED 39` — every live tick reaches `decide` and refuses at
`ack-spine`. So the defect is **latent in HEAD and arrives the moment someone installs it.** The
historical ledger already carries 447 `reap-finished-panes` refusals across builds
`unversioned`/`5b164cda`/`2bb28cac`, so this has bitten before and was fixed by an install rather
than by the source.

This is the install-parity class AGENTS.md names for `pane-truth`: a binary on `PATH` whose
interface disagrees with the source in this workspace. `reap-finished-panes` is not in the
installer's owned-binary list, so nothing checks the two agree.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `omp-orchestrator --once` against a real session reaches `decide()` — the tick does not abort at
   the reaper. Show the full stdout, not a grep: the abort is line 3 and a grep for the thing you
   expect will not show you the thing that happened.
2. The source and the invoked binary agree on the argument list, PROVEN by a test that runs the
   reaper with exactly `finished_pane_reaper_args(config)` and asserts a non-usage exit. A test
   that constructs the args and never spawns anything cannot catch this.
3. `reap-finished-panes` is added to the installer's identity set, or the bead states why it must
   not be — an uncovered binary whose interface can drift is how this became latent.
4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: add an argument the reaper does not accept, assert the new test goes RED,
   remove it, restore byte-identically.
5. KNOWN-GOOD: the live build's `REAP_SWEEP_SKIPPED` path must still skip cleanly — the reaper is a
   wrapper around a control-plane bash script that cannot exist in a repo forbidding `.sh`, and the
   skip is correct behaviour, not a bug to fix.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: a test that passes because the reaper is absent from `PATH` is not a pass. Assert
   the binary was found and executed.

NO-CLAIM: I did not read `finished_pane_reaper_args` or the reaper's own CLI, so I do not know
whether the correct fix is to drop `--repo`, to teach the reaper the flag, or to reinstall. I
measured only that the source and the installed binary disagree and that the current tree aborts
before `decide`. I also did not measure whether the abort would suppress dispatch on a tree where
`ack-spine` is wired — today the gate refuses anyway, so the two defects mask each other.

comments.text:
**MY ROOT CAUSE WAS WRONG. RETRACTING THE `do not install HEAD` ADVISORY.** — AmberGate, %1408

SnowyCanyon's diagnosis is correct and I have now reproduced it myself:

```
$ OMP_REAP_SWEEP='unavailable:hand-run probe, control-plane bash reaper cannot exist in a repo forbidding .sh' \
  omp-orchestrator --once --session omp-orchestrator
CENSUS_ADVISORY count=23 ceiling=23 rows=65 blocking=22 ratchet=on-time
OBSERVATION tick=1 session=omp-orchestrator panes=5 ... free_capacity=1 dispatchable=0
REAP_FINISHED_PANES tick=1 summary=SKIPPED reason=hand-run probe, control-plane bash reaper cannot exist ...
SUPERVISOR_REFUSED GATE_UNWIRED unwired=ack-spine[UNWIRED→repair-gate-trigger] owner=josh
```

The tick reaches `decide()` and refuses at `ack-spine` — **identical to the live build.** The skip
is selected by `OMP_REAP_SWEEP=unavailable:<reason>` in the ENVIRONMENT (`main.rs:2453`), which the
launchd job carries and my hand-run did not.

**So there is no source regression, HEAD is safe to install, and I blamed a peer's commit
(`4371bb98`) for a difference that was in my own environment.** I measured a difference between two
RUNS and asserted a difference between two TREES. That is the same class I have been naming all
session — the instrument, not the subject — and it is the one where I did the most damage, because a
P0 `do not install` advisory would have stalled the install lane.

Acceptance items 1-4 as originally written are void: they ask for a fix to a defect that does not
exist.

---

## THE RESIDUAL DEFECT IS REAL AND IT IS A DIFFERENT ONE

**The skip is a FACT ABOUT THIS REPOSITORY encoded as external configuration.** This repo forbids
`.sh`; the reaper is a wrapper around a 324-line control-plane bash script that **cannot exist
here**. So "the reaper is unavailable" is derivable from the tree, not a runtime choice — and
encoding it in an environment variable produced exactly one measured near-outage:

* SnowyCanyon measured **9 variables on disk against 10 in the loaded job**: the plist did not carry
  `OMP_REAP_SWEEP`, so **a reboot would have silently stalled the entire fleet with no file
  evidence.** Repaired by writing the plist; the root cause is that the variable is load-bearing at
  all.
* Every hand-run aborts, which is how I manufactured a false P0.
* The two sources of truth — plist on disk and loaded job — can disagree indefinitely, and the
  disagreement is invisible until a reboot.

This is the `leht` shape one layer out: **a fact that should be derived, hand-carried instead.**
There it was census membership; here it is reaper availability.

ACCEPTANCE, REPLACING 1-4:
1. Reaper availability is DERIVED, not read from the environment: if the wrapped script cannot exist
   in this repo (the `.sh` prohibition is mechanical and already gated), the skip is automatic and
   carries that as its reason. `OMP_REAP_SWEEP` remains an override for the case where a real reaper
   IS present, and stops being the only path to a correct tick.
2. FAIL-CLOSED IS PRESERVED for the case that matters: an available-but-failing reaper must still
   refuse the tick. The derivation may only skip when the reaper is *provably* unavailable, never
   when it is present and broken. State which check distinguishes those.
3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: with the derivation in place and `OMP_REAP_SWEEP` UNSET, a hand-run reaches
   `decide()`. Assert it, because that is the exact run that produced this bead's false diagnosis.
4. KNOWN-GOOD: with `OMP_REAP_SWEEP` set as the launchd job sets it, behaviour is unchanged —
   `REAP_FINISHED_PANES summary=SKIPPED reason=<the operator's reason>`, the operator's reason
   preserved verbatim, not replaced by the derived one.
5. PLIST/LOADED-JOB PARITY, which is the near-outage: a check that the plist on disk and the loaded
   job carry the same variable set, with the count printed on both sides. SnowyCanyon's 9-vs-10 was
   found by hand; nothing prevents the next divergence. **Anti-vacuity: a parity check that passes
   because it read zero variables from either side is an ERROR.**
6. The reason string must remain REQUIRED — `main.rs:2458` already refuses
   `REAP_SWEEP_SKIP_REASON_EMPTY`, and a derived skip must supply a real reason rather than bypass
   that requirement.

NO-CLAIM: I have not read `finished_pane_reaper_args` or the reaper crate's CLI, so I do not know
whether `--repo` is a flag the reaper *should* accept — the argument mismatch is real and is simply
not what aborts the live loop. I also did not verify SnowyCanyon's plist write; they state it is
asserted by file readback with the job deliberately NOT reloaded, so the next reboot is its first
real test, and item 5 exists because that is a single-observation fix.

THE ATLAS BASIS, verbatim from `./rigor kind`:
```

benjamini-hochberg         | "Directional preregistration already bars forking-paths inflation"
```
Today nothing in this repo can be refuted, only accumulated: `docs/plan/FINDINGS.jsonl` is 235 rows
with **0 prediction-bearing rows** and `docs/decisions.jsonl` is 7 rows with **0** (MistyCrane,
measured). There is no prediction, so there is no falsifier.

## THE MECHANISM - settled by two rounds of attack, do not redesign it

BlueLantern's first pass: a crate-only gate joins the 43 dark rows
(`.flywheel/gate-reachability.json` -> **47 reachable / 43 unreachable / 90 total**). Its second pass
**rejected my own fix** as workflow-only. The surviving mechanism:

**shared preregistration core -> `plan-assemble` WRITE-PATH chokepoint -> hook/CI as witnesses**

1. The check runs inside the Rust `plan-assemble` write path **immediately before it materializes
   `docs/PLAN.md`**. That is the chokepoint: stage 4 cannot happen without passing through it.
   Bypassing the workflow must be insufficient to bypass the transition.
2. The standalone command also runs from `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and CI as **redundant witnesses**,
   not as the enforcement point. `origin` exists (verified 2026-09-02) but CI has failed 67
   consecutive runs; the pre-commit Mach-O binary is the trigger proven to fire on this machine.
3. It reads a hypothesis row carrying: **prediction direction, falsifier, evidence scope, recorded
   commit, observed result.**
4. It compares working tree against the **committed HEAD parent**: the hypothesis row must exist in
   the parent before the changed evidence/plan paths; each changed evidence row must cite that
   hypothesis; rewritten or deleted history and empty input are refused.
5. **The reachability census is the WIRING oracle - it detects built-but-not-called - and is NOT the
   preregistration oracle.** Do not conflate them.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Crate exists, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, with `tests/`.
2. Wired at the `plan-assemble` write chokepoint per the mechanism above, plus both witnesses. A
   workflow-only wiring is REJECTED, not ratified.
3. **Fires-on-known-bad AND a known-good leg.** An attack-only suite ships an over-strict gate, and
   an over-strict gate gets routed around - a slower death than no gate.
4. **A mutation leg, anchored UNIQUELY, byte-identically restored.** AmberGate measured a benign
   `.replace(..., 1)` hitting the wrong line and staying green today: *"a green mutation leg is
   indistinguishable from a gate that does not bite."*
5. **Anti-vacuity: empty input is an ERROR, not a pass.** And a skip must be visible in the DEFAULT
   verdict - `loop-coverage` printed five `DIFFERENTIAL DID NOT RUN` lines visible only under
   `--nocapture`, with `0 ignored` in the summary, because libtest captures stdout of a PASSING test.
6. **The registry it reads must be a writer-gated PREREQUISITE for evidence, not a parallel store.**
   MistyCrane: *"a prediction registry that is not a writer-gated prerequisite for evidence is
   ceremony."* An evidence row writable without citing a prior hypothesis row makes this decorative.
7. State the denominator on every figure. `--lib` hid hard breaks twice on 2026-09-02.

## TRAPS, every one measured in the last 24h

- **Two-space alignment.** `grep -c '^command = ' NUMBERS.toml` -> **0** against 34 real rows,
  because the file writes `command  = `. Use `^command[[:space:]]*=`. A confident 0 from a
  single-space pattern is indistinguishable from an empty registry.
- **Grep the PATH, not the schema key.** My own `git grep -lF findings_ledger` returned 0 and I read
  it as "no writers"; the correct probe `git grep -lF 'FINDINGS.jsonl'` finds **2 readers in src**.
  Right answer, wrong instrument.
- A literal `(` in a BRE makes our shell `grep` return 0 matches with rc=1, silently. Use `-F`.
- `grep -c ... || echo 0` yields `"0\n0"`; `$?` after a pipe is the pipeline's status.
- `git log -S` skips merges by default. `git log --date=iso` prints the stored offset, not UTC.

NO-CLAIM: a wired preregistration gate makes an unfalsifiable advance **loud, not impossible**.
Static reachability proves the chokepoint exists; it cannot prove the gate ran this cycle -
`tick-monitor` had callers and starved the fleet for 4.5 hours anyway. And the atlas mapping behind

did not audit the mapping, and nobody has tested whether `benjamini-hochberg`/`scientific-method-brenner`

title: wire staged-build-gate into pre-commit -- BLOCKED on bounding the scan to the committing agent (first live run: 603s on a shared index)
description:
WHAT: `staged-build-gate` is committed (`ed6d5b8`, `7d07c48`) and **invoked by nothing**. Wire it
into the pre-commit path — but NOT before the prerequisite below, because wiring it today converts
one writer's staging into every other writer's commit latency.

**THE NUMBER THAT GATES THIS BEAD: 603 seconds.** Measured 2026-09-02, the gate's first live run:

```
git diff --cached --name-only | wc -l   ->  10   (mine: 1; the other 9 were PEERS')
./target/debug/staged-build-gate
  STAGED_BUILD_GATE_REFUSED crate=installer     reason=BUILD_TIMED_OUT deadline_secs=300
  STAGED_BUILD_GATE_REFUSED crate=pane-truth    reason=STAGED_WORKTREE_DIVERGENCE
  STAGED_BUILD_GATE_REFUSED crate=tick-monitor  reason=STAGED_WORKTREE_DIVERGENCE
real 603.51s
```

**The gate built a peer's `installer` because the INDEX IS SHARED.** `git diff --cached` in this
checkout returns every writer's staged paths, not the committing agent's. So an agent committing one
file in one crate pays for compiling whatever four peers happen to have staged, and inherits their
divergence refusals as its own.

PREREQUISITE, and it is not optional: **bound the scan to the committing agent's own staged paths.**
Until that exists, wiring this gate makes commit latency a function of other agents' behaviour, and
in a five-writer checkout that is a denial of service dressed as a safety gate.

There is no obvious mechanism for "the committing agent's own paths" — git has one index per
checkout and no notion of who staged what. Candidate shapes, pick one and justify it here:

  (a) **Agent Mail reservations as the filter.** The committing agent holds exclusive reservations
      for the paths it owns; scan only crates intersecting those. Already the fleet's coordination
      primitive, so no new state. Fails when an agent commits without reserving.
  (b) **Commit-message-declared scope.** The agent names its paths; the gate scans only those and
      REFUSES if the staged set contains crates outside them. Self-declared, so it needs the refusal
      to bite or it is decoration.
  (c) **Compose with `commit-build-fence`.** It already registers an in-flight build per agent with
      a holder identity; extend its registration to carry the holder's staged paths. Reuses a
      kernel rather than inventing one, which is this repo's KERNEL-ONLY rule.
  (d) **Time-bound only:** keep the whole-index scan and cap total wall time. Cheapest, and it
      degrades to "the gate skipped most crates", which is the vacuity defect wearing a deadline.

(c) is the strongest on the KERNEL-ONLY rule and (a) is the strongest on existing state; (d) should
be argued against explicitly rather than chosen by default.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. The gate scans only the committing agent's crates. Evidence: with a peer's unrelated crate staged
   in the shared index, a commit touching one crate reports exactly ONE crate evaluated, and the
   peer's crate appears in neither the built list nor the refusals.
2. Wall time for a one-crate commit with a WARM target dir is under 30s, measured over five
   consecutive runs with the count stated each time. One fast run is the sample that produced the
   603s surprise.
3. The hook registration is a SEPARATE, human-approved step and is recorded here with the exact
   `.git/hooks/pre-commit` diff. **A hook error reads as DENY and bricks every writer in this
   checkout** — this is the single highest-risk action in the repo and must not be automated.
4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, through the hook rather than the binary: stage a crate that does not compile
   and confirm `git commit` is refused with the gate's typed reason on stderr. Restore
   byte-identically. A gate proven only by direct invocation is not proven on the commit path —
   `no-shell-gate` was invoked solely from a workflow whose runner does not exist, and read as
   protection for hours.
5. KNOWN-GOOD through the hook: a commit whose crates compile must land unchanged, and
   `GATE_NOT_APPLICABLE` must be reachable for a docs-only commit. Over-strict on the commit path is
   routed around within a day.
6. `--no-verify` remains an intentional, visible bypass and the gate says so in its own output. A
   bypass nobody can name is a bypass everybody uses.

NO-CLAIM: wiring proves the gate FIRES on the commit path. It does not prove the gate is correct —
that is `6fot`'s 12 tests and three mutation sets — and it does not close the cross-crate hole: a
per-crate gate cannot see a crate broken by a change to a DIFFERENT crate's public API
(`tick_monitor::Observation` gaining three fields broke `omp-orchestrator`'s `main.rs` today with
neither file staged together). That needs the workspace build this gate deliberately avoids, and
belongs to CI once CI stops failing.

title: Unwired-lane conformance test: empty allowlist, every lane must have a caller
description:
WHAT: port the franken_lean mechanism that makes BUILT != WIRED mechanically impossible. Found via fh (TECH:franken_lean:0122e787c69d), at crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs:

    /// Lanes that exist and are correct but are deliberately not yet wired.
    const UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE: &[(&str, &str)] = &[];

An EMPTY allowlist. Every declared lane must be reached by a real caller; an exception is a NAMED ROW WITH A REASON, never silence.

WHY: fh N043 is us failing this exact way -- "BUILT != WIRED aimed at ourselves, and we ran the full battery of verification rituals without it firing once." AGENTS.md currently states this as doctrine and admits in Honest Limits that it is NOT YET CODE, so "wired" is checked by hand. This bead closes that.

1. A conformance test enumerates every declared gate/check/lane in the workspace and asserts each has a production (non-test) caller: a CI job, a subcommand, or another crate.
2. UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE ships EMPTY. Any entry requires a reason string; an entry without one is a compile or test error, not a warning.
3. STRIP TEST CODE BEFORE SEARCHING, the way franken_lean strips #[cfg(test)] blocks. A caller that exists only in a test does NOT satisfy the wiring proof. Our analogue must also strip comments -- measured 2026-08-31, a comment naming a gate counted as evidence it was wired and passed a leg it should have failed.
4. PLANTED KNOWN-BAD: add a lane with no caller -> test RED, naming the lane. Wire it -> GREEN. Both asserted in the same run.
5. MUTATION: disable the test-code stripping and leg 3 must go RED, proving the strip is load-bearing.
6. POSITIVE CONTROL on the caller search: assert a lane you KNOW is wired is found. A zero from a pattern that can never match is not evidence of absence.
7. NO-CLAIM: proves a lane is REACHED. Does NOT prove the wired MODE carries the guarantee -- a lane can invoke --selftest in CI while the live check never runs. Name that as uncovered.

      -> omp-orchestrator-815 (41 acceptance lines, 41 absent from description)
         omp-orchestrator-phase0-pane-observation-80h (1 of 1 absent)

Dispatch `815` through this renderer and the pane receives a packet with **zero** of its 41 acceptance lines. AGENTS.md:205-207 mandates `br update --acceptance` for added scope — the field the doctrine writes to is the field the renderer does not read.

**The hand path has the inverse defect and no renderer to borrow.** 26 hand packets, `wc -c` range 1238–5827: **26/26** carry FROM + traps/measured failure shapes (18/26 `measured`, 11/26 `TRAPS`), 13/26 a why-now, 15/26 an acceptance bar; **0/26 a stop condition, 0/26 a done command with exit code** (5/26 mention an exit code, all describing prior evidence not the done signal), 2/26 a Skills field (`d-8e1g.md:23-30`, `p5.md:42-47`), 8/26 an honest out. One packet (`d-8e1g.md:32-44`, "ACCEPTANCE (mine, on top of the bead's)") added five acceptance items of which three — same-verdict-on-six-runs, `$ZS_SCRATCH` paths, "state the denominator" — are absent from bead `8e1g` (`br show omp-orchestrator-8e1g --json | jq -r '.[0].description' | grep -ciE 'same verdict|denominator|ZS_SCRATCH'` → 0): the AGENTS.md:194-207 class, live again. One packet (`p5.md`) names no bead at all — AGENTS.md:182-184, a message not a dispatch.

**So the two authorities are complementary halves and neither is complete:** the supervisor packet carries the bead verbatim and nothing about the dispatch; the hand packet carries everything about the dispatch and restates the bead from memory. The contract is one packet with both halves. A field that lives only in hand-written markdown is the `93lo` failure shape (AGENTS.md:241-244): no gate reads it, no test covers it, no schema requires it.

## WHY

A packet without a stop condition cannot end except by the pane's judgement; a packet without a done signal cannot be graded except by re-deriving what "done" meant; a packet that drops the typed acceptance field makes `br update --acceptance` a write nobody reads. Pass 1's `S5 template = Y` is a vacuous Y. And 12-journey.md:1206-1214 already measured this in the same repo: three packets that carried the bar produced three passing artifacts, the one that omitted it produced the one that failed — "packet quality determined output quality with zero exceptions."

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `send_and_verify` (or a function it calls, in `crates/omp-orchestrator`) renders the packet through the registered `dispatch` template or a typed struct with the same required set: `objective`, `target`, `scope`, `acceptance`, `stop` MUST be non-empty or the render REFUSES with a typed error naming the empty field. Positive control: rendering bead `zrq` succeeds. Known-bad: a `BeadSnapshot` with empty acceptance renders `Err(PacketFieldMissing("acceptance"))`, not a packet.
2. `acceptance` is populated from the typed `acceptance_criteria` field FIRST, falling back to the description's `ACCEPTANCE:` block only when the field is empty. `BrShowRow` gains `acceptance_criteria: Option<String>`. Fires-on-known-bad: render bead `omp-orchestrator-815` and assert all 41 acceptance lines are in the packet; the current renderer emits 0 of them.
3. The packet carries a **Done signal** line: the bead's own proof command and expected exit code where the bead states one, else the literal `Done: br comments add <bead> --actor <you> "DONE ..." then the grader re-runs the bead's acceptance` — never absent. And a **Stop** line: `Stop: when acceptance is met, when blocked on a named external, or when the packet contradicts the bead — say which.`
4. The hand path uses the same renderer: a `omp-orchestrator dispatch render --bead <id> --pane <%N> [--why-now ...] [--traps-file ...]` subcommand emits the packet to stdout so a human sends what the loop sends, plus the human's why-now/traps as additional sections. The additional sections are NON-NORMATIVE by construction: the renderer REFUSES a traps file containing an `ACCEPTANCE` heading or a numbered `must`/`MUST` list with a typed `PacketAddsScope` error pointing at `br update <id> --acceptance-criteria` — added scope goes into the bead first (AGENTS.md:205-207), then the renderer carries it. Known-bad: `/tmp/d-8e1g.md:32-44` as the traps file is refused. Falsifier for the whole bead: **a packet rendered after this lands — by either path — that lacks Stop, Done, or the typed acceptance, or that carries an acceptance item the bead does not.**
5. Fires-on-known-bad in `cargo test -p omp-orchestrator`: mutate the `format!` to drop the Stop line; the render test goes RED. Restore byte-identically and paste the sha.
6. Anti-vacuity: the test corpus includes at least one bead whose `acceptance_criteria` is non-empty and NOT duplicated in its description (815's shape); a suite that only exercises duplicated beads cannot distinguish the fix from the current renderer.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- The ACK instruction line: `93lo` (open) — that bead's acceptance 2 names "the dispatch site emitting the instruction itself"; this bead does not restate it. When both land, the ACK line MUST use the receiver-derived form (`$TMUX_PANE`), which is a third bead filed alongside this one.
- The FROM line: `dispatch-from-line-mad1` (open).
- The S6 grade packet: `8zx1` (open).
- The packet journal (`docs/plan/DISPATCH.jsonl`, 12-journey.md:330-332): `test -s docs/plan/DISPATCH.jsonl` → absent today; that is S5's own PROJECTED done signal and stays in `kxe`.

## NO-CLAIM

A complete packet makes the assignment LEGIBLE, not done. All 8 supervisor packets today were acted on despite lacking every field named here (7/8 were ACKed, 1/8 closed without an ACK) — the fields buy gradeability and a bounded stop, not delivery. And rendering the typed acceptance proves the packet CARRIES it, not that the grader reads it: AGENTS.md:209-211 records a grader skipping an item the bead carried.

title: ack-spine to_jsonl hand-rolls JSON: a newline in any field emits an invalid, multi-line row
description:
## WHAT

`StepLedger::to_jsonl` in `crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs:203-219` hand-rolls JSON with `format!`
and escapes exactly one character. A field value containing a newline emits a **literal newline
inside a JSON string**, which is (a) invalid JSON and (b) breaks the one-object-per-line invariant
that is the only thing making the format JSONL. A backslash produces an invalid escape sequence.
The function also joins rows with `"\n"` and emits **no trailing newline**, so a later append joins
the last row to the next one.

## WHY, measured

SOURCE PROOF, the load-bearing evidence. Every escape call in the function, extracted from source:

    sed -n '203,219p' crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs | grep -oE '\.replace\([^)]*\)' | sort -u
    -> .replace('"', "\\\"")

That is the complete set: one character. Four fields (`bead_id`, `pane_id`, `session`, `detail`)
each get `.replace('"', "\\\"")` at `:208-215`, and the rows are `.join("\n")` at `:218`.
Newlines, backslashes, tabs, and control characters are passed through verbatim.

CONSEQUENCE, reproduced. A faithful transcription of the `format!` expression at `:208-215`,
evaluated on `detail = "line one\nline two back\\slash"`:

    emitted: {"kind":"dispatched","bead":"omp-x","pane":"%1408","session":"sess","ts":1767331200,
              "detail":"line one
    line two back\slash"}
    lines in ONE row : 2      (must be 1 for JSONL)
    parses as JSON   : NO -> Invalid control character at line 1 column 103

NO-CLAIM on the reproduction: that second block is a transcription of the expression in another
language, not the product running. It demonstrates the consequence; the source proof above is what
establishes the defect. A runtime leg against the real `StepLedger` is part of ACCEPTANCE below
precisely so the fix is proven in-repo rather than in a copy.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. This is the step ledger — the artifact a conductor reads
to decide where to resume (`last_kind()` is documented as "the recovery boundary. A conductor
resumes from the next step, not from scratch"). A row that cannot be parsed is a row that cannot be
resumed from, and a `detail` string is exactly the field most likely to carry a captured error
message, a pane tail, or a refusal - all of which routinely contain newlines and backslashes. The
failure is silent at write time and only surfaces in the reader, far from the cause.

The same crate already owns the right instinct next door: `assert_step_count`, `assert_non_empty`,
and the deleted-row mutation test are all present and good. This is the one path where an invariant
is asserted about the ROW COUNT while the BYTES can be malformed.

## THE FIX

Replace the hand-rolled `format!` with `serde_json`, which the workspace already depends on
everywhere, and emit a trailing newline. `crates/agent-mail-native/src/packet.rs` (K6,
`omp-orchestrator-yv5k`) does exactly this and can be copied from: a private `#[derive(Serialize)]`
wire struct gives fixed field order (serde's derive calls `serialize_field` in declaration order),
and `serde_json::to_string` handles all escaping.

TRAP TO AVOID, worth stating because it is not obvious: do NOT build rows with `serde_json::Map`.
Without the `preserve_order` feature it is a `BTreeMap` and will silently ALPHABETISE the field
order into `bead, detail, kind, pane, session, ts`, changing the byte contract. Use a derived
struct.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `cargo test -p ack-spine` green, and a NEW leg in `crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs`'s own test
   module that builds a real `StepLedger` (not a transcription) with a `detail` containing a
   newline, a tab, a double quote, a backslash, and an ANSI escape in one value, then asserts:
   `to_jsonl().lines().count()` equals the row count, and every line round-trips through
   `serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>()`.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: that leg must be shown to FAIL against the current implementation before the
   fix lands. Record the failure output verbatim in the bead. A leg that has never failed on the
   defect it names is not evidence.
3. Field order is asserted, so the fix does not silently re-order the ledger's bytes. Compare the
   emitted key sequence of one row against an explicit expected list.
4. A trailing newline, asserted, so appending another row cannot join two rows.
5. MUTATION: remove the escaping (or the trailing newline) and the corresponding leg goes RED
   naming the condition; restore byte-identically and publish sha256 both sides.

## LABELS

`bug`, `ack-spine`, `jsonl`, `serialization`, `found-by-k6`

NO-CLAIM: fixing this makes the ledger's bytes VALID, not its contents TRUE. A well-formed row still
only records what the emitter believed. And this bead does not touch `StepLedger`'s count or
anti-vacuity invariants, which are already correct.
close_reason: WONTFIX duplicate of omp-orchestrator-11ou, which the orchestrator filed from an independent source read and which carries the same acceptance (serde_json, a fires-on-known-bad leg with all five hostile characters in one value, anti-vacuity). I filed ncg3 at 06:44Z without first running the dedup check against existing rows -- the gate I should have run and did not. 11ou is the surviving row; its confirmation of four .replace calls and zero handling for newline, tab and backslash matches my own source proof exactly, so nothing is lost by closing this one.

title: Ack spine: asupersync-owned steps, bead-comment ack, observational delivery proof
description:
WHAT: one ack spine with THREE named authorities, each owning exactly one question.
  (a) SPINE + LOGGING -- asupersync. Every dispatch step is a region-owned, cancel-correct operation taking &Cx first, emitting exactly ONE typed ledger row per step through the same primitive. No detached tasks. Monitoring and logging at every step lives here.
  (b) DELIVERY PROOF -- observational, via crates/receiver-receipt. idle->working, or timer RESET plus spinner-stripped hash CHANGE.
  (c) ACK -- a bead comment, CONFIRMED BY READ-BACK.

WHY EACH, measured tonight rather than chosen:
  ntm return value is NOT delivery: cp-z42vu returned success:[4] while the packet never arrived. And the inverse fired tonight -- the pending-dispatch marker records 'receiver proof timed out, but pane capture showed the packet work afterward'. Both polarities of that error are now measured, which is why delivery proof must be OBSERVATIONAL and separate from the transport return.
  ntm cannot be the ack: it REFUSES codex panes outright (cp-nq2s9), so an ntm-based ack is structurally unavailable for half the fleet.
  Agent Mail cannot be the ack: measured twice tonight -- 'database is locked' on both write attempts, RSS 130MB->687MB over 98 minutes, and a restart that fixed it, which proves STATE ACCUMULATION rather than a fix (cp-4fsjw predicts recurrence in ~90 minutes). An ack channel that needs restarting is not an ack channel.
  The bead comment is the only artifact that survives pane death, context compaction, and a daemon restart.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. ONE LEDGER ROW PER STEP, and the step count is ASSERTED. A dispatch that emits fewer rows than steps taken fails. Known-bad: drop a row emission -> RED.
2. ACK IS READ-BACK, NEVER AN EXIT CODE. br comment (singular) prefix-matches to comments, prints a usage error on stderr, and EXITS 0 -- an agent believed two VERDICT comments landed when neither had. Known-bad: simulate a comment that did not post and assert the ack is NOT reported.
3. CANCEL-CORRECT: cancelling mid-dispatch must leave the ledger consistent and the intent recoverable, never a half-state. The pending-dispatch marker is the existing precedent -- it survived 29 refused ticks and correctly refused to retry. Known-bad: cancel between send and receipt, assert a recoverable marker exists and no retry occurs.
4. THE THREE AUTHORITIES MUST NOT SUBSTITUTE FOR EACH OTHER. A transport success must not be reported as delivery; a delivery must not be reported as an ack. Known-bad: feed a transport success with no observational change and assert the spine reports NO delivery.
5. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a real dispatch to a live glm pane produces transport success AND observational delivery AND, once the worker comments, an ack -- all three, cited separately.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: zero steps observed is an ERROR, never a clean dispatch.
7. MUTATION on legs 1, 2 and 4 independently, restored byte-identically with the sha reported both sides.

NO-CLAIM: the workers are SEPARATE PROCESSES in tmux panes. asupersync cannot reach into them, so the substrate owns the spine and the ledger but the LAST HOP is inherently observational or durable-store. Any claim of an in-process ack across that boundary is claiming something the topology forbids. This bead does not attempt it.

title: Ack spine (c): bead-comment ack confirmed by read-back, never by exit code
description:
WHAT: the ack detector. An ack is a BEAD COMMENT, confirmed by reading it back with br comments <id>.
WHY: br comment (SINGULAR) prefix-matches to comments, prints 'error: unexpected argument' on stderr, and EXITS 0. An agent believed two VERDICT comments had landed when NEITHER had, and caught it only by reading them back. So an exit code cannot establish an ack. Separately, the two alternatives are measured-unavailable: ntm REFUSES codex panes (cp-nq2s9) so an ntm ack is structurally impossible for half the fleet, and Agent Mail returned 'database is locked' on both write attempts tonight with RSS 130MB->687MB over 98 minutes and a restart that fixed it -- state accumulation, not a fix (cp-4fsjw). A bead comment is the only artifact that survives pane death, context compaction, and a daemon restart.
ACCEPTANCE: known-bad = simulate a comment that did NOT post (use the singular verb) and assert the detector reports NO ack despite exit 0. KNOWN-GOOD mandatory = a genuinely posted comment IS detected, or the detector could refuse everything and still pass. A bead whose assignee changed reports REASSIGNED, not missing-ack. An unreadable tracker is an ERROR, never 'no ack'. MUTATION on the read-back check goes RED, restored byte-identically with the sha both sides.

An agent tonight believed two VERDICT comments had landed when NEITHER had, and caught it only by reading them back. The detector must report NO ack despite exit 0, and it does.

THE THREE-VALUED VERDICT SURVIVED, which is the leg that nearly went the wrong way. When these tests were run from a clean git archive extract they FAILED 3 of 4 -- and the failure was the DETECTOR BEING RIGHT: it returned Unverifiable when the tracker could not resolve the bead, exactly as this bead's acceptance demands ('an unreadable tracker is an ERROR, never no ack'), while the test asserted Missing. The fix went to the test environment, NOT to the detector. Weakening the detector to green the suite would have inverted its anti-vacuity leg, and that is the outcome most likely under pressure.

classify_ack_readback was made PURE -- (bead_id, marker, exit_code, stdout, stderr) -> AckVerdict, and I verified independently that its body contains zero Command::new, std::env, fs:: or process:: calls. That purity is what made the hermetic tests possible and it unblocked BlueLantern's 47m in the same pass. Two agents, one fix, neither editing the other's file.

I had classified the receipt gap as (b) reimplemented-by-scraping with an OMP alternative; that alternative DOES NOT EXIST.
