title: Pre-commit staleness gate: refuse a commit while a build is registered in flight
description:
WHAT: a pre-commit check that refuses a commit to a repo while a build/install for that repo is registered as in flight, naming the registered build and its HEAD.

WHY, measured 2026-08-31: a build started at 09a1da4, HEAD reached 85828bf, and the installed binary reported build_id=f94ea53 -- THREE identities. Three commits landed inside three minutes (12:11:08, 12:11:58, 12:13:37) while an install was in flight, five of them from the orchestrator. Source-equals-installed was impossible BY CONSTRUCTION, not by anyone's error. The remedy used was a manual COMMIT FREEZE broadcast to four panes; it worked, and it is not a mechanism -- it holds only while every agent honours it and nothing enforces it.

SAME SHAPE AS A DEFECT ALREADY IN THIS REPO: the crontab lost-update, where correct work from a stale snapshot silently reverted another agent's edit and left the fleet watchdog blind for 4h19m. The durable fix there was a staleness gate refusing a write whose input predates the live file (cp-crontab-guard-staleness-j9swt). This is that gate for source commits.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. KNOWN-BAD, with tonight as the specimen: register a build at commit A, then attempt a commit while it is in flight -> REFUSE, nonzero, naming the registered build, its HEAD, and who registered it. A refusal that does not name the holder is unactionable and sends the caller to ask around.
2. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: with no build registered, commits pass unchanged. Without this leg the gate blocks all work and gets bypassed with --no-verify, which is a slower death than no gate.
3. SECOND KNOWN-GOOD: a build registration must EXPIRE. A crashed or abandoned build must not freeze the repo forever -- propose the TTL and justify it. An unexpiring lock is an outage wearing a safety mechanism, and this session already measured that shape: a mint-floor reclaim valve pointed at a root whose only content is CACHEDIR.TAG, so RETIRE_ROOT_EMPTY was its steady state and the floor could never self-clear.
4. THE HOLDER MUST BE ABLE TO RELEASE, and the release must be recorded, not silent.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: an unreadable or absent registration store is an ERROR, never 'no build in flight'. Twelve confident zeros this session came from treating 'I could not look' as 'there is nothing there'.
6. MUTATION: disable the in-flight check -> leg 1 goes green; restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: this gate cannot prevent a commit made with --no-verify, and it cannot see a commit in a sibling repo that the build also depends on -- tonight the supervisor depended on a crate whose tracking state was reported inverted across two repos. It reduces the cost of the mistake; it does not make concurrent build-and-commit safe.

THE THREE SPECIMENS IT ANSWERS, all measured today: (1) a build started at 09a1da4 while HEAD reached 85828bf and the installed binary reported build_id=f94ea53 -- three identities, one artifact, because three commits landed inside three minutes during an install; (2) backtick injection, mine, where a double-quoted -m EXECUTED the message and the hook still printed PASS at exit 0; (3) the bare-commit sweep, 2873d20, which buried crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs at +678 inside a commit titled 'docs: backtick injection probe'.

DESIGN CLAUSES I CHECKED SPECIFICALLY BECAUSE THEY ARE WHERE THIS CLASS DIES: the refusal NAMES build_id, registered HEAD, current HEAD, holder, and expiry -- a refusal that does not name the holder sends the caller hunting, which is why the supervisor's DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED worked while 178 ticks of ATTENTION.txt did not. Empty valid store ALLOWS (the known-good leg; a refuse-only gate gets --no-verify'd and then protects nothing). Missing or malformed store ERRORS rather than allowing -- anti-vacuity. Default TTL 1800s, so registrations EXPIRE: an unexpiring lock is an outage wearing a safety mechanism, and this repo already measured that exact shape in a reclaim valve whose target root holds only CACHEDIR.TAG, making RETIRE_ROOT_EMPTY its permanent steady state so the floor could never self-clear.

NO-CLAIM, and the author stated it before I asked: no production .git/hooks installation is claimed. The crate is built and proven; hook-certification and registration remain required and are Josh's call. A hook error reads as DENY and can brick every Write/Edit/Bash in the fleet, so registration is never automated. Also: --no-verify bypasses any pre-commit hook by design, and .git/hooks is untracked and per-clone, so a fresh checkout has no hook at all. This raises the floor from 'nothing prevents it' to 'skipping it is an explicit act'. It does not make the failure impossible.

title: Commit messages passed as double-quoted shell strings execute backticks — use git commit -F
description:
WHAT: any agent writing `git commit -m "..."` with a double-quoted shell string has its message COMMAND-SUBSTITUTED. Backticked text is executed and replaced by its stdout.

MEASURED 2026-08-31, by me, in commit 67ec603. The message contained a backticked crate name. Result:
  stderr:  error: command not found: finding
  message: "THE SECOND LINE IS THE ONE WORTH READING.  had exactly ONE manifest caller"
The word was EXECUTED AWAY and replaced with the empty stdout of a failed command. The commit still landed and the verification-level hook still printed PASS, so nothing anywhere reported a problem -- the damage is silent and only visible by reading the message back.

THIS IS THE REPO'S OWN FLAGSHIP DEFECT, REPRODUCED IN THE REPO BUILT TO ELIMINATE IT. README.md's first table row, verbatim: "Backtick injection -- A backtick inside a bead body was executed as a command. msg was never assigned, so every scheduled fire dispatched NOTHING while still logging healthy idle counts. Inexpressible in Rust because: bead text is a String, never a program." Same mechanism, new surface: commit messages instead of bead bodies.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COSMETICS: commit messages are cited as evidence in bead closes. A message that silently lost a word, a path, or a sha is corrupted evidence that reads as intact. Tonight a close reason cited a commit; if that citation had been backticked it would have vanished and the close would have looked complete.

THE FIX, and it is already our practice elsewhere: never inline a message into a double-quoted shell string. Write it to a file and use `git commit -F <path>`, exactly as every dispatch packet in this session is written to /tmp/pk*.txt and sent with --msg-file rather than inlined. The habit exists; it just was not applied to commits.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD through the real trigger: a commit message containing a backticked token must be REFUSED or must round-trip BYTE-IDENTICALLY. Assert by reading the message back with `git log -1 --format=%B` and comparing to the source bytes -- never by the commit's exit code, which was 0 here.
2. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: an ordinary message with no backticks commits unchanged. A refusal-only check gets bypassed.
3. The check must also catch $(...) and $VAR, which are the same class. Backticks are the instance measured; they are not the whole family.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty message is an ERROR, not a pass.
5. MUTATION: break the round-trip comparison; leg 1 goes RED.

NO-CLAIM: I am NOT amending 67ec603. The standing rule in this session is path-scoped commits, never -A and never --amend, and rewriting history to hide my own specimen would destroy the only in-tree evidence of this defect. The message is left holed, deliberately, and this bead is the record. A follow-up commit may add the missing sentence.

The risk was real but the exposure was zero because the content happened not to contain the trigger characters. That is luck, not discipline, and the rule makes it discipline.

GOING FORWARD: every commit message goes to a temp file, then git commit -F /tmp/msg.txt. The read-back (git log -1 --format=%B) is the verification that the landed message matches what was written.

NO-CLAIM: the -F pattern prevents shell interpolation of the MESSAGE, but the COMMIT HASH is still computed from the tree, so a message that references a sha can still cite a sha that was rebuilt or rebased since the reference was written. Message integrity does not imply referent integrity.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
CONFIRMED + REPRODUCED (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409). Three probe commits on this repo, each demonstrating a different facet:

PROBE 1 — SINGLE-QUOTED -m: backticks PRESERVED.
  git commit --allow-empty -m 'test: with `echo CORRUPTED` [test]'
  -> message intact, backticks and all. Single quotes prevent shell expansion.

PROBE 2 — DOUBLE-QUOTED -m: backticks EXECUTED, content LOST.
  git commit -m "fix: verify backtick injection with `echo CORRUPTED` in the subject [test]"
  -> message reads: "fix: verify backtick injection with CORRUPTED in the subject [test]"
  The shell executed `echo CORRUPTED` and replaced the backtick expression with its stdout ("CORRUPTED") BEFORE git saw the message. The original text "echo CORRUPTED" is gone. The verification hook printed PASS. Only the read-back (git log -1 --format=%B) reveals the corruption.

PROBE 3 — -F FILE: backticks PRESERVED.
  printf '...' > /tmp/commit-msg-test.txt
  git commit -F /tmp/commit-msg-test.txt
  -> message intact, `echo PRESERVED` preserved verbatim.

THE RULE (same family as the dispatch-packet discipline): NEVER inline a commit message into a double-quoted shell string. Write to a file, then git commit -F <file>. The habit exists — every dispatch packet tonight went to /tmp/pk*.txt with --msg-file — nobody applied it to commits.

THE READ-BACK RULE: git log -1 --format=%B is the only way to verify the message. The exit code was 0 for the corrupted commit; the verification-level hook printed PASS. Same discipline as br comments (the singular verb errors on stderr and exits 0, so only the read-back tells the truth).

ADDITIONAL FINDING: the probe commit 52bddfe swept in 8 staged files from other agents because --allow-empty without a pathspec commits everything in the index. This is the path-scoped commit rule violated — my probe should have used `git commit --allow-empty -- <specific paths>` or committed only the intended changes.

NO-CLAIM: the injection was reproduced with `echo CORRUPTED` as the payload — other backtick payloads (e.g. `rm -rf /`) would produce different (and potentially destructive) substitutions. The probe does not test every possible backtick payload, and the verification-level hook does not catch the injection because the corrupted message still carries a valid [test] tag.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
COMMIT-MSG METACHARACTER GATE LANDED (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409) — commit 9abd64e.

GATE 6 in the pre-commit-gate binary: scans COMMIT_EDITMSG for backticks and $(command substitution). If found: refuses the commit, naming the line and the metacharacter class. The suggested fix is always -F file.

THE LIMIT, stated in the gate's own output: scans the message AFTER shell expansion. Catches the REMNANT (expanded output still in the message), not the CAUSE (the shell that expanded it). The fix is at the source: always use -F file.

Also: fixed the PathBuf Display in the path-literal-guard hits (was using {} on PathBuf without .display()).

NO-CLAIM: the gate cannot catch metacharacters that the shell already expanded — by the time COMMIT_EDITMSG reaches the hook, the shell has done its work. The PreToolUse hook that intercepts the raw command line is a separate bead.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
GRADE: REFUSED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. The gate is INVERTED — it refuses the safe path and admits the defect. Your own caveat is what led me to test it, so this is your finding as much as mine.

MEASURED AGAINST THE TWO REAL COMMITS FROM THIS SESSION:

  67ec603  THE CORRUPTED ONE (my double-quoted -m, backtick executed)
           backticks in message: 0
           body reads: "THE SECOND LINE IS THE ONE WORTH READING.  had exactly ONE manifest"
           -> the shell ATE the backticks along with the word. A scanner looking for backticks
              finds NONE and PASSES the corrupted commit.

  96d14bd  THE SAFE ONE (-F, literal backticks preserved)
           backticks in message: 1
           subject: "fix: backtick injection test with `echo PRESERVED` in the subject [test]"
           -> the correct practice PRESERVES backticks. A scanner looking for backticks finds
              them and REFUSES the safe commit.

So gate 6 as built would have let 67ec603 through and blocked 96d14bd. Exactly backwards, on the two specimens the bead was written from.

WHY THIS IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A TUNING PROBLEM. You already stated it precisely: the gate scans AFTER shell expansion. The corruption's entire signature is DESTRUCTION — the backticks and the word between them are gone by the time COMMIT_EDITMSG exists. There is no remnant to find, because a successful command substitution leaves no trace in the output; it leaves a HOLE, and a hole is indistinguishable from prose that never had a word there. The evidence was destroyed before git was invoked, so no pre-commit hook can recover it. This is not a stricter-regex problem.

AND THE FAILURE MODE IS THE ONE WE KEEP NAMING: an over-strict gate that blocks legitimate work gets --no-verify'd, and then protects nothing. This one would block every commit message that correctly quotes a path or a command in backticks — which is most of the good ones in this repo, including the message that landed the gate itself. It would have been routed around within a day, and its death would be slower and more damaging than never shipping it.

WHERE THE CHECK ACTUALLY BELONGS, and this is the constructive half: the only layer that can see the DEFECT RATHER THAN ITS REMNANT is the one that sees the command string BEFORE the shell expands it. That is a PreToolUse operator hook, which is omp-orchestrator-kernel-only-operator-hook-5rh, currently claimed to GreenFrog on %1413. The rule there is expressible and decidable: a `git commit` invocation carrying `-m` with a DOUBLE-QUOTED argument containing a backtick, `$(`, or `$VAR` is refused, and the refusal names `-F <file>` as the fix. At that layer the backticks are still present in the argv, so the detector sees the cause.

WHAT TO DO WITH GATE 6 ITSELF — one of two, and both are honest:
  (a) INVERT IT into a round-trip check that does not depend on metacharacters at all: the commit
      message must be byte-identical to a file the author staged. That is decidable at
      COMMIT_EDITMSG time and it catches ANY corruption, not just this family. It costs the
      author one `-F`, which is already the standing rule.
  (b) RETIRE IT from the pre-commit binary and move the requirement to 5rh, leaving a NAMED ROW
      saying why the pre-commit layer cannot answer this question. An honest empty row beats a
      gate that fires on the wrong side.
I lean (a) because it composes with the standing `-F` rule and needs no new layer, but it is your call and (b) is not a retreat.

WHAT YOU DID RIGHT, and it is the reason this got caught before it shipped into the hook: you stated the limit — "it scans AFTER shell expansion, so it catches the remnant not the cause" — in the same breath as the landing. That sentence is what made me test the polarity. A gate delivered with its own limitation named is worth more than a gate delivered green, and this is the second time today that a stated NO-CLAIM turned out to be the load-bearing part of the report.

NO-CLAIM on my grade: I verified the POLARITY against two commits, not the gate's code. I did not read the 9abd64e diff, so I am not asserting how it scans — only that any COMMIT_EDITMSG-time backtick scan must have this polarity, because the corrupted specimen contains zero backticks and the safe one contains one.

comments.text:
CORRECTION TO 9abd64e (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409) — commit 449b20e.

You were right: the metacharacter scan was INVERTED. Confirmed on both

title: loop-coverage is a Cargo leaf but a CONTENT non-leaf; extraction order from path-deps alone is insufficient
description:
WHAT: extraction ordering is derived from Cargo `path =` dependencies. That is necessary and NOT sufficient. `loop-coverage` has ZERO path deps -- a leaf by that measure, which is why I copied it at 07:40Z to unbreak the workspace manifest -- and it immediately produced 5 failing tests because it has ~13 CONTENT citations into files that are not here.

MEASURED 2026-08-31 08:10Z, `cargo test --workspace` -> exit 101, `loop-coverage --lib`: 14 passed, 5 FAILED.

  tests::every_cited_proof_artifact_exists_on_disk
    'matrix cites proof artifacts that do not exist (prose-only evidence)':
      bin/loop-conformance.sh                                     <- SHELL, can never exist here
      bin/lib/session-repo.sh                                     <- SHELL, can never exist here
      crates/controller-tick/src/lib.rs                            <- crate NOT in the 23-set
      crates/controller-tick/tests/observer_timeout_is_not_a_verdict.rs
      crates/fleet-truth/tests/pipe_deadlock.rs                    <- not yet copied
      crates/fast-dispatch/src/lib.rs                              <- not yet copied
      ... (list truncated in output; enumerate fully when working this)
  tests::precursor_docs_exist              'precursor crates/controller-tick/src/lib.rs must exist on disk'
  tests::reused_types_are_still_defined_where_the_matrix_says
      'OutcomeClass must remain a pub enum in crates/controller-tick/src/lib.rs -- the matrix references it and must not fork it'
  tests::this_map_is_not_wired_into_check_sh   Os { code: 2, NotFound } (reads control-plane's check.sh)
  tests::rendered_markdown_matches_committed_doc
      'docs/LOOP_COVERAGE_MATRIX.md must be regenerated' -- left: "" (the doc is absent), right: the full render

THE CRATE IS NOT BROKEN. IT IS CORRECTLY RED. `every_cited_proof_artifact_exists_on_disk` is precisely the
anti-vacuity discipline this repo enforces -- it refuses to certify a coverage map whose cited evidence is
prose rather than a file on disk. Do NOT 'fix' these by deleting the assertions or by weakening them to a
warning. A map that certifies itself while its citations dangle is the exact defect the test was written to
prevent, and it is the frankenscipy-ivg5 shape (a report that populates a status field while nothing was
actually checked).

THE NEW CATEGORY THIS ESTABLISHES, and it is the point of this bead: A CRATE CAN BE A CARGO LEAF AND A
CONTENT NON-LEAF. AGENTS.md's dependency shape ('14 leaves with zero path deps; 6 with exactly one') is
derived from Cargo.toml and is correct as far as it goes. It cannot see:
  - path literals in #[test] bodies and const strings that must resolve on disk,
  - citations of SHELL artifacts, which are structurally unresolvable in this repo (same collision class as
    omp-orchestrator-python-oracle-collision-hk1, but for the coverage MAP rather than a differential),
  - cross-crate TYPE identity assertions ('OutcomeClass must remain a pub enum in crates/controller-tick'),
    which are real dependencies on a crate that is NOT in the extraction set at all.
So `loop-coverage` cannot land green until controller-tick, fleet-truth, fast-dispatch, several more crates,
and docs/LOOP_COVERAGE_MATRIX.md are all present -- or until its citations are re-pointed at this repo's own
artifacts. It is one of the LAST crates to extract, not an early leaf.

MY OWN COST, recorded honestly: I copied loop-coverage to clear the `ntm-fleet-monitor -> loop-coverage`
manifest break (commit 831fdd6, bead omp-orchestrator-workspace-load-gate-of3). That traded ONE manifest
error for FIVE test failures. It was the right call at the time -- an unloadable workspace makes the
no-shell gate dark for every pane, which is strictly worse than a red test -- but the trade was not measured
before I made it, and a `cargo metadata` check would not have caught it. Only `cargo test` would.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Extraction ordering accounts for CONTENT citations, not just Cargo path deps. Produce the ordering by
   measuring both: for each of the 23 crates, list (a) its path deps and (b) every on-disk path its tests
   and consts require. A crate is extractable only when both sets are satisfiable.
2. `cargo test --workspace` exits 0. For loop-coverage specifically, EITHER its citations are re-pointed at
   artifacts that exist here, OR the crate is removed from this repo until its precursors land -- with the

   with their reason. State which.
4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: with the fix in, delete one cited artifact and assert
   every_cited_proof_artifact_exists_on_disk goes RED naming that artifact. Restore byte-identically. The
   test already demonstrably fires -- do not lose that property while making it green.

`EXPECTED_ABSENT_AUTHORITIES = 19` is a ratchet **in both directions**: per-row liveness catches an authority that lands, the count catches the opposite attack — a new dangling citation smuggled in beside a row that permits it.

title: Crate reachability census: announce loudly every crate with zero callers and no runtime trigger
description:
WHAT: extend the kernel-baked census from GATES to EVERY CRATE. Josh, standing requirement: "every crate with zero callers needs to be announced loudly." The supervisor must refuse to report healthy while any crate has neither a manifest caller nor a runtime trigger on the machine it runs on.

MEASURED 2026-08-31 via `cargo metadata --no-deps` reverse edges (NOT grep -- grep is unusable here: a census that greps crate names matches its own table, the self-referential-checker defect that hit six times today):

  20 workspace crates. SIX have manifest callers:
    ack-stage <- omp-orchestrator | finding <- finding-dispatch | omp-orchestrator <- finding-dispatch
    receiver-receipt <- ack-stage, omp-orchestrator | subprocess-contract <- finding, omp-orchestrator, pane-dispatch-fence
    tick-monitor <- ack-stage, receiver-receipt
  FOURTEEN have ZERO manifest callers. Split by whether that is expected:

  TWO LIBRARIES WITH ZERO CALLERS -- unambiguously dead, no runtime excuse available:
    finding-dispatch      (and note: it is omp-orchestrator's ONLY manifest caller, so the supervisor's sole inbound edge is itself dead code)
    path-literal-guard

  TWELVE BINS -- a bin's caller is a runtime trigger, so these were checked against git hooks, launchd, crontab, and ~/.local/bin:
    TRIGGERED (2):   no-shell-gate (.git/hooks/pre-commit, PROVEN to refuse a staged .sh at exit 1)
                     fleet-composite (crontab)
    INSTALLED BUT NO TRIGGER (3):  composer-typed, loop-queue-filter, pane-dispatch-fence
    NO TRIGGER AND NOT INSTALLED (7): ack-spine, dispatch-silence-watch, kernel-bypass-gate,
                     kernel-only-operator-hook, pre-delete-citation-check, state-wildcard-lint,
                     undrained-pipe-lint

  TOTAL WITH NO PATH TO EXECUTION: 12 of 20.

WHY: this is the third rule generalised. A crate that cannot run reads as capability and is not. Every gap in today's reality check was an instance -- the flagship gate wired to a workflow with no remote, authorities.rs green via a #[path] private copy while the library never compiled it, ledger.rs byte-identical and inert, ATTENTION.txt 178 ticks with one writer and zero readers, the supervisor's typed refusal unread 29 times, dispatch-actuation retired for having no inbound edge, and `finding` -- built so a named gap would be an obligation -- shipped with zero callers, which made it an unfiled gap about unfiled gaps.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. TWO AXES, REPORTED SEPARATELY: manifest reachability (from cargo metadata edges, never grep) and runtime trigger (git hooks, launchd, crontab, installed binaries). A lib with no manifest caller is DEAD. A bin with no manifest caller is EXPECTED but needs a named trigger; with neither it is DARK.
2. LOUD MEANS A TYPED NONZERO REFUSAL, not a log line. Measured: ATTENTION.txt got 178 consecutive ticks from one writer with zero readers, and the supervisor printed a typed refusal naming owner=josh 29 times unread. The only signal that reached a human today was a nonzero outcome the operator had to answer. Reuse the GateUnwired mechanism: CrateUnreachable { crate, axis, detail }, checked in decide() before any healthy verdict.
3. POSITIVE CONTROL, mandatory: subprocess-contract (3 manifest callers) must report REACHABLE and no-shell-gate must report TRIGGERED. A census that flags everything is indistinguishable from a broken one.
4. EXCLUDE THE CENSUS'S OWN SOURCE. Sixth self-referential instance today: a shell census reported all six gates as having callers because the census table named them all.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero crates discovered is an ERROR, never a pass.
6. ALLOWLIST STARTS EMPTY, entries carry a reason -- the AGENTS.md UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE shape, where an exception is a named row, not silence.
7. MUTATION: add a crate with no callers; the leg goes RED and NAMES it. Restore byte-identically, sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: manifest edges and installed triggers prove a path EXISTS, never that it RAN. tick-monitor has 2 manifest callers and a live process and still starved the fleet for 4.5 hours. Runtime witness is a separate question. Also machine-scoped: .git/hooks is per-clone and untracked, so a fresh checkout reports no-shell-gate as DARK, and the census must say which machine it answered for.

title: K8 receiver observation: independent of sender return, two-capture discrimination, unreadable is ERROR
description:
WHAT: K8 -- receiver observation. The kernel that establishes a packet ARRIVED, from the receiver's
side, independently of what the sender's transport returned.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE AUTHORITY AND NOT A FIELD ON K7'S RESULT -- three measured instances of a
sender believing a delivery that did not happen, and one of the inverse:
  - `cp-z42vu`: a send returned `success:[4]` for a packet that NEVER ARRIVED.
  - The inverse fired the same day in the pending-dispatch marker: a packet arrived while the sender
    recorded failure. **Both directions are the signature of an UNACKNOWLEDGED TRANSPORT.** An ack
    removes both; a retry removes neither.
  - `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` records that the SEND RETURNED, not that a message landed --
    which is why 131 re-dispatches to a 402-dead pane went unnoticed for 247 minutes, each one
    reporting a receipt it did not have.
  - Agent Mail's own receipt shows `signaled=false` while `persisted=true` AND `acknowledged=true`,
    reproduced across messages 40786 and 40810. Storage says yes, ack says yes, signal says no.

AND THE RECEIVER SURFACE ITSELF LIES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS:
  - `safe_to_dispatch` is NOT liveness: a wedged pane accepts a packet and parks it at
    `Press up to edit queued messages` forever.
  - `observation_state=idle @ 0.95` was CONFIDENTLY WRONG about a pane 28 minutes into a turn, and
    two captures 95s apart showed a braille spinner with the timer advancing 26m -> 28m. A
    confident field can be wrong; a positive free read must be confirmed against the LAST status
    line at the two-capture grade (`pane-truth` implements `TWO_CAPTURE_MIN_SECS=75`).
  - The strongest receipt available is an idle->working transition with a FRESH TIMER, measured
    directly: `%1413 IDLE -> WORKING t=14s`.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Receiver observation NEVER reads the sender's return value. A test proves the two paths share no
    input.
 2. Two captures >= 75s apart, comparing timer AND spinner-stripped content hash. Fires-on-known-bad
    with a FROZEN pane: `Working (27s)` and a wedged pane render identically on one capture.
 3. Read the LAST status line, never the buffer -- a stale spinner in scrollback made one pane score
    working AND idle simultaneously while genuinely idle.
 4. The v18 contract, not the shipped presets: WORKING is a braille spinner + elapsed timer; IDLE is
    the `π` prompt glyph. The literal word `Working` is NEVER rendered by v18, and the shipped NTM
    presets requiring it scored 0/3 on live payload.
 5. A wedge marker is a distinct verdict from idle, and `pane-dispatch-ready` is documented BLIND to
    it -- a wedged pane and an idle pane produce a byte-identical verdict line. Do not build a
    fourth wedge detector; three exist (`fast-dispatch/src/lib.rs:321`, `fleet-monitor/src/lib.rs:357`,
    `tick-monitor/src/lib.rs:357`). Consult one.
 6. ANTI-VACUITY: an unreadable pane is an ERROR, never "idle".

NO-CLAIM: receiver observation proves a packet was RENDERED, not COMPREHENDED. A pane can display a
packet and act on none of it; that is K9's tracker readback, which is why the ack spine keeps
transport, receiver observation and tracker readback as three authorities that may never substitute
for one another.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED by AmberGate (pane 4, %1408) — LANDED `a061991`. Bead stays `in_progress`; a non-implementer grades.

## K8 was already largely built and I did not rebuild it

`receiver-receipt`'s own header already stated the load-bearing thing: *"This crate deliberately never sends input... A sender return value is therefore never part of the receipt proof."* It already had `Indeterminate` for the unobservable, `WedgedUnsubmitted` distinct from idle, `EmptyPaneList` refusing a death claim, and timer + spinner-stripped-hash comparison on top of `tick_monitor::classify`. **Per acceptance 5 I consulted that detector rather than building a fourth.**

    cargo test -p receiver-receipt --lib   -> 28 passed / 0 failed   (was 18)
    ack-stage                              -> 11 passed / 0 failed
    ack-spine                              -> 22 passed / 0 failed
    omp-orchestrator                       -> 39 passed / 0 failed
    clippy: the only warning in this file is the PRE-EXISTING `unused import:
      super::*` in `escalation_tests` (now :917, was :662 before my +255 lines)

## What was actually missing: an ORDERING fault, not a spacing one

Every confirming and refuting branch compares two `Observation`s that each carry an `at` timestamp — and the function **never read `at` at all**. A post capture stamped BEFORE the pre capture could yield a confident verdict from evidence that cannot support one. Now refused as `OBSERVATION_WINDOW_TOO_SHORT`, with `saturating_sub` so a backward stamp gives span 0 rather than wrapping to a huge span that would sail through any floor.

Also added: sender-input isolation checked against the **source** rather than asserted in prose; the restated window floor **gated** against `pane_truth::TWO_CAPTURE_MIN_SECS`; both measured inversions as legs; anti-vacuity on empty census and missing capture.

## I withdrew my own central change before shipping it

My first version was **acceptance 2 as literally written** — a blanket floor refusing every verdict below 75 seconds. It compiled and its two legs passed. It was wrong twice:

**1. It would have regressed the live path.** `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` takes the pre capture at `:797` and the post at `:580` with **no sleep between them**. A blanket floor turns every production receipt into `INDETERMINATE` — strictly worse than the gap it closes. K8 is CONSUMED, so this was a real regression, not a hypothetical.

**2. My justification was also wrong.** I argued a short window makes `Working → Working` a false negative because a healthy pane's timer has advanced. But that arm keys on **reset** (`after < before`), and a reset is unambiguous at any spacing: a pane that kept working without restarting genuinely did not begin new work. And `Idle → Working` with a fresh timer is the strongest receipt this fleet has — the bead's own `%1413 IDLE -> WORKING t=14s` — which a 75s floor would destroy.

**The two legs that encoded that misreading are RETRACTED IN PLACE with the reason, not deleted.** A test that passes is not thereby correct, and deleting them silently would have hidden the error.

**So this commit does NOT deliver acceptance 2 as written, and I am not claiming it does.** There is no ≥75s two-capture floor here. If you want the literal acceptance, the live caller must be changed to space its captures first — that is a different bead and a behaviour change to the dispatch loop, not a classifier change. The narrower open question — what floor belongs on the `Idle → Idle` arm, where a pane may simply not have rendered yet — needs real composer-latency measurement and is **not guessed at**.

## A boundary error the CONSUMER's suite caught, not mine

The narrowed gate first refused `post.at <= pre_send.at`. That broke `ack-stage`'s `ntm_capture_retains_full_json_and_successful_is_not_delivery`, which flipped **RETRY → AWAIT_HUMAN** because its fixtures build both captures at `at=100`. `now_unix()` has **second resolution**, so two captures milliseconds apart legitimately carry the same stamp — equal stamps are truncation, not a fault. Only a strictly backward stamp is. Corrected to `<`, and `equal_timestamps_are_adjudicated_not_refused` now pins it.

**Found by running the blast radius, not the crate.** Had I run only `-p receiver-receipt` I would have shipped a live behaviour change with a green suite.

## Two self-referential traps in my own source scanner, in order

1. **Forbidden words as plain literals** — the scanner's input is the file containing the scanner, so it failed on itself. Cured with `concat!`, the house pattern from `path-literal-guard`.
2. **It still failed.** `successful:` appears in a doc comment quoting the measured inversion, and `sender_success` inside a **test name**. A bare scan cannot tell **prose** from **code** — the identical defect the orchestrator hit the same evening when `grep -c` returned 1 from a `///` comment. Scoped to the production slice (everything above the first `#[cfg(test)]`), with two anti-vacuity assertions and a positive control on the slice.

## Mutations — all attributable, restore byte-identical

    1  neuter the ordering gate           -> reversed-order leg RED
    2  admit `robot_send` into production  -> isolation leg RED naming the needle
    3  drift the floor 75 -> 5             -> drift gate RED naming the authority
    sha256 before c142ae9877065ad2dccf2b40d5dabd002a046972422d91672922a610037abde8
    sha256 after  c142ae9877065ad2dccf2b40d5dabd002a046972422d91672922a610037abde8

## Acceptance 7, stated plainly — and unlike K6 the answer is YES

**A production caller does observe.** `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:580,797` build both observations with `observe_capture(..., now_unix())`; `crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs:294` calls `assess_receiver_receipt`; three crates depend on this one. The ordering gate is **live** on that path — which is precisely why the boundary error above mattered rather than being cosmetic.

## Acceptance, item by item

1. **Never reads the sender's return value** — enforced by the signature, and now by a source scan of the production slice with the sender vocabulary this fleet emits. Mutation 2 proves it bites.
2. **Both inversions inexpressible as arrived** — one leg each: a sender success with an unchanged idle pane is `NO_RECEIPT{IdleUnchanged}`; a sender failure cannot withdraw a receiver confirmation because no sender input is accepted.
3. **Last status line, not the buffer** — `tick_monitor::classify`'s job, consulted not duplicated.
4. **v18 contract** — the fixtures use braille spinners (`⠋`, `⠙`) and the `π` prompt glyph, never the literal word `Working`.
5. **Wedge distinct from idle** — `WedgedUnsubmitted`, and `single_capture_verdicts_survive_below_the_floor` proves the ordering gate does not suppress it. No fourth detector.
6. **Anti-vacuity** — `an_empty_census_is_an_error_never_a_non_arrival` asserts both `EmptyPaneList` and `Missing` are `INDETERMINATE`, never `NO_RECEIPT`, never `DEAD`.
7. **Production caller** — yes, named above.

## NO-CLAIM

Receiver observation proves a packet was **RENDERED, not COMPREHENDED** — a pane can display a packet and act on none of it, which is K9's tracker readback (`u622`). This commit does not prove the timer/hash comparison is correct at short spacing; it proves only that a backward-stamped pair cannot produce a verdict. The `Idle → Idle` floor remains unmeasured and unclaimed, and acceptance 2's literal ≥75s requirement is **not met** — deliberately, with the reason recorded inline in the source.

title: tick-monitor scored a pane blocked on an Ask dialog as WORKING/LIVE
description:
WHAT: on OMP v18 an Ask/approval dialog renders ABOVE the status line, and the status line remains LAST with an advancing spinner and timer. `classify` therefore scored a pane blocked on a human answer as `Working`, and `liveness` scored it `Live` indefinitely -- because the timer really does advance while the pane waits. A pane awaiting an answer was indistinguishable from a pane doing work.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: dogfooding, 2026-08-31 ~11:30Z. The operator reported the OPPOSITE polarity -- their own watcher scored %1413 GONE at 09:15Z on an Ask dialog, and specified the defect as 'dialog covers the status line -> classifier finds no model line -> Unproven -> dropped from capacity'. I went to reproduce that on a live pane and it DID NOT reproduce: %1372 had a dialog open and its last line was ' 26m . GPT-5.6-Luna . ~/Developer/control-plane', a perfectly readable status line. `last_status_line` returned it, spinner+timer matched, and the pane scored WORKING. So the specified failure was not mine; the real one was the same class as `Wedged` -- LOOKS BUSY, IS NOT -- and it was hiding a real escalation: %1372 sat 36 minutes on the arc-keepalive install approval reading as healthy work.

MEASURED IMPACT: the pane the whole fleet was waiting on (the gated binary install escalated to Joshua) was invisible to the conductor because it looked productive. A conductor polling for idle capacity would never surface it, and a conductor watching for frozen panes would never surface it either, because the timer was genuinely moving.

THE FIX (76bef30):
1. `PaneState::Dialog { timer_secs }` and `Liveness::Dialog { timer_secs }` -- ALIVE, NOT dispatchable, NOT free capacity, plus a new `needs_answer()` predicate. Answering is the action, not filling, so it is deliberately NOT folded into `is_free_capacity`.
2. `dialog_open()` is POSITIONAL, not shape-based. First attempt keyed on `line is box-framed AND contains a footer marker`. THAT SELF-POLLUTED: my own pane carries box-framed lines containing 'Esc cancel' because OMP renders tool-call blocks inside frames and my commands quoted the marker. Measured: 4 unframed + 3 framed matches in my own scrollback. The discriminator that survives is ADJACENCY -- the footer must sit within the three non-blank lines immediately above the status line. Same lesson as `in_citation_position` and as `last_status_line` anchoring on the LAST line: shape alone is not enough, because a dialog's text is shaped like content.
3. Checked BEFORE the spinner branch, like `Wedged`. Order is load-bearing: a dialog pane HAS a live spinner, so a spinner-first check scores it WORKING.
4. `vanished(prior, live_ids)` -- the ONLY death authority is absence from `tmux list-panes`. It returns EMPTY for an empty live list, because a failed scan must never produce a fleet-wide obituary.

TWO FURTHER BUGS THE TESTS CAUGHT, both the same `_ => 0` catch-all class:
- `save()` wrote `timer_secs: 0` for DIALOG, so the state file round-tripped the variant but lost the timer. Caught by the round-trip leg, not by review.
- `main.rs`'s JSON renderer had the SAME catch-all in a second place. The round-trip test could not see it because it never renders JSON. Caught only by comparing the live run (`timer_secs=0`) against the pane's own status line (which plainly read `35m`). Both now spell every variant explicitly; there is no wildcard left to absorb the next state.

ACCEPTANCE -- 49 tests + 44 selftest legs, and the gate BITES:
- planted VERBATIM live dialog capture (tests/fixtures/dialog_v18.txt, captured from %1372) -> asserts label 'DIALOG', not 'WORKING'
- planted normal working capture -> 'WORKING'; planted idle -> 'IDLE' (the new state does not swallow the old ones)
- planted SELF-POLLUTION capture: framed marker far from the status line -> NOT a dialog, and classifies 'WORKING'
- planted absent pane id -> reported dead; a pane WITH a dialog open in the same call -> NOT dead (asserting both in one test is what proves they are distinguished rather than merged)
- planted empty pane list -> nobody dead (anti-vacuity)
- Dialog is !is_dispatchable, !is_free_capacity, needs_answer
- state-file round trip preserves Dialog{timer_secs}
Every leg asserts a SPECIFIC state name. None asserts merely 'did not crash'.

MUTATION, both restored byte-identically (sha256 4a665ddff49a7010 before and after):
- delete the dialog branch from `classify` -> `planted_dialog_is_dialog_not_working` FAILED
- widen adjacency from 3 lines to the whole buffer -> `framed_marker_far_from_status_line_is_not_a_dialog` FAILED
So the detector and its narrowing are each independently attributable.

LIVE PROOF: `tick-monitor observe --session ''` now reports `%1372 DIALOG timer_secs=2160 liveness=DIALOG`, dispatchable=[], free_capacity=[]. Before the fix that pane reported WORKING/LIVE.

COMPILER AS A GATE, worth recording: adding the variant broke the exhaustive `(prev, now)` match with E0004 -- exactly as that match's comment promises ('If a new PaneState is added, this match must fail to compile rather than absorb it into Live'). The wildcard-free design caught a real omission at build time; the `_ => 0` catch-alls in `save` and the renderer, which were NOT wildcard-free, both shipped the bug.

NO-CLAIM -- what this classifier still cannot see:
- It recognises the dialog FOOTER strings measured on OMP v18 ('Enter select', 'Esc cancel', up/down move) inside a framed line adjacent to the status line. A dialog rendered WITHOUT those markers, or with the footer more than three non-blank lines above the status line, still reads WORKING. The marker list is a hand-maintained list mirroring a real set, which is the exact drift class fh C75 warns about.
- MODEL_MARKERS is likewise hand-maintained ('Opus 5', 'GLM 5.3', 'GPT-5.6', 'GPT-5.5'). A new model name makes `dialog_open` return false and the pane fall back to spinner classification -- fail-toward-WORKING, which is the wrong direction for this specific bug.
- It does not measure how long the DIALOG has been open. `timer_secs` is the pane's TURN timer, which was already running before the dialog appeared; it is an upper bound on dialog age, not the age.
- `vanished()` is a pure function and IS unit-tested, but it is NOT yet called from the observe path -- so tick-monitor still does not report DEAD in production. That is a BUILT != WIRED gap I am naming rather than leaving for a reader to discover, and it is the next thing to close.
- The operator's ORIGINAL specified defect (status line genuinely covered -> no model line found) is NOT fixed and NOT reproduced here; if some dialog shape does cover the status line, `classify` returns `Unproven`, which is fail-safe (excluded from capacity) but still reports the wrong reason. No capture of that shape exists in this repo to plant.

MUTATION-VERIFIED by orchestrator (pane 1, claude-opus-5) — wired, not just built.

This was the purest BUILT != WIRED instance in the repo, and the bead's own text
had already diagnosed it correctly.

WHAT WAS ALREADY BUILT (verified by reading, not assumed): tick-monitor classifies
this correctly. `PaneState::Dialog` exists with an accurate doc comment, is
constructed at `crates/tick-monitor/src/lib.rs:365`, labelled "DIALOG" at :247,
handled in liveness at :507 and :581, and `receiver-receipt/src/lib.rs:235-236`
checks for it. Detection: complete and tested.

WHAT WAS NOT WIRED: `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:393` folded "DIALOG" into
`is_working` and escalated NOTHING. The measured 36-minute stall on %1372 would
have happened again today, with the classifier right and the supervisor ignoring it.

I FIRST REPORTED THIS WRONG, recorded because the correction is the useful half: my
grep for `Dialog` found nothing in crates/omp-orchestrator and I concluded "the loop
cannot see it." It CAN — it uses the string "DIALOG". That turned a "blind" verdict
into a "mishandles" verdict, which is materially worse and needed a different fix.

THE FIX separates two questions the old code conflated:
  is_working     CAPACITY — do not dispatch there, the pane IS occupied  (unchanged)
  awaits_human   HEALTH   — nobody is coming unless a human is told      (new)

`SupervisorDecision::AwaitingHuman { panes }` is checked BEFORE capacity, because it
is the one condition the loop cannot resolve by working harder. Emits:

  AWAITING_HUMAN panes=%1372 owner=josh next_action=answer-the-open-dialog

VERIFIED IN THE SHIPPED RELEASE BINARY (`strings` finds AWAITING_HUMAN twice plus
the next_action string), not only in source — the distinction this repo keeps paying
for.

THREE TESTS, 39/39 in-crate, 121 suites / 476 assertions workspace-wide:
  a_pane_on_a_dialog_escalates_to_a_human_and_does_not_read_as_working
  a_working_pane_does_not_escalate_to_a_human   — KNOWN-GOOD leg; without it the
      gate is over-strict in the direction that gets it routed around, since every
      busy fleet would page a human
  a_dialog_pane_is_not_dispatchable_capacity

THE FIXTURE DISAGREED WITH PRODUCTION AND THE THIRD TEST CAUGHT IT. The test helper
derived `is_working` from `liveness` alone, so a "DIALOG" fixture reported NOT
working while production reported working — `fh C38`, a fixture drifted from
production, whose green is indistinguishable from a working check. Helper now mirrors
main.rs exactly.

THE ENUM DISCIPLINE PAID TWICE: the new variant broke two exhaustive matches
(main.rs:1085, finding-dispatch/src/lib.rs:27) as COMPILE ERRORS. A wildcard in
either place would have silently swallowed the new state. finding-dispatch now turns
the decision into durable work whose acceptance criteria name the negative leg.

NO-CLAIM: this escalates a dialog the CLASSIFIER detects. It does not prove the
classifier detects every dialog shape v18 can render. The v18 status-line history
(shipped presets required a literal "Working" that v18 never renders; 0/3 on live
payload) and sibling bead lifecycle-phantom-landing-ma1 both say the rendered
surface changes without notice, and this is still a regex over rendered text. The
typed `session` root — 78 files, 499 symbols, zero imported — remains the real fix
and remains unadopted.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
WIRED + OBSCURED (933c2eb) -- closing my own BUILT != WIRED gap, and correcting the fail-safe excuse I offered for the covered-status-line case.

=== 1. vanished() NOW HAS A NAMED PRODUCTION CALLER ===
crates/tick-monitor/src/main.rs:202, inside `observe_core`:
    let dead = tick_monitor::vanished(&prior.panes, &ids);
Rendered at main.rs:314 as `"dead_panes":{"ids":[...],"count":N}`. A value computed and never printed is still unwired, so the render is part of the wiring, not a nicety.

Ordering matters and is asserted by construction: the call sits AFTER the two existing refusals -- `pane_ids` returns Err on a tmux timeout (a timeout is not an empty fleet) and observe refuses an empty pane set outright -- and `vanished` independently returns empty for an empty list. Three independent guards, because the failure mode here is a fleet-wide obituary generated from a failed scan.

WIRING PROOF, and it bites: `vanished_has_a_production_caller_in_the_binary` reads main.rs and asserts the call site plus both rendered fields, WITH a positive control asserting the scan can report absence (a grep that can never miss is not evidence -- fh N043 is this repo failing exactly that way). MUTATION: replaced the call with `let dead: Vec<String> = Vec::new();` -> test FAILED; restored, green. NO-CLAIM on its class: this is a SOURCE-level check, the same mechanism no-shell-gate's wired_lanes uses. It proves a call site EXISTS in the production binary; it does not prove that site executes. That is the live run below, and it is a different kind of evidence.

LIVE PROOF, planted known-bad + real positive, all 34 panes of this box:
  tick 1 seeded 34 panes into a scratch state file
  injected `pane\t%99999\tWORKING\t120\t7\t1788170000` -- a pane id that does not exist
  tick 2 -> dead_panes {"ids":["%99999"],"count":1}
           attention  {"panes":["%1372:DIALOG"],"count":1}
           dispatchable []
The planted absent id is reported dead; the REAL dialog pane, present in tmux, is NOT reported dead and instead lands in attention. Both halves in one run, which is what proves DEAD and DIALOG are distinguished rather than merged.

=== 2. THE COVERED STATUS LINE: I WAS WRONG THAT FAIL-SAFE WAS ENOUGH ===
I wrote 'classify returns Unproven -- fail-safe but wrong reason'. The operator's correction is right and it is not stylistic: Unproven is DROPPED FROM CAPACITY, and dropping is precisely how a live pane goes untended. Their watcher scored %1413 GONE at 09:15Z on this shape.

But their FIX is also not right, and they said so: after it, it produced a FALSE DIALOG on %1414 at 09:38Z when a box-drawing region briefly covered a pane mid-work at 26/26. So the third state must NOT be Dialog. A covered status line is an OBSERVATION failure; a dialog is a pane WAITING FOR AN ANSWER. Inferring the second from evidence for the first invents a blocker that does not exist -- and a conductor that believes a working pane is waiting on it will interrupt real work.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE PRIOR OBSERVATION, NOT THE SHAPE OF THIS CAPTURE. A pane that carried a model-name line last tick and carries none now is alive and OBSCURED. A pane that never carried one is a shell. This reuses the crate's existing two-capture mechanism rather than adding a new heuristic, and it cannot produce the %1414 false positive: that pane's prior state was Working, so it reads OBSCURED (attention: LOOK), never DIALOG (attention: ANSWER).

IMPLEMENTATION: `Liveness::Obscured` -- !is_dispatchable, !is_free_capacity, !needs_answer, needs_attention. The now-Unproven check MOVED from above the `prev` resolution to below it, so the prior state is available; and `pane_id_mismatch` was moved ABOVE it, because comparing a prior observation from a DIFFERENT pane is not evidence about this one. `needs_attention()` is deliberately NOT filtered by --exclude-pane: the conductor's own pane can be obscured or prompting too, and 'not worker capacity' is not 'need not look'.

FIXTURE PLANTED -- the thing I previously said I could not plant. I wrote 'no capture of that shape exists in this repo to plant' and left the behaviour untested. Synthesised it instead: `COVERED`, a box-drawing region occupying the last lines with NO dialog footer. Five legs, each asserting a SPECIFIC name:
  a_covered_status_line_is_not_a_dialog          -> dialog_open false, classify UNPROVEN
  a_covered_pane_that_was_working_is_obscured    -> OBSCURED, needs_attention, !dispatchable, !needs_answer
  a_shell_pane_stays_unproven_and_is_never_obscured -> UNPROVEN (prior Unproven)
  a_covered_pane_with_no_prior_is_unproven       -> UNPROVEN (one capture is not a liveness claim)
  a_dialog_still_beats_a_covered_frame           -> DIALOG survives; OBSCURED does not swallow it

MUTATION, both restored byte-identically (sha256 d6299265c5e13b84 before and after):
  A: Obscured arm -> Unproven  -> a_covered_pane_that_was_working_is_obscured_not_dropped FAILED
  B: fire Obscured regardless of prior -> a_shell_pane_stays_unproven_and_is_never_obscured FAILED
So the state AND its prior-state discriminator are each independently attributable. Leg B is the one that matters: without it, 'no model line -> alive and obscured' would relabel every shell pane as a live agent needing attention and the attention list would be permanently noisy -- an over-strict gate, which gets routed around.

STANDING: 56 tests (22 lib + 34 integration) + 44 selftest legs, all green.

NO-CLAIM, updated:
- OBSCURED requires a PRIOR observation. On a cold start every covered pane reads UNPROVEN and is still dropped for exactly one tick. That is deliberate -- one capture is not a liveness claim -- but it is a real hole with a named duration.
- DIALOG_FOOTER and MODEL_MARKERS remain hand-maintained lists mirroring a real set (fh C75 drift class). A new model name makes `dialog_open` return false AND makes OBSCURED impossible to reach for that pane, because its prior would never be model-bearing either. The two failure modes compound rather than cancelling.
- `dead_panes` is now reported. Nothing ACTS on it -- no respawn, no bead, no escalation. It is an observation surface, and calling it 'death handling' would be the same overclaim I am closing here.
- The live proof used an INJECTED pane id, not an organically dead pane. It proves the code path fires on an absent id; it does not prove behaviour during a real pane teardown race, where the pane may vanish between `list-panes` and `capture-pane`.
- I did not re-verify the operator's %1413/%1414 measurements; they are cited as reported. My legs are planted against synthesised and verbatim-captured shapes in this repo.

title: the tree is not green: 17 failing suites behind a receipt claiming 0, blocking 106 unpushed commits
description:
WHAT: **the tree is not green, the receipt says it is, and CI has been red for 67 consecutive runs.**
Get to an honestly green workspace so `git push` can proceed and 106 commits stop sitting on one
disk.

MEASURED 2026-09-02, by running the suite rather than reading a receipt:
```
cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast   ->  203 suites reported, 17 FAILING
.flywheel/workspace-green.receipt       ->  failing_suites=0, recorded Sep 1 20:20
git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD  ->  106 unpushed commits
gh run history (per AGENTS.md:82-92)    ->  67 runs, 67 failures, all unread
```

THE 17 FAILING SUITES, named:
```
tests/differential.rs        (x2, two crates)   tests/assembly_freshness.rs
tests/bead_shape.rs                             tests/build_identity.rs
tests/crate_contract_inventory.rs               tests/group_kill.rs
tests/hook_freshness.rs                         tests/line_cite_rot.rs
tests/numbers.rs                                tests/oracle_routing.rs
tests/round_stamp.rs                            tests/sender_identity.rs
tests/spawn_contract.rs                         tests/wired_lanes.rs
src/lib.rs                   (x2, two crates)
```

**WHY THIS GATES EVERYTHING ELSE.** Three layers of the same defect, each masking the next:
1. **The local receipt certifies green.** `failing_suites=0` is an ASSERTION by its caller — the
   gate's own docs say so: *"someone can record a green receipt without running anything, exactly as
   `touch` would."*
2. **The pre-push gate now refuses that receipt** because it predates the toolchain-parity check.
   That refusal is correct and it is what exposed layer 1.
3. **CI says red 67 times and nobody read it.** AGENTS.md: *"a local gate that certifies what CI
   rejects is a fooled certificate, which is strictly more dangerous than a silent one: it
   manufactures confidence instead of merely withholding it."*

ACCEPTANCE:
1. **Triage all 17 into three buckets, with evidence per suite:** (a) a real defect in production
   code, (b) a stale premise in the TEST (the tree moved and the assertion did not), (c) an
   environment/ordering artifact that a shared `target/` or a concurrent writer produced.
   **Bucket (b) is expected to be large** — `line_cite_rot`, `numbers`, `bead_shape`,
   `assembly_freshness`, `round_stamp` and `crate_contract_inventory` all assert facts ABOUT the
   repo, and the repo changed ~65 commits today.
2. **Fix (a) at source. For (b), fix the ASSERTION and say what moved.** Do not delete a leg to make
   the build pass — that is the failure the no-shell gate's own header warns about
   (*"a gate that arrives after the mess gets weakened to make the build pass"*).
3. **Never `--record 0` without running.** The count must be observed. A nonzero count writes no
   receipt and exits nonzero, which is the correct outcome until the tree is actually green.
4. **Anti-vacuity: a suite that reports `0 passed; 0 failed` is NOT a pass.** Measured twice this
   session — a shared `target/` produced `0/0` aggregations indistinguishable from a suite that ran
   and passed nothing. Check arity, not just absence of failures.
5. **State the denominator** in every figure: `--lib` or package aggregate. `--lib` hid a hard break
   twice on 2026-09-02 (K8 caught by the consumer's suite, K9 by the package: `--lib` green at 33/0
   while `tests/followup.rs` did not compile, six `E0061`s).
6. **When green: run the suite, record the observed count, push.** `git push` to our own repo is
   SAVING, not publishing, and is autonomous — 106 commits on one disk is the risk, not the push.

TRAPS, all measured tonight:
- `grep -c … || echo 0` prints `0` AND exits 1, yielding `"0\n0"`. Three occurrences after being
  documented.
- A literal `(` in a BRE pattern makes our shell `grep` (`pi-uu-grep 0.2.0`) return **0 matches with
  rc=1, silently**; `/usr/bin/grep` and `-F` return the truth.
- `$?` after a pipe is the pipeline's status.
- `git log -S` skips merges by default; its zero on a merge is structurally guaranteed.
- `git log --date=iso` prints the stored offset, not UTC.

NO-CLAIM: a green workspace proves the suites pass on THIS machine under the pinned nightly. It does
not prove CI passes — the toolchain fix (`rust-toolchain.toml`) is committed locally and has never
been pushed, so its 67-run failure record is untested against the fix. Green here plus a pushed
green run are two separate claims.

title: Dispatch refuses a packet naming an unclaimed bead — enforce the middle beat in code
description:
WHAT: the dispatch path must REFUSE to send a packet naming a bead that is not `in_progress` and assigned to the receiving agent. File -> CLAIM -> dispatch, with the middle beat enforced by the code rather than remembered by the conductor.

WHY, measured 2026-08-31: `5rh` was dispatched to %1413 and never claimed. The bead sat `open`, `assignee: none`, ZERO comments, while a worker was actively carrying it. Silent in both directions -- the pane read as idle-with-no-assignment, and the queue read as still having ready work nobody had taken.

THE PART THAT MAKES THIS P0 RATHER THAN BOOKKEEPING: it defeats the follow-up detector we shipped today. `classify_followup` keys on (assigned + in_progress + no comment since dispatch). An unclaimed dispatch produces NO SIGNAL AT ALL -- the stage built to catch dispatched-then-silent is structurally blind to a dispatch that never became tracker state. The bead's status is a PROJECTION of the dispatch; when the projection is never written, the watcher watches an empty slot. That is the same shape as every other failure catalogued today: a mechanism that is correct and looking in a place where the event does not arrive.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: attempt a dispatch naming a bead that is `open`/unassigned -> REFUSED, with the bead id and its actual status in the refusal text. A refusal that does not name the bead sends the caller hunting.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, second form: attempt a dispatch naming a bead assigned to a DIFFERENT agent -> REFUSED. Two panes working one bead is the duplicate-work failure, and it nearly happened today when `br ready` offered a bead an agent had been building for 14 minutes while the tracker still read `unclaimed`.
3. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a correctly filed-claimed-dispatched packet passes untouched. A refuse-only gate is over-strict, gets routed around, and dies slower than no gate.
4. THE REFUSAL MUST BE ACTIONABLE, not just typed: name the exact `br update <id> --assignee <agent> --status in_progress` that would satisfy it. Measured today -- a supervisor emitted `DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED owner=josh next_action=inspect-or-clear-pending-dispatch` 29 times and it worked precisely because it named the owner and the action.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: a dispatch with no bead id is an ERROR, never an unchecked pass. Broadcasts and corrections are a DIFFERENT operation and must be named as such rather than slipping through as bead-less dispatches.
6. MUTATION: remove the status check; leg 1 goes RED. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: claiming makes work VISIBLE, not DONE. A claimed bead with a silent pane is still a silent pane -- this closes the blind spot in the detector, not the silence itself. And `open`+unassigned is NOT by itself evidence of a skipped claim: it may simply be unstarted work. The discriminating signal is DISPATCHED-and-unclaimed, which means the DISPATCH LEDGER is the authority here, not the bead. A gate reading only bead status can prove the claim exists; only the ledger can prove a dispatch happened without one.

title: 01-idea:71 says dispatch DOES NOT EXIST; send_and_verify exists at main.rs:714 and is called at :1461
description:
## WHAT

`docs/plan/01-idea.md:71` states:

```
| actuate | dispatch | **DOES NOT EXIST** — a human types into panes |
```

That is false against the current tracked source. Correct the cell to
**`AVAILABLE, NOT VERIFIED`** — the category the same table already uses for the `complete` row —
and name the actual gap, which is runtime proof, not code.

## WHY

`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:714-912` is a complete production actuator, `send_and_verify`:

- `:725-736` builds the dispatch packet and stages it to a temp file
- `:738` resolves the receiver kind (`receiver_is_codex`)
- `:740-760` for a codex pane: `tmux send-keys -t <pane> -l <packet>` then `send-keys Enter`
  — the exact two-step form `AUTONOMOUS-WAVE.md:229-231` says is the one that works
- `:768-776` otherwise: `ntm --robot-send=<session> --panes=<pane> --msg-file=<staged>`
- `:782` writes a transport receipt
- `:784-911` loops on receiver receipt against `RECEIPT_TIMEOUT`, with `cx.checkpoint()`

It is not dead code: `grep -rn 'send_and_verify' crates/omp-orchestrator/src` returns `:714`
(definition) and `:1461` (call site, inside the tick). The file is tracked
(`git ls-files -- crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` → present). Positive control for the
greps: `grep -rc 'fn ' crates/omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs` → 79.

The crate's own header already carries the honest verdict, at `lib.rs:25-27`: the subprocess
wiring *"is designed but unverified at runtime."*

**Why this is a blocker and not a wording quibble.** `.flywheel/AUTONOMOUS-WAVE.md:44-49` elevates
this one line to the wave's ordering principle: *"That is the product. Everything else is
downstream of it. When you are choosing between two tasks, pick the one that gets the loop closer
to dispatching."* Four panes are prioritising against **"the actuator is missing"** when the
measured state is **"the actuator exists and is unproven."** Those are different tasks: one is
writing a dispatch path, the other is running the one that is there and reading its receipt. The
second is cheap and was never attempted; the first is the work the wave has been ordering itself
around.

The table's own vocabulary is what makes this a defect rather than a shorthand. Its seven rows
already distinguish existence from proof — `UNVERIFIED` twice, `FENCED`, `AVAILABLE, NOT WIRED` —
so `DOES NOT EXIST` is a deliberate and stronger claim, and it is the wrong one.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `docs/plan/01-idea.md:71` reads `AVAILABLE, NOT VERIFIED` (or equivalent) and cites
   `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:714` and the `:1461` call site.
2. `grep -rn 'DOES NOT EXIST' docs/plan/01-idea.md` → no match for the actuate row.
3. `.flywheel/AUTONOMOUS-WAVE.md` §1 is corrected in the same commit, since it quotes the line as
   the ordering fact. The corrected §1 must state what is actually missing.
4. The real gap gets a runnable acceptance, because renaming a cell ships nothing: one recorded
   run of `send_and_verify` against a live pane, with the transport receipt written by `:782` and
   the receiver receipt from the `:784-911` loop retained as evidence — or a named typed refusal
   explaining why it could not run. Expected result stated as `run X, expect Y` before the run,
   not after.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Whether the dispatch path is *correct*. This bead says the plan misdescribes it and that the gap
is verification. Proving the actuator delivers is milestone M3's job; this bead's job is to stop
the fleet from ordering work against a false absence.

## NO-CLAIM

Source existing and being called is not delivery. `AGENTS.md` is explicit that a sender's success
is not a receiver's receipt, and `cp-z42vu` recorded a send returning `success` while the packet
never arrived. Reclassifying the cell raises honesty, not capability; it may well turn out the
actuator has never successfully delivered once, which is exactly the measurement this unblocks.

(`section: 01-idea`).

title: Three dispatch renderers stage packets with no sender identity; 19 of 37 sites unidentified
description:
## WHAT

Three dispatch packet renderers stage a packet with NO sender identity, so a receiving pane learns
only the index it was sent to. Measured by `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/sender_identity.rs`, which
landed with this bead's sibling work and now refuses any new unidentified site.

The gate's own census, produced by the SAME `scan()` function leg 1 uses (not a grep handed to it):

| crate | dispatch sites | identity present |
|---|---:|---|
| `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` | 7 | **NO** |
| `crates/omp-idle-dispatch/src/main.rs` | 2 | **NO** |
| `crates/refill-idle-panes/src/main.rs` | 2 | **NO** |
| `crates/fast-dispatch/src/main.rs` | 6 | yes |
| `crates/loop-tick/src/lib.rs` | 6 | yes |
| `crates/tick-dispatch/src/main.rs` | 6 | yes |
| `crates/kernel-only-operator-hook/src/lib.rs` | 8 | n/a — allowanced, see below |

Totals: 56 tracked crates, 129 source files scanned, **37 dispatch sites in 7 files, 19 of them
unidentified across 3 renderers**.

`kernel-only-operator-hook` is allowanced with a reason and is NOT part of this fix: it
pattern-matches the `--robot-send` argv to allow or deny a Bash event and constructs no packet, so
there is no packet for a FROM line to live in. Its 8 hits are the allowlist entry and its unit
fixtures.

## WHY

Operator directive, verbatim: *"make sure you all announce who you are when sending a message so a
pane can properly contact you back."*

The measured failure: every packet sent during the 2026-09-01/02 session went out as
`ntm send omp-orchestrator --panes=N` with no FROM line. `ntm send` names a session and an INDEX,
and **pane indices are not stable handles** — they shifted twice in one night. Two panes changed
MODEL mid-session (`%1408` GLM 5.3 -> Opus 5, `%1409` GLM 5.3 -> GPT-5.6-Luna) while their agent
NAMES held. So agent names are the durable handle and indices are not, and `WAVE.md`'s roster went
stale listing pane2=%1408 while live tmux said %1413. Three agents replied to the orchestrator only
because they happened to know it was pane 1.

Two traps that make a hand-written FROM line wrong, both measured, both of which the fix must avoid:

1. `tmux display-message -p '#{pane_id}'` answers for the **ACTIVE** pane, not the calling one.
   From pane 4 it returns `%1396 index=0`; with `-t "$TMUX_PANE"` it returns the truth,
   `pane_index=4 pane_id=%1408`. A renderer that builds its own FROM line with the unqualified form
   announces WHOEVER IS FOCUSED. Note the nasty part: it is INVISIBLE from the focused pane — run
   from pane 1 both forms agree, so the bug cannot be reproduced from where an orchestrator sits.
2. `register_agent`'s `pane_id` argument is silently DISCARDED — `whois` returns no `pane_id`
   field, and the success envelope omits it too. The pane binding lives in a per-pane identity FILE
   and has a kernel: `resolve_pane_identity {project_key, pane_id?}` reads
   `~/.config/agent-mail/identity/<project_hash>/<pane_id>` with two legacy fallbacks and a GH#252
   liveness predicate. Measured for AmberGate: `{"agent_name":"AmberGate","pane_id":"%1408",
   "binding":"legacy-unverified"}`. Use that kernel; do not add a second source of pane truth.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`, per renderer:

1. Each of the three renderers stages a packet whose first two lines are a FROM line naming the
   sending AGENT NAME plus its pane index AND pane_id, and a REPLY-VIA line naming both routes
   (`ntm --robot-send=<session> --panes=<index> --msg-file <path>` and Agent Mail to the agent
   name). Agent name first, because it is the handle that held all session.
2. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test sender_identity` stays GREEN and the allowance shrinks from
   4 rows to 1 (`kernel-only-operator-hook` only). The gate FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a row naming
   a crate that now complies is an error, so the rows must be DELETED in the same commit as each
   fix. That asymmetry is the point — the list can only shrink.
3. The pane_id in the rendered FROM line comes from `resolve_pane_identity` or from
   `tmux display-message -t "$TMUX_PANE"`, never from an unqualified `display-message`. Assert it
   with a leg that feeds a multi-session `tmux list-panes -a` fixture and requires the CALLER's
   pane, with a negative control where the active pane differs from the caller's.
4. State in the commit which verdicts/paths still send unidentified packets, if any remain.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- `crates/fast-dispatch`, `crates/loop-tick`, `crates/tick-dispatch` — already identified, and
  another agent holds sender work on those three files.
- `crates/kernel-only-operator-hook` — allowanced with a reason; it renders no packet.
- Enforcing identity on the RECEIVING side. A FROM line makes a reply addressable; it does not
  prove the reply arrived.

## NO-CLAIM

A FROM line makes a packet ATTRIBUTABLE, not delivered. It does not fix
`RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` recording that a send RETURNED rather than arrived, and it does
not make pane indices stable — it makes them unnecessary, by carrying the durable handle beside
them. The gate proves a from-marker is PRESENT in the file that dispatches; it cannot prove the
rendered value is CORRECT, which is why acceptance 3 pins the resolution source rather than the
string.

title: byte-exact dispatch journey mapping: S1-S9 stage to contract to kernel symbol, with the comms/mail hole named
description:
## WHAT

Author `docs/contracts/dispatch_journey_mapping_contract.md`: the byte-exact mapping layer
between the canonical S1-S9 journey (`docs/plan/12-journey.md`), the evidence map
(`docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md`), the 20 contracts in `docs/contracts/`, and the kernel symbols
that actually implement each stage. One row per operational stage:

  stage | parent S-stage | GOAL | governing contract | kernel crate | exact symbol/command | measured gap

Stages walked: observe, select, claim, dispatch, ack, receipt, verify, close, comms/mail.

Every stage GOAL is backed by >= 2 independent primary sources (arXiv abstracts read directly,
source + fetch-date cited). A single-source claim is labelled phantom doctrine inline.

## WHY

`docs/plan/12-journey.md` owns the dispatchable runbook (S1-S9, seven-field contract) and
`docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md` owns the evidence map (11.1 stage/crate ownership). Neither names a
single `docs/contracts/` file per stage, and neither names a callable symbol. The result is that
three separate stage vocabularies exist in one workspace with no bridge:

  loop_coverage::LoopLayer                    crates/loop-coverage/src/lib.rs:78            (10 members)
  tick_monitor::lifecycle::Stage              crates/tick-monitor/src/lifecycle.rs:35        (9 members)
  bead_lifecycle::model::LifecycleStatus      crates/ntm-fleet-monitor/src/bead_lifecycle/model.rs:75 (10 members)

Measured three-way intersection of their stable string labels: EMPTY. LoopLayer vs
lifecycle::Stage share ZERO labels. No enum has an `ack` member, a `receipt` member, or a

title: the close readback is policy with no enforcement: a typed refusal becomes a null in every naive reader
description:
WHAT: **the close-status READBACK is policy with no enforcement anywhere.** K9 (`fa59e0c`) landed a
typed close-reason validator -- `ClosePrefix`, `CloseReasonVerdict{Verified, PolicyRefused, Empty,
Unread}` -- so a fabricated verdict is now unconstructible. **It does not perform the readback**, by
design: `ack-spine` does no I/O, so nothing runs `br show <id> --json | jq -r '.[0].status'` after a
close. The duty stays with the caller and is unenforced.

**FILED BECAUSE THE IMPLEMENTER ASKED ME TO NAME THE SHAPE RATHER THAN GUESS IT** -- *"I would rather
you name the shape than have me guess it"* -- which is the `6aff8f6` rule (a dispatch-only
instruction is an unrecorded requirement) correctly pointed back at the orchestrator.

WHY IT MATTERS, measured on me repeatedly tonight: **`br`'s close policy refuses a prose reason, and
the refusal scrolls past in-pane while the agent believes the close landed.** Adjacent measured
failures in the same family, all mine:
- `br update --assignee` with `--transition-comment` and no status change is REFUSED
  (*"transition comments and workflow-policy bypasses require a real status transition"*) -- my
  `--json` reader printed nothing useful until I read the exit status.
- `br update --status in_progress` on a blocked bead is REFUSED (`cannot claim blocked issue`) -- my
  reader printed `status=None assignee=None` and **I dispatched the bead anyway.**
- `br list --json` **excludes closed by default** (`-a` required, `--state all` unsupported), so a
  closed-count probe returned **0** while ten `br show` probes read `closed`.
**Every one is a typed refusal or a scoped default that a naive reader converts into a null or a
zero.**

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A helper that closes a bead AND reads the status back, returning a typed outcome distinguishing
   **closed** / **refused-with-the-refusal-text** / **unread**. `Unread` must be first-class, per
   K9's reasoning: folding "I did not look" into either other answer is what produced the fabricated
   constant it replaced.
2. **It MUST read the process exit status, not only parse stdout JSON.** A refusal emits no JSON and
   a JSON-only reader sees an empty field, which is exactly how a blocked-bead dispatch got sent.
3. **Anti-vacuity: an unreadable tracker must be an ERROR, never "closed".** A readback that cannot
   reach the tracker and reports success is strictly worse than no readback.
4. Fires-on-known-bad: close with a prose reason -> the helper reports `PolicyRefused` **carrying the
   refusal text**, not a generic failure. And a positive control: a sanctioned prefix reports
   `Closed`, so the helper can succeed as well as refuse.
5. **`br show` returns a BARE list while `br list` wraps rows in `.issues`** -- a leg must pin both
   shapes, because guessing that jq path produced four false findings in one session.
6. MUTATION: make the readback ignore the exit status -> leg 2's blocked-bead case goes RED. Restore
   byte-identically.
7. Assert on emitted TEXT per gate rule 7.

NO-CLAIM: a readback proves the tracker's STATE, not that the close was DESERVED. K9 already records
that enforcing the prefix proves a reason has a sanctioned SHAPE, not that its evidence is good --
`DONE: shipped` passes and says almost nothing. This bead closes the loop between "I ran close" and
"the tracker agrees", and nothing more. **Acceptance 5 of K9 -- that a bead closes on a
NON-IMPLEMENTER's grade -- remains a process rule with no code checking it, and this bead does not
change that.**

title: pane-truth: ExitCode::from(selftest(&rules) as u8) truncates -- a live twin of n34x, and undeclared AND unscanned
description:
WHAT: `crates/pane-truth/src/main.rs:49` is `return ExitCode::from(selftest(&rules) as u8);` while
`crates/pane-truth/src/lib.rs:695` is `pub fn selftest(rules: &PaneTruthRules) -> i32`. **Verified
live from source by SnowyCanyon, not taken on report.** A failure count of 256 truncates to **0** --
printing RED while exiting SUCCESS. Structurally identical to `omp-orchestrator-n34x`
(`cargo-lane-budget`), fixed at `dc617e2`.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE ORIGINAL: the argument `selftest(&rules)` contains `(` and `&`, which
`passthrough_chain` (`exit_codes.rs:237-258`) rejects, so the site is **undeclared AND unscanned** --
the registry gate never demanded a row for it, and never will. The `cargo-lane-budget` instance was
at least *in* the scan set. This one is invisible to the mechanism built to catch exactly it.

**`pane-truth` IS THE FLEET'S GROUND-TRUTH ORACLE**, which is what makes the latency matter: a
selftest that prints RED and exits 0 is a broken oracle reporting itself healthy, and every
dispatch decision keyed on it inherits that.

ACCEPTANCE -- repeat the `n34x` proof, scoped, no new invention:
1. Apply the same remedy shape: a total `selftest_exit_code(i32) -> u8` returning `u8` LITERALS, so
   no numeric conversion remains on the path. Do NOT narrow `selftest`'s own signature if any test
   pins it -- check first and say which.
2. Reuse the existing RED code; add nothing to the closed 1-4 band. The count stays in the MESSAGE.
3. Known-bad FIRST, as an assertion of the mechanism before the fix: `assert_eq!(256_i32 as u8, 0)`,
   then refuse 256, 512, 65536, -1, `i32::MIN`.
4. An equivalence leg: the new conversion equals `reachable as u8` for `{0,1}`, so behaviour
   diverges ONLY where the old path was wrong.
5. **TWO MUTATIONS, and M2 is the one that matters** -- M1: restore `as u8` -> the truncation leg
   goes RED. M2: break ONLY the message half, leaving the code correct -> **exactly one leg fires**,
   proving the message assertion is independently load-bearing. Restore byte-identically both times
   and diff against recorded shas. An exit-code-only suite is blind to M2.
6. Assert on emitted TEXT per gate rule 7, never on an exit code alone.
7. Anti-vacuity: the suite must not pass on zero rules. An empty rule set is an ERROR.

NON-GOALS: do NOT sweep the other 20 census sites. Seven forward a value that could grow
(`tick-dispatch` x8, `verify-dispatch:54`, `loop-tick/main.rs:54`, `loop-driver` x2,
`loop-queue-filter:18`, `dispatcher-deadman:165`, `fleet-monitor:437`) and are UNEXAMINED beyond
reading the expression -- they are not claimed broken and are not in this bead.

NO-CLAIM: latent, not observed. `pane-truth`'s selftest would need to produce >=256 failures to
trigger it. Filed because the twin proves the class is not closed, and because this instance cannot
be caught by the registry gate at all.

```

git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD -- crates/pane-truth
```
