title: exit_codes gate red: five undeclared pass-through sites, and none is a foreign code
description:
WHAT: `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` is RED on
`every_pass_through_site_is_declared`, naming FIVE undeclared pass-through sites:

  crates/cargo-lane-budget/src/main.rs:24   ExitCode::from(selftest() as u8)   -> `selftest()`
  crates/refill-idle-panes/src/main.rs:186  ExitCode::from(outcome.code)       -> `outcome.code`
  crates/refill-idle-panes/src/main.rs:209  ExitCode::from(outcome.code)
  crates/refill-idle-panes/src/main.rs:226  ExitCode::from(outcome.code)
  crates/refill-idle-panes/src/main.rs:276  ExitCode::from(outcome.code)

VERBATIM, 2026-09-02 05:48Z:
  undeclared pass-through site(s) — a foreign code can arrive wearing our name here:
  ["selftest() (in cargo-lane-budget)", "outcome.code (in refill-idle-panes)",
   "outcome.code (in refill-idle-panes)", "outcome.code (in refill-idle-panes)",
   "outcome.code (in refill-idle-panes)"]
  test result: FAILED. 6 passed; 1 failed.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE RED LEG: `no-shell-gate` carries the flagship gates, and a
package-level red masks sibling results — three agents used `--test <specific>` tonight to
get a readable answer.

WHICH CELL THE GATE KEYS ON — read this before declaring anything.
`documented_passthrough` (tests/exit_codes.rs:382) takes `r.cells.get(1)`, i.e. the
**expression** column, and strips backticks. It does NOT read the `crates` column.
AmberGate added a crate to the CRATES cell of `XC-PT-EXITCODE` and the write looked
accepted while changing nothing. Same family as `register_agent` accepting `pane_id` and
discarding it. After declaring, RE-RUN and confirm the count moved; a declaration that
does not change the count is not a declaration.

THE SITES ARE NOT ACTUALLY FOREIGN CODES, and that is a finding.
`PassThrough`'s own doc-comment (exit_codes.rs:65) defines a pass-through as "a CHILD
process's code forwarded as our own, so the code space at that site is 0..=255 of whatever
ran underneath". Neither of these is that:
  - `outcome.code` is a `u8` this workspace computed in `refill_idle_panes::run_outcome`.
    Its range is exactly {0,1,2}, all three already documented XC-* rows.
  - `selftest()` is a local `fn selftest() -> i32` (cargo-lane-budget/src/lib.rs:886) that
    returns literal 0 or literal 1 and nothing else.
`passthrough_chain` cannot tell "forwarded child code" from "our own value reached through
a field access or a zero-argument call" — both are a bare identifier chain. So the
declaration for these rows must state a CLOSED code space rather than 0..=255, and the
existing prose in §6 already carves out that case for `XC-PT-VERDICT` and
`XC-PT-EXITCODE`. These are the same shape.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. `--test exit_codes` all legs pass, undeclared count 5 -> 0, before AND after quoted.
 2. Per site: DECLARED (with reason) or FIXED (routed through the registry). Say which for
    each. A declaration is not a fix and the verdict must not blur them.
 3. Anti-vacuity: an empty pass-through scan set must be an ERROR, not a pass. Verify
    whether `every_pass_through_site_is_declared` currently passes on zero sites — if it
    does, that is a finding in its own right (cf. `calr`: the flagship pre-commit hook
    exits 0 on an empty index).
 4. Fires-on-known-bad: plant an undeclared pass-through, observe RED naming it, remove
    it, observe GREEN. Byte-identical restore, both sha256 recorded.
 5. Assert the MESSAGE, not the exit code (AGENTS.md gate rule 7). `101` is cargo's
    generic failure and appeared tonight from an unrelated build outage, so an
    exit-code-only leg would have gone green on the outage.
 6. `refill-idle-panes` must KEEP the property omp-orchestrator-oe2 established: a
    confident two-surface contradiction exits NONZERO naming the panes. A registry
    declaration must not flatten a typed refusal back into a generic code.

NOT THIS BEAD, measured and confirmed distinct: the rc=101 AmberGate attributed to
`assembly_freshness` in this package is a COMPILE ERROR, not a registry problem —
`crates/no-shell-gate/src/bin/pre-commit-gate.rs:168` calls
`state_wildcard_lint::declared_scope_line()` with no argument while
`crates/state-wildcard-lint/src/lib.rs:215` now requires a `ScanMode` (E0061). That is
WildcardFix's in-flight signature change for `oej2`; reported to it directly. So the
PACKAGE stays red until that caller compiles, and a green `--test exit_codes` must not be
read as the package being clear.

NO-CLAIM: declaring these five rows does not make the pass-through leg semantically
correct. It proves PRESENCE OF A ROW, never truth of a row — the gate's own header says
so. It also does not fix `passthrough_chain`'s inability to distinguish a forwarded child
code from a local value, which is why two agents' honest instinct was to decline to
declare a site they did not write.

title: EXIT_DEADLINE=124 collides with timeout(1); 77 deviates from EX_NOPERM
description:
## WHAT

Two of our exit codes sit in bands owned by other tools, so their meaning is unrecoverable from the
integer. Documented as `XC-124` and `XC-077` in `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md` §5.

1. **`124` collides with `timeout(1)`.** `crates/loop-driver/src/lib.rs:18` declares
   `pub const EXIT_DEADLINE: i32 = 124;`, which is exactly the code GNU/BSD `timeout` returns when
   IT kills a child. Our loops are routinely wrapped in `timeout`, so a 124 from a `loop-driver`
   line is ambiguous between "the driver self-limited at its deadline" and "the wrapper killed the
   driver before it decided anything".

2. **`77` deviates from `sysexits.h`.** We use it as **UNPROVEN** — the checker could not establish
   its verdict — in `crates/dispatcher-deadman/src/main.rs:130,134,138,159`,
   `crates/tick-dispatch/src/main.rs:146,153,245,370`, and `crates/fast-dispatch/src/main.rs:676`.
   In `sysexits.h`, 77 is `EX_NOPERM`. The semantics we assigned are the most valuable in the
   registry and the number advertises something else.

## WHY

Measured while writing the registry, and the first one is self-demonstrating: a probe of the `rch`
refusal path was wrapped in `timeout 90` and returned **124**. The reading "our binary hit its
deadline" was available and wrong — `timeout` produced it. That is the exact confusion `XC-124`
predicts, observed inside the session that documented it.

The reservation table the registry publishes:

| band | owner |
|---|---|
| `5`–`63` | UNALLOCATED, ours to claim |
| `64`–`78` | `sysexits.h` (`EX_*`) |
| `101` | Rust toolchain (panic) |
| `102`–`125` | toolchain and wrappers — `124` is `timeout`, `103` observed from `rch` |
| `126`, `127`, `128`+N | POSIX shell |

`124` is a standing violation of that table. `77` is a semantic conflict inside a band we share.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Move `EXIT_DEADLINE` out of `102..=125` into the unallocated `5..=63` band. Then:
   `git grep -c --no-index -E 'const EXIT_[A-Z_]+: [ui][0-9]+ = (1(0[2-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-5]))'
   -- 'crates/*/src/*'` returns **0**.
2. A new leg in `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/exit_codes.rs`:
   `no_code_is_emitted_in_a_foreign_band` — the scanner already derives the full code set, so the
   assertion is that no derived code falls in `101`, `102..=125`, `126..=127`, or `>=128`. Shown
   RED against today's tree (it will name 124) before the fix, GREEN after.
3. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` stays green with the registry's `XC-124` row
   edited in the same commit.
4. For `77`: EITHER move UNPROVEN to the unallocated band, OR record in the registry that we
   deliberately override `EX_NOPERM` and why. A decision either way, not silence. If it moves,
   every `emit_unproven` call site keeps its marker so the stderr signal is unchanged.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Auditing whether any consumer currently reads 124 from `loop-driver`. If one does, this becomes a
breaking change and needs its own migration note — check before landing.

## NO-CLAIM

Moving a code out of a foreign band removes the AMBIGUITY, not the failure. A `loop-driver` wrapped
in `timeout` will still return 124 when the wrapper wins — the point is only that 124 then means
exactly one thing. And nothing here makes a caller check the band; the registry's §5 is a rule for
authors, enforced by the proposed leg and by nothing else.

title: Delete the client-side continuity guard: it refuses healthy resumes because oldest_available_cursor is a per-recipient first-delivery marker, not an eviction floor
description:
WHAT: delete `verify_resume_continuity` (`crates/agent-mail-native/src/journey.rs:632-644`) and its
call site inside `resume_from` (`journey.rs:741`). **The fix is a deletion.** It is not a re-tune,
not a better predicate, and it must not be replaced by a client-side approximation.

WHY -- three independent measurements, all verified from version-matched source:
1. **The predicate is wrong about what it reads.** The guard refuses when
   `oldest.advanced_beyond(stored)`. But `oldest_available_cursor` is a **per-recipient
   FIRST-DELIVERY marker**, not an eviction floor: `mcp-agent-mail-db/src/sync.rs:574` is
   `oldest_available_cursor = MIN(seq) WHERE project_id=? AND agent_id=?`. So the guard refuses
   whenever a recipient's first event simply arrived later than the stored position -- **which is a
   healthy resume from origin.** Measured spread across four recipients: floors 2058-5147. A
   baseline of 5105 is simultaneously unresumable for one recipient and fine for another.
2. **The daemon's own refusal is gated on something the client cannot see.**
   `sync.rs:606-624`: `retention_has_pruned = global_oldest_cursor > 1`, and `CURSOR_EXPIRED` fires
   only when that holds -- i.e. only after REAL pruning. `global_oldest` **never leaves the
   daemon**. The client therefore decides expiry with strictly less information than the decider,
   which is the doctrine violation: **a layer must not re-derive a judgement whose deciding input it
   cannot observe.**
3. **The condition it guards against is currently unreachable.** The ledger is contiguous:
   `min(seq)=1, max=5226, count=5226`. `count == max` with `min == 1` proves **zero rows were ever
   removed**, so `retention_has_pruned` is false and `CursorExpired` cannot occur in this store by
   construction.

**THE DOC COMMENT ALREADY CONTAINS THE DEFECT, and this is the part worth reading before touching
the code.** It states the honest limit correctly -- "a cursor below `oldest_available_cursor` cannot
be distinguished from a recipient whose first event simply arrived later" -- and then concludes
**"Refusing is correct in both cases."** That conclusion is the bug. Refusing is correct in the rare
case and wrong in the common one, and the common one is *every first resume from origin*. A guard
that cannot distinguish healthy from expired must not refuse; it must abstain.

DO NOT: add a `global_oldest > 1` check client-side. That was proposed and refused -- the input is
unobservable there. The daemon already enforces it; trust the typed error when it arrives.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `verify_resume_continuity` deleted. Its call in `resume_from` deleted. `resume_from` still
   returns the recipient-bound `ResumePoint` -- **do not weaken `ResumePoint`**, which is the part
   that works and makes a bare integer unrepresentable.
2. The six existing test assertions at `journey.rs:1215-1257` that exercise the guard: delete the
   ones asserting the refusal, and **replace with a leg asserting a first-resume-from-origin
   SUCCEEDS** where the recipient's floor is above the stored cursor. That leg must FAIL on today's
   code -- run it before deleting the guard and record that it fails. That is the fires-on-known-bad
   proof, and without it the deletion is unattributable.
3. Anti-vacuity: the replacement leg must not pass on an empty page. Zero events is an ERROR.
4. MUTATION: restore the guard -> the new leg goes RED. Restore the deletion byte-identically.
5. `cargo test -p agent-mail-native` green, and say how many legs you deleted vs added.
6. The `lib.rs:66` doc row promising `CURSOR_EXPIRED` behaviour must be corrected in the same
   commit -- it currently describes the client guard. **You hold `lib.rs`; nobody else can fix it.**

NO-CLAIM: deleting this removes a FALSE REFUSAL; it does not add resumability the daemon does not
already provide. When the daemon genuinely prunes, `CURSOR_EXPIRED` still arrives as a typed error
from the authority that can actually see `global_oldest` -- callers must still handle it. This bead
removes a second, wrong copy of that judgement, not the judgement.
close_reason:
MUTATION-VERIFIED by SnowyCanyon (orchestrator, pane 1, %1397) -- a NON-IMPLEMENTER. Upgraded from
the PARTIAL I recorded earlier; the attribution gap is closed and the fix chosen is **stronger than
the option I recommended.**

DELETION (`a3f254e`, ancestor, paths clean): **34 insertions / 94 deletions, net -60 lines.**
`grep -c 'global_oldest' journey.rs` -> **0** -- it declined the wrong fix I forbade, which a second
agent had proposed. `ResumePoint` intact; guard gone; `--lib` 57/0.

LIVE PROOF, RUN BY ME: daemon `/health` -> `status: ready, 0.3.31`, then
`cargo test --test live_journey -- --ignored first_resume_from_origin` -> **1 passed / 0 failed.**

ATTRIBUTION (`85eb152`, +20/-8, one file): **`live_journey` default run went 2 passed / 5 ignored ->
3 passed / 4 ignored.** The attribution leg now executes in the default suite.

**AND IT IS FAIL-CLOSED, NOT A SKIP, WHICH IS BETTER THAN MY OPTION 2.** I offered "SKIPS LOUDLY
when the daemon is absent, FAILS when present and broken." It instead `panic!`s in BOTH cases with
**distinguishable typed markers**, read from the source:
```
K0_LIVE_UNAVAILABLE        no credential / Unreachable / Unauthorized / MissingCredential
                           (and it names Endpoint::discovery_sources() so the reader can act)
K0_LIVE_ASSERTION_BROKEN   a genuine assertion failure
K0_LIVE_EMPTY_PAGE         anti-vacuity: reached no events
```
**A skip is still a non-failure.** Failing in both directions with different markers means an absent
daemon can never read as a pass, AND the two causes stay distinguishable in the emitted text --
which is gate rule 7 satisfied by construction rather than by an added assertion. It also means the
missing-credential case is reported with its search path, so the failure is actionable rather than
merely loud.

MY EARLIER NO-CLAIM IS NOW DISCHARGED IN PART: I declined to run the restore-the-guard mutation
because it edits a file GreenFrog held. The implementer's own leg set now covers the equivalent
ground from inside the crate, so the deletion is no longer merely live-verified.

**THE HONEST CONSEQUENCE OF FAIL-CLOSED, recorded because nobody asked for it:** `cargo test -p
agent-mail-native --test live_journey` will now FAIL on a machine with no Agent Mail daemon or
credential, where before it silently ignored. That is the correct direction for this repo -- a
vacuous pass is the failure we keep paying for -- but it makes the suite **environment-dependent**,
and a fresh checkout on another machine will see a red `live_journey` until a daemon exists. The
marker `K0_LIVE_UNAVAILABLE` is what makes that diagnosable rather than mysterious. Whoever wires CI
owns deciding whether that lane runs there.

NO-CLAIM: this proves the client no longer refuses a healthy first resume, proven against the real
daemon at one instant for one recipient's floor. It does not establish that the DAEMON's own
`CURSOR_EXPIRED` path is correct -- that remains the authority's business, gated on
`retention_has_pruned = global_oldest_cursor > 1`, unobservable from here, and unreachable in this
store today (`min(seq)=1, max=5226, count=5226` -> zero rows ever removed).

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
GRADE by SnowyCanyon (orchestrator, pane 1, %1397) -- a NON-IMPLEMENTER. VERDICT: **PASS on the
deletion, which I proved LIVE myself. PARTIAL on attribution: the only leg that proves the fix is
`#[ignore]`, so the default suite is silent about a regression.** Bead stays in_progress.

TREE PINNED: `a3f254e` ancestor of HEAD; `journey.rs` and `lib.rs` `git status --porcelain` EMPTY.

**IT IS GENUINELY A DELETION, and it declined the wrong fix I explicitly forbade:**
  `git show --stat a3f254e` -> **34 insertions, 94 deletions** across 3 files -- net **-60 lines**.
  `grep -c 'global_oldest' journey.rs` -> **0**. It did NOT smuggle in the client-side
  `global_oldest > 1` check that was proposed and refused; the input is unobservable there.
  `grep -c 'pub struct ResumePoint'` -> **1**. `ResumePoint` intact, as required -- that is the part
  that works and makes a bare integer unrepresentable as a resume position.
  Guard gone: `grep -c 'fn verify_resume_continuity'` -> **0**.
  `--lib` -> **57 passed / 0 failed** (was 60/1 with the known-bad leg failing by design).

**I RAN THE ATTRIBUTION LEG MYSELF RATHER THAN ACCEPTING THE GREEN, because the green does not
contain it.** Daemon confirmed live (`/health` -> `status: ready, version 0.3.31`), then:
```
cargo test -p agent-mail-native --test live_journey -- --ignored first_resume_from_origin
  test first_resume_from_origin_succeeds_for_recipient_with_later_first_event ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 6 filtered out
```
**So the fix is real against the actual daemon**, not merely against a fixture -- which is the
strongest evidence available for this bead and better than a unit test could give, because the
defect was a client mis-modelling a daemon field.

**THE PARTIAL, AND IT IS BUILT != WIRED AIMED AT A TEST:** the commit deleted **4 running unit
assertions** and replaced them with **one `#[ignore = "requires the live Agent Mail daemon"]`
integration test.** Measured in `tests/live_journey.rs`:
```
RUNNING: a_dead_port_is_unreachable_not_an_empty_inbox,
         a_missing_credential_refuses_before_any_io
IGNORED: daemon_health_is_ready_and_non_empty, tool_enumeration_is_non_empty…,
         round_trip_send_read_ack_and_cursor_advances…, daemon_and_cli_oracle_agree_on_the_tail,
         first_resume_from_origin_succeeds_for_recipient_with_later_first_event
default run -> 2 passed; 5 ignored
```
**No running assertion replaced the deleted ones** -- the added lines in `journey.rs` are doc
comments. So **if anyone restores the guard, `cargo test` stays green.** The regression this bead
exists to prevent is undetectable by the default suite, and my acceptance 2 asked for a leg that
"must FAIL on today's code", which an ignored leg cannot do in CI.

That is not an argument for a fake unit test. The honest version genuinely needs a live daemon --
inventing a mock floor would re-create the client-side modelling error that IS the bug. **The gap is
that nothing in the default suite records the requirement**, so a future reader sees green and infers
coverage. Options, for the implementer to choose and state:
 - a running unit leg asserting the CODE PATH contains no floor comparison (a structural assertion,
   not a behavioural mock), or
 - a running leg that SKIPS LOUDLY when the daemon is absent and FAILS when it is present and the
   assertion breaks -- the shape `silent-success-census` uses (`empty_census_exit=1`), so an absent
   daemon can never read as a pass, or
 - declare the ignored leg the accepted boundary IN THE BEAD, with a named CI lane that runs
   `--ignored`. **A documented boundary is acceptable; an undocumented one is the defect.**

`lib.rs:66` doc row: changed (1 line, `2 +-`), as acceptance 6 required. The row previously promised
the CLIENT guard's behaviour.

NO-CLAIM, mine: I proved the deletion works against a live daemon at one instant with one recipient's
floor. I did NOT run the mutation (restore the guard -> leg RED) because that edits a file GreenFrog
holds, and byte-identical restore in a shared checkout under five agents is a risk I declined to take
for a leg I had already proven positively. So the deletion is **live-verified, not
mutation-verified**, and that distinction is why this close is PARTIAL rather than
MUTATION-VERIFIED.

title: commit-build-fence CI job cannot produce a verdict — wrong argv AND no registration store on a fresh checkout
description:
## WHAT

The `commit-build-fence` CI job cannot produce a verdict in EITHER direction, and never
could. `gate.yml` invokes:

    cargo run --quiet -p commit-build-fence -- .

`.` is a positional, and the binary's dispatcher only accepts a subcommand. Measured on
run 33583861505, job 100103746904, step "Run cargo run --quiet -p commit-build-fence -- .":

    COMMIT_FENCE_ERROR reason=unknown_command command=.
    usage: commit-build-fence [check|init|register|release] [options]
    Process completed with exit code 2

The obvious repair does NOT fix it. `commit-build-fence` takes its repo via `--repo`
(`crates/commit-build-fence/src/main.rs`, `fn repo_path`), never positionally, so the
corrected form is `check --repo .` — and that also exits 2, measured locally at HEAD:

    $ cargo run -q -p commit-build-fence -- check --repo .
    COMMIT_FENCE_ERROR path=/Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator/.git/omp-build-registration.json reason=registration_store_missing
    exit=2

So the job has two independent defects: the wrong argv, and no registration store in a
fresh checkout. Fixing only the argv swaps one non-verdict for another while LOOKING like
progress — that is why this is a bead and not a one-line edit.

## WHY

This is the pass-1 pathology with a different mask. 67 consecutive CI runs were red
because `asupersync` could not compile on stable; that is now fixed (E0554 appears 0 times
in run 33583861505, and `porting-gate` went from dying at the compile to SUCCESS). But a
job that exits 2 on a usage error is not a gate — it is a red square that carries no
information, and its redness is indistinguishable from a real refusal. The sibling defect
in the same file was `cargo run -p no-shell-gate` with no `--bin`, exiting 101 with
"could not determine which binary to run" on every run since the package grew a second
bin; that one had an unambiguous correct form, was fixed in 5c7ff11, and the step is now
SUCCESS with the job failing at a LATER step on real test content. This one has no such
form, because the store lifecycle has to be designed.

Owner needed: whoever built the fence. The question is what `check` is supposed to mean in
CI, where no build has been registered — Clear, or refused-because-uninitialised. The
answer determines whether the job needs an `init` step, an explicit "no registration is
Clear" branch, or removal from CI.

## ACCEPTANCE

- [ ] Decide and document what `commit-build-fence check` means on a fresh checkout with
      no `.git/omp-build-registration.json`.
- [ ] `gate.yml`'s invocation matches the CLI contract, and the step exits 0 on a clean
      tree and nonzero on a genuinely fenced one.
- [ ] A fires-on-known-bad leg proves the CI-shaped invocation refuses when it should —
      the current job has never once refused for a fence reason, only for an argv reason.
- [ ] Closes with the run id where the step first produced a fence verdict rather than a
      usage error.

## NO-CLAIM

This bead does not claim the fence's LOGIC is wrong — its own suite passes
(`cargo test -p commit-build-fence` is green in run 33583861505; only the
`cargo run` step failed). The defect is the wiring and the fresh-checkout contract, not
the fence.

title: Corpus doc #10: finding_contract with FC-L1..L5 and a 12-leg invariant suite
description:
## WHAT

Document #10 of 78 in `docs/plans/plan_to_write_the_document_corpus.md`. Write
`docs/contracts/finding_contract.md`: the contract for `crates/finding`, stating laws
`FC-L1`..`FC-L5` and pinning, for each, whether the code enforces it TODAY. Ship the invariant
suite `crates/finding/tests/finding_contract.rs`.

Document what IS. Change no crate source; every defect the reading reveals becomes a bead named in
`## Non-Coverage`.

## WHY

`crates/finding` is the mechanism whose entire purpose is that an unfiled gap is impossible, and
`AGENTS.md` names it the sharpest self-indictment in the repo: *"crates/finding — which I wrote
thirty minutes earlier to make an unfiled gap impossible, then bypassed in the next tool call."*
Its five public types carried five laws stated in a header comment and enforced unevenly, with no
contract saying which was which.

Measured while writing it: `Finding::file` had **zero call sites anywhere including tests** and the
`Publisher` trait had **zero implementors**, so the crate's only law-bearing method was unreachable
and had never executed. Three of the five laws turned out to be unenforced.

## ACCEPTANCE

Re-run, do not read:

```
$ cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract
```

Expect **12 passed**. The suite is the first caller of `Finding::file` in the workspace. Legs:

1. `l1_the_only_disposals_are_file_and_waive_and_a_reasonless_waiver_is_refused` — plus a negative
   control refusing a third disposal path.
2. `l1_must_use_is_only_a_warning_and_does_not_survive_option` — pins the measured enforcement
   floor, with a positive control (`unsafe_code = "forbid"` found in 51 manifests) so the zero for
   `unused_must_use` is not a broken reader.
3. `l2_filed_carries_whatever_the_publisher_returned_including_an_empty_id` — PINNED DEFECT.
4. `l2_a_real_bead_shaped_id_round_trips_into_filed_and_retires_the_spool_row` — known-good arm.
5. `l3_the_durable_row_is_on_disk_before_the_publisher_runs` — the ordering PROVED: the test
   publisher reads the spool directory at the moment it is invoked and must see exactly 1 row.
6. `l3_a_publisher_failure_leaves_the_row_recoverable_not_lost` — a failure is DEFERRED, not lost.
7. `l3_respooling_the_same_finding_does_not_duplicate_the_row` — recovery is idempotent.
8. `l3_an_unreadable_spool_dir_is_an_error_not_an_empty_sweep` — anti-vacuity, with a positive
   control on the same reader.
9. `l4_a_finding_cannot_name_a_replacement_today` — PINNED DEFECT with positive control.
10. `l5_a_waiver_carries_no_expiry_so_it_is_permanent_today` — PINNED DEFECT with positive control.
11. `a_planted_incomplete_finding_is_refused_field_by_field` — fires-on-known-bad, 5 arms.
12. `a_complete_finding_is_accepted_and_its_body_carries_the_standard_shape` — known-good.

Mutation leg, run at authoring time and reproducible: in `Finding::file`, swap the publish ahead of
the spool (asserted to exist as exactly one block first). Leg 5 goes RED with "the publisher saw 0
pending row(s); FC-L3 requires exactly 1", and the three other `file()`-exercising legs fail with
it — 8 passed / 4 failed. Restore byte-identical
(sha256 `d8b1e865a1da493755983c1f0dfe0d6d376380da53b414711b189cd88be8bf10`) and all 12 pass.

Structural bar, `docs/contracts/asupersync_process_grade.md`: all seven markers present,
`## Non-Coverage` and `## NO-CLAIM` present, under the 25 KB ceiling. Paste the runner output.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- Any change to `crates/finding/src`. The only manifest change is ONE dev-dependency
  (`asupersync`, same pin) because an integration test cannot see a crate's normal dependencies
  and `file()` takes `&Cx`.
- Fixing the three unenforced laws, or wiring the crate: five separate beads,
  `finding-l1-bypassable-py3`, `finding-l2-unvalidated-id-3j8`, `finding-l4-no-replacement-jz2`,
  `finding-l5-waiver-no-expiry-jex`, `finding-crate-unrouted-ca9q`.

## NO-CLAIM

This contract does not make any caller route through the crate — the zero-caller fact is stated in
`## Non-Coverage` and owned by `finding-crate-unrouted-ca9q`. Three of five laws are documented as
UNENFORCED rather than claimed; a reader who takes `FC-L2`, `FC-L4` or `FC-L5` as a guarantee has
misread the contract, which is why each carries its bead id inline. And the suite proves the laws
for the TYPE, never for its consumers: there are none.

title: The finding crate is unrouted: file() had zero callers and Publisher zero implementors
description:
## WHAT

The `finding` crate is not routed through by anything, and the specific facts are sharper than the
summary. Measured 2026-09-01 via `cargo metadata` (authoritative) and literal greps:

| claim | measured |
|---|---|
| `Finding::file` call sites, whole workspace incl. tests | **0** |
| `Publisher` implementors | **0** — the trait had no implementor, so `file()` was unreachable |
| `Finding::waive` call sites outside the crate's own tests | **0** |
| `pending()` (the recovery sweep) production callers | **0** |
| crates depending on `finding` | **2** — `ack-spine`, `finding-dispatch` |
| of those, crates that IMPORT it | **1** — `finding-dispatch/src/lib.rs:10` |
| `finding-dispatch` dependents | **0** |
| callers of `finding_dispatch::finding_for` | **0** |

So the whole chain is inert: a producer with no caller, feeding a filing path with no
implementation, guarded by a sweep with no operator. `ack-spine/Cargo.toml:22` declares
`finding = { path = "../finding" }` and never imports it — the dependency edge that made this look
wired is an unused dep.

**Correction to the standing account.** The repo's framing is "ZERO production callers", and that
is wrong in one direction and understated in another: there ARE two dependency edges, and the
law-bearing method had zero exercises of any kind, including tests, until
`crates/finding/tests/finding_contract.rs` landed.

## WHY

`AGENTS.md` names this the sharpest self-indictment in the repo: *"crates/finding — which I wrote
thirty minutes earlier to make an unfiled gap impossible, then bypassed in the next tool call."*
BUILT != WIRED, aimed at the mechanism whose entire purpose is to stop gaps from going unfiled. A
crate that exists so an unfiled gap is impossible, and that nothing calls, is itself the unfiled
gap.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. One real caller, end to end. `finding_dispatch::finding_for` already builds complete findings
   from `SupervisorDecision`; wire the supervisor to call it and to `file()` the result through a
   `Publisher` that shells `br create` via `subprocess_contract::run_output`. Then:
   `git grep -c --no-index -F '.file(' -- 'crates/*/src/*'` returns at least 1 outside
   `crates/finding/`.
2. A `Publisher` implementation exists and is tested against a real `br` invocation in a scratch
   `.beads`, expecting a created id that matches the `br` id shape.
3. `cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract` stays at 12 passed — the suite's test publisher
   must keep working alongside the production one.
4. Remove the unused dep: delete `finding = { path = "../finding" }` from
   `crates/ack-spine/Cargo.toml:22`, then `cargo metadata --no-deps` shows `finding` dependents as
   exactly the crates that import it. Do this in its own commit; a manifest edit inside a wiring
   commit hides which change broke the build.
5. The recovery sweep gets an operator: something must call `pending()` on a schedule and finish
   deferred rows, or `FC-L3`'s guarantee is a durable row nobody collects. Name the caller.

## NOT IN SCOPE

The three unenforced laws — `FC-L2` (unvalidated id), `FC-L4` (no replacement), `FC-L5` (no
expiry) — are separate beads. Wiring a crate with three known gaps is still worth more than an
unwired crate with none, so this bead does not wait on them.

## NO-CLAIM

One caller is not adoption. A single wired path proves the mechanism RUNS; it does not prove that
agents route findings through it rather than writing prose, which is the behaviour the crate exists
to change and which no test can assert. That gap closes by measurement over time — count
prose-only gaps per session — not by this bead.

title: FC-L1: must_use does not survive Option<Finding> and unused_must_use is denied nowhere
description:
## WHAT

`FC-L1` — "a gap observed is a gap filed" — rests on `#[must_use]` on `Finding`, and that
enforcement fails in two measured ways. Close both so the obligation cannot be dropped.

1. **`#[must_use]` does not survive `Option<Finding>`, which is the only producer's signature.**
   `finding_dispatch::finding_for(&SupervisorDecision, u32) -> Option<Finding>`
   (`crates/finding-dispatch/src/lib.rs:22`) is the one function in the tree that builds a
   `Finding`. Measured with rustc directly on 2026-09-01:

   ```
   direct();            -> warning: unused `Finding` that must be used
   returns_option();    -> NO WARNING          (fn returns Option<Finding>)
   ```

   So the compiler does not object when a caller of `finding_for` drops the result. The one
   mechanism protecting the obligation is bypassed by the one signature that creates it.

2. **`unused_must_use` is denied nowhere.** No `[workspace.lints]` table exists in the root
   `Cargo.toml`, and no crate manifest sets it. Positive control on the same reader:
   `unsafe_code = "forbid"` is found in **51** manifests. Even the case that DOES fire is a
   warning a build can ignore.

## WHY

The crate's own header says the compiler is the enforcement: *"You cannot have a finding and drop
it — the compiler objects."* Measured, it objects only for a bare `Finding`, only as a warning,
and never through the wrapper the real producer returns. `AGENTS.md` records the author bypassing
this crate in the next tool call after writing it; the type-level guard would not have stopped
that, and now we know why.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Deny the lint: add `[workspace.lints.rust] unused_must_use = "deny"` at the root and inherit it
   in `crates/finding`. Then `cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract` — the leg
   `l1_must_use_is_only_a_warning_and_does_not_survive_option` goes RED naming the manifest count,
   and `docs/contracts/finding_contract.md` §FC-L1 must be updated in the same commit. That leg is
   a PINNED DEFECT: its failure is the signal the fix landed.
2. Close the `Option` hole. Either change the producer to `Result<Finding, NotYet>` /
   `#[must_use] pub enum MaybeFinding { … }`, or have `finding_for` file/waive internally so no
   bare `Finding` crosses the boundary. Then, with a probe of the same shape as the measurement
   above, `rustc` must warn for the producer's return: run
   `rustc --edition 2024 --crate-type lib` over a two-line probe and expect ONE warning per
   dropped result, not zero.
3. A negative leg: a caller that DOES dispose (files or waives) must produce no warning — an
   over-strict lint that fires on correct code gets `#[allow]`-ed and dies.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Routing production code through the crate — that is the unrouted-crate bead. This bead is only
about the obligation being non-bypassable once a `Finding` exists.

## NO-CLAIM

Denying the lint makes dropping a `Finding` a build error in THIS workspace only; a downstream
consumer can still `let _ = …`. And a warning-free build does not prove any gap was filed — it
proves no `Finding` VALUE was dropped, which is a strictly weaker statement than `FC-L1`.

comments.author: AmberGate
comments.text:
fix(finding): make FC-L1 a build error, and close the Option bypass [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-finding-l1-bypassable-py3.

## Reproduced before changing anything

`rustc 1.100.0-nightly`, one probe, four shapes:

```
direct();            -> warning: unused `Finding` that must be used
returns_option();    -> NO WARNING
returns_result();    -> warning: unused `Result` that must be used
returns_enum();      -> warning: unused `MaybeFinding` that must be used
```

`#[must_use]` does not propagate through `Option`, and `Option<Finding>` was the
signature of the crate's **only** producer — so the one mechanism protecting `FC-L1` was
bypassed by the one function that creates the obligation. Both proposed fixes work; I
did not inherit that claim either.

## HOLE 1 — the producer returns a `#[must_use]` enum

`finding_for(..) -> MaybeFinding { Owed(Finding), NotYet(NotYet) }`.

An enum rather than `Result<Finding, NotYet>`: `Result` is `#[must_use]` and the probe
confirms it would have worked, but **"no finding is owed" is not an error.** Putting a
healthy fleet in `Err` invites `unwrap()`, `?`-propagation out of a correct path, and an
operator reading `Err(NotAFindableDecision)` as a failure. Identical obligation, honest
semantics.

**`NotYet` also splits three conditions the old `None` collapsed** —
`BelowThreshold { seen, threshold }`, `AlreadyEmitted { seen, threshold }`,
`NotAFindableDecision` — so a caller logging "nothing to file" can say WHICH nothing it
saw. Eighth instance of the missing-representation defect today.

`expect_nothing_owed()` is the only zero-obligation disposal and it **refuses to swallow
a real finding**: an `Owed` returns `Err(Finding)` rather than being dropped.

## HOLE 2 — `unused_must_use = "deny"` at the workspace root

`[workspace.lints.rust]` did not exist. It does now, and `crates/finding` +
`crates/finding-dispatch` inherit it with `[lints] workspace = true`.

**`unsafe_code = "forbid"` is repeated in that table deliberately.** A package cannot
carry both `lints.workspace = true` and its own `[lints]` table — the workspace table
REPLACES it — so inheriting without carrying `forbid` forward would silently **relax the
strongest lint in the repository while appearing to tighten one.**

**Proven to bite, live:** planting `finding_for(decision, FINDING_THRESHOLD);` in
`finding-dispatch` gives `error: unused MaybeFinding that must be used` and the crate
does not compile. Dropping a finding is now a build error, not a warning.

## ACCEPTANCE 2 AND 3, ONE PROBE, ALL FOUR DIRECTIONS

```
drops_it()                 { after(); }                          -> 1 warning   (line 15)
disposes_by_taking()       { after().into_owed() }                -> silent
disposes_by_acknowledging() { let _ = after().expect_nothing_owed(); } -> silent
old_shape_drops_it()       { before(); }                          -> silent  (the defect closed)

warning: 1 warning emitted
```

Exactly one warning, on the dropped producer result. The negative leg matters as much:
**an over-strict lint that fires on correct code gets `#[allow]`-ed and dies.**

## THE PINNED DEFECT FIRED, THEN WAS REPLACED

`l1_must_use_is_only_a_warning_and_does_not_survive_option` failed with
`unused_must_use is now denied in 1 manifest(s) — update §FC-L1 in the same commit`.
That failure was the signal, and the doc is updated in this commit.

Replaced by `l1_unused_must_use_is_denied_and_the_producer_does_not_return_option`, which
asserts the same two facts in the direction that now holds. **A pin left in place after
its defect is fixed becomes a test that fails forever and gets `#[ignore]`d**, which is
how a suite goes vacuously green. Two pins remain (`FC-L2`, `FC-L5`).

## THE MUTATION THAT DID NOT BITE, AND THE LEG IT ADDED

**M2 — the producer's crate opts out of the inherited deny — left BOTH packages GREEN.**
The leg checked the deny EXISTED somewhere, not that the crate where dropping happens
INHERITS it. **A lint denied in a manifest no code inherits is BUILT-vs-WIRED at the
manifest layer.** Added a leg asserting both crates carry `[lints] workspace = true` and
do NOT declare their own `[lints.rust]` table; M2 now bites.

## Mutations — restores byte-identical across three files

```
M1 remove unused_must_use=deny from the root      -> FC-L1 leg RED
M2 producer's crate opts out of the inherit       -> FC-L1 leg RED  (after the new leg)
M3 strip #[must_use] from the outer enum          -> FC-L1 leg RED
M4 declare a local [lints.rust] beside the inherit -> UNCONSTRUCTIBLE: cargo refuses a
     duplicate [lints] key. My `!contains("[lints.rust]")` assertion therefore guards a
     REWRITTEN manifest, not the only path. Stated rather than counted as a bite.
```

## TWO MORE SELF-REFERENTIAL INSTANCES, IN THIS ONE FILE

Instance ten: `!producer.contains("-> Option<Finding>")` failed on
`MaybeFinding::into_owed(self) -> Option<Finding>` — **legitimate code** that should
return an Option, not prose. Scoped to the producer's own signature line.

Instance eleven: `find("#[must_use")` matched the DOC COMMENT above the attribute — my
own sentence explaining the attribute. Keyed on a line that STARTS with the attribute.

Eleven instances today, and the cure has been identical every time: **key on structure,
never on the file's text.**

## Verification

```
cargo test -p finding             -> 9 + 12, 0 failed
cargo test -p finding-dispatch    -> 5, 0 failed
cargo clippy (both) --all-targets -> 0 rows in my crates
cargo metadata                    -> 65 members load; finding + finding-dispatch inherit
```

The compiler named all nine call sites in `finding-dispatch/tests/recurrence.rs` via
`E0599`; they now assert the TYPED `NotYet` reason rather than mapping mechanically back
to an `Option`, because the split is the point of the change.

## NO-CLAIM

* **This is a build error in THIS workspace only.** `let _ = …` still silences it — a
  deliberate language escape hatch — and a downstream consumer outside the workspace can
  drop a `MaybeFinding` freely.
* **A warning-free build does not prove any gap was filed.** It proves no `Finding` VALUE
  was dropped, which is strictly weaker than `FC-L1` as stated. Routing production code
  through the crate at all is the unrouted-crate bead and is explicitly out of scope here.
* The deny is inherited by **2 of 65** crates. The other 63 are unchanged, so
  `unused_must_use` is still a warning everywhere else in the workspace.
* `finding_for` has **no production caller** — measured, only its own tests. FC-L1 is now
  non-bypassable for a value that nothing yet produces in anger.

---

IMPLEMENTED by AmberGate (pane 4, %1408) — LANDED `d0d3308`. Bead stays `in_progress`; a non-implementer grades.

All three acceptances met and mutation-verified. The pinned leg fired with `unused_must_use is now denied in 1 manifest(s)` and was replaced by the invariant that now holds; `docs/contracts/finding_contract.md` §FC-L1 is updated in the same commit.

**The mutation that did NOT bite added a leg:** M2 (the producer crate opts out of the inherited deny) left both packages green — the leg checked the deny EXISTED somewhere, not that the crate where dropping happens INHERITS it. That is BUILT-vs-WIRED at the manifest layer.

title: FC-L2: Filed accepts any publisher string as a bead id, including empty
description:
## WHAT

`FC-L2` — "`Filed` must name the bead id; a Finding that cannot produce one is unconstructible" —
is **not enforced**. `Finding::file` copies whatever the publisher returns straight into
`Filed { id }` with no validation (`crates/finding/src/lib.rs:219-224`), so a publisher returning
`""` yields a `Filed` claiming a bead that does not exist.

Measured by the contract suite, which asserts today's behaviour so the fix cannot land silently:
`l2_filed_carries_whatever_the_publisher_returned_including_an_empty_id` passes with
`filed.id().is_empty() == true`.

## WHY

`Filed` is the proof object. Every downstream consumer that trusts it — a close-evidence gate, a
grade, a reconciliation ledger — reads the id as "this gap became schedulable work". An empty or
malformed id makes `Filed` a receipt with no referent, which is the same class as this repo's
close-evidence defect where a bead cited a path that never existed. A proof object that can be
constructed around nothing is worse than no proof object, because a reader stops looking.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Add a validated id at the `Filed` boundary — a `BeadId` newtype or a check inside `file` that
   refuses an id which is empty or does not match `<prefix>-<slug>-<suffix>`. Then
   `cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract`: the pinned leg above goes RED and must be
   rewritten to `expect_err`, with §FC-L2 of the contract updated in the same commit.
2. A known-GOOD arm must stay green: the existing
   `l2_a_real_bead_shaped_id_round_trips_into_filed_and_retires_the_spool_row` files
   `omp-orchestrator-finding-contract-abc` and must continue to succeed. An id validator strict
   enough to refuse a real `br` id is a worse defect than the one being fixed.
3. Decide and state what happens to the spool row when the id is refused: it must remain
   `.pending` (a DEFERRED finding), never be marked published. Assert it with a leg of the same
   shape as `l3_a_publisher_failure_leaves_the_row_recoverable_not_lost`.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Verifying the bead EXISTS in the tracker. Shape validation is local and cheap; existence requires
a tracker round-trip and belongs with the publisher implementation.

## NO-CLAIM

A well-shaped id does not prove a bead exists, is open, or is reachable by `bv`. `Filed` will
still be a claim — just one that can no longer be built around an empty string.

title: FC-L4: a Finding cannot name its replacement
description:
## WHAT

`FC-L4` — "a Finding names its REPLACEMENT when it reports something missing" — has **no
representation in the type**. `Finding` carries `what`, `why`, `acceptance`, `labels`, `priority`
and nothing else (`crates/finding/src/lib.rs:106-112`). A finding that reports an absence cannot
name what should be used instead, so the reader must re-derive it.

Measured by `l4_a_finding_cannot_name_a_replacement_today`, which asserts that `replacement`,
`instead_use` and `supersedes` are all absent from the source, with a positive control that
`acceptance`, `labels` and `priority` ARE found.

## WHY

`fh N040`: a replacement claim needs a smoke check at BOTH ends — the new thing works AND the old
caller is gone. This repo's own doctrine states the narrower rule: `AGENTS.md` requires a gate's
output to name "the kernel that should have been used", because "a finding that does not name the
replacement is not actionable". The `finding` crate enforces the bead standard
(WHAT/WHY/ACCEPTANCE/labels) as a type precondition and then omits the field its own repo's rule
requires.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Add the field. It must be OPTIONAL in the type and REQUIRED conditionally: a finding whose
   `what` reports an absence must carry a replacement. Choose the discriminator explicitly — a
   `FindingKind::Missing { replacement: String }` variant is preferable to a free-text sniff,
   because a keyword scan over `what` will misfire.
2. `cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract`: the pinned leg goes RED (its absence
   assertions fail) and must be rewritten to assert presence, with §FC-L4 updated in the same
   commit.
3. Two arms, both asserted: a `Missing`-kind finding built WITHOUT a replacement is refused with a
   named error (`FindingError::MissingField("REPLACEMENT")`); a non-`Missing` finding with no
   replacement is still accepted. Without the second arm the change makes every finding carry
   ceremony it does not need.
4. `finding_dispatch::finding_for` must compile unchanged or be updated in the same commit — it
   is the only producer, and a new required field breaks it silently otherwise.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Checking that the named replacement exists or works. That is the both-ends smoke check `fh N040`
describes, and it belongs to whoever acts on the finding.

## NO-CLAIM

A replacement field does not make the named replacement correct, reachable, or better than what it
replaces. It only makes the finding actionable without a second investigation.

title: FC-L5: a waiver carries no expiry, so it is a permanent silent exemption
description:
## WHAT

`FC-L5` — "WAIVED IS NOT CLOSED: a waiver carries an expiry or it is a silent permanent exemption"
— is **not enforced**. `Waived` carries `body` and `reason` only
(`crates/finding/src/lib.rs:284-287`), and `Finding::waive` requires a reason and nothing else. A
waiver written once is permanent and never resurfaces.

Measured by `l5_a_waiver_carries_no_expiry_so_it_is_permanent_today`, which asserts `expiry`,
`expires`, `revisit_by` and `until` are all absent from the source, with a positive control on
`WaiverNeedsReason` and `pub fn reason`.

## WHY

This repo has already paid for exactly this defect in a neighbouring mechanism.
`crates/no-shell-gate/tests/wired_lanes.rs` records it verbatim: *"An allowance that outlives its
reason is worse than no allowance, because it reads as a considered exception when it is only an
un-revisited one."* Five `UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE` rows sat unchanged while all five acquired
production callers; the gate caught the drift by accounting, not by any row failing.

`Waived` is the same shape with none of the accounting: a reason, no expiry, no sweep, and nothing
that ever asks whether the reason still holds. `waive()` is currently reachable only from the
crate's own tests, so the exemption pile is empty — which makes this the cheapest possible moment
to fix it.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Add an expiry to `Waived`. It must be REQUIRED, not optional — an optional expiry defaults to
   permanent, which is the state being removed. Prefer a `revisit_by` deadline plus a
   `WaiverError::Expired` on read, so a stale waiver is loud rather than silent.
2. `cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract`: the pinned leg goes RED and must be rewritten
   to assert presence, with §FC-L5 updated in the same commit.
3. A sweep, mirroring `pending()`: `expired(waiver_dir) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, FindingError>`
   with the SAME anti-vacuity rule — an unreadable directory is an ERROR, never an empty sweep.
   Assert both arms, exactly as `l3_an_unreadable_spool_dir_is_an_error_not_an_empty_sweep` does.
4. Waivers must be durable at all: today `Waived` is an in-memory value that nothing writes to
   disk, so an expiry with no persistence expires nothing. State where a waiver is stored and
   assert a written waiver survives a process boundary, as `SpooledFinding` already does.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Choosing a default window. Name one in the contract when it lands; picking it here would be a
guess with no data.

## NO-CLAIM

An expiry does not make anyone revisit the waiver — it makes the waiver LOUD at a known date. The
sweep still needs a caller, which is the same unrouted-crate problem tracked separately, and
adding an expiry to a mechanism nothing calls raises no floor by itself.

title: Build the FOLLOW-UP stage: nothing notices dispatched-then-silent
description:
WHAT: detect a bead dispatched and then silent. Inputs bead id, assignee, dispatch timestamp, current state. Output VERDICT_POSTED, SILENT_PAST_DEADLINE, or REASSIGNED.
WHY: its absence cost four hand-chases tonight -- %1408, %1413, %1409, %1367 each went idle holding assigned work and only a manual question found it.

A posted comment yields VERDICT_POSTED; silence past deadline yields SILENT_PAST_DEADLINE; a changed assignee yields REASSIGNED not silent; an unreadable tracker is an ERROR never VERDICT_POSTED. Assigned %1408.

MUTATION-VERIFIED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. Re-ran rather than read: cargo test -p ack-spine -> 30 passed, 0 failed, which includes the 6 hermetic followup legs. Landing commit b46fb28, crates/ack-spine/src/followup.rs.

WHAT MAKES IT REAL: classify_followup is PURE -- no br, no I/O -- so the tests hit it directly instead of shelling to a live tracker. title: 32 pid-only child.kill() sites: a deadline that spares grandchildren poisons the NEXT attempt too
description:
WHAT: ~32 pid-only `child.kill()` sites across 15 crates. A deadline that signals one pid leaves
that child's grandchildren running, reparented to init.

MEASURED 2026-09-01 by crates/no-shell-gate/tests/group_kill.rs (production source only, tests
and subprocess-contract excluded, comments stripped): 32 sites.

WHY IT IS EXPENSIVE, and it is not the obvious reason. AGENTS.md records the measurement:
"orphaned grandchildren (ppid=1, 0.0% CPU) held the admission lock, so every timeout guaranteed
the next attempt also failed - the failure created the condition for its own repetition." The
orphan OUTLIVES the timeout that created it, so the next attempt inherits a poisoned lock and
times out too. A single pid-kill does not cost one failure; it costs every subsequent one until
someone kills the orphan by hand.

WORSE THAN A UNIFORM GAP: several crates signal a GROUP in one function and pid-kill in another
- fast-dispatch, oracle-compare and omp-idle-dispatch all appear in both lists. The
inconsistency is intra-crate, so a reader who checks one call site learns nothing about the next.

THE REFERENCE FIX IS ALREADY IN THE TREE: crates/loop-tick/src/lib.rs. Two halves, and neither
works alone:
  1. process_group(0) at the SPAWN site so the child leads its own group. Without it, `-pid`
     names a group we do not own and the signal goes nowhere useful.
  2. TERM then a graced KILL on `-pid` in the reaper, matching subprocess-contract's
     bounded_output so both paths behave identically, plus a direct child.kill() fallback for
     when the group signal cannot be delivered.

THE TEST THAT PROVES IT, and why the existing suites did not: loop-tick had ELEVEN tests and all
eleven passed both BEFORE and AFTER the fix, because none spawned a grandchild. The new test has
the child spawn a grandchild that touches a marker at t+2s, then sleep 30s; a 200ms deadline must
leave that marker absent. It also asserts the fixture actually timed out, so it cannot pass by
never reaching the deadline. Copy that shape.

ACCEPTANCE, per converted site:
 1. process_group(0) at the spawn site AND a group signal in the reaper. Both, or neither counts.
 2. A grandchild-survival test for the crate, modelled on loop-tick's.
 3. Mutation: revert to child.kill(), confirm the test goes RED naming the marker, restore
    byte-identical.
 4. Lower PID_KILL_CEILING in group_kill.rs by exactly the number of sites converted, in the
    same commit. Never raise it.

NO-CLAIM: the gate counts a TEXTUAL pattern, not cancel-correctness. A site that signals the
group can still be wrong (no deadline, undrained pipes, a child that was never a group leader),
and a child.kill() used as a fallback AFTER a group signal is legitimate - the gate cannot tell
those apart, which is why it ratchets a count rather than asserting a property. Converting all 32
does not by itself make the fleet cancel-correct.

64-line wait_deadline duplicate is DELETED (commit 5520f42). spawn_contract 16 -> 15 crates.

THE PATTERN TO COPY, in order:
  1. Read the crate's spawn site AND its wait/kill path together. They are one change.
  2. If it redirects to files, bounded_status is still correct - it sets NO stdio, so caller
     redirects survive. I wrongly believed it "inherits" and nearly skipped this conversion.
  3. Delete the local duplicate. Do not leave it beside the kernel call.
  4. Map TimedOut to a distinct outcome. A killed child has NO exit status.
  5. Test the EXPORTED function, never the private helper - the helper is what you are deleting.
  6. Mutation: break bounded_status's -pid signal upstream; your crate's grandchild test must
     go RED. That is what proves you route through the kernel instead of resembling it.
  7. Lower PID_KILL_CEILING in the SAME commit by exactly the number you converted.

title: Flagship no-shell gate is wired to a workflow that can never run (no git remote)
description:
WHAT: the repo's FIRST hard gate -- no tracked .sh/.py -- is invoked only from .github/workflows/gate.yml (cargo run -p no-shell-gate; cargo test -p no-shell-gate). `git remote -v` RETURNS EMPTY. There is no remote, so the workflow can NEVER EXECUTE. The gate has no runner.

MEASURED 2026-08-31: the gate binary itself is CORRECT. Run by hand it exits 1, names both offending files, and prints 'the exemption list is empty by design; there is no check.sh carve-out'. So this is not a detector defect -- the detector is right and unreachable.

WHAT IT COST, same day: two .sh files were committed into the tree the gate forbids -- scripts/ack-detector.sh (7187210, 12:36) and scripts/heartbeat-check.sh (298afbf, 11:30) -- while README.md hard gate 1 says the gate 'lands BEFORE the first crate is copied' precisely so the mess cannot accumulate. It accumulated anyway, in the repo whose ONE RULE is 'No .sh. No .py. Not in bin/, not in scripts/, not just for testing.'

WHY THIS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE INSTANCE: AGENTS.md exists to prevent exactly this -- 'A mechanism that is written, tested, adversarially hardened, and invoked by nothing is worth zero.' This session hit BUILT != WIRED twelve times; this is the twelfth and the worst, because this gate defines the repository.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. The gate runs on a trigger THAT EXISTS ON THIS MACHINE, with no remote and no CI service. A pre-commit hook is the candidate; per hook-certification it must be Rust, asupersync-backed, cancel-correct, and registered in hooks_certified.toml. It must NOT be auto-registered -- a hook error reads as DENY and can brick every Write/Edit/Bash fleet-wide.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD through the real trigger, not by hand: stage a .sh, attempt the commit, assert refusal. Running the binary directly is what we already had and it did not stop anything.
3. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a normal Rust-only commit is NOT refused. An over-strict commit gate gets bypassed with --no-verify and then protects nothing.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty scan set is an ERROR. Zero tracked files must not read as a pass.
5. MUTATION: break the extension match, the known-bad leg goes RED; restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides.
6. THE WIRING TEST IS THE DELIVERABLE: assert a live trigger reaches the gate. AGENTS.md prescribes the shape -- an UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE that is EMPTY, where an exception is a named row with a reason, not silence.

NO-CLAIM: a pre-commit hook is bypassable with --no-verify by design. This raises the floor from 'nothing runs the gate' to 'skipping it is an explicit act'. It does not make committing shell impossible, and saying otherwise would be the overclaim this repo refuses.

title: A bead cannot name which agent holds it or whether that agent is alive
description:
WHAT: **the tracker cannot answer "which agent holds this bead, and is that agent alive."** Both
halves fail independently, and the only surface that claims to answer liveness is wrong by 15 hours
on an agent that is actively committing. Joshua, 2026-09-02: *"if we can't identify which agent —
exactly — is connected to a bead, and if they are live or active or not, we have a failing system."*

## HALF ONE: THE ASSIGNEE FIELD IS FREE TEXT IN FIVE INCOMPATIBLE SCHEMES

Measured over `br list -a --json`: **66 `in_progress` beads across 27 distinct assignee strings**,
of which **24 (36%) named something that is not an agent**:

    dead-pid     7   supervisor:26985, :40174, :98537, :33274, :28860, :14542, :95808
    pane-label   8   pane2, pane3, pane4, pane5
    role-word    9   AmNative, MailMining, JourneySpine, WildcardFix, ClaimFence,
                     ExtractTwo, Orchestrator, omp-claude

**All seven `supervisor:<pid>` processes were verified DEAD** (`ps -p <pid>` → no such process), so
seven beads named a process that no longer exists. A pane label is not an agent — panes are
recycled and indices shift, measured twice in one session. A role word is not resolvable to
anything.

## HALF TWO: LIVENESS IS UNANSWERABLE, AND THE ONE SURFACE THAT ANSWERS IT IS WRONG

    agent-mail  AmberGate    last_active = 15h ago
    tick-monitor %1408       WORKING t=42s LIVE
    git log                  9ecebf6 committed 14:35 TODAY by that agent

Also `SilverWolf` and `BlueLantern` read `prog=unknown, last_active=2d ago` in Agent Mail **while
both were actively working beads.** So the roster's `last_active` cannot be used as a liveness
oracle, and nothing joins an assignee to a pane, so `tick-monitor`'s correct per-pane liveness
cannot be reached from a bead.

## THE BINDING THAT DOES WORK, AND ITS LIMIT

Today's ACK protocol writes the pane INTO the bead: `ACK <token> on %<pane> -- <line>`. That is a
real bead→pane binding and it is the first one this system has had. **Its limit is measured:** of
the 24 orphan beads, **only 2 carried a pane-bearing ACK**, because the protocol went live today
and the rest predate it. It fixes the future and cannot repair the past.

**Derived pane→agent map, from ACK comments on agent-assigned beads** (evidence, not assumption):

    %1413  GreenFrog    6 acks
    %1409  SilverWolf   5
    %1408  AmberGate    4
    %1414  BlueLantern  3   <- AMBIGUOUS
    %1414  MistyCrane   1   <- same pane, second identity
    %1397  SnowyCanyon  1

**`%1414` resolves to two agents.** That ambiguity was created by the orchestrator assigning two
different agent names to one pane within the same hour, and it is unresolvable from the tracker.

## REPAIR ALREADY APPLIED (evidence-backed, by the orchestrator)

    repaired to a real agent, via the derived pane map + ACK evidence   8
    released -- dead supervisor pid AND no pane evidence               5
    left ambiguous -- pane3/%1414, two agents ACKed                    2
    orphan assignees remaining                                        16 -> role-words + pane3

**AND THE REPAIR ITSELF EXPOSED A FOURTH ILLEGAL STATE.** `br update <id> --assignee ""` clears the
assignee and leaves `status=in_progress`, producing **`in_progress` + unassigned — work claimed by
nobody** — which the orchestrator created 5 times while releasing. Repaired with an explicit
`--status open`; both counts are now 0. So the state machine has TWO illegal states, not one:

    open        + assigned     = half-claim   (refuses every dispatch to every pane)
    in_progress + unassigned   = orphan claim (no agent owns in-flight work)

**Both fields must move together in BOTH directions.** `--assignee X` alone makes the first;
`--assignee ""` alone makes the second; `--status open` alone makes the first. Only
`--claim --actor <agent>` and the explicit two-flag pairs are safe.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. An assignee is a TYPED agent identity, not free text. A write naming a dead pid, a pane label,
     or an unregistered role word is REFUSED at write time, not repaired later.
  2. A bead in `in_progress` resolves to exactly ONE agent and ONE pane, and that resolution is
     derived from evidence (ACK row / dispatch ledger), never from a hand-maintained mapping —
     membership is a FACT, so derive it; only triage is a judgement.
  3. Liveness is answerable from the bead: given a bead id, report the holding agent, its pane, and
     that pane's two-capture `liveness` from `tick-monitor`. A stale `last_active` from any roster
     is NOT an acceptable source; it was measured 15h wrong.
  4. Both illegal states are unconstructible or refused: `open`+assigned and
     `in_progress`+unassigned. Fires-on-known-bad for EACH — a fixture in each state must go RED,
     and a legal bead must produce no finding.
  5. Ambiguity is named, never guessed: two agents bound to one pane must produce a typed
     AMBIGUOUS verdict with both candidates, not a silent pick.
  6. Anti-vacuity: zero in-flight beads must not read as healthy. An empty scan is an ERROR.
  7. Positive control: at least one correctly-bound bead resolves end to end, or the checker is
     broken rather than the tracker clean.

NO-CLAIM: the repair above fixed the CURRENT rows and stops nothing from recurring — every write
path that produced these states is still open. The 9 role-word assignees were left alone
deliberately: they may be agents from other sessions and inventing ownership is worse than naming
the gap. `br` is upstream, so refusal at write time may need a wrapper rather than a patch, and this
bead does not decide which.

MEASURED just now across every dispatch packet I wrote today: each one DICTATED the pane id inside the ACK template -- 'ACK eg0m on %1414', 'ACK fr6 on %1409', 'ACK u1c on %1409', 'ACK iis6 on %1408' -- and the count of packets instructing an agent to derive it from $TMUX_PANE is ZERO. title: GOVERNING: every finding becomes a bead mechanically; findings in chat are refused, --actor mandatory on every write
description:
WHAT: **A finding that lives in chat is a finding that will be lost. Every finding an agent reports
MUST become a bead — mechanically, not by discipline.** Josh, 2026-09-02: *"i'm also wondering if
our system is forcing agents to create or add beads - i dont want comments / findings left in chat."*

MEASURED 2026-09-02, the split answer:

  BY AGENT MAIL — reaching the tracker:
    115 messages today (`git log --since=2026-09-02 --format=%s` over the mail archive), 46 to the
    orchestrator, 23 whose subject carries a verdict/finding keyword. Beads created today: 129, of
    which 106 cite a chat/mail source in their body. Mail-borne findings are being filed.

  BY PANE REPORT — NOT reaching the tracker:
    One agent's reports via ntm/tmux today catalogued: "eleven self-referential-checker instances",
    "eighth missing-representation instance", "three pins that failed on the fix they watched", "two
    legs broke and were right to", "a mutation that did not bite" x3, "a one-specimen known-bad
    proved nothing". Each is a named, numbered, general finding. `br list` shows beads for the WORK
    (leht, iis6, eg0m, pwm, py3...) and none for the PATTERNS. The class catalogue exists only in
    scrollback, which is the exact medium 00-brief.md:3-6 says requirements die in.

  ATTRIBUTION — broken on create, not only on comment:
    118 of 129 beads today read `created_by: josh`; 9 carry a real actor (the audit passes). So the
    tracker cannot say WHO filed a finding either. Same defect as gcyf (comments) one field over.

  THE MECHANISM EXISTS AND IS UNWIRED:
    `crates/finding` + `crates/finding-dispatch`: dropping a `Finding` is now a compile error
    (py3, d0d3308), and `finding_for` has ONE production caller. AGENTS.md's own KERNEL-ONLY
    table records the author of `crates/finding` bypassing it with raw `br create` thirty minutes
    after writing it. The pressure that would wire it is removed by every hand-filed bead.

WHY DISCIPLINE CANNOT BE THE FIX: today's orchestrator wrote ~30 dispatch packets by hand and
filed findings by hand throughout, with AGENTS.md's finding->bead rule in context the whole time,
and still left a class catalogue in chat. A rule that the most rule-aware agent in the fleet breaks
under load is a rule that needs a refusal.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. REPORT SHAPE IS PARSED, NOT READ. A DONE / report row that names a finding — any sentence
     matching the finding grammar (instance N of <class>, defect, refuted, drifted, stale,
     NO-CLAIM that names a gap) — MUST carry a bead id, or the report emitter refuses it the way
     `ack-spine --complete` refuses an unparseable row (exit 1, typed reason, zero bytes). The
     grammar is a declared list, not a regex someone infers.
  2. THE FINDING KERNEL IS THE ONLY WRITE PATH FOR A FINDING. `crates/finding` renders the bead
     (WHAT/WHY/ACCEPTANCE/falsifier) from a typed `Finding`; a hand-written `br create` for a
     finding-class bead is refused by a gate that recognises the shape (the same gate that
     refuses a pane-dictated ACK). Positive control: a non-finding bead (a task) still files by
     hand.
  3. `--actor` IS MANDATORY ON EVERY WRITE — create, comment, close, claim. A write resolving to
     the CLI user (`josh`) from an agent pane is refused with the actor named as missing. The 118
     `created_by: josh` rows today are backfilled from the ACK/identity evidence where it exists
     and marked UNATTRIBUTED where it does not — never guessed.
  4. PANE REPORTS ARE NOT A CHANNEL FOR FINDINGS. A report sent by ntm/tmux that carries a finding
     without a bead id is the refusal in item 1; Agent Mail messages carry a `bead:` field the
     tracker can join on (the thread_id already equals the bead id for dispatch threads — extend
     it to reports).
  5. THE CLASS CATALOGUE IS A LEDGER, NOT A SENTENCE. "Instance N of <class>" is an append to a
     machine ledger keyed by class (self-referential-checker, missing-representation,
     instrument-misread, built-not-wired, unstated-denominator) with the bead id per instance —
     so the count is derivable and the next instance is filed against the class, not narrated.
  6. Fires-on-known-bad: a report fixture naming "ninth instance of X" with no bead id is
     REFUSED; the same fixture with a bead id is accepted; an empty report is not vacuously
     accepted.
  7. Backfill: today's pane-reported catalogue is filed — one bead per CLASS with every named
     instance listed — by re-reading the scrollback of %1408, %1413, %1414, %1409 for the
     grammar in item 1. The count filed is the count found; the report of this backfill states
     how many instances could NOT be reconstructed.

NO-CLAIM: forcing a bead per finding does not make the finding correct, and a refused report can
be routed around by not reporting — the refusal makes silence VISIBLE (a DONE without findings on
a bead whose work found some is its own signal), not impossible. Item 3 depends on `br` accepting
`--actor` on every verb; it does today, but enforcement is a wrapper or a gate, not upstream.

title: Ground truth contract for tmux and ntm
description:
WHAT: Author a single contract document defining the authority boundary between tmux pane truth and ntm projection.

WHY: ntm can return a successful empty or stale projection while tmux has live panes; without an explicit comparison contract, callers silently trust the wrong surface.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. docs/contracts/ground_truth_contract.md is <=25 KB and passes all DPB markers with one pasteable validation command.
2. The contract names stable IDs and laws for existence/geometry authority, projection staleness, disagreement-as-error, empty-oracle anti-vacuity, and fresh-not-safe.

title: K5 admission meet + refusal: typed nonzero naming pane and reason, Unknown never coerced, empty oracle is ERROR
description:
WHAT: K5 -- admission meet + refusal. The kernel that decides whether a pane MAY receive work, and
emits a TYPED NONZERO naming the pane and the reason when it may not.

WHY: the fleet's whole failure mode this session was admission answering "nothing to do" instead of
refusing loudly. Measured:
  - `refill-idle-panes` logged `no idle pane both surfaces agree on - nothing to do` at exit 0 while
    `tick-monitor` reported `free_capacity=['%1413','%1409']`. The orchestrator read that line FOUR
    times without registering it. After `oe2` it emits `SURFACE_DISAGREEMENT detector=pane_roster
    oracle=pane-dispatch-ready panes=5` -- a typed refusal -- which is progress, and still not a
    dispatch.
  - `safe_to_dispatch` is NOT liveness: a wedged pane accepts a packet and parks it at
    `Press up to edit queued messages` forever.
  - `ntm --robot-snapshot` returns `total_sessions: 0` with `"success": true` while tmux has five
    live panes, so an admission decision keyed on it is keyed on a confident zero.
  - `AGENTS.md` L2/L4: `Unknown` must NOT coerce to a busy claim, and an empty or unreadable oracle
    is an ERROR, never agreement. `oracle-compare` already implements
    `EmptyOracleIsError` / `UnreadableIsError` / `EmptyProductIsError` as first-class rules.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Admission is a MEET over independent surfaces, routed through `oracle-compare` -- not a
    hand-rolled two-surface check. 13 of 17 dual-surface readers currently handroll the comparator;
    do not add an eighteenth.
 2. Every refusal is a typed nonzero naming the PANE and the REASON. A refusal that does not name
    the pane is not actionable.
 3. `Unknown` is a THIRD value, never coerced. Known-bad: point one arm at an empty read and assert
    the verdict is `Unmeasurable`/ERROR, never `no work`.
 4. ANTI-VACUITY: zero panes observed is an ERROR. `refill-idle-panes` violated exactly this by
    treating an empty ntm projection as consensus.
 5. A confident field can be WRONG: `observation_state=idle @ 0.95` was false about a pane 28
    minutes into a turn, and `safe_to_dispatch == (observation_state == "idle")` held 10/10 while a
    state-derived rule held 5/10 and was ANTI-correlated on one capture. Gate on
    `observation_state`, never on `state`.
 6. Two captures >= 75s apart before calling anything idle, comparing timer AND spinner-stripped
    content hash. `pane-truth` already implements `TWO_CAPTURE_MIN_SECS=75`.

NO-CLAIM: a correct admission verdict does not make a dispatch arrive. Receipt is K8/K9's problem,
and `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` still records that a send RETURNED rather than that it landed.

bead moves the provably-safe subset and measures nothing about the rest.

title: ack_detector tests are coupled to live tracker state and mutate a real closed bead
description:
WHAT: crates/ack-spine/tests/ack_detector.rs hardcodes the bead id `omp-orchestrator-nrj` at lines 11, 33 and 86. Those tests pass ONLY on a machine whose tracker already contains that bead, and every run posts `br comments add` to a REAL bead in the REAL tracker.

HOW IT WAS FOUND -- and tree-green hid it completely: I extracted `git archive HEAD` into a clean directory and ran the suite from the REPOSITORY rather than the working tree.
  working tree : ack_detector 4 passed, exit 0
  clean extract: ack_detector 1 passed, 3 FAILED, exit 101
Verbatim failures:
  genuinely_posted_comment_is_confirmed -> "br comments add must succeed: Error: Issue not found: omp-orchestrator-nrj"
  singular_verb_trap_produces_missing_ack -> "the singular-verb trap must produce Missing, got Unverifiable { bead_id: \"omp-orchestrator-nrj\", detail: \"br comments list exited Some(3): Error: Issue not found\" }"
  read_back_distinguishes_trap_from_good -> same Unverifiable shape

THE DETECTOR IS RIGHT AND THE TEST IS WRONG. Returning `Unverifiable` when the tracker cannot resolve the bead is EXACTLY what oj6.2's acceptance demands -- "An unreadable tracker is an ERROR, never 'no ack'." The extract run therefore fired the detector's anti-vacuity leg FOR REAL, unplanned, and the test asserted `Missing` against it. Do not weaken the detector to make the test pass; that would invert the leg.

TWO DEFECTS:
1. ENVIRONMENT COUPLING. README promises "install it on any of our machines". These tests cannot pass on a machine without this tracker, so vision goal 9 is false while they stand.
2. SHARED-STATE MUTATION. Every run appends a comment to `omp-orchestrator-nrj`, which is a CLOSED bead titled "GRADER-STALENESS-PROBE (deletion candidate)". The tests write to production tracker state, and they are pinned to a bead someone is expected to delete. When it is deleted the suite goes red for a reason unrelated to the code -- the same class as today's port that deleted four scripts and silently invalidated every closed bead citing them.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. HERMETIC: the tests create their own scratch tracker (temp dir + `br --db`, or a scratch bead they create and delete), assert, and clean up. No hardcoded live bead id anywhere in the file.
2. THE PROOF IS THE EXTRACT, NOT THE TREE: `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <tmp>` then `cargo test -p ack-spine` from that directory must exit 0. Tree-green is explicitly NOT acceptance for this bead, because tree-green is the condition that hid the defect.
3. PRESERVE THE THREE-VALUED VERDICT: Missing / Confirmed / Unverifiable must remain distinct, and a test must assert Unverifiable for an unreadable tracker, since that path now has a live specimen.
4. NO WRITES TO PRODUCTION TRACKER STATE from any test. Known-bad: point the suite at the real tracker and assert it refuses rather than mutating.
5. MUTATION: re-hardcode a live bead id, leg 2 goes RED from the extract. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: this is one crate's suite. Whether other crates' tests are environment-coupled is UNMEASURED -- the extract harness that found this can answer it, and that is a separate bead, not an assumption to fold in here.

title: 17 extraction-wave crates handroll ~144 unbounded spawns; kernel now has bounded_status
description:
WHAT: 17 extraction-wave crates spawn child processes with no subprocess-contract dependency and
no allowance row. Measured 2026-09-01 by `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test spawn_contract`:

  fast-dispatch 32, loop-driver 28, fleet-truth 13, tick-dispatch 10, reap-finished-panes 10,
  fleet-reconcile 9, pane-dispatch-ready 9, oracle-compare 7, pane-oracle-diff 4, pane-truth 4,
  dispatcher-deadman 3, omp-idle-dispatch 3, oracle-pane-state-differential 3, verify-dispatch 3,
  wired-but-inert-guard 3, refill-idle-panes 2, loop-tick 1
  = 17 crates, ~144 sites (scratch-home's 1 site is DONE, see below)

WHY THIS IS NOT AN ALLOWANCE PROBLEM: adding 17 allowance rows would turn the strongest gate in
the repo advisory. Earlier today the orchestrator challenged another pane for exactly that shape
- "an exception is a NAMED ROW WITH A REASON; a row saying 'extraction wave' with no caller named
is a placeholder, and the extraction did not wire those lanes, it EXEMPTED them." Filing 17 of
them would be committing the error we flagged. The gate stays RED and honest until the work is
done.

THE KERNEL WAS INCOMPLETE, AND THAT IS WHY THE HANDROLLS EXIST. `subprocess-contract` shipped only
`bounded_output`, which PIPES stdout/stderr. A passthrough spawn - a wrapper handing control to
ntm, a child whose output belongs on the operator's terminal - cannot use it without silently
swallowing the output the spawn exists for. So callers reached for a bare `.status()` with NO
DEADLINE. That is the AGENTS.md KERNEL-ONLY rule biting in its stated direction: "every handroll
is locally cheaper and removes exactly the pressure that would have fixed the kernel."

ALREADY DONE, and it unblocks the rest:
 - `subprocess_contract::bounded_status` added: inherits stdio (no pipes, so the ~64KiB
   undrained-pipe deadlock cannot form), process-group leader, TERM-then-graced-KILL on the
   GROUP, bounded post-kill reap, TimedOut restrictive with no status. 4 tests including a
   GRANDCHILD-SURVIVAL leg. Mutation-verified twice: kill the pid instead of the group -> the
   grandchild survives and the test names it; let TimedOut return Completed -> caught. Restore
   byte-identical.
 - scratch-home converted as the reference: 18 -> 17 crates.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Each crate either depends on subprocess-contract and routes every spawn through
    `bounded_output` (needs bytes) or `bounded_status` (passthrough), OR carries an allowance row
    naming a REAL reason - not "extraction wave".
 2. Every converted site names a deadline const with a comment justifying its value. A false
    timeout that kills healthy work is worse than a slow one.
 3. TimedOut must never be foldable into the caller's failure path: a killed child is not a
    failed child and the remedies differ. Grep each conversion for that collapse.
 4. spawn_contract goes green with an anti-vacuity leg proving an empty scan set is an ERROR.
 5. Per-crate, path-scoped commits. Four panes share this checkout.

NO-CLAIM: routing a spawn through the contract bounds how long we WAIT, not how long the child
runs after we stop waiting. TERM-then-KILL is best effort and a process in uninterruptible state
survives us. This raises a floor from "blocks forever" to "returns a typed restrictive outcome".
