Not "it is an asupersync ledger" — that part was wrong. The reason is: **the heartbeat has no completion record.** `Closed`, `GradeReceived`, `Redispatched` are the three facts a grader needs to answer "did this dispatch finish", and none exists in 6,305 rows. Retiring `ack-spine` deletes the only typed home for them.

**The prerequisite, and it is the same shape as everything else tonight:** ack-spine's emit sites live ONLY in `crates/ack-spine/src/{main.rs,spine.rs}` — nothing outside the crate emits a `StepRecord`, so **its ledger holds no production data today.** Wiring means the supervisor emits through it, not that the crate gains a caller for the census's benefit. **A bin with a manifest dependency added to satisfy a gate is the census defect I just fixed, running backwards.**

SYSTEM FAILURE AUDIT — GreenFrog. Source/doc review only; no build or live-pane re-probe. Josh's report of all worker panes idle is treated as incident ground truth.

Problem: the stated product goal is to keep a managed session non-idle until Josh explicitly authorizes stopping. The current master plan does not encode that goal. README.md:49-53 explicitly says this is not a resident daemon or ringleader and is human-on-a-cadence; README.md:106-110 says nothing is installed and the project is pre-extraction. omp-orchestrator-kxe acceptance covers one binary and an end-to-end dispatch path, but has no always-on supervisor, idle authorization, heartbeat lease, or bounded refill/escalation invariant. WAVE.md:49-50 also says kxe starts last and is blocked on extraction. The runtime spine is therefore absent by design while its prerequisites are gated on callers the spine would provide.

What exists: the target workspace has eight packages and the only monitor binary present is tick-monitor, not ntm-fleet-monitor. tick-monitor main.rs:23-27 exposes observe, watch, emit-tick, and lifecycle. watch is a manually invoked infinite loop at main.rs:376-390 and 432-519; it records JSON and ATTENTION.txt, but main.rs:388-389 explicitly says it does not dispatch, notify, or mutate a bead. Its alarm only prints DISPATCH OR GRADE NOW at :499-512. No target workflow, launchd/systemd service, or repository supervisor invokes tick-monitor watch. .github/workflows/gate.yml runs only workspace metadata, no-shell-gate, and path-literal-guard.

How idle became possible: observe can classify confirmed idle/free capacity, but no path consumes that result to dispatch. emit-tick is a separate manual write path and watch never calls it. ATTENTION.txt has no consumer. The current no-shell-gate wired_lanes.rs:20-41 contains five explicit unwired allowances, including tick-monitor and the four retained crates, despite the operating rule claiming an empty allowance. wired_lanes.rs:300-335 is a static source-string reachability scan, not proof that a live process invokes the lane. tick-monitor/tests/monitor.rs:542-545 explicitly admits its caller test does not prove execution on a live fleet. Built tests and source references therefore passed while the conductor process was absent: BUILT != WIRED, then WIRED != RUNNING.

Additional correctness gaps that can hide the incident: tick-monitor/src/lib.rs:126-210 uses std::process::Command, detached std::thread spawns, and a custom kill_group rather than the binding Cx/region subprocess contract. watch uses std::thread::sleep and ignores ledger/ATTENTION write errors. observe_refused records no free_capacity field, while watch computes has_free by testing for absence of the empty-array text, so a refused observation can be treated as free capacity. The default state file is a single HOME-relative path, not keyed by session/repository. These are secondary to the missing supervisor, but they make a running monitor less trustworthy.

Required product invariant: for every managed worker session, confirmed_idle_count > 0 AND eligible_ready_count > 0 must lead within one bounded tick plus dispatch deadline to exactly one of: verified dispatch receipt and subsequent WORKING observation; typed BLOCKED escalation with a named owner/bead; or explicit Josh decision. It must never produce a healthy/no-op tick or silent process exit. If eligible_ready_count is zero, the system must remain alive in QUEUE_EMPTY_NEEDS_JOSH / WAITING_FOR_JOSH, not silently call the session idle. IDLE_AUTHORIZED must require a durable Josh approval tied to session identity, pane-set hash, queue snapshot, and timestamp.

Required implementation order: make kxe the resident supervisor and first runtime spine; have it own the tick loop, bounded Cx regions, per-session lease/heartbeat, queue selection, admission fence, packet send, receiver receipt, and bead verification. Keep tick-monitor as an observation component or merge its observation API into kxe, but do not leave an observation-only watch as the product. Route all subprocesses through subprocess-contract. Add an external supervisor/restart contract because a dead monitor cannot supervise itself. Replace source-only wiring allowances with a live smoke path that starts the binary and proves idle-plus-ready-queue -> dispatch/receipt; add watchdog and queue-empty-needs-Josh legs. Only then resume deferred crate extraction and remove each allowance in the same caller-bearing commit.

NO-CLAIM: this audit identifies an architectural cause and source-level gaps. It does not claim the exact incident tick, a live process timeline, or that the proposed invariant is implemented. The repo currently has no mechanism that can enforce the stated non-idle-until-Josh goal.

comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE CHOICE RECORDED — resident supervisor, not monitor-as-actuator. 2026-08-31T16:22Z.

%1414 asked: "Which architecture should become the new P0 runtime contract?"
  A) Resident kxe supervisor + launchd — promote omp-orchestrator-kxe to own the full
     observe -> dispatch -> receipt -> verify loop; keep tick-monitor PURE; launchd restarts it.
  B) Make tick-monitor the actuator — the monitor dispatches directly. Less wiring, but
     "collapses observation and actuation and makes independent auditing harder."

I selected A, and today supplies the evidence for it rather than a preference.

WHY SEPARATION IS THE RIGHT CALL, MEASURED TODAY:

arc-keepalive is both the observer and the reporter for pane liveness. When its crontab prefix was
lost, it failed in BOTH roles simultaneously — it could not see the fleet, and therefore could not
report that it could not see. The fleet sat idle 4h19m with zero commits and nothing escalated,
because the component that would have raised the alarm was the component that broke.

Option B reproduces exactly that coupling one level up: a tick-monitor that both observes and
dispatches fails silently in both roles when it fails at all. Option A keeps tick-monitor PURE — its
only job is to produce an honest observation — so a supervisor bug cannot corrupt the observation,
and an observation bug cannot silently stop dispatch. Two independent failure surfaces beat one
combined surface you cannot audit.

THE launchd HALF MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE SPLIT. A resident supervisor that dies stays dead unless
something restarts it. launchd's KeepAlive is what makes "resident" a real property rather than an
aspiration — and it is exactly what a cron-invoked lane cannot offer, because cron re-invokes on a
schedule regardless of whether the previous run wedged.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTATION MUST CARRY, from today's failures:
 - EVERY REFUSAL VISIBLE. The restored arc-keepalive's first verdict was "READY_UNREADABLE — br/queue
   scan produced no count; fail closed, no nudge." Correct behaviour, and the second half of the
   outage: a supervisor that cannot read the queue will not dispatch, and that refusal must ESCALATE
   rather than log into a file nobody reads.

REQUIREMENT CHANGE — Josh approved 2026-08-31 16:23Z: this bead is now the resident runtime spine, not merely a one-shot lifecycle CLI.

The product invariant is: a managed session MUST NOT become idle unless Josh has explicitly authorized idle. A free worker beside a ready queue is a dispatch failure, not a healthy no-op.

Acceptance extension:
1. Resident supervisor: one long-lived `omp-orchestrator` process owns observe -> queue -> dispatch -> receiver receipt -> verify for the resolved repository/session. `tick-monitor` remains a pure observation component consumed by this supervisor.
2. Idle authorization: default ON. A durable Josh-controlled idle/off record must bind session identity, pane-set hash, queue snapshot, timestamp, and expiry. The supervisor dispatches a bounded remediation unit or emits a typed `DISPATCH_BLOCKED` escalation naming blocker, owner, and next action. No successful `nothing to do` path for unreadable or blocked state.
4. Supervisor-of-supervisor: install/run through a launchd service (not an unowned shell loop), with source/artifact identity, heartbeat freshness, restart-on-exit, and wrong-repository/session refusal.
5. Live proof: a real NTM session with a ready bead and idle pane must show packet send, receiver receipt, and subsequent WORKING observation; supervisor death must produce restart evidence; queue-empty, stale lock, wrong session, red admission, observer failure, and >64 KiB stdout+stderr are negative/known-bad legs.

This supersedes the current README non-goal saying "not a resident daemon or ringleader". Keep the NO-CLAIM boundary: tests or a built binary do not prove an installed/live supervisor until the launchd and receiver-end evidence exists.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
RECEIPT SEMANTICS CORRECTED -- a design error in the receiver-receipt crate, found by BlueLantern reviewing the crate against real main behaviour rather than against its own tests.

THE ERROR: assess_receiver_receipt required PRE-SEND WORKING. Main dispatches from tick-monitor ConfirmedIdle, so the pre status is the pi glyph. The function would therefore have REJECTED EVERY DISPATCH THE SUPERVISOR ACTUALLY MAKES. Idle-to-Working is not an edge case; it is the only path main takes.

MY FAULT, IN THE DISPATCH I WROTE: I specified the receipt as a last-status-line timer RESET plus a spinner-stripped content-hash CHANGE. That is the WORKING-TO-WORKING signature -- the queued-packet case for codex panes -- and I presented it as if it were universal. A pane that was IDLE has no timer to reset. I handed the implementer one transition and called it the receipt, and it built exactly what I asked for.

THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS THE free_capacity DEFECT I FIXED AN HOUR AGO. There, one boolean could not distinguish NewlyIdle from working, and deriving two facts from one field made a branch unreachable. Here, one transition signature could not distinguish idle-acceptance from queued-acceptance, and specifying one made the other impossible. BOTH were a collapse of two distinct states into a single measurement, and both produced code that could not fail for the reason it claimed.

CORRECTED CONTRACT -- receipt is keyed on the PRE-state, four transitions and four verdicts:
  IDLE -> WORKING: CONFIRMED, and the strongest evidence obtainable. The transition cannot occur without the pane accepting AND starting. Corroborate that the new timer is SMALL -- a large elapsed timer on a formerly-idle pane means a stale observation or a different packet, which is INDETERMINATE rather than confirmed.
  WORKING -> WORKING with timer RESET and hash CHANGE: CONFIRMED. BOTH signals required. Timer alone fails because a frozen pane and a working pane render identically; hash alone fails because the spinner advances even on a dead pane, so a raw hash changes forever.
  IDLE -> IDLE: NO_RECEIPT, unambiguous.
  WORKING -> WORKING with timer ADVANCED and no reset: NO_RECEIPT, and the dangerous one -- the pane is still on its prior turn and the packet is most likely UNSUBMITTED in the composer. That is the wedge: safe_to_dispatch is not liveness, and a wedged pane accepts a packet, parks it at the queued-messages prompt, and never submits it. Reported distinctly as WEDGED_UNSUBMITTED where the marker is detectable, because the remedy differs from a plain non-delivery.
Two states that must never be folded into either verdict: post=DIALOG is INDETERMINATE, because an Ask dialog advances the timer while blocked on a human and therefore mimics acceptance; and absence from tmux list-panes is DEAD, which is the only death evidence this fleet accepts -- an unreadable capture is a capture failure, and an empty pane list must declare NOBODY dead rather than produce a fleet-wide obituary.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE for the wiring: the pre-observation must be captured BEFORE the send. It is the function input and it cannot be reconstructed afterwards. A receipt check that only looks at the post-state is not a receipt check.

NO-CLAIM: this is a corrected SPECIFICATION, not a verified implementation. It is untested as of this comment. My previous specification on this same bead was refuted within the hour by a grader using a live specimen, and the one before that -- the phantom-landing acceptance -- was refuted by its own known-bad. Specifications are the cheapest artifact here to get wrong. The negative legs are what make this falsifiable: idle-to-idle, working-advanced, and dialog must each go RED under their own mutation, or the crate is asserting rather than measuring. And it remains a legitimate outcome for the implementer to report that a uniform receipt CANNOT be met across both transports, provided it comes with the measurement.

comments.text:
test(convergence): assert the convergence verdict, and add the section it silently omitted [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-kxe.6.

## The zero-assertion test

`report_convergence_state` computed `converged` and `capability_regressed` over the real
ledger and only `println!`d them. **It exited 0 whatever the ledger said** — including on
an empty ledger, where `SECTIONS.iter().filter(...)` yields nothing and the loop body
never runs. A test with no assertion is a program that prints.

The predicate is NOT weakened (acceptance 4). What is added is a claim about its output
that can fail.

## THE ASSERTION FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN

```
ledger rows name sections the report does not iterate, so their grades are
invisible to the verdict: ["12-journey", "12-journey"]
```

**`SECTIONS` had 12 entries and the plan has 13.** `12-journey` was graded in five
`CONVERGENCE.jsonl` rows and once each in `round20` through `round24`, and **every one of
those grades was invisible to the verdict** — a section that could never converge and
could never block. `CONVERGED n/12` against a 13-section plan is the unstated-denominator
defect, sitting in the gate that decides when the plan is done.

Adding it STRENGTHENS the predicate: one more section must now converge before
`every_section_converged_before_dag_conversion` can pass.

## What is asserted now

* **Reportability**, extracted as `reportability(rows, sections) -> Result<(), String>`:
  `EMPTY_LEDGER`, `EMPTY_SECTIONS`, `ORPHAN_SECTIONS`, each typed and each refusing.
* **The headline must equal the marks.** `CONVERGED n/13` is computed twice — once as a
  filter, once in the print loop — and the two must agree. A fact stated in two places
  will disagree in one.
* **Every section lands in exactly one of three states**, and the count of marks equals
  the count of sections, so a section cannot go unreported.
* **A CONVERGED section must have ≥2 graded rows**, because `converged` requires two
  rounds under two lenses — a CONVERGED section with one row would mean the predicate
  accepted something it documents as impossible.

## Mutations — byte-identical restore, sha `58b7314e…55ea5777c`

```
M1  drop 12-journey from SECTIONS      -> orphan assertion RED (the defect it found)
M2  neuter the empty-ledger arm        -> guard leg RED
M3  compare the headline to the wrong mark -> count assertion RED
M3b neuter the orphan arm              -> the leg that found 12-journey RED
```

**M2's FIRST attempt was a BENIGN MUTATION and stayed GREEN.** Neutering the in-body
`!rows.is_empty()` assertion changed nothing observable, because today's ledger is not
empty — so the guard could not be shown to bite on real data, which makes it
indistinguishable from a comment. **Extracting it into a pure function made both
directions checkable with fixtures**, and M2 then goes RED. Same repair the planted-lock
leg in `nh5` needed, and the third benign mutation I have had to re-anchor today.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test convergence   -> 5 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
```

Live output, now asserted: `12-journey graded=2`, so the section that was invisible is
now counted and is `open` on two rows.

## An instrument note, because it nearly cost a wrong conclusion

My first orphan check read `CONVERGENCE.jsonl` **and** every `round*.jsonl`, and reported
four orphans (`CONVERGENCE`, `cross-cutting`, `cross-section`, `cross-section-more`).
`ledger()` reads **`CONVERGENCE.jsonl` only** — a differently-shaped reader again. Under
the real reader the orphan set with `12-journey` added is EMPTY. Had I acted on my own
reader I would have added three non-section names to `SECTIONS`.

## NO-CLAIM

* This makes the convergence test enforce a result. **It does not make the plan
  converged**, and `12-journey` is `open` on two rows — adding it moved the denominator,
  not the verdict.
* `every_section_converged_before_dag_conversion` remains `#[ignore]`d, and it is now

* Acceptance 5 needs a neighbour to re-run these legs on a pinned revision. **I am the

* The package could not be compiled for several minutes mid-work because a peer's

  CommandExt` after its use site. Not mine, and it resolved on retry — recorded because
  "the package does not build" was briefly true for reasons unrelated to this change.

title: identity row absent is unsatisfiable: supervisor filters by pane_id, ntm answers with pane index - the join can never match
description:
WHAT: **`RECEIVER_OBSERVATION_MISSING ... identity row absent` is structurally unsatisfiable. The
supervisor asks `ntm` for a pane by `pane_id` and then filters the answer by `pane_id`, but `ntm`
answers with a pane INDEX. The comparison can never be true, for any pane, ever.**

MEASURED 2026-09-02 with both identifier domains:
```
$ ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator --panes '%1409'
  -> 1 row,  agents[0].pane == '5'        <- accepts a pane_id, ANSWERS with an index
$ ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator --panes 5
  -> 1 row,  agents[0].pane == '5'
$ ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator          (no filter)
  -> 5 rows, panes = ['1','2','3','4','5']  <- never a %-prefixed id
```
The failing code, `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:553-557`:
```rust
let agent = snapshot.agents.iter()
    .find(|agent| agent.pane == pane)      // `pane` is "%1409"
    .ok_or_else(|| format!("RECEIVER_OBSERVATION_MISSING pane={pane} identity row absent"))?;
```
`"%1409" != "5"` -> `None` -> refusal. **The request succeeds, the row exists, and the filter drops
it.** Two callers are affected: `:615` and `:931`.

**THIS IS A CORRECT DISCIPLINE COLLIDING WITH `ntm`'s CONTRACT, NOT CARELESSNESS.** The operating
brief for this session is explicit: *"PANE INDICES ARE NOT STABLE HANDLES. They shifted twice
tonight. Address by pane_id (%1408)."* The supervisor obeys that everywhere - and `ntm` normalises
the identifier to an index on the way out. **Following the right rule produced an unsatisfiable
predicate.**

**WHY IT SURVIVED `nqvk`'s LANDING AND INSTALL.** The identity kernel is correct and fully live:
```
tick-monitor installed Sep 2 11:00   build_id=dbaa09af5214 == live HEAD
observe emits per-pane: epoch, sequence, changed_at
omp-orchestrator installed           build_id=dbaa09af5214 == live HEAD
```
Both binaries are at HEAD, parity-clean, and the identity fields are present. **The failure is not
staleness and not a missing field** - it is a join on two different key spaces, which no amount of
correct implementation on either side can fix.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Resolve the identifier domain **once, explicitly**, and state which is canonical. Either
   (a) map `pane_id -> index` before the filter, or (b) filter on the field `ntm` actually returns
   given that `--panes <pane_id>` already selects the right row - in which case a single-row response
   needs no client-side `find` at all, and the `find` is the defect.
2. **A single-row response must not be re-filtered by a key the response does not carry.** Whichever
   fix is chosen, the request and the filter must agree on the key space by construction, not by
   convention.
3. **Fires-on-known-bad using this exact specimen:** assert that a `pane_id` request whose response
   carries an index still resolves. Anchor the mutation uniquely and restore byte-identically.
4. **Anti-vacuity:** a zero-row response must remain a typed refusal, distinct from a row that was
   found and filtered away. Today those two produce the same message, which is why this cost hours -
   `identity row absent` reads as "ntm has no data" when the truth is "we discarded the data".
5. **Rename the refusal** so the two cases are distinguishable, e.g. `IDENTITY_ROW_ABSENT` vs
   `IDENTITY_ROW_KEY_MISMATCH`. Per this repo's own error-taxonomy discipline, a failure that cannot
   name its own cause sends the next reader to the wrong subsystem - it sent me to check binary
   staleness, install parity and `tick-monitor` fields first, all of which were healthy.

NO-CLAIM: fixing the join makes the identity lookup *reachable*; it does not prove the downstream
receiver-receipt logic is correct, and it does not establish that `ntm`'s index is stable enough to
key on - the brief says indices shift, which is the very reason the supervisor used `pane_id`. If
option (b) is chosen, the stability question is answered by never persisting the index; if (a), it
needs a fresh mapping per call and must not be cached across cycles.

title: the gate census has 25 rows for 65 crates: 40 have no row at all, so the census has no opinion on 61% of the tree
description:
WHAT: **the gate census has 25 rows and this workspace has 65 crates. 40 crates have NO census row
at all** — so for 61% of the tree the census has no opinion, and `all_reachable()` is true over a
set that never included them.

MEASURED 2026-09-02, from the census's own two hand-listed sets in
`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs`:

```
census rows total                     25
crates on disk                        65
crates with NO census row             40
commit-build-fence has a row          False
absent (first 12): admission-reason, agent-mail-native, asupersync-conformance,
  bead-availability, cargo-lane-budget, commit-build-fence, convergence-stamp,
  crate-soundness-verify, dispatch-claim-fence, dispatcher-deadman, extraction-roster,
  fast-dispatch, ...
```

**THIS IS THE THIRD CLASS THE VERDICT ENUM DOES NOT HAVE.** `GateReachability` offers
`Reachable`, `Unreachable`, `NotInstalled`, `NotExtracted`. There is no variant for *"this crate was
never asked"*, and there is no row to carry one — so an unasked crate is indistinguishable from a
crate that does not exist. `kwo9` fixed the PROBE and left the MEMBERSHIP hand-listed.

**The census's own source already condemns this**, at `lib.rs:513-514`:

> *"A frozen snapshot presented as a census is the defect class this whole repository keeps finding —
> a hand-maintained list masquerading as a probe."*

That comment was written about two hardcoded `Unreachable` rows and it fixed those. The membership
list one scope out is the same defect and the comment does not reach it — **an observation in a
comment that the code ignores**, which `kwo9`'s bin/lib finding already named as the cheapest defect
there is and the hardest to see.

WHY IT MATTERS RIGHT NOW: `6fot`'s grade asked whether the census "counts a test and an installer
reference as reachability, or reports it correctly and nobody read it." **Neither.**
`commit-build-fence` is absent from the census, so the census never had an opinion about it, and
`no-shell-gate/src/bin/gate-reachability.rs` reports on a set that excludes it. A crate can be
uninstalled, unwired, and invisible at the same time, and today the third is silent.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Census membership is DERIVED from the workspace, not hand-listed: every directory under
   `crates/` that carries a `Cargo.toml` gets a row. `crates on disk` and `census rows` must be
   equal, asserted, with both numbers printed.
2. A crate whose reachability cannot be classified gets a typed variant naming that — not silence,
   and not a borrowed `Unreachable`. `next_action()` must return something an operator can do.
3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: add a crate directory with a `Cargo.toml` and no caller, and assert the
   census gains exactly one row for it whose verdict names the absence. Remove it and assert the
   count returns. Restore byte-identically.
4. KNOWN-GOOD: every currently-Reachable row must stay Reachable, and `no-shell-gate` must remain
   the positive control. A membership fix that flips existing verdicts is a different change and
   must be argued separately.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: a census whose row count equals zero, or is less than the number of crates on

comments.text:
feat(census): derive membership from disk, advisory-first with a shrink ratchet [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-leht. Advisory-first per SnowyCanyon's ruling, with all three
binding conditions and one amendment to condition 1.

## The defect, and a CORRECTION to the number I reported

`census_gates` returned **22 rows against 65 crates on disk**. 43 crates — 66% of
the tree — had no row at all, and `all_reachable()` was therefore true over a set
that never included them. A crate could be uninstalled, unwired, and **invisible**
at the same time, and only the third was silent.

**I first reported 25 rows / 40 missing / 61%. That was wrong.** It came from a
script that read the source lists; the real function walks push order and answers
22. The script counted the three `UNEXTRACTED` names as rows, and that loop
`continue`s for every one of them because all three are now on disk. Third
instrument error of the same shape today: **a reader that did not model the code it
was summarising.** The live function is the authority over my script.

`lib.rs` already contained the sentence that condemns this, written about two
hardcoded verdicts while the membership list twenty lines below stayed hand-written:

> *"A frozen snapshot presented as a census is the defect class this whole
> repository keeps finding — a hand-maintained list masquerading as a probe."*

An observation in a comment that the code ignores. `kwo9` fixed the PROBE and left
the MEMBERSHIP hand-listed.

## A SHARPER DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING THIS: extraction DELETED a crate from the census

The `UNEXTRACTED` loop `continue`s when a crate lands, with the comment *"it landed
— fall through to the normal measurement below."* **There was no normal measurement
below for those names**, because the generic hand-list did not contain them. So
`fleet-truth`, `oracle-compare`, and `oracle-pane-state-differential` each vanished
from the census **on the day they were extracted**. Landing a crate made it
invisible. All three now carry real rows.

## AMENDMENT TO CONDITION 1: the missing state is a DISPOSITION, not a reachability

Condition 1 asked for `NotAsked` / `Uncensused` on `GateReachability`. **After
derivation that would be false**: the probe now runs on every crate on disk, so a
newly-censused crate's reachability is genuinely MEASURED. Labelling a measured row
`NotAsked` is the same false-label defect that forced `NotExtracted` to exist.

What those crates lack is not a measurement — it is a **triage judgement about the
measurement**. So:

* `CensusDisposition { Blocking, Advisory { reason } }` — the new axis. This is what
  condition 1's *purpose* needs: without it "advisory" is a word in a comment.
* `GateReachability::Unprobed { reason }` — the genuine cannot-look case, a crate
  directory with no readable manifest. Checked BEFORE the trigger arms, because they
  all read that file and would otherwise render an unreadable manifest as "library
  with no manifest dependency" — a measurement we did not take, whose remedy sends
  the operator to wire a crate whose manifest is the actual problem.

**And the ruling's own distinction, made mechanical:** membership is a FACT about
the repo, so it is derived; triage is a JUDGEMENT, so it lives in a list. Hand-listing
the facts produced 43 invisible crates. `CURATED_BLOCKING_ROSTER` is a list on
purpose, and says so.

## Condition 1's second payoff: the compiler found every consumer

`E0063` named **9 construction sites** across `lib.rs`, its own test module, and
`tests/gate_wiring_wave3.rs`. Same mechanism as `E0004` handing me
`ProviderError402` and `Unproven` on `iis6`. A consumer I did not know existed
cannot be missed.

## Condition 2: loud in the decision output, every cycle

`CENSUS_ADVISORY count=23 ceiling=23 rows=65 blocking=22 ratchet=on-time
next_action=wire-or-retire-one-advisory-crate`

Printed **ahead of the `match`**, so it appears on every branch including those that
`return` early. Not into a log and not into a file, because every other signalling
path here is measured silent: `ATTENTION.txt` 178 ticks / zero readers, a typed
refusal naming `owner=josh` printed 29 times unread, `gate.yml` failing six
consecutive runs unread. The only path that has ever reached a human is a verdict
the operator had to answer.

Past the deadline with no decrease it prints `CENSUS_ADVISORY_RATCHET_OVERDUE
owner=josh` — the operator's own falsifier, in their own output.

## Condition 3: the ratchet, in three legs, and leg 3 is the teeth

```
ADVISORY_ALLOWANCE: 23 NAMED rows, each with the reason it is not yet blocking
leg 1  advisory + non-reachable + not named        -> BUILD FAILS
leg 2  allowance length != ADVISORY_CEILING        -> BUILD FAILS
leg 3  a row whose crate is now REACHABLE or GONE  -> BUILD FAILS
```

**Leg 3 is what makes advisory-first distinguishable from permanent silence:** wiring
a crate makes its row stale, so the row must be deleted and the ceiling lowered in
the same edit. Nobody has to remember. This is `franken_lean`'s
`UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE` applied to a set that is required to shrink.

**A named list, not a count**, because a bare count of 23 is satisfied by any 23
crates and cannot tell "we fixed one and broke another" from "nothing happened".

**Leg 2 tightened during review**: `len() <= CEILING` alone permits slack to
accumulate forever — delete a row and the bound quietly stops meaning anything. It
now requires EQUALITY, and the live census count must equal the ceiling too, so the
number cannot drift from the measurement it describes.

**The falsifier as a number, per the request:** `ADVISORY_RATCHET_DEADLINE_TICKS =
200` — 200 ticks at the 90s interval, **5 hours**, asserted arithmetically so a
reader checks it rather than trusting the comment.

## KNOWN-GOOD: not one verdict flipped

```
blocking rows        22  == PRE_LEHT_BLOCKING_ROWS   (asserted)
refusing rows         1  == ack-spine, exactly as before (asserted)
advisory rows         43, of which 23 non-reachable
positive control     no-shell-gate REACHABLE (asserted)
```

Without `CURATED_BLOCKING_ROSTER`, derivation would have silently demoted all six
old generic-loop crates to advisory — `ack-spine` among them, the row that refused
the loop in `kwo9`. **That is a membership fix quietly unblocking the fleet**, which
the ruling forbids, and M3 proves the leg catches it.

## Mutations — byte-identical restore, `ec4b1369…c27e0f66`

```
M1 LEG 3, THE TEETH: keep an allowance row for a now-REACHABLE crate
     -> an_allowance_row_for_a_wired_or_absent_crate_is_stale_and_fails RED
M2 LEG 1: delete one allowance row
     -> every_advisory_unreachable_row_is_named_in_the_allowance RED
M3 KNOWN-GOOD: drop ack-spine from the roster (silent unblock)
     -> no_pre_existing_verdict_was_flipped_by_derivation RED
M4 MEMBERSHIP: partial directory walk -> 3 legs RED including the row/disk equality
M5 ANTI-VACUITY: empty walk -> 4 legs RED. A census of zero must ERROR, never
     read as a fully-wired fleet
M6 SLACK: ceiling 23 -> 99 -> the new equality leg RED
```

M5 is the one that matters most: **an empty census reports identically to a green
fleet**, so the anti-vacuity legs assert `disk.len() > 20` and a non-empty advisory
set before anything else can pass.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p omp-orchestrator --test census_membership -> 10 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p omp-orchestrator (whole package)         -> 42/50/10/1/3/3/2/8/4, 0 failed
cargo clippy -p omp-orchestrator --all-targets         -> 0 rows in the files I touched
```

Clippy correctly flagged three const assertions; they are const-drift guards whose
job is to fail the build when the constant is edited, now `allow`ed with that reason
stated and a live assertion added beside them.

## NO-CLAIM

* **43 advisory rows are not individually assessed.** I measured membership and
  wired the ratchet; nobody has checked whether any of the 23 unreachable crates
  should be wired, retired, or are correctly dormant. That triage is the queue this
  creates, not work this commit did.
* **This does not prove the supervisor's advisory line is READ.** It proves it is
  emitted on every branch. The 178-unread-ticks precedent applies to me too.
* The `Unprobed` variant is proven distinct in label, remedy and `is_reachable`, but
  **no live crate produces it today** — planting a manifest-less directory would race
  peers in this shared checkout, so its production path is asserted by construction
  rather than observed.
* `PRE_LEHT_BLOCKING_ROWS = 22` is re-derived from `HEAD`'s source by walking push
  order. It is a second instrument, not the original function, and my first count of
  25 is exactly why that distinction is stated.

omp-orchestrator-leht, follow-up to 437e11a. **Two defects in my own condition-2
work, both found by RUNNING the binary rather than reading the diff.**

## 1. A count printed after something that can refuse is not printed every cycle

The first version sat immediately after `decide()`. That reads as "every branch",
and it is not: **MEASURED against the current tree, the tick aborts at
`reap-finished-panes` BEFORE `decide` is ever called**, so the count printed on
zero of my probe runs.

```
$ omp-orchestrator --once --session omp-orchestrator
OBSERVATION tick=1 session=omp-orchestrator panes=5 ... free_capacity=1
SUPERVISOR_REFUSED reap-finished-panes exited=2 stderr=usage error: unknown argument --repo
```

The live build reaches `decide` on **39 of 39 ticks** (`GATE_UNWIRED 39 ==
SUPERVISOR_REFUSED 39` in the heartbeat), which is exactly why the placement bug was
invisible from the ledger — the ledger says the branch is reached, and it is, on the
INSTALLED build. Moved to the head of `run_cycle`, ahead of every kernel invocation
that can abort a tick.

The reap abort itself is NOT mine (`git blame` -> `4371bb98`, 09-01) and is filed
separately: the source passes `--repo` and the installed reaper rejects it.

## 2. A deadline already past is not a deadline

`ADVISORY_CEILING_RECORDED_AT_UNIX` was `1_756_845_000` — **one year off**. The live
run printed `CENSUS_ADVISORY_RATCHET_OVERDUE` on tick 1: 350,394 elapsed ticks
against a 200-tick deadline. A verdict true the instant it is recorded carries no
information and would have trained the operator to ignore the line — the fifth
instance today of a signal that is loud in principle and silent in fact.

The constant now records the moment it was set, and the decision is a PURE function
so both directions are checkable instead of only the one the clock happens to be in:

```rust
pub fn advisory_ratchet_overdue(now, recorded_at, interval, deadline_ticks,
                                advisory_count, ceiling) -> bool
```

**Third direction, which the inline version did not have:** past the deadline but
the count DECREASED returns `false`. The falsifier is about a stalled ratchet, not
elapsed time — without it the verdict would nag forever after 5 hours no matter how
much work landed.

## LIVE, both directions

```
clean:            CENSUS_ADVISORY count=23 ceiling=23 rows=65 blocking=22 ratchet=on-time
                    next_action=wire-or-retire-one-advisory-crate
M7 re-date the ceiling into the past -> CENSUS_ADVISORY_RATCHET_OVERDUE   restored IDENTICAL
```

First line of output, before the abort. That is the whole of condition 2.

cargo test -p omp-orchestrator                          -> 42/50/11/1/3/3/2/8/4, 0 failed

documentation was separated from its constant by a blank line, so it documented

with `endswith("src/lib.rs")`, which matches `omp-rpc-session` too, and twice
reported peer warnings as mine. Same class as a keyword grep over `--help`: the
pattern matched the SHAPE of the path rather than the path.

## NO-CLAIM

* The probe ran with `OMP_HEARTBEAT_LEDGER` redirected to `/tmp`, and the live
  ledger gained no rows from it. It was safe to run against the real session only
  because `ack-spine` still refuses at the gate, so `decide` cannot return

* `ratchet=on-time` today is trivially true: the ceiling was recorded minutes ago.

title: tick-monitor lifecycle attributes CITED SHAs as a bead's own landing, inflating LANDED_UNGRADED with phantom work
description:
WHAT: `tick-monitor lifecycle` harvests commit SHAs from a bead's PROSE and records them as that bead's own landing. A SHA cited as ANOTHER bead's evidence therefore promotes the citing bead into LANDED_UNGRADED, so the grading queue fills with beads where nothing was ever built.

MEASURED 2026-08-31, found by a grader disputing my premise rather than by me:
  tick-monitor lifecycle reported: omp-orchestrator-2lo  author=-  deps=0  landed=3f821d4
  git log --all --grep='2lo'      -> EMPTY. No commit references 2lo at all.
  git log -1 3f821d4              -> 'gate: no-shell-gate - fail the build on tracked .sh/.py [mutation-verified]'
                                    which is omp-orchestrator-4ak's work, not 2lo's.
  3f821d4 in 2lo's comments      -> present, as a CITATION, in a comment I wrote myself.
So the tool read my own cross-reference to a different bead's commit and reported it as this bead's implementation.

IMPACT, and it is a ROUTING-SAFETY defect rather than a cosmetic one. LANDED_UNGRADED is what I use to decide who grades what. A phantom row causes a grader to be dispatched at a bead with no artifact, which is a wasted slot under a build freeze when grading is the only work available. Worse, it is INDISTINGUISHABLE from real work in the output: the row carries a real SHA that resolves in git, so a conductor checking 'does the cited commit exist?' gets YES and proceeds. It took a grader re-deriving the premise -- `git log --grep` on the bead id -- to catch it. That check is exactly what the tool should be doing and is not.

THIRD DEFECT IN THIS TOOL IN ONE SESSION, and all three are the same failure of attribution:
  1. author= reads the current ASSIGNEE, not the implementer. Observed live: r3h flipped author=GreenFrog -> author=AmberGate when I routed AmberGate as its GRADER. I nearly handed a bead back to its own implementer.
  2. dangling SHA citations were counted as unresolvable commits -- fixed in fa5129e/b352af1 by requiring `in_citation_position` for marker words and excluding truncated sha256 content hashes.
  3. THIS: a SHA in citation position is still credited as a landing. Fix (2) narrowed which TOKENS count as commit-shaped; it never asked WHOSE commit a resolvable SHA is.
The generalisation the tool keeps failing: a SHA appearing NEAR a bead is not a SHA belonging to that bead. Adjacency is not authorship -- the same lesson as the DIALOG detector, where a framed marker in scrollback is not a dialog, and only ADJACENCY TO THE STATUS LINE discriminated.

THE FIX, stated as a contract rather than a patch:
A bead's landing set must be derived from the OBJECT STORE keyed on the bead, not from the bead's text. The authoritative join is `git log --all --grep=<bead-short-id>`: the commit must NAME the bead. A SHA that appears only in prose is a CITATION and belongs in a separate field -- `cites=` -- which must never feed LANDED_UNGRADED.
That also fixes defect 1 in the same pass: the implementer is the author of the commits in the derived landing set, and where the landing set is empty there IS no implementer, so `author=` must render as NONE rather than borrowing the assignee.

ACCEPTANCE - must FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, and the known-bad already exists in the tracker:
1. PLANTED (real specimen, no fixture needed): run lifecycle over this repo. omp-orchestrator-2lo must NOT appear in LANDED_UNGRADED and must NOT carry landed=3f821d4. It is now CLOSED, so use a scratch bead citing a foreign SHA if a live open specimen is needed.
2. KNOWN-GOOD leg, mandatory: a bead WITH a real commit naming it (e.g. 4ak / 3f821d4, or npq / f9f4e37) must STILL appear with its landing intact. Without this leg the fix ships an over-strict rule that empties the queue and gets routed around.
3. author= must render NONE for a bead with an empty landing set, and must NOT equal the assignee. Assert on a bead whose assignee is set and whose landing set is empty -- 2lo before its close was exactly that shape.
4. cites= must be POPULATED for the citation case, so the information is preserved rather than deleted. A fix that silently drops the cross-reference loses the audit trail I was building when I wrote it.
5. MUTATION: revert to prose-harvesting -> leg 1 must go RED. Restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty bead set must be an ERROR, not a pass. A lifecycle run that parses zero beads currently reports 'zero beads parsed; an empty scan set is an ERROR, never a pass' -- keep that.

BLOCKED ON cp-oakbv: the fix requires `cargo build` and builds are refused fleet-wide (CARGO_MINT_CONTAINER_EXHAUSTED / cargo_floor_guard exit 75, refused even at CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=7). I am not lowering the override further and not editing the installed default. Until the floor clears, LANDED_UNGRADED must be treated as an UPPER BOUND on real ungraded work, and every row confirmed with `git log --all --grep=<bead-id>` before a grader is dispatched at it.

NO-CLAIM: I have not audited how many CURRENT LANDED_UNGRADED rows are phantoms. 2lo is one confirmed instance; the count is unknown and I am not guessing it, because a remembered number dying on derivation is the exact failure class this session has produced four times. I also have not verified whether the `deps=` field suffers the same prose-harvesting problem, though `dep_count` was already found once to be measuring OUT-edges only.

title: 18 of 102 closes use a prefix outside the four the policy documents; PARTIALLY closed a bead
description:
WHAT: **18 of 102 closed beads (18%) carry a close-reason prefix outside the four AGENTS.md says the
policy admits**, so the documented claim "the close policy REFUSES a prose reason" is false for one
close in five, and one bead closed with the reason `PARTIALLY`.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 over `br list -a --json`, first ALL-CAPS token of `close_reason`:

    MUTATION-VERIFIED        43
    DONE                     24
    COMPLETE                 11   <- all on omp-coverage-mission-ipg.*
    WONTFIX                   9
    APPROVED                  8
    PARTIALLY                 1   <- omp-orchestrator-8b1
    VERIFIED-ALREADY-FIXED    1
    VERIFIED-COMPLETE         1
    CONFIRMED                 1
    VERIFIED-ALREADY-WIRED    1
    -----------------------------
    outside the documented four: 18 / 102

Surfaced by `ack-spine`'s new completion classifier on its first run over production data
(`eg0m`, `a3ab48d`): `ipg.11` received `Closed` and NOT `GradeReceived` because `COMPLETE:` is not a
grade prefix. The classifier discriminating on real rows is what made this visible.

WHY IT MATTERS: AGENTS.md states the close policy refuses prose and that a close reason MUST begin
`MUTATION-VERIFIED / DONE / APPROVED / WONTFIX`. Either (a) the ENFORCED list is wider than the
DOCUMENTED one — it evidently accepts any leading capitalised token — or (b) some write path bypasses
the policy. In both cases the 18 rows are closes whose grading evidence is unverified by the
mechanism that was supposed to verify it. `PARTIALLY` closing at all is a credit debt by
construction: a reason that begins by saying the work is partial should never have satisfied a
close gate.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. Determine which: read the close-policy implementation and state the actual accepted set. If it
     accepts any capitalised prefix, the documentation is wrong and must say what is enforced. If it
     accepts exactly four, find the bypass path and name it.
  2. Documented set == enforced set, and a test asserts equality between them (a fact stated in two
     places will disagree in one).
  3. Fires-on-known-bad: a close attempt with reason `COMPLETE: ...` and one with `PARTIALLY ...`
     are REFUSED with the refusal text naming the admitted prefixes.
  4. The 18 existing rows are dispositioned: each is either re-graded by a non-implementer and its
     reason rewritten to an admitted prefix with cited evidence, or reopened. `8b1` (`PARTIALLY`) is
     reopened unless a grader shows the partial was the accepted scope.
  5. Anti-vacuity: a scan of closed beads that finds zero rows is an ERROR; positive control is the
     43 `MUTATION-VERIFIED` rows.
  6. `ack-spine`'s completion classifier treats an unadmitted prefix as a typed
     `ClosedWithoutGrade` outcome, not silently as `Closed` — the row that surfaced this must stay
     distinguishable.

NO-CLAIM: prefix conformance is not evidence quality — a `MUTATION-VERIFIED` reason can still be

feat(spine): ClosedWithoutGrade is its own kind, not a bare Closed [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-mcq2 acceptance 6, requested by SnowyCanyon. Plus the AGENTS.md
row for the seventh self-referential-checker instance.

## The defect in my own first version

`completion_kinds` emitted a bare `Closed` for a close whose reason the policy does
not admit. So **an ungraded close was distinguishable only by the ABSENCE of a
sibling `GradeReceived` row** — and absence cannot separate *"closed without a
grade"* from *"the grade row was lost"*. A query for ungraded closes had to join rows
and infer from a gap.

That is not an edge case. SnowyCanyon measured the first capitalised token of every
close reason: **18 of 102 closes (18%) fall outside the four documented prefixes** —
`COMPLETE` ×11 (every one an `ipg.*`), `PARTIALLY` ×1, `CONFIRMED`, and three
`VERIFIED-*` variants. One close in five, and **a bead closed as `PARTIALLY`**.

## The sixth missing-representation defect of the day, and it was mine

`iis6` busy/dead. `leht` unasked/nonexistent. `t784` awaiting-grade/unstarted.
`--claim` actor/agent. Identity asserted/occupied. **And now graded-close /
ungraded-close.** Same shape every time: a real, distinct condition with no
representation gets coerced into a neighbouring value, and the coercion reads as
normal. I named the pattern this afternoon and then shipped an instance of it.

`StepKind::ClosedWithoutGrade`, wire string `closed_without_grade`. A distinct
string deliberately — reusing `"closed"` with a flag somewhere else would put the
distinction back into a field a reader must remember to check, which is the substring
problem the typed ledger exists to replace.

## The compiler named the blast radius, again

`E0004` on `as_str`, the one exhaustive match over the enum: adding a variant without
a wire string is a compile error, not a row that serialises as something plausible.
Third time today the type system found the consumer — after `E0004` on
`receiver-receipt`'s pane states and `E0063` on nine `GateCensusRow` sites.

## LIVE on production data

```
$ omp-orchestrator --once --session omp-orchestrator      (heartbeat COPY, real br calls)
SPINE_COMPLETIONS_RECORDED steps=9
kinds: {grade_received: 4, closed: 4, closed_without_grade: 1}

closed_without_grade  omp-orchestrator-omp-coverage-mission-ipg.11
                      close_reason=COMPLETE: coverage table ...
```

Before this change that row read `closed`, identical to the four graded ones. The
four graded closes are unchanged, so the split is attributable.

## Mutations — byte-identical restores, `cmp`-verified

```
M1 THE FOLD: production emits a bare Closed for an ungraded close  -> 2 legs RED
M2 WIRE COLLISION: both kinds serialise as "closed"                -> 1 leg RED
```

M2 is the leg that matters: typing that is invisible on the wire is decoration, and a
JSONL reader would be back to inference. My first attempt at M1 asserted the literal
appeared once and **the assertion fired** — three occurrences, two in tests. Mutating
by line number instead. An assertion that catches the mutation harness is the harness
working.

## AGENTS.md: the seventh self-referential instance, as requested

Added as item 5 under the census family: *a doc comment warning about a needle
contained the needle, so the gate stayed GREEN with its emit site deleted.* The
general fix is stripping `//` and `/* */` before matching — splitting the needle only
protects the checker from its own code, and a peer's comment mentioning a primitive
would still register as a caller. Over-stripping is the safe direction: it can only
report LESS reachability, and the failure it prevents is a false green.

The row's closing line is the transferable part: **a mutation that fails to bite is
the most valuable result available.** The suite was green and acceptance 4 was
satisfied on paper.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p ack-spine        -> 33/6/6/6/6, 0 failed
cargo test -p omp-orchestrator -> 51/50/11/1/3/3/2/6/8/4, 0 failed
cargo clippy --all-targets     -> 1 row in my files, PRE-EXISTING
```

The clippy row is `too many arguments (8/7)` on `pub async fn step`, which exists
unchanged in `HEAD` and whose signature I added zero lines to. Attributed rather than
claimed, because I twice today reported peer warnings as mine by matching a path
suffix.

## NO-CLAIM

* **This types the distinction; it does not decide the 18 closes.** Whether the
  enforced prefix list is wider than documented or a write path bypasses the policy
  is `mcq2`'s subject and SnowyCanyon's ruling. `ClosedWithoutGrade` makes the
  population countable, not adjudicated.
* The live evidence is **one** `closed_without_grade` row, because the reconcile pass

  the classifier and the enum, not `spine.rs`'s call sites, which are that crate's
  contract and not mine.

title: close_reason/delete_reason evidence gap: 22 tombstones retired with delete_reason="delete" and no rationale
description:
WHAT: 22 terminal beads in this tracker carry NO closure rationale of any kind. All 22 are
tombstones deleted in a single 7-second `br delete` sweep (deleted_at 2026-09-01T06:13:31.779Z ..

- extraction-epic 815.x rows [live]"; 1 (dag-ready-gate-kwb) landed in e5dc05a.

WHY: the measured coverage figure that motivated this bead was `close_reason` present on 67 of
142 beads = 47%, against a 79% corpus baseline. That framing is half wrong and half worse than
it looked, and both halves matter:

  (a) NOT a discipline gap on CLOSES. Every one of the 67 `closed` beads has a close_reason:
      67/67 = 100%. Mean length 1115 chars, median 459, min 27, max 4370 -- 5.9x the corpus mean
      of 190. Our closes are RICHER than the corpus, not thinner. The 47% denominator was all
      142 beads, and the 22 tombstones (15% of the graph) can never populate `close_reason`
      because `br delete` writes `delete_reason` instead. Comparing our 47% to a corpus 79%
      without normalising for tombstone share compares two different fields.

  (b) IS a real evidence gap on DELETES. `delete_reason: "delete"` is not a rationale, it is
      the subcommand name echoed back. 22 work units -- an entire 21-crate extraction epic plus
      the DAG-ready gate that governed it -- were retired with zero recorded WHY. A future agent
      reading this tracker cannot tell whether 815.1..815.21 were superseded, duplicated,
      re-scoped into the flat 815 epic, or abandoned. The corpus's close-reason first-token
      vocabulary (SUPERSEDED 95, DUPLICATE 110, STALE 56) exists precisely to answer that.

  Compounding: `br update` REFUSES tombstone mutation ("cannot update tombstone issue"), so
  these rows are frozen. Backfilling them is not a `br update` away.

1. A decision is recorded on which of the two halves is in scope. Half (a) is a METRIC fix, not
   a data fix: any coverage figure quoted for this tracker states its denominator and either
   excludes tombstones or counts `delete_reason` alongside `close_reason`.
2. For half (b): each of the 22 ids listed in the comment on this bead either receives a real
   rationale, or the tracker records that the rationale is unrecoverable and why. Whichever

   backfilled with a plausible-sounding guess. A fabricated SUPERSEDED is worse than a blank.
4. Known-good leg: the 67 closed beads are NOT touched. Their close_reasons are already at or
   above standard and shortening them toward the 190-char corpus mean would be a regression.

NO-CLAIM: this bead does not establish that 815.1..815.21 SHOULD have been deleted, nor that the
flat 815 epic that replaced them is the right shape. It establishes only that the deletion left

title: Rounds 8-14: 340 declared findings predate per-finding identity; recorded not dispositioned (Josh ruling, not a blocker)
description:
## WHAT

Rounds **8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14** declared **340 findings** and have **zero** rows in
`docs/plan/FINDINGS.jsonl`. They are RECORDED in `docs/plan/ROUNDS.md` as rounds that happened,
with their declared counts and the honest note that they predate per-finding identity. They are
**NOT dispositioned**, and HD-0006's 15-22 scope stands.

This bead exists for whoever later wants them mined. It is **not a blocker** and must not be
treated as one.

| round | declared | dispositioned |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 9 | 0 |
| 9 | 13 | 0 |
| 10 | 77 | 0 |
| 12 | 89 | 0 |
| 13 | 80 | 0 |
| 14 | 72 | 0 |
| **total** | **340** | **0** |

Re-derive at any time:

```bash
python3 -c "
import json,collections
c=collections.Counter()
for l in open('docs/plan/CONVERGENCE.jsonl'):
    if l.strip():
        r=json.loads(l); c[r.get('round')] += r.get('new_findings') or 0
print({k:v for k,v in sorted(c.items()) if k and k < 15})"
```

## WHY IT IS A BEAD AND NOT A BLOCKER

Joshua's ruling, 2026-09-01, recorded here because the reasoning is the load-bearing part and a
future pane will otherwise re-open this as a P0:

> Those rounds predate the finding-id discipline entirely — their rows carry no `finding_ids`
> field, so there is no per-finding identity to disposition against. Reconciling them means
> MINTING 340 ids that join back to nothing, which is precisely the defect I found in the R16
> migration: *"the R16-00-001 ids were minted by the reconciling pane and do not join back."*
> Doing that 340 times would manufacture a ledger that looks complete and cites nothing.

Verified: no round below 15 carries `finding_ids`.

```bash
python3 -c "
import json
rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/plan/CONVERGENCE.jsonl') if l.strip()]
old=[r for r in rows if (r.get('round') or 99) < 15]
print('pre-15 rows:', len(old))
print('with finding_ids:', sum(1 for r in old if r.get('finding_ids')))"
```

So a "complete" ledger over these rounds would be **worse than the gap it closes**: 340 rows,
every one citing an id no grader ever assigned, indistinguishable from 340 real dispositions to
every downstream reader and gate. The gap is visible and honest; the manufactured ledger would
be invisible and false.

## ACCEPTANCE — for whoever picks this up, not for closing it now

A mining pass is complete when, for each round in 8-14, one of these is true and the choice is
stated per round:

1. **MINED** — the round's `note` field is parsed into per-finding text, each finding gets an id
   that is derived from the note content (a content hash, not a sequence number, so it joins
   back to something), and each gets FIXED / RETRACTED / DEFERRED under the `findings_ledger`
   schema. `run X, expect Y`: `jq -sc 'map(select(.round==N))|length' docs/plan/FINDINGS.jsonl`
   equals the declared count for that round.
2. **DECLARED UNMINABLE** — the round's rows carry no per-finding text to split, so the round is
   recorded in `ROUNDS.md` with a `pre_identity: true` marker and excluded from coverage in
   BOTH directions, exactly as void rounds are.

Whichever is chosen, the anti-vacuity rule holds: a round with zero mined rows and no
`pre_identity` marker is an ERROR, not a pass.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- HD-0006's 15-22 reconciliation scope. It stands.
- Round 22, which is VOID under HD-0005 and excluded from coverage in both directions — its
  dispositions must not appear as done OR as outstanding.
- Round 11, which is absent from every ledger on disk. That is a separate hole and it is not
  measured here.

## NO-CLAIM

Filing this does not make the 340 findings safe to ignore. It records that they exist, that
nothing joins them to an identity, and that minting identities would produce a false ledger.
If a real defect dies in that gap, the correct response is an example and a re-ruling — not a
mass id mint.

Recorded by `omp-orchestrator-5by` follow-on; ledger view in `docs/plan/ROUNDS.md`.

title: the supervisor can select and dispatch but cannot CLAIM: it refuses every unclaimed head forever, so the fleet stalls without a human claiming by hand
description:
WHAT: **the resident supervisor can select work and dispatch work, but it cannot CLAIM work — so it
refuses every unclaimed bead forever, and the fleet stalls the moment no human is claiming by hand.**

MEASURED 2026-09-02, three consecutive distinct beads, one tick apart each:
```
DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=omp-orchestrator-2z2                          receiver agent is missing next_action=claim-bead
DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=omp-orchestrator-content-citation-ordering-r3h  receiver agent is missing next_action=claim-bead
DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=omp-orchestrator-idle-capacity-never-alarmed-8bw receiver agent is missing next_action=claim-bead
```
`br ready` currently holds **80 beads**. Each one produces this refusal in turn. Closing or claiming
the head only advances the supervisor to the next unclaimed head — I did exactly that twice and it
failed twice more.

**THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED.** It is the repo's fourth rule: the dispatch path
refuses to send a packet naming a bead that is not `in_progress` and assigned to the receiving agent,
because *"a dispatch that cannot be projected into the tracker is not a dispatch — it is a message."*

**AND THE PENDULUM IS THE DEFECT.** K9 (`u622`, `fa59e0c`) fixed the opposite failure:
`prepare_bead_dispatch` used to run `br update --assignee <receiver> --status in_progress` **on the
receiver's behalf**, reload the snapshot, and only then call `authorize()` — *"the dispatcher forged
the precondition immediately before checking it, so the fence could never refuse anything."* 139 of
139 dispatches from that pid named bead 815 and not one was ever claimed.

**Forging was removed. Nothing replaced it.** So the loop swung from a fence that could never refuse
to a fence that can never pass. Both states stall the fleet; only the second one does it honestly.

**THIS IS THE ANSWER TO "WHY DOES THE FLEET STOP WHEN JOSHUA STOPS."** Every dispatch this session
proceeded because *I* claimed the bead first, by hand, one at a time. That is not a workflow, it is
a human standing in for a missing state transition — and the standing instruction is *"there should
be no stopping for me; this should be a continuous ongoing arc."*

ACCEPTANCE:
1. **An authorized claim step that is not a forge.** The distinction K9 established must survive: a
   dispatcher may not assert a precondition it is about to check on the receiver's behalf. Candidate
   shapes, pick one and justify it in the bead:
   - **supervisor-held claim** — the supervisor claims to ITSELF (`assignee=supervisor:<pid>`,
     `status=in_progress`), dispatches, and the receiving agent re-assigns on first contact. The
     fence then checks a real transition the supervisor is entitled to make about its own holding,
     not one it invented about someone else.
   - **claim-request handshake** — the supervisor emits a typed claim request; the receiving agent
     claims and acks; the supervisor dispatches only on the ack. Slower, and it needs the receiver
     to be live, which `receiver-receipt` can already establish.
   - **delegated claim with attribution** — the supervisor claims on the receiver's behalf but
     **records that it did so** (`claimed_by=supervisor`, `claimed_for=<agent>`), so the forge is
     visible rather than indistinguishable from a real claim. This is the weakest option and must be
     argued against the K9 finding if chosen.
2. **Fires-on-known-bad: the old forge must still be refused.** A leg that reproduces K9's shape —
   assert-then-check on the receiver's behalf with no attribution — must go RED. Without it this
   bead re-opens the hole K9 closed.
3. **Anti-vacuity: an empty ready queue must remain `QUEUE_EMPTY_NEEDS_JOSH`, not a silent pass.**
   The fix must not convert "nothing to do" into "dispatched nothing successfully". Note the ledger
   shows `QUEUE_EMPTY_NEEDS_JOSH` fired **699** times historically, **505 of them with
   `free_capacity=3`** — three idle panes while it asked for permission — so this escalation path is
   already the loop's loudest and least-read signal.
4. **A positive control:** a bead already claimed to the receiving agent must dispatch unchanged.
   A fix that refuses everything is indistinguishable from today.
5. MUTATION: disable the new claim step -> the loop returns to `DISPATCH_BLOCKED` on the head bead.
   Restore byte-identically.
6. Assert on emitted TEXT per gate rule 7, and write the claim decision into the heartbeat so a
   degraded or delegated claim is a typed row someone can find.

NON-GOALS: do not remove the fence; do not restore forging; do not special-case the current head
bead. And do not route this through `2z2`-style substrate work — this is loop-owned under the
2026-09-02 split (observe, select, **claim**, dispatch, receipts, verification, escalation).

NO-CLAIM: a claim makes work VISIBLE, not DONE — K9's own no-claim, and it still holds. This bead
lets the loop dispatch without a human; it does not make the dispatched work correct, and it does
not address the measured `209 dispatches -> 1 TRANSPORT_RECEIPT_CAPTURED` ratio, which is the
separate unacknowledged-transport problem the estimator and identity beads (`ei2i`, `nqvk`) own.
close_reason: APPROVED by AmberGate (pane 4, non-implementer grade of BlueLantern's 4893b36). All six acceptance items re-derived, not read. Item 1: supervisor-held claim via real br update --claim --actor with a real post-claim readback (main.rs:812-819); INDEPENDENT PROJECTION CONFIRMED - br show ack-spine-oj6.3 returns status=in_progress assignee=supervisor:95808 an hour after the dispatch, so the claim exists in the tracker and not only in the supervisor's self-report. Item 2 MUTATION-VERIFIED: reintroducing K9's forge literal into the scanned production slice turns dispatch_path_never_claims_on_the_receivers_behalf RED; the scan is correctly scoped so it is not self-referential. Item 5 MUTATION-VERIFIED: replacing the post-claim readback with the pre-claim snapshot turns both claim legs RED. sha 08bfd96a...39f18d3 byte-identical both sides. Items 3, 4, 6 verified by source plus live rows. title: inbox-monitor reads the CLI oracle, not the authenticated daemon; the two disagree 0 vs 20 unread
description:
## WHAT

`crates/inbox-monitor` reads its two surfaces by spawning the `am` CLI. Per the fleet's measured
finding, **the `am` CLI does not talk to the authenticated daemon at all** — it opens
`storage.sqlite3` directly, `/mcp/` returns 401 to an unauthenticated caller, and the CLI carries
no token. So the monitor currently consumes what the house pattern now calls the differential
ORACLE, not the primary authority.

Move it to the authenticated daemon, keep the CLI as the oracle, and make the disagreement
observable instead of invisible.

## WHY

The two authorities disagree RIGHT NOW, on my own mailbox, and the disagreement is not cosmetic:

| surface | unread for AmberGate |
|---|---|
| MCP `fetch_inbox` (daemon) | **0** — every row carries a `read_ts` |
| `am inbox` (CLI, storage.sqlite3) | **20** — oldest from AirTrafficControl, 2026-08-31 |

The monitor's live wiring evidence is `rc=12 MAIL WAITING — 20 unread`. That is the CLI's answer.
Under the daemon's answer the same run is `Clear`, exit 0. **Which number the monitor reports
depends entirely on which authority it asked, and today it asks the one the house pattern
designates as the oracle.**

The row shapes differ too, which is why this is not a one-line swap: the daemon's rows carry
`read_ts` (null when unread); the CLI's rows carry `priority` in {read, unread, urgent,
ack-overdue} and `ack_status` in {none, required, overdue}, with envelope keys `_meta`, `_alerts`,
`_actions`, `_diagnostics`, `count`, `inbox`. The crate already contains an adapter for the CLI
shape, written because a hard requirement on `read_ts` would have parsed nothing in production with
every test green.

This also explains a contradiction the fleet burned an hour on: `am agent start` reported "no
listener on 127.0.0.1:8765" while `curl /health` returned `status: ready` and two robot calls
returned live data. That was an AUTH FAILURE REPORTED AS ABSENCE — and the monitor's
`Unreachable` verdict (exit 13) currently inherits exactly that ambiguity, because it probes
`/health` unauthenticated and spawns a CLI that never authenticates.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. The monitor's primary read is the authenticated daemon (MCP over HTTP with the token), and the
   CLI read is retained as a SECOND arm. Then: a run where the two arms AGREE reports the shared
   answer; a run where they DISAGREE reports a distinct typed verdict naming BOTH numbers and both
   sources. Reuse the exit-code discipline already in the crate: a new code from the UNALLOCATED
   5..=63 band, registered in `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md` with a populated
   `does NOT mean` cell, or `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` goes RED.
2. Prove the disagreement leg fires on today's real data: with the daemon at 0 unread and the CLI
   at 20 for `AmberGate`, the run must emit the disagreement verdict, not pick a side. Paste the
   row. If the two have converged by then, plant the divergence in a fixture and say so.
3. `Unreachable` (13) must distinguish UNAUTHENTICATED from ABSENT. A 401 is not an absent
   listener. Assert both arms: a reachable-but-unauthorized daemon and an actually-absent one must
   not produce the same detail string.
4. `cargo test -p inbox-monitor` stays GREEN with every existing leg intact — the 13 that landed
   plus the cursor-floor legs. Report the `test result:` line.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- Fixing `am robot search` (RED on four independent readers: `column not found: m.topic`, while
  `.schema messages` shows `topic TEXT COLLATE NOCASE`, so the fault is the query builder's ALIAS).
  That is the hardening epic's first fix-at-source task.
- The daemon's silent CLAMP on an out-of-window `--after` cursor. Measured by me: asked from 1 for
  GreenFrog, served from 2108, rc=0, and NO error/code/status key anywhere in the payload — 2,107
  positions skipped behind a normal success shape. Already DEFENDED in `agent-mail-native` and
  upstreamed; the monitor's own client-side floor guard covers it.
- Changing which surface owns read state. This bead makes the disagreement LOUD; deciding which
  number is true is a separate question with a separate owner.

## NO-CLAIM

Consuming the daemon does not make the daemon right. It makes the monitor consume the designated
primary and makes a two-authority disagreement observable — which is strictly more than picking the
convenient arm silently, and strictly less than knowing whether 0 or 20 is the truth. Nothing here
establishes that; it establishes that a monitor reporting one of them without saying which authority
answered is not evidence.

title: cargo-lane-budget: ExitCode::from(selftest() as u8) truncates 256 to 0, exiting SUCCESS while printing RED
description:
WHAT: `ExitCode::from(selftest() as u8)` narrows an `i32`, so a failure count of 256 truncates to
**0** -- printing `SELFTEST RED failures=256` while exiting **SUCCESS**. Latent today, load-bearing
the moment anyone returns the count.

MEASURED AT HEAD, two reads:
  `crates/cargo-lane-budget/src/main.rs:24`   `return ExitCode::from(selftest() as u8);`
  `crates/cargo-lane-budget/src/lib.rs:886`   `pub fn selftest() -> i32 {`
An `i32 -> u8` cast in Rust is a wrapping truncation, not a saturating one. Today `selftest()`
returns 0 or 1 so nothing fires. The defect activates on the ONE change most likely to be made next
-- returning the already-computed `failures` count instead of `1`, which is the obvious improvement
because it is strictly more informative. At `failures == 256` the process exits 0 while its own
stdout says RED. At 512, 768, any multiple of 256, likewise.

WHY IT BELONGS IN THIS REPO'S CENSUS AND NOT A TODO: this is the silent-success class **in our own
code**, and it is the worst variant -- the output and the exit code DISAGREE, and every automated
consumer reads the exit code. `1p0u` catalogued 337 candidate sites across 144 files; this one is
not a candidate, it is a demonstrated mechanism with a named activation condition.

IT IS ALREADY PINNED BY A RANGE TEST. OracleGate added one while declaring the pass-through row, so
the truncation cannot be reintroduced silently once fixed. Read that test before changing the
signature -- it is the known-good leg you must keep green.

WHY IT WAS DECLARED RATHER THAN FIXED, and this is the honest constraint: `cargo-lane-budget` has
NO equivalence oracle in this repo. Its differential test spawns `bin/cargo-lane-budget.sh`, which
**can never exist here** -- the one rule forbids the extension and the exemption list is empty by
design. So a behavioural change to its exit contract cannot be proven equivalent to the shell it
replaced. A DECLARATION asserts nothing new; a FIX asserts behaviour it cannot verify. That is
`EE-P4` biting on a landed port, and it is why the fix needs a locally-verifiable acceptance rather
than a differential one.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. The cast cannot truncate. Either the return type is narrowed at the source so the value is
    representable, or the conversion saturates explicitly, or the failure count is mapped to a
    registered code -- state WHICH and why, and do not pick the option that merely moves the cast.
 2. **A KNOWN-BAD LEG THAT FIRES ON 256 SPECIFICALLY.** `failures = 256 -> exit != 0`. A test at
    `failures = 1` proves nothing here; the defect is invisible at every value below 256 and at
    every value that is not a multiple of it. Byte-identical restore, both sha256 recorded.
 3. KNOWN-GOOD leg: `failures = 0 -> exit 0`, and OracleGate's existing range test stays green.
 4. If the failure count becomes the exit code, it needs a REGISTERED entry with a populated
    `does NOT mean` cell, per the five codes allocated from the UNALLOCATED `5..=63` band. Note the
    band rule: `1`-`4` is "legacy, overloaded, do not add meanings", so a count cannot land there.
    And a count is a poor exit code in general -- 256 distinct meanings is not a contract.
 5. ASSERT THE MESSAGE, NOT JUST THE CODE (`AGENTS.md` gate rule 7): the test must read the emitted
    `SELFTEST RED failures=N` line as well as the exit status, because the whole defect is that
    those two disagree.
 6. Verify against a PINNED TREE (gate rule 8): `git status --porcelain -- crates/cargo-lane-budget`
    must be EMPTY before citing any `cargo` figure against a sha. This crate has had uncommitted
    third-party edits in it twice tonight, and a grade of exactly this crate was retracted for
    reading the worktree instead of the commit.

NON-GOALS: do not add a `bin/*.sh` oracle; do not touch `refill-idle-panes`' four `outcome.code`
pass-through sites, which are separately declared; do not renumber existing registry codes.

NO-CLAIM: fixing the cast removes a demonstrated truncation. It does NOT establish that
`cargo-lane-budget`'s exit contract is otherwise correct -- the crate has no equivalence oracle in
this repo, so its agreement with the shell it replaced is UNPROVEN and stays unproven after this
bead. And the range test pins the truncation, not the semantics.

RE-RAN: the `exit_codes` suite green at the commit; `ExitCode::from` 328 and the positive control
`process::exit` 14 both matching the report. Two mutations fire attributably with byte-identical
restores, and **M2 -- breaking ONLY the message half, leaving the exit code correct, firing exactly
one leg** -- is the proof gate rule 7 asks for: it shows the message assertion is independently

THREE OF MY READINGS DIVERGED AND ALL THREE WERE MINE OR A SIBLING'S IN-FLIGHT WORK, not this
