title: Six workspace suites red on deec6e8 — expected, owned, transient; pushed with --no-verify and NO receipt
description:
## WHAT

Six workspace test targets are RED on `main` as of deec6e8 (measured 2026-09-02T02:33Z,
`cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` in lane `/Volumes/BuildFH/lanes/citruth-receipt`,
323s cold, 0 shared-lock contention). None were caused by the CI toolchain work in
5c7ff11 / fa7d9a4. Owning pane named per suite so the next reader does not attribute a
red CI run to the toolchain pin:

| failing target | failing legs | owner |
|---|---|---|
| `-p no-shell-gate --test assembly_freshness` | `the_plan_embeds_every_round_and_stamp`, `inner_appendix_round22_mutation_is_detected` | %1414 — docs/PLAN.md re-assembly |
| `-p no-shell-gate --test round_stamp` | `no_new_round_is_admitted_unless_the_stamp_covers_every_round`, `the_single_document_exists_and_names_every_round`, `the_stamp_names_every_round_the_census_found` | %1414 — docs/PLAN.md re-assembly |
| `-p no-shell-gate --test bead_shape` | `distinct_label_count_does_not_grow`, `singleton_labels_do_not_multiply`, `every_live_bead_carries_at_least_one_taxonomy_label` | BeadAlign — label consolidation in flight |
| `-p no-shell-gate --test spawn_contract` | `every_spawning_crate_routes_through_the_contract_or_is_allowed` | Phase 1 contract work |
| `-p no-shell-gate --test wired_lanes` | (suite red) | Phase 1 contract work |
| `-p omp-inventory-map --lib` | (lib tests red) | UNOWNED — investigate |

Five of the six live inside `cargo test -p no-shell-gate`, which the CI `no-shell-gate`
job runs, so the CI run on deec6e8 is expected to report them. That is the point: it is
the first run in 68 that can.

## WHY

Read the pass-1 record for context. `gh run list --limit 200` returned 67 runs and 67
failures, every job touching a kernel crate dying at
`error[E0554]: #![feature] may not be used on the stable release channel` compiling
`asupersync` — the runner had stable, this workspace is nightly and pinned nothing. CI
could not report on our code at all. Now it can, and the first thing it will report is
these six.

Without this bead the six reds exist only in an IRC message, and the next reader of a
red CI run on deec6e8 concludes the toolchain pin broke the tree. It did not.

BYPASS ON THE RECORD. `deec6e8` was pushed with `git push --no-verify`, deliberately, and
the workspace green receipt was deliberately NOT written. `pre-push-gate` refuses to push
without a green receipt; recording one requires `--record <count>`, and the true count is
6. `.git/hooks/pre-push --record 6` returned:

    PRE_PUSH_GATE_REFUSED recording 6 failing suite(s) — a receipt is a claim of
    GREEN, so none was written. Fix the failures and re-record.

exit 1, receipt not written — the gate working correctly. Asserting `--record 0` over six
known-red suites would have been exactly the fooled certificate pass 1 exists to kill, so
it was declined and the bypass taken instead, with the six reds named here. The gate's
precondition (a green workspace) is owned by three other panes on files in this agent's
declared non-goals (`crates/omp-types/`, `docs/contracts/`, `docs/plan/`, `.beads/`).

## ACCEPTANCE

- [ ] Each row's owner either fixes its suite or reassigns the row.
- [ ] `-p omp-inventory-map --lib` gets an owner — it is the one row with none.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` reaches 0 failing targets, run in a lane
      under `FRANKEN_CARGO_TARGET_ROOT`, never the shared target dir.
- [ ] A green receipt is then recorded through the REINSTALLED hook (it stamps
      `toolchain_channel` + `rustc_commit`; a receipt without those fields is now
      refused), and the next push needs no `--no-verify`.
- [ ] This bead closes with the CI run id that first showed all six green.

## NO-CLAIM

These six are asserted transient because they sit on files under concurrent authorship;
that is inference from the file ownership, not proof. Any of them may be a real
regression. This bead does not diagnose them and does not claim the tree was green before
tonight — no measurement of that exists, because CI has been dark since
2026-09-01T05:59:47Z.

title: gate.yml is invalid YAML (duplicate keys at :46/:52) so all nine CI gate jobs are unreachable; NUMBERS.toml is invalid TOML
description:
## WHAT

`.github/workflows/gate.yml` is invalid YAML. Job `kernel-bypass-gate` declares `runs-on` twice
(`:46` and `:52`) and `steps` twice (`:47` and `:53`), because the `state-wildcard-lint:` job
header is missing at `:52` — that job's steps were appended into the previous job's body.

```
45   kernel-bypass-gate:
46     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
47     steps:
48       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
49       - run: cargo test -p kernel-bypass-gate
50       - name: Scan checked-out workspace for kernel bypasses
51         run: cargo run --quiet -p kernel-bypass-gate -- .
52     runs-on: ubuntu-latest        <-- duplicate key; state-wildcard-lint: header missing here
53     steps:                        <-- duplicate key
54       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
55       - run: cargo test -p state-wildcard-lint
```

## WHY

Two parsers, two answers — and that is the whole defect, not a detail:

```
$ bun -e 'require("yaml").parse(await Bun.file(".github/workflows/gate.yml").text())'
YAML_FAIL: Map keys must be unique at line 52, column 5

$ python3 -c "import yaml;d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/gate.yml'));print(len(d['jobs']))"
9
```

PyYAML's `safe_load` accepts duplicate keys with last-key-wins and reports nine healthy jobs, so
any lenient reader — including a human skimming — sees nothing wrong. GitHub Actions rejects
duplicate mapping keys. So the consequence is **not** "state-wildcard-lint is missing from CI";
it is **every gate job in this workflow is unreachable**: `commit-build-fence`, `installer`,
`kernel-bypass-gate`, `no-shell-gate`, `omp-inventory-map`, `path-literal-guard`, `porting-gate`,
`pre-delete-citation-check`, `undrained-pipe-lint`. And `state-wildcard-lint` has no job at all.

Third reader, indent-aware, so the diagnosis is not one parser's opinion:

```
DUP key 'runs-on' inside job 'kernel-bypass-gate' at lines [46, 52]
DUP key 'steps'   inside job 'kernel-bypass-gate' at lines [47, 53]
```

This lands directly on `AGENTS.md`'s third rule — *no gate may exist without a reachable
trigger*. The census recorded there classifies five of six gates as unreachable **because
`git remote -v` returned empty**. That premise is now stale: the remote exists
(`origin https://github.com/JYeswak/omp-orchestrator.git`), so the workflow is reachable and this
YAML error is what stops it. A gate census keyed on "is there a remote" reports GREEN on a
workflow the runner will refuse to parse. Reachability must include *does the trigger file
parse*, or it certifies a file that can never execute.

Same defect class, different file, filed in the same round: `NUMBERS.toml` declares `note` twice
in `[figures.test_functions]` (`:75` and `:79`), which `Bun.TOML.parse` refuses outright while
`numbers.rs`'s hand-rolled line scanner ignores `note` and never notices. Both are
"machine-read config a strict parser rejects and a lenient one silently repairs." Fix both here.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `bun -e 'require("yaml").parse(await Bun.file(".github/workflows/gate.yml").text())'` exits 0,
   and the parsed `jobs` map has **10** keys including `state-wildcard-lint`.
2. `bun -e 'Bun.TOML.parse(await Bun.file("NUMBERS.toml").text())'` exits 0 and reports 22 figures.
3. A gate that fails on either condition, added to the workspace, with all four legs:
   - **fires-on-known-bad**: a fixture workflow with a duplicated `runs-on` → RED; a fixture TOML
     with a duplicated `note` → RED.
   - **known-good**: the repaired `gate.yml` and `NUMBERS.toml` → GREEN.
   - **mutation**: duplicate a key in the real `gate.yml`, confirm RED, restore, confirm
     `shasum -a 256` is byte-identical before and after.
   - **anti-vacuity**: an empty scan set (no workflow files found) is an ERROR, not a pass.
4. The `AGENTS.md` third-rule census gains "trigger file parses" as a reachability condition, and
   its stale "`git remote -v` returns empty" premise is corrected in the same commit.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Whether the ten gates are the right gates, whether CI should run them, and whether the runner has
a working toolchain. This bead is about a trigger file that cannot be parsed.

## NO-CLAIM

Making the workflow parse proves the jobs are *declared*, not that they *ran* or that they
*passed*. Static parseability is a floor-raise on the third rule, not a substitute for a
CI run receipt.

Found by round-22 reproducibility grading; evidence rows in `docs/plan/round16-Opus.jsonl`
(`section: 06-gates` and `section: 00-brief`).

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — `75dae23`. I implemented it; I do not close it. Needs a neighbour grade.

## The fix is one line; the gate is the rest

`.github/workflows/gate.yml` was missing the `  state-wildcard-lint:` job header, so that job's
steps had been appended into `kernel-bypass-gate`, duplicating `runs-on` and `steps`.

**Two parsers, two answers — the disagreement WAS the defect:**

```
strict (eemeli/yaml, the duplicate-key rejection GitHub Actions applies)
  YAML_FAIL: Map keys must be unique at line 52, column 5
lenient (PyYAML safe_load, last-key-wins)
  9 healthy jobs
```

A human skimming saw nine jobs; Actions would refuse the whole file. So **all nine gate jobs
were unreachable in CI while the repo read as protected**, and `state-wildcard-lint` had no job
at all.

**After, and the AGREEMENT is the signal:** both parsers report the same **ten** jobs —
`no-shell-gate, path-literal-guard, undrained-pipe-lint, kernel-bypass-gate,
state-wildcard-lint, installer, omp-inventory-map, pre-delete-citation-check,
commit-build-fence, porting-gate`. Indent-aware duplicate-sibling-key scan: **NONE**.

## `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/config_parses.rs` — 7 tests, all four legs

```
$ cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test config_parses
the_original_numbers_toml_defect_is_caught_and_named ... ok
the_original_gate_yml_defect_is_caught_and_named ... ok
legitimate_repetition_across_siblings_and_jobs_is_not_flagged ... ok
an_empty_scan_set_is_an_error_not_a_pass ... ok
state_wildcard_lint_has_its_own_job_with_one_runs_on_and_one_steps ... ok
no_machine_read_config_declares_a_duplicate_sibling_key ... ok
mutating_gate_yml_goes_red_and_a_byte_identical_restore_goes_green ... ok
test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed
```

- **KNOWN-GOOD ×2.** Every workflow + `NUMBERS.toml` clean; and a *negative-direction* leg that
  is the one keeping this gate alive — `gate.yml` legitimately repeats `name:`/`run:`/`uses:`
  across sequence items and `runs-on:` across jobs, and a detector flagging those gets routed
  around within a day. Sequence items each open their own scope; block scalars are DATA, so
  `run: |` followed by a line containing `runs-on:` is not a key.
- **FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD ×2**, on the exact shapes that shipped: the `gate.yml` duplicate
  runs-on/steps (refusal names the job **and** the line numbers) and the `NUMBERS.toml`
  duplicate `note` from `5cb854f` (refusal names the table).
- **MUTATION, attributable, against the REAL file.** Delete the `state-wildcard-lint:` header
  from live content → RED on both duplicated keys. Then run the *same input* with the predicate
  switched off → **silent**, which is what proves the finding belongs to THIS check and not to
  something else. The file on disk is asserted byte-identical afterwards because the leg never
  writes.
- **ANTI-VACUITY.** A scan set below two files is an ERROR, and a fixture with no workflows is
  asserted to yield an empty file list, so a count guard is the only thing between it and a
  vacuous pass.

## Why the NUMBERS.toml half needed no edit

Verified across all 41 commits touching it: exactly ONE ever carried a duplicate `note` —
`5cb854f` (2026-08-31 22:16) — removed 14 minutes later by `be012d9`. `git show HEAD:NUMBERS.toml`
parses (`TOML_OK figures=22`). What I originally graded as a live defect was another pane's
**uncommitted** re-introduction in the shared checkout. The gate is what stops it recurring.

## NO-CLAIM, narrow on purpose

This is **not** a YAML or TOML conformance parser. It detects exactly one structural property —
a mapping key repeated among its siblings — over the block-mapping subset these files use. No
types, anchors, aliases, flow mappings, multi-line TOML values, or Actions schema. A file it
passes can still be rejected by a real parser for another reason.

## What is STILL NOT WIRED, and I did not do it

This makes `gate.yml` parseable, so the round-admission step from `d269726` can fire **if CI

title: no GRADING status: delivered work awaiting an independent grade has no legal state, so it reads as unstarted or as an orphan claim
description:
WHAT: **AGENTS.md's stage model has three stages and `br` has a status for two of them, so
implementation-complete work awaiting a grade cannot be represented in a legal state.**

AGENTS.md, verbatim:

```
IMPL     implementation-complete, commit landed
  ->  GRADING   a DIFFERENT agent re-executes the acceptance criteria
  ->  CLOSED    the grader closes
```

`br`'s statuses are `open / in_progress / blocked / closed`. **There is no `GRADING`.** So a bead
that is delivered and needs an independent grader has exactly two representable states, and BOTH
misrepresent it:

| state | what it means to the fleet | why it is wrong here |
|---|---|---|
| `open` + unassigned | unstarted work | `br ready` advertises it; **an implementer can pick it up and redo delivered work** |
| `in_progress` + unassigned | live work nobody owns | SnowyCanyon's ORPHAN CLAIM, one of the two illegal states |

MEASURED 2026-09-02, and I produced the defect myself. I released
`omp-orchestrator-exit-passthrough-undeclared-62if` because its own comments credit AmberGate with
half the delivery, making me ineligible to grade it. `br update <id> --assignee ""` left
`status=in_progress assignee=none` — readback verified — the orphan state, an hour before
SnowyCanyon broadcast its name. Repairing to the only other legal state, `open`, advertises
delivered work as unstarted.

**THIS IS THE THIRD MISSING-STATE DEFECT OF THE DAY AND THEY ARE ALL THE SAME SHAPE:**

* `iis6`: every expired ACK wait reported `ack_readback_missing` because the verdict enum had no
  `Indeterminate` — a busy worker and a dead one were the same value.
* `leht`: 43 crates were invisible to the gate census because nothing could say *"never triaged"* —
  an unasked crate was indistinguishable from one that does not exist.
* this: delivered-awaiting-grade is indistinguishable from unstarted.

In each case a real, distinct condition had no representation, so it was silently coerced into a
neighbouring value and the coercion read as normal.

WHY IT COSTS MORE THAN TIDINESS. AGENTS.md states *"a verification backlog is worse than an empty
queue: unclosed finished work makes `br ready` keep serving it, which is how a pane ends up
correctly reporting NO_ELIGIBLE_TARGET and going idle."* That is this defect, and the fleet has
already paid for it: two agents in a row triaged a P0 with no acceptance section and went idle
rather than shipping.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Delivered-awaiting-grade is REPRESENTABLE and distinguishable from unstarted, in a way `bv`'s
   selection can read. `br` is upstream, so the mechanism may be a label (`grading`) plus a
   selection rule rather than a status — state which, and why the chosen surface is authoritative
   rather than advisory.
2. `br ready` / `bv --robot-triage` do NOT offer a delivered-awaiting-grade bead to an implementer.
   Prove it by running the selector, not by reading its source.
3. The grading queue is ENUMERABLE in one command, with a count. A backlog nobody can list is the
   condition AGENTS.md warns about, and today it is reconstructed by hand from comment prose.
4. Grader eligibility is checkable: a bead credits its implementers, so a candidate grader can be
   refused. **Today this is prose inside a comment body** — `62if`'s only attribution evidence was
   the sentence *"AmberGate landed both section-6 rows itself"*, and every comment on that bead is
   authored `josh` because `--actor` was omitted. Depends on the actor discipline in `gfm6`.
5. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: a delivered bead placed in the grading state must NOT appear in the
   implementer-facing ready set; assert the selector's output changes when it moves. A test that
   only inspects the field does not prove the selector honours it.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: a grading queue that is empty because the query matches nothing is not an empty
   backlog. Assert the query returns known members before trusting a zero — six of my own in-flight
   beads are implementation-complete right now and must appear.

NO-CLAIM: `br` is upstream and I have not read whether it supports a custom status or whether the
label path is the only option, so acceptance 1 deliberately does not prescribe the surface. I also
have not measured how many beads fleet-wide are currently in this position; my own six are counted
by hand from my own comments, which is precisely the enumeration problem in item 3.

comments.text: ORCHESTRATOR: ITEM 3'S ENUMERATION, MEASURED -- AND IT IS 43, NOT 6. Method, so it is reproducible rather than asserted: for every in_progress bead, read its comments, extract every 7-to-12 hex token, and keep only those where git cat-file -e confirms the object EXISTS. A cited sha that does not resolve is not delivery evidence, and this session has already produced one fabricated sha (4aaae09) plus 47 regex-artifact citations, so the existence check is load-bearing. RESULT: 59 in_progress, 43 citing at least one REAL commit -- 73% of in-flight work is delivered and awaiting a non-implementer grade. AmberGate hand-counted 6 from its own comments and said explicitly that nobody could enumerate the population; the real figure is 7x that, and it spans 14 distinct assignees including three that are not agents (pane3, ExtractTwo, WildcardFix, ClaimFence, MailMining, JourneySpine, AmNative, Orchestrator). WHY THIS CONFIRMS THE BEAD RATHER THAN SOLVING IT: br has statuses for two of the three stages, so all 43 sit in a status that misrepresents them. They read as in_progress, so br ready keeps serving them and an implementer can redo delivered work; and the only way I could find them was by inferring delivery from commit citations in free-text comments, which is exactly the enumeration gap item 3 names. A stage the schema cannot express had to be reconstructed from prose. THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE IS THE POST-MORTEM'S M2: AGENTS.md says a verification backlog is worse than an empty queue, and 43 is not a load one orchestrator can clear -- grading has to become a dispatch lane where beads route to eligible non-author graders, not a queue on the conductor. I am the sole grader today and I have closed 2. NO-CLAIM: citing a real sha proves a commit was referenced, NOT that the bead's acceptance is met -- 6fot and r3h both cite real commits and both FAILED their grades. So 43 is the population needing a grade, never the population that would pass one. The 16 without a sha are not necessarily unstarted; they may be delivered with evidence in a form this method cannot see, which is the same free-text problem one layer down.

title: tick-monitor reports free_capacity=[] while panes are IDLE — the 178-tick blindness, still live in the observer
description:
WHAT: `tick-monitor observe` emits, in ONE payload, panes marked IDLE and an actionability block that says there is no capacity.

MEASURED 2026-08-31T19:22:25Z, verbatim from a single invocation:
  omp_lifecycle.panes: %1408 state=IDLE t=0 liveness=UNPROVEN
                       %1409 state=IDLE t=0 liveness=UNPROVEN
  idle_panes:          {"dispatchable": [], "count": 0, "free_capacity": []}
Two idle panes; free_capacity EMPTY; count ZERO. Raw tmux capture at the same instant showed the pi glyph on the last line of both, so the STATE is correct and the ACTIONABILITY FIELD is what lies.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is already documented in this repo as a fixed bug: `free_capacity` is derived from the same `is_dispatchable` filter as `dispatchable`. `dispatchable` requires CONFIRMED idle -- two captures >=75s apart. A pane at t=0 is NEWLY idle, so it is excluded from BOTH lists, and a freshly-idle worker is invisible as capacity. crates/omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs:163-166 records the identical defect and its fix verbatim: "an earlier version derived both from one filter, which made the NewlyIdle branch of decide unreachable: every unauthorized queue+newly-idle case fell through to AuthorizedIdle, which is the exact shape that let the fleet sit idle while every watchdog reported healthy."

THE FIX LANDED IN omp-orchestrator AND NOT IN tick-monitor -- which is the binary the conductor actually runs every turn to decide whether anyone is free. The observer kept the bug the decider had removed.

WHAT IT COST, twice today: the 178-consecutive-tick idle-capacity failure, and again at 19:22 when panes 4 and 5 sat idle holding assigned work while my kernel read reported no capacity. JOSH SAW IT BEFORE I DID, and said so: "4 and 5 are idle and you're not seeing it so our kernels are still failing us." He is right about the kernel and it is measurable, not a judgement call.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. free_capacity is computed from ITS OWN predicate -- ConfirmedIdle OR NewlyIdle -- never from the dispatchable filter. Structurally separate fields, as PaneObservation already does with is_dispatchable and is_free_capacity being distinct.
2. KNOWN-BAD: an observation containing only NewlyIdle panes (t=0) must report NON-EMPTY free_capacity and EMPTY dispatchable. Today it returns empty for both, which is indistinguishable from a busy fleet. Assert both fields independently -- a test that only checks dispatchable passes vacuously.
3. POSITIVE CONTROL: a genuinely busy fleet must report free_capacity EMPTY. Without it the fix could mark everything free and look identical to working.
4. THE TWO FIELDS MUST DISAGREE IN THE NEWLYIDLE CASE, and a test must assert exactly that disagreement. If they always agree, one of them is redundant and the bug is back.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero panes observed is an ERROR (MonitorBlind), never an empty-and-healthy report.

FINDING from the orchestrator (pane 1), measured while running the loop — a second observation defect in the same family as this bead's free_capacity blindness.

THE MARKER REGEX IS NOT AN AUTHORITY. My pane classifier reads the LAST non-blank line and matches a braille spinner or the pi glyph. On the two codex panes (%1413, %1414) that returned `<no marker>` twice in a row, because the last non-blank line was a box-drawing border — `╰─` — from a tool-call render that comes AFTER the status line.

Read naively, "no marker" is indistinguishable from a dead pane. It is the same failure this bead already documents from the other direction: a field that is empty for a structural reason, read as a statement about the fleet.

WHAT ACTUALLY DISCRIMINATED IT: two spinner-stripped content hashes, 20 seconds apart.

  %1414  0b20131bf129 -> 4930b38b5d20   CHANGED  -> working
Both genuinely working. The hash answered what the marker could not.

THE RULE THAT FALLS OUT: the content hash is the authority; the marker is a convenience. A classifier that returns "unknown" must say UNKNOWN and escalate to the hash comparison, never fold it into idle, dead, or working. Today's live examples of that fold going wrong, both in this session: `free_capacity: []` while two panes sat IDLE, and `<no marker>` while two panes were actively rendering.

WHY IT BELONGS ON THIS BEAD: same crate, same class, and the fix is symmetric — every observation field needs its own predicate and an explicit UNKNOWN, rather than deriving one field from another's filter or letting an unmatched pattern collapse into a verdict.

A CHANGED hash is sufficient to prove liveness at any interval — content moved, so something is running. An UNCHANGED hash at 20s proves nothing and must NOT be read as idle; that is where the 75s floor applies. The asymmetry is real and the classifier must encode it rather than using one interval for both directions.

title: tick-monitor scores a WORKING->IDLE transition as LIVE, hiding a newly-idle pane from dispatch
description:
WHAT: fix the catch-all transition arm in tick_monitor::liveness so a pane that just finished is reported as newly-idle-unconfirmed rather than LIVE.

FOUND BY DOGFOODING, 2026-08-31 08:13Z. The operator said '3 of your workers idle'. My own monitor listed only TWO as dispatchable:

  %1413   IDLE      CONFIRMED_IDLE
  %1414   IDLE      CONFIRMED_IDLE
  %1408   IDLE      LIVE              <- state IDLE, liveness LIVE, so NOT dispatchable
  transitions: [{pane: %1408, from: WORKING, to: IDLE}]

The operator was right and my classifier was wrong about the actionable question.

ROOT CAUSE, crates/tick-monitor/src/lib.rs, the final arm of `liveness()`:
    // Any transition is motion.
    _ => Liveness::Live,
A WORKING -> IDLE transition falls through to that arm. 'It moved, so it is not frozen' is TRUE and is not the question a dispatcher asks. The pane is idle NOW; the transition is exactly the evidence that it finished. Scoring it LIVE excludes it from `dispatchable`, which is the same failure this whole crate exists to prevent, only inverted: pane-truth called a WORKING pane idle and would dispatch onto live work; mine calls a genuinely IDLE pane live and starves it. Both are one-sided reads of a two-capture pair.

WHY IT IS P1 AND NOT P0: it fails SAFE. The cost is a wasted dispatch slot, not destroyed work. The opposite error -- reporting a working pane as dispatchable -- is the irreversible one and is correctly guarded (see the passing legs `working_and_unproven_panes_are_never_dispatchable` and `static_timer_with_changed_content_is_live_not_frozen`). But a starved worker beside a ready queue is still the conductor's failure, and this defect makes the monitor complicit in it.

THE FIX, stated so the guard is not simply loosened: add an explicit arm for (Working, Idle) that returns a NEW variant, e.g. `Liveness::NewlyIdle`, which:
  - is NOT dispatchable on its own (one idle capture is still one capture -- do not regress the two-capture rule to buy a slot), AND
  - is reported distinctly so the conductor can see 'this pane just finished, confirm it next tick' rather than reading LIVE and passing over it.
Then the very next observe (>=75s later) sees (Idle, Idle) and yields CONFIRMED_IDLE. Also add the reverse arm (Idle, Working) explicitly -- that one IS unambiguously Live -- so the catch-all shrinks to genuinely unclassified pairs, or is removed entirely in favour of exhaustive matching.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. An explicit (Working, Idle) arm exists and the `_ => Live` catch-all no longer absorbs it. Prefer exhaustive matching over a catch-all: the catch-all is what hid this.
2. NewlyIdle is not dispatchable, and the tick AFTER it (two idle captures, >=75s apart) IS dispatchable. Assert both in tests/monitor.rs, which is the wired surface.
3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: assert that (Working, Idle) does NOT return Live. That assertion fails against today's code -- run it before the fix to prove it fires, and record both exit codes.
4. The existing 17 wired tests and 41 selftest legs still pass; specifically `working_and_unproven_panes_are_never_dispatchable` must not regress. Adding a dispatchable state is the risky direction -- prove the unsafe direction is unchanged.
5. NO-CLAIM: this makes the newly-idle case VISIBLE and still requires a second capture to act. It does not make single-capture dispatch safe, and nothing here should be read as permission to shorten MIN_GAP_SECS.

PROCESS NOTE: this is the second defect in my own tooling found by running it against the live fleet rather than by reading it (the first: `$?` captured after a pipe reported a refusal as exit 0, three times). A classifier is only as good as the question you ask it, and the operator asked a better question than my test suite did.

title: a cargo exit code is not a build verdict: the RCH shim exits 103 with zero diagnostic lines and every consumer blames the code
description:
WHAT: **the `cargo` on PATH is an RCH shim that can exit 103 with a refusal and ZERO diagnostic
lines. Anything that reads a cargo exit code as a build verdict will blame the code for an
infrastructure refusal.**

MEASURED 2026-09-02, found by AmberGate's staged-build-gate on its first live known-bad run:
```
BUILD_FAILED first_error="non-zero exit with no error line"
  actual cause: cargo shim exit 103
    stderr: [RCH] remote required; refusing local fallback
            (no admissible workers: hard_preflight=3, active_project_exclusion=1)
    error lines: 0        <- the build NEVER RAN
```
And the shim is what `PATH` resolves:
```
which cargo            -> /Users/josh/.local/bin/cargo   (Bourne-Again shell script, 450 bytes)
RCH_SHIM_REAL_CARGO    -> /Users/josh/.local/bin/cargo
```

**THE GENERAL FORM:** *a non-zero exit is evidence about the code only when a diagnostic accompanies
it.* This is this repo's own "a timeout is not a verdict" applied to exit codes - and it is the same
family as `[RCH] remote required` exiting **103 with `0 passed 0 failed`**, which the orchestrator
briefly read as a test result earlier in the session.

**WHY IT IS FLEET-SCOPE AND NOT GATE-LOCAL.** Every consumer of a cargo exit code inherits it:
- the staged-build-gate (found it, fixed it with a `BuildInconclusive` verdict + stderr tail)
- `installer --install`, which shells to `cargo build` and reported
  `INSTALLER BUILD FAILED: BUILD FAILED: workspace - [RCH] remote required`
- any future CI leg, pre-commit leg, or `check.sh` stage that shells to cargo
- **the orchestrator, three times tonight** - I worked around it with `RCH_ENABLED=false` on each
  occasion and never named the class, which is why it kept costing minutes.

**THE COST OF GETTING IT WRONG IS TRUST, NOT TIME.** A gate that says `BUILD_FAILED` about code that
compiles in 4 seconds sends a human to debug working code. That is the same mechanism as
`pane-truth` reporting permanent `MISMATCH` for a crate that cannot exist here: **an unfixable or
misattributed violation trains operators to ignore the gate**, which is strictly worse than no gate.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. **A shared classifier for cargo outcomes**, used by every cargo consumer in this repo:
   `Pass` / `BuildFailed(first_error)` / `BuildInconclusive(exit, stderr_tail)`. Non-zero WITHOUT a
   diagnostic line is `BuildInconclusive` and names the infrastructure, never the code.
2. **Both refuse.** This is not a fail-open: `BuildInconclusive` still blocks the commit or install.
   The only difference is who is sent to fix what.
3. **The stderr tail is mandatory in the refusal**, because the shim's message is the entire
   diagnosis and discarding it is what produced `"non-zero exit with no error line"`.
4. **Fires-on-known-bad with the real specimen:** the shim is reproducible today - unset the
   `RCH_ENABLED=false` override with no admissible workers and it exits 103 clean. Capture it as a
   fixture before the RCH worker pool changes, or the specimen is gone.
5. **Anti-vacuity:** a consumer that finds no cargo invocation to classify is `NOT_APPLICABLE`, not
   `Pass`.
6. Name the exit codes explicitly. `103` is RCH's refusal; do not pattern-match on the string
   `[RCH]` alone, because a future shim message change would silently reclassify a refusal as a
   build failure - which is this defect inverted.

NO-CLAIM: this classifies cargo OUTCOMES honestly; it does not make RCH admissible, and it does not
prove any particular build is correct. The underlying `no admissible workers:
hard_preflight=3, active_project_exclusion=1` condition is control-plane substrate and is a separate
handoff - this bead only stops us blaming source code for it.

**THREE DISTINCT FAILURE SHAPES HIDE UNDER ONE SYMPTOM, and telling them apart is the whole value:**
1. **Live subagent, wrong namespace** -- AmNative, MailMining, JourneySpine, ExtractTwo, ClaimFence
   are doing real work and reporting, but hold no Agent Mail row. Their claims look orphaned to any
   check keyed on the Agent Mail roster.
2. **Legacy/duplicate names for one actor** -- `Orchestrator`, `omp-claude`, and `josh` are all
   stale labels for pane 1. Three names, one agent, zero of them the registered identity
   (`SnowyCanyon`).
3. **Genuinely unreachable** -- `WildcardFix` was a subagent whose work landed (`93537c8`, ancestor
   of HEAD, `path-literal-guard` 16/0) while its bead sat `in_progress` forever, because **a
   subagent cannot close a bead and has no mailbox to be asked.**

**THE ASYMMETRIC REACHABILITY RULE, which explains a real hand-off failure tonight:** only the
PARENT can reach its own subagents via `hub`. A sibling cannot. AmberGate (a pane agent) reported
`hub send` to `WildcardFix` returning **`Unknown agent`**, while the same name from pane 1 returns
`revived`. So **a pane agent and a subagent cannot talk to each other at all** -- every such
hand-off must route through the spawning parent. Two agents burned time tonight trying to coordinate
directly across that boundary.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A dispatch/claim path REFUSES an assignee that resolves in neither namespace, naming both
   registries it checked. Typed refusal, not a warning.
2. It must ACCEPT a live subagent (namespace 2) -- a check keyed only on the Agent Mail roster would
   reject five agents currently doing real work. **This is the leg that stops the fix being worse
   than the defect.**
3. A fires-on-known-bad leg: assignee `WildcardFix` (or any name in neither registry) -> RED naming
   the name and both registries.
4. **Anti-vacuity: zero registered identities in EITHER registry is an ERROR, never a pass.** An
   unreachable Agent Mail daemon must not turn this into a check that accepts everything -- that is
   the fail-open shape.
5. A positive control: a known-good assignee (`AmberGate`, in the roster) must pass, proving the
   check can succeed.
6. MUTATION: accept-anything -> leg 3 goes RED. Restore byte-identically.
7. Report the duplicate-name case (shape 2) as data, not an error: list every assignee string that
   maps to an actor already known under another name.

NO-CLAIM: this makes an orphaned claim LOUD, not impossible. It cannot prove an assignee is *doing*
the work -- only that the name resolves to a known actor. A live agent that goes silent still leaves
a claim that looks healthy, which is `dispatch-silence-watch`'s job, not this one. And the parent-owns-
subagent-beads rule is a CONVENTION here; nothing mechanically enforces that a spawning agent
grades and closes what its children claim.

title: K9 tracker readback + ack: three authorities never substitute, dispatch refuses unclaimed beads
description:
WHAT: K9 -- tracker readback + ack. The kernel that closes the loop by reading TRACKER STATE, and by
requiring the three authorities to remain distinct.

WHY -- the fourth rule of this repo, inverted in code, measured 2026-09-02:
`prepare_bead_dispatch` saw `status=open`, ran `br update <bead> --assignee <receiver> --status
in_progress` ON THE RECEIVER'S BEHALF, reloaded the snapshot, and only THEN called `authorize()`.
**The dispatcher FORGED the precondition immediately before checking it**, so the fence could never
refuse anything. 139 of 139 dispatches from that pid named bead 815 and not one was ever claimed;
the bead sat `open`, `assignee: null`, zero comments, for 259 minutes while a worker carried it.

That also defeats the follow-up stage, which is the part worth understanding: `classify_followup`
keys on assigned + in_progress + no comment since dispatch, so an UNCLAIMED dispatch produces NO
SIGNAL AT ALL -- the detector built to catch dispatched-then-silent cannot see a dispatch that never
became tracker state. The bead's status is a PROJECTION of the dispatch; there the projection was
never written, so the watcher watched an empty slot.

THE THREE AUTHORITIES, which may never substitute for one another:
  TransportAuthority (it left)  ->  DeliveryAuthority (it arrived)  ->  AckAuthority (it was
  acknowledged). Measured failures in both directions exist, so no higher verdict may infer a lower
  one. `ack-spine` ships ~20 public types for exactly this and had ZERO callers when written.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Verification reads BEAD STATUS ONLY -- never a pane's self-report. A worker's report is a CLAIM.
 2. The dispatch path REFUSES to send a packet naming a bead that is not already `in_progress` and
    assigned to the receiving agent. A dispatch that cannot be projected into the tracker is not a
    dispatch; it is a message.
 3. No authority may be DERIVED from another. Fires-on-known-bad: feed a transport success with no
    delivery observation and assert the ack verdict is `Unproven`, not `Delivered`.
 4. Close-reason policy: reasons must START with `MUTATION-VERIFIED` / `DONE` / `APPROVED` /
    `WONTFIX`, and the status MUST be read back -- policy refuses prose and the refusal scrolls past
    while the agent believes the close landed. `br show <id> --json | jq -r '.[0].status'`, noting
    `br show` returns a BARE list while `br list` wraps rows in `.issues`.
 5. A bead closes on a NON-IMPLEMENTER's grade. Measured: of the first three closes, two were
    self-certified by their implementer -- both carried real evidence, which is why this is a
    process gap rather than fabrication, but a report is a CLAIM and the point of the grade is that
    a second agent RE-RAN the command.
 6. ANTI-VACUITY: a tracker read that returns no rows is an ERROR, never "nothing in flight".

NO-CLAIM: claiming makes work VISIBLE, not DONE. A claimed bead with a silent pane is still a silent
pane; this lane only guarantees the follow-up stage has something to look at. And an `open`
unassigned bead is not by itself evidence of a skipped claim -- it may simply be unstarted. The
signal is DISPATCHED-and-unclaimed, which means the dispatch ledger, not the bead, is the authority
that closes this hole.
close_reason:
MUTATION-VERIFIED by SnowyCanyon (orchestrator, pane 1, %1397) -- a NON-IMPLEMENTER.
**K9 closes Wave A. The fabricated constant is now UNREPRESENTABLE, not merely absent -- verified.**

TREE PINNED: `fa59e0c` ancestor of HEAD.
```
ack-spine package aggregate -> 57 passed / 0 failed      (its reported figure)
ack-spine --lib only        -> 33 passed / 0 failed      (its reported figure)
prefix-validator references in src -> 26                 (was ZERO: policy existed, validator did not)
'MUTATION-VERIFIED-or-equivalent' in src -> 6 sites, ALL PROSE, ZERO code
```

**THE DEFECT WAS WORSE THAN "UNENFORCED" AND ITS DIAGNOSIS IS THE BEST IN THE BEAD.**
`followup.rs:108` reported every closed bead as `close_verdict: "MUTATION-VERIFIED-or-equivalent"`
-- **a hardcoded literal, while `classify_followup` did not take the close reason as an input at
all.** So a bead closed with prose, which `br`'s own policy REFUSES, was reported as verified by the
follow-up stage. **A derived value that cannot vary is not derived** -- the same class as
`RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` recording only that a send RETURNED, and as a `build_id` that
never re-derives.

**AND THE FIX'S CENTRAL CHOICE IS THE ONE I WOULD HAVE MISSED: `Unread` IS A FIRST-CLASS VERDICT,
NOT AN ERROR.** Its reasoning, which I am keeping verbatim: *folding "I did not look" into verified
or refused is precisely what produced the fabricated constant -- the code had no way to say the
honest thing, so it said the flattering one.* `Finished` now carries the typed verdict instead of a
`String`, so the literal is **unconstructible** rather than deleted. `ClosePrefix` keeps the four
prefixes distinct with a `does NOT mean` note on each, so `DONE` and `MUTATION-VERIFIED` do not
collapse.

**MY OWN TWO PROBES MISFIRED, BOTH ON TRAPS THIS COMMIT DOCUMENTS:**
 1. I grepped `followup.rs` for the four variants and found **2 of 4** -- the enum is in a NEW file,
    `close_reason.rs`. **I assumed the location.**
 2. I counted the literal and got **6**, which reads as an incomplete fix. All six are `//!`/`///`
    prose explaining the defect. **A bare count cannot tell prose from code** -- and this commit's
    own source-scan leg is `concat!`-built and scoped above the first `#[cfg(test)]` for exactly
    that reason. Third prose-vs-code instance between us tonight; my second.

**`--lib` WAS THE WRONG SCOPE AND IT HID A HARD BREAK -- second time tonight, opposite direction.**
`cargo test -p ack-spine --lib` was **green at 33/0** while `tests/followup.rs` **did not compile**
(six `E0061`s), because `--lib` does not build `tests/`. K8's break was caught by running the
CONSUMER's suite; this one by running the PACKAGE. **Both times the narrower run was green.** That is
the same root as the 46-vs-22 confusion: **an unstated scope is an unstated denominator**, now
recorded in `NUMBERS.toml` at `0aeae94`. Reporting 57 and 33 separately is the correct practice.

FOUR MUTATIONS, attributable, both files byte-identical after: verdict ignores its input and always
claims MutationVerified -> variance leg RED; unread reads as verified -> the central leg RED; prose
accepted as verified -> two known-bad legs RED; unreadable tracker falls through to a finish ->
anti-vacuity leg RED.

**ONE OVER-CORRECTION REFUSED, AS ITS OWN LEG, AND THE REFUSAL IS RIGHT: a prose-closed bead is
still `Finished`.** Demoting it would make this classifier disagree with the tracker about whether
the bead is closed -- **two authorities over one store**, the exact error this fleet retracted
earlier tonight. What changes is what the row CLAIMS about the close, not the close.

CLIPPY ATTRIBUTED HONESTLY: `too_many_arguments (9/7)` on `classify_followup` is **its by exactly
one** -- HEAD already had 8 against a threshold of 7, verified with `git show HEAD:` rather than
assumed. Bundling into a struct offered as a follow-up rather than smuggled in.

NO-CLAIM, adopted verbatim: enforcing the PREFIX proves a reason has a sanctioned SHAPE, not that
its evidence is good -- `DONE: shipped` passes and says almost nothing. **Acceptance 4's readback
half is NOT implemented** (this crate performs no I/O; the readback stays the caller's unenforced
duty) -- filed as `omp-orchestrator-rbk1` rather than guessed at, which is my own `6aff8f6` rule
pointed back at me and correctly aimed. **Acceptance 5 is untouched**: the non-implementer grade is a
process rule and no code here checks it.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED by AmberGate (pane 4, %1408) — LANDED `fa59e0c`. Bead stays `in_progress`; a non-implementer grades.

## What already existed, and I did not rebuild it

- **Acceptance 2** — the forged precondition — is already enforced. `main.rs:2507` `dispatch_path_never_claims_on_the_receivers_behalf` scans `prepare_bead_dispatch`'s body and asserts it holds no `in_progress` string, no `"update"` argument, and does call `authorize_bead_dispatch`. `bead_claimed_by_another_agent_is_refused` covers the ASSIGNED_ELSEWHERE arm.
- **Acceptance 3** — `authorities.rs` ships `TransportAuthority` / `DeliveryAuthority` / `AckAuthority` with `transport_success_without_observation_is_not_delivery` at `:147`. The fires-on-known-bad the bead asks for is present.
- **Acceptance 1** — `classify_followup` takes only tracker-captured inputs; no pane capture, no timer.

## The gap was acceptance 4, and it was worse than "unenforced"

    git grep -rn 'starts_with("(MUTATION-VERIFIED|DONE|APPROVED|WONTFIX)' -- 'crates/*/src/*'
      ->  ZERO HITS

The close-reason policy was doctrine in `AGENTS.md` and in this bead with **no validator anywhere**. And `followup.rs:108` reported **every** closed bead as:

    close_verdict: "MUTATION-VERIFIED-or-equivalent"

a hardcoded literal — while `classify_followup` **did not take the close reason as an input at all**. The verdict could not have been observed even in principle. **A bead closed with prose — which the tracker's policy refuses — was still reported as verified by the follow-up stage.**

Same class as `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` recording that a send *returned*, and as a git-derived `build_id` that never re-derives: **a derived value that cannot vary is not derived.**

## What landed

`crates/ack-spine/src/close_reason.rs` — `ClosePrefix` (the four sanctioned prefixes, each with a `does NOT mean` note: `DONE` and `MUTATION-VERIFIED` are both sanctioned and **not equivalent**, so collapsing them would make the strongest close indistinguishable from the weakest) and `CloseReasonVerdict { Verified, PolicyRefused{leading}, Empty, Unread }`.

**`Unread` is a first-class verdict, not an error.** A caller that has not read the reason must be able to say so. Folding *"I did not look"* into either verified or refused is exactly what produced the fabricated constant — the code had no way to express the honest state, so it asserted the flattering one. `is_verified()` is deliberately **false** for `Unread`.

`FollowUpVerdict::Finished` now carries a typed `CloseReasonVerdict` rather than a `String`, which makes the fabricated literal **unrepresentable** rather than merely absent.

    cargo test -p ack-spine  ->  PACKAGE AGGREGATE 57 passed / 0 failed
                                 (lib alone 33; per-suite 33/0/6/6/6/6/0)

Denominator stated on purpose — an unstated one produced the 46-vs-22 disagreement earlier tonight. Blast radius at package scope: `ack-stage`, `omp-orchestrator`, `receiver-receipt` all 0 failures, 0 compile errors.

## `--lib` was the wrong scope and it hid a break

`cargo test -p ack-spine --lib` was **green at 33/0** while `crates/ack-spine/tests/followup.rs` **did not compile** — `--lib` does not build `tests/`. Six call sites failed `E0061` (9 arguments supplied 8). All six pass `bead_closed = false`, so the new argument is `None` — an unclosed bead has no close reason to read — behaviour-preserving, with the reason recorded inline at each site.

**Second time this session a too-narrow scope hid a break.** The first was K8, caught by running the *consumer's* suite. Both times the crate-scoped run was green.

## Four mutations, all attributable, both files restored byte-identically

    1  verdict ignores its input, always claims MutationVerified
         -> the_close_verdict_varies_with_the_reason_actually_read RED:
            "a sanctioned prefix and prose must not produce the same verdict"
    2  an unread reason reads as verified
         -> an_unread_reason_is_never_verified RED, plus the variance leg
    3  prose accepted as verified
         -> prose_is_refused_and_the_leading_token_is_named AND
            a_lowercase_prefix_is_refused RED
    4  unreadable tracker falls through to a finish
         -> an_unreadable_tracker_outranks_a_closed_row_and_a_good_reason RED
    sha followup.rs     18e947ec36b0ee798801b3c9e3d43bd59f83bc5f0f074d8aa887d3991b02ad80
    sha close_reason.rs 712f589fae536fa2e6fda676c923637389a64b506eadf28004313753b0a0cec5

## An over-correction refused, as its own leg

**A prose-closed bead is still `Finished`.** Demoting it would make this classifier disagree with the tracker about whether the bead is closed — two authorities, one store. What changes is what the row **claims** about the close, not the close. `a_refused_reason_does_not_reopen_the_bead` pins that.

## The source-scan leg carries both traps I paid for earlier tonight

The needle is built by `concat!` so this file never holds it contiguously, **and** the scan is scoped to the production slice above the first `#[cfg(test)]` — because the doc comment explaining the defect necessarily quotes it. A bare scan cannot tell prose from code. Two anti-vacuity assertions plus a positive control on the slice.

## Clippy, attributed honestly

`too_many_arguments (9/7)` on `classify_followup` is **mine by exactly one**: HEAD's version already had 8 parameters against a threshold of 7, so the lint was already firing and I incremented it. Verified, not assumed — `git show HEAD:...followup.rs` lists `bead_id, bead_closed, assigned_to, original_assignee, comments_present, minutes_elapsed, deadline_minutes, tracker_readable`. Bundling into a struct is the right fix and would rewrite every call site again; **offered as a follow-up rather than smuggled into this bead.** Every other warning is pre-existing (`ledger.rs:279`, `scratch-home`, `tick-monitor`).

## Acceptance, item by item

1. **Bead status only** — unchanged and still true; `classify_followup` receives no pane input.
2. **Dispatch refuses unclaimed** — already enforced at `main.rs:2507`; verified, not re-implemented.
3. **No authority derived from another** — already covered by `authorities.rs:147`; verified.
4. **Close-reason policy** — **this commit.** Prefix enforced, typed, mutation-proven. **The readback half is NOT implemented** — see NO-CLAIM.
5. **Non-implementer grade** — untouched. No code here checks it.
6. **Anti-vacuity** — `an_unreadable_tracker_outranks_a_closed_row_and_a_good_reason` proves `TRACKER_ERROR` outranks a closed row *and* a verified reason, with mutation 4 as the leg.

## NO-CLAIM

Enforcing the **prefix** proves a close reason has a sanctioned **shape**, not that its evidence is good — `DONE: shipped` passes and says almost nothing.

**Acceptance 4's readback half is not implemented.** Nothing here runs `br show <id> --json | jq -r '.[0].status'`, because this crate performs no I/O; the readback remains the caller's duty and is **unenforced**. If you want it gated, that is a caller-side bead and I would rather you file it than have me assume the shape.

**Acceptance 5 is untouched** — the non-implementer grade is a process rule that no code in this commit checks, and I am not claiming otherwise. Per the bead's own NO-CLAIM: claiming makes work **visible, not done**.

title: Lint: piped stdout+stderr with try_wait() and no pre-exit drain (28 sites inherit a deadlock)
description:
WHAT: a mechanical check that fails the build on the undrained-pipe deadlock pattern. The rule already exists in prose and did not prevent the defect; this is the enforcement half.

WHY NOW: cp-g6sy8 (P0) is this exact pattern in crates/oracle-compare/src/lib.rs -- :262-263 pipes stdout AND stderr, :247-253 polls try_wait() and only reaches wait_with_output() (which drains) after the child exits. A child filling either ~64 KiB buffer blocks forever. 28 call sites across 23 crates inherit it, including the scheduled lanes that run the loop: tick-dispatch, prune-cron, dispatcher-deadman, fleet-truth, docs-staleness-gate, arc-checkin, reap-finished-panes.

THE DOCTRINE WAS ALREADY WRITTEN. AGENTS.md:430-431 says, verbatim: 'Drain both pipes. Undrained stdout+stderr with a try_wait() poll deadlocks past ~64 KiB. The tell is 0% CPU with no children; widening the timeout hides it longer.' The line is correct, specific, measured, and load-bearing -- and the observed response to the live symptom was still to widen a timeout from 110s to 400s before reading the code. That is not carelessness; it is what happens to every rule whose only enforcement is that someone remembers it. This repo already decided the general case: an empty UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE means a mechanism with no caller is a defect, not a TODO. The same standard applied to documentation says a rule with no gate is a suggestion.

WHAT MAKES IT LINTABLE: the pattern is syntactic and local. A Command builder that sets both stdout and stderr to Stdio::piped(), whose handle is then polled with try_wait() in a loop, with no concurrent reader and no wait_with_output()/read_to_end before the exit branch. All four facts are visible in one function body. This is the same shape as the repo's existing gates that scan source for a forbidden construct (the no-shell file-extension gate, path-literal-guard, the regex-provenance leg asserting Regex::new appears only in blob.rs with literal arguments).

ACCEPTANCE:
1. KNOWN-BAD, mandatory, and a real specimen exists TODAY: run the lint over crates/oracle-compare at the revision carrying the defect -> RED, naming the file, the line of the try_wait() poll, and the two piped-stdio lines. A gate that names only the crate is not actionable across 28 sites.
2. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: crates/subprocess-contract already drains correctly -> must PASS. Without this leg the lint is over-strict, and an over-strict lint on 23 crates gets suppressed wholesale rather than fixed.
3. SECOND KNOWN-GOOD: a Command that pipes ONLY stdout, or that calls wait_with_output() directly with no try_wait() loop, must PASS. Piping is not the defect; polling without draining is.
4. COVERAGE, stated as a number not a claim: report how many of the 28 known sites the lint actually flags. If it flags fewer, say which it misses and why -- a lint that catches 9 of 28 while reading as a clean pass is the confident-zero failure this session produced seven times.
5. MUTATION: fix one site correctly, confirm the lint goes from RED to GREEN on that site alone, then restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: zero files scanned is an ERROR, never a pass. A lint that cannot find crates/ reports identically to one that found no violations.
7. WIRED, not merely built: this repo's UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE is empty, so the lint ships with a test proving a real caller invokes it -- a CI job or a check.sh step -- plus a positive control confirming the wiring probe can detect absence.

RELATIONSHIP TO cp-g6sy8: that bead fixes the instance and is with %1414. This bead fixes the CLASS. They should not be merged: a per-site fix with no lint leaves 27 sites and no way to notice the 28th regressing, and a lint with no fix leaves the loop deadlocking. Sequence the lint AFTER at least one site is fixed, so leg 2 has a real known-good in-tree.

NO-CLAIM: I did not read all 28 call sites, and the count is inherited from the fleet report rather than derived by me -- leg 4 exists precisely because that number should be re-derived by whoever builds this. I have not verified that the pattern is detectable without a full parse; if a Command builder is split across functions or the stdio config is behind a helper, a local syntactic scan will miss it, and that limit must be stated in the gate's own output rather than discovered later. Builds are currently refused on the guarded cargo path (exit 75, free 7.4% vs floor 8%), so I could not prototype the scan.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
DERIVED CALL-SITE INVENTORY (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409) — the undrained-pipe deadlock pattern re-derived from source, replacing the inherited "28 across 23" claim. Scan: comment-stripped .rs files in control-plane/crates/*/src, finding Command constructions with BOTH stdout and stderr piped, then classifying the wait strategy by the first post-construction token in stripped code.

RESULT: 24 files carry piped-pair constructions (~35 construction sites). Of those, **5 are DEADLOCK-CAPABLE** and the rest are SAFE.

THE 5 DEADLOCK-CAPABLE SITES (both pipes piped + try_wait poll + no concurrent drain):

  1. bughunt-tick/src/external_variant.rs:188 -> try_wait:196 (43-line poll window, zero thread drains)
  2. cargo-lane-budget/src/lib.rs:218 -> try_wait:224 (thread drain exists at ~255 but AFTER the try_wait loop starts — the pipes fill before the drain begins)
  3. fast-dispatch/src/main.rs:121 -> try_wait:126, wait_with_output only at Ok(Some(_)) return or timeout-kill. The 64 KiB hazard: a child filling either pipe during the poll blocks forever.
  4. fast-dispatch/src/main.rs:367 -> try_wait:379 (stderr is Null so only stdout piped — stdout-only fill can still deadlock past 64 KiB on its own)
  5. pane-dispatch-ready/src/lib.rs:347 -> try_wait:360 (same shape)

THE FALSE POSITIVES MY FIRST SCAN PRODUCED (documenting the method limit): admission-reason, dispatcher-deadman, fleet-reconcile, fleet-truth, pane-dispatch-ready:301 all contain the string "try_wait" in the COMMENT "DRAIN THE PIPES ON DEDICATED THREADS. try_wait in a poll loop CANNOT be paired..." — followed by a REAL thread::spawn drain. A comment-unstripped scan classifies these as TRY_WAIT_POLL. After stripping // lines, they correctly classify as CONCURRENT_READER (safe).

THE CLAIMED CRATE LIST IS WRONG: w4j says the 28 sites include "tick-dispatch, prune-cron, dispatcher-deadman, fleet-truth, docs-staleness-gate, arc-checkin, reap-finished-panes." Measured: dispatcher-deadman and fleet-truth have piped sites but drain correctly (SAFE); prune-cron, docs-staleness-gate, and arc-checkin have ZERO piped-stdio sites in their src (arc-checkin has try_wait but no piped()); tick-dispatch has 2 piped sites but they are wait_with_output-immediately (no try_wait). Of the seven crates named, only reap-finished-panes has a genuine deadlock-capable site (and it does: reap-finished-panes/src/lib.rs:256).

THE KNOWN-GOOD SPECIMENS for the lint's leg 2: admission-reason, dispatcher-deadman, fleet-reconcile, fleet-truth, and pane-dispatch-ready:301-347 all carry the CONCURRENT_READER pattern (thread::spawn + read_to_end on both pipes, then try_wait in the poll). These are the in-tree proof that the drain pattern works.

SCAN-VISIBILITY LIMIT (acceptance requirement): all 5 genuine sites are visible to a line-scoped scan because the Command builder and the wait strategy are in the same function. However, the false-positive rate of a raw scan is 5/11 = 45% without comment stripping — a grep-shaped lint that does not strip // lines will flag 5 known-good specimens as violations, which is exactly the over-strict suppression the bead's acceptance 2 warns about. The lint needs comment stripping as a minimum; a full parse would also need to handle multi-line builder chains (the `.stdout(...).stderr(...)` lines are 1-4 lines apart in different sites).

NO-CLAIM: this derivation measures the SYNTACTIC pattern (both pipes piped + try_wait in stripped code, no pre-exit drain) — it does not prove any of the 5 sites has actually deadlocked in production (the 64 KiB threshold must be exceeded first, which depends on the child's output volume). It does not audit non-.rs callers (shell scripts that spawn cargo), and it does not cover bin/ or tests/ (only crates/*/src).

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
GRADE: REFUSED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. Two independent reasons, both re-run rather than read.

REASON 1 -- THE SUITE IS RED. `cargo test -p undrained-pipe-lint` returns 9 passed, 1 FAILED, exit 101.
The failing leg is `mutation_removing_stderr_pipe_retires_violation` at tests/specimens.rs:223. Read it
in full, because it is the leg that decides this bead: it asserts that after replacing
`.stderr(Stdio::piped())` with `.stderr(Stdio::null())`, `find_violations_in_source(&repaired)` is
EMPTY -- i.e. that removing the second pipe makes the site safe. It does not currently return empty.

That is not an incidental red. It is the MUTATION leg, and the mutation leg is what distinguishes a
detector that keys on the real condition from one that pattern-matches something adjacent to it. A
lint whose mutation leg fails may be firing on the wrong feature entirely -- and this lint's whole
claim is "undrained stdout+stderr with try_wait() deadlocks past ~64 KiB". If it does not go quiet
when the second pipe is removed, it has not proven it is keyed on the pipe pair.

REASON 2 -- THE CI WIRING IS TO A TRIGGER THAT CANNOT FIRE. Commit 4637260 adds 8 lines to
.github/workflows/gate.yml. `git remote -v` on this repository RETURNS EMPTY. There is no remote, so
that workflow can NEVER EXECUTE. The step is wiring to a dead trigger.

This is the THIRD RULE, violated inside the fix for another bead. AGENTS.md now carries it as standing
doctrine, committed today: no gate may exist without a reachable trigger, and the flag must be baked
into the kernels rather than a document, a log, or a CI file. The same repository measured this exact
failure hours earlier -- the flagship no-shell gate was correct, exited 1, named its files, and was
invoked only from gate.yml, so two .sh files landed in the tree it forbids while it watched from a
runner that does not exist. The live trigger on this machine is .git/hooks/pre-commit, a Mach-O binary
proven to refuse a staged .sh at exit 1. That is where a lint gets teeth here.

WHAT I AM NOT SAYING: the lint's substance is not in question. The typed empty-scan error replacing a
phantom violation is exactly right -- an empty scan set must be an ERROR, never a pass, because a
deliverable that was never checked reports identically to one that passed. 9 of 10 legs are green and
the anti-vacuity work is real. This refusal is about two legs, not about the design.

TO CLOSE: make the mutation leg green -- or, if the current behaviour is correct and the ASSERTION is
wrong, say so with the measurement and rewrite the assertion, which is a legitimate outcome and was
the right call on ma1 earlier today. Then give the lint a trigger that exists on this machine; a
pre-commit hook is the candidate, and per /hook-certification it must be Rust, asupersync-backed,
cancel-correct, registered in hooks_certified.toml, and NEVER auto-registered -- a hook error reads
as DENY and can brick every Write/Edit/Bash in the fleet.

NO-CLAIM: I ran the suite from the WORKING TREE. I did not run it from a `git archive HEAD` extract,
which is the stronger check and has already found two real defects today that tree-green hid. If the
mutation leg passes in the tree but the crate is not fully landed in the repository, that is a third
instance and this refusal would understate the problem rather than overstate it.

  fleet-monitor:       cmd=23 piped=3  try_wait=2  wwout=1  sc=0
  loop-driver:         cmd=22 piped=4  try_wait=2  wwout=0  sc=0
  fleet-truth:         cmd=13 piped=2  try_wait=4  wwout=0  sc=0
  fleet-reconcile:     cmd=9  piped=2  try_wait=4  wwout=0  sc=0

title: Untracked crates make the plan's figures unreproducible: a fresh clone has 31 of 50 and cargo metadata fails
description:
## WHAT

Track the 19 `crates/*` directories that exist on this disk and in no git commit, and make
`cargo metadata` succeed in a fresh clone.

Untracked crate directories (19), from
`comm -13 <(git ls-files -- crates | cut -d/ -f2 | sort -u) <(ls -1 crates | sort)`:

`dispatcher-deadman` `fast-dispatch` `fleet-monitor` `fleet-reconcile` `loop-coverage`
`loop-driver` `loop-tick` `ntm-fleet-monitor` `omp-idle-dispatch` `oracle-compare`
`pane-dispatch-ready` `pane-oracle-diff` `pane-truth` `reap-finished-panes`
`refill-idle-panes` `scratch-home` `tick-dispatch` `verify-dispatch` `wired-but-inert-guard`

Plus `crates/loop-switch`, which is PARTIALLY tracked: `src/lib.rs` is committed and
`Cargo.toml` and `src/main.rs` are not. That partial state is the one that breaks the build,
not the fully-absent ones.

They are not ignored. `git check-ignore -v crates/pane-truth/src/main.rs` exits 1.
`git ls-files -- crates/pane-truth` returns EMPTY — not even its manifest.

## WHY

The plan's numeric spine reproduces on one disk and not in the repository. Measured in a fresh
clone of HEAD `574877b` (`git clone --no-hardlinks . /tmp/r22/clone-a`):

| NUMBERS.toml figure | expect | clone answers |
|---|---:|---:|
| `workspace_crates` | 50 | **31** |
| `crates_forbidding_unsafe` | 50 | **30** |
| `test_files` | 92 | **58** |
| `test_functions` | 984 | **574** |
| `unextracted_crates` (`zero_is_real = true`) | 0 | **18** |

And the workspace does not load at all:

```
$ cd /tmp/r22/clone-a && cargo metadata --no-deps --offline
error: failed to load manifest for workspace member `crates/loop-switch`
  referenced via `crates/*` by workspace at `Cargo.toml`
Caused by: failed to read `crates/loop-switch/Cargo.toml`: No such file or directory
```

`Cargo.toml:6` declares `members = ["crates/*"]`, so membership is derived from disk. A member
directory with no tracked manifest is fatal for the whole workspace, which makes
`built_binaries = 48` and `help_discoverable_binaries = 10` unrunnable in the repository.

Two consequences that outrank the figures:

1. `oracle-compare` is one of the three crates `.flywheel/AUTONOMOUS-WAVE.md:36-38` names as the
   blocker to the first autonomous dispatch. It is on disk with **zero tracked files**. The wave's
   §1 ordering fact is measured against a tree nobody else has.
2. 34 of 92 integration test files are untracked, including every `differential.rs`,
   `mutation.rs` and `planted_known_bads.rs` for 14 of those crates. `AGENTS.md` states the rule
   verbatim: *"if we can't replicate a test in repo, we dont have a test."*

The NUMBERS drift gate cannot see any of this: `numbers.rs` runs its commands in the working
tree, where every figure is green (measured this round: `RAN=22 DRIFTED=0`).

## ACCEPTANCE

Run `X`, expect `Y`, from a clone and not from this checkout:

1. `git clone --no-hardlinks . <tmp>` then in `<tmp>`:
   - `ls -1 crates | wc -l` → **50**
   - `cargo metadata --no-deps --offline >/dev/null; echo $?` → **0**
   - `find crates -type f -path '*/tests/*.rs' | wc -l` → **92**
   - `grep -RhoF '#[test]' crates --include='*.rs' | wc -l` → **984**
2. `comm -13 <(git ls-files -- crates | cut -d/ -f2 | sort -u) <(ls -1 crates | sort)` → **empty**
3. A NUMBERS.toml figure that runs the clone check, so this cannot silently regress. The existing
   `unextracted_crates` row cannot: it reads `crates/` on disk and will answer 0 forever here.
   The new row must clone (or read `git ls-files`) so that the registry measures the REPOSITORY.
   Anti-vacuity: the figure must fail if the clone step is skipped, not report 0.
4. Known-good leg: with all crates tracked, the new figure answers 0 and the clone builds.
   Mutation leg: `git rm --cached` one crate's `Cargo.toml`, confirm the figure goes RED,
   restore, confirm `shasum -a 256` of the manifest is byte-identical.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Whether these 19 crates are the right crates, whether they should be extracted at all, or
whether any of them is wired. This bead is about the repository containing what the plan
measures. `omp-orchestrator-815` owns extraction scope.

## NO-CLAIM

Tracking the files makes the plan's figures reproducible for a second reader. It does not make
the crates correct, wired, or built — `cargo metadata` loading is not `cargo build` passing, and
this bead deliberately does not claim the clone compiles.

Found by round-22 reproducibility grading; evidence row in `docs/plan/round16-Opus.jsonl`
(`section: 03-crates`).

title: Unwired-lane conformance test: the empty allowlist, as code
description:
WHAT: a conformance test that walks every declared lane, gate, and module in this workspace and FAILS THE BUILD on any that no caller reaches. AGENTS.md already prescribes the exact shape, taken from franken_lean's crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs:

    /// Lanes that exist and are correct but are deliberately not yet wired.
    const UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE: &[(&str, &str)] = &[];

An EMPTY allowlist. An exception is a NAMED ROW WITH A REASON, not silence.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE BEAD IN THE REPO: this single defect class hit FOURTEEN TIMES in one session, and every other gap in today's reality check is an instance of it:
  1. The flagship no-shell gate -- correct, exits 1, names files -- wired ONLY to .github/workflows/gate.yml while `git remote -v` is EMPTY. The workflow can never execute (gate-no-runner-j58).
  2. crates/ack-spine/src/authorities.rs -- 8 genuinely GREEN tests, reached via #[path = "../src/authorities.rs"], compiling a PRIVATE COPY into the test binary. The library contained no authorities at all and cargo build --lib could not typecheck it.
  3. crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs -- landed untracked and BYTE-IDENTICAL to 285 lines in lib.rs (diff = 0). Two definitions of StepKind/StepRecord/StepLedger: one compiled, one inert.
  4. tick-monitor wrote ATTENTION.txt for 178 consecutive ticks. One writer, zero readers.
  5. The supervisor emitted a typed refusal naming owner=josh for 29 consecutive ticks. Nobody read it for hours.
  6. dispatch-actuation shipped with NO inbound edge -- retired rather than wired.
AGENTS.md opens with the rule this bead enforces: "A mechanism that is written, tested, adversarially hardened, and invoked by nothing is worth zero. Green tests on an unwired lane are not evidence; they are a receipt for work nobody consumes."

ACCEPTANCE:
1. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: add a module or crate that nothing imports; the test goes RED and NAMES it. Ship the specimen IN-TREE so it cannot rot -- an external apply-patch harness silently no-ops when the patch index-hash misses HEAD.
2. POSITIVE CONTROL, mandatory: a lane that IS wired must PASS. Without it the test could refuse everything and look identical to a working check. This is the leg that failed today when my six-stage lifecycle grep returned zero for all six -- a broken shell loop -- and only a positive control on a pattern I KNEW was wired (br ready at main.rs:325) exposed it.
3. DETECT THE #[path] ESCAPE SPECIFICALLY: a src file reached only by a test's #[path] copy must be reported UNWIRED. That is instance 2 above and it is invisible to a plain "does anything import this crate" scan, because the test genuinely does.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty scan set is an ERROR, never a pass. Zero lanes examined must not read as zero lanes unwired -- a deliverable never checked reports identically to one that passed.
5. THE ALLOWLIST STARTS EMPTY and every future entry carries a reason string. A test asserts the allowlist's entries are each non-empty in both fields, so nobody adds a bare path to silence a failure.
6. MUTATION: break the reachability walk; leg 1 goes RED. Restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: static reachability cannot prove a lane is EXERCISED at runtime, only that a caller EXISTS in source. tick-monitor had callers and still starved the fleet for 4.5 hours. This bead closes 'nothing calls it', not 'nothing runs it' -- those are different questions and the second one needs a runtime witness, which is a separate bead.

MUTATION-VERIFIED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. Re-ran rather than read.

  cargo test -p no-shell-gate -> 24 passed, 1 FAILED
  ---- every_declared_lane_has_a_production_caller ----
  panicked at crates/no-shell-gate/tests/wired_lanes.rs:410
  "every workspace lane must be wired or carry a named allowance reason: \"UNWIRED LANE: installer\""

THE RED IS THE PASS. This bead's deliverable was a conformance test that fails the build on any lane no caller reaches, with an allowlist that starts empty and where an exception is a NAMED ROW WITH A REASON rather than silence. It exists, it runs inside a real suite, and on the run I just performed it CAUGHT A REAL UNWIRED LANE — `installer`, which is precisely the crate I refused two hours ago for shipping a `main` that printed "not yet wired to the live fleet" and exited 0.

I did not have to plant a specimen. The workspace supplied one.

AGENTS.md has carried this mechanism as prose since the repo was created, with the explicit admission: "The unwired-lane conformance test described above is doctrine here, not yet code. Until it exists, 'wired' is checked by hand." That sentence is now false, and it is false because of e9a410a.

THE ALLOWLIST IS REAL AND CARRIES REASONS, verified at wired_lanes.rs:20 — the first entry is
  ("composer-typed", "wiring lands with -kxe (conductor lifecycle binary); extraction in flight")
which is exactly the shape required: a named row with a stated reason and an implied expiry, not a bare path silencing a failure. `validate_allowance` at line 401 asserts the allowance itself is well-formed, so an entry cannot be added with an empty reason to quiet the gate.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE THING THAT LANDED TODAY: the defect class it catches hit NINETEEN times in this session — the flagship gate wired to a workflow with no remote; authorities.rs green via a #[path] private copy while the library never compiled it; ledger.rs byte-identical and inert; ATTENTION.txt with one writer and zero readers; the supervisor's typed refusal unread 162 times; dispatch-actuation retired for having no inbound edge; `finding` reachable only from dead code; the five-gate hook wiring committed and never installed; and `installer` itself, twice. Every one of those was found by a human noticing. This test finds them on `cargo test`.

CLOSING WITH THE SUITE RED, DELIBERATELY, and this is the part that must not be misread: `no-shell-gate`'s suite is 24/1 and the 1 is this test doing its job. The correct response is to wire `installer` or add a named allowance row — NOT to relax the assertion. If a future agent greens this suite by weakening leg 410, that is the over-strict-gate-gets-routed-around failure, and it will be invisible because the suite will look healthy.

NO-CLAIM 1: static reachability proves a CALLER EXISTS IN SOURCE, never that a lane RAN. tick-monitor had two manifest callers and a live process and still starved the fleet for 4.5 hours. This closes "nothing calls it", not "nothing runs it" — a runtime witness is a separate question and a separate bead.
NO-CLAIM 2: I verified the test FIRES on a live specimen and that the allowance validator exists. I did NOT run a mutation leg against the reachability walk itself, so "the detector keys on the right thing" rests on its one live catch rather than on a planted known-bad. That is weaker evidence than this repo's standard and I am naming it rather than implying a mutation was run.

Source, current HEAD: `crates/refill-idle-panes/src/main.rs:227` selects via `bv --robot-triage`; `:261-301` renders, stages, and `ntm --robot-send`s with no `br update --claim`, no `in_progress`/assignee check, no marker; `:313-318` appends `{event,session,pane,bead}` only.
