title: 5 supervisor-dispatched beads closed DONE while the ledger's last word is DISPATCH_FAILED/AWAIT_HUMAN: no close-to-dispatch reconciliation
description:
WHAT: **Five beads the resident supervisor dispatched today were closed DONE while the supervisor's own ledger's last word on each dispatch is `DISPATCH_FAILED / ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE / action=AWAIT_HUMAN`, with 5–8 `DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED` rows apiece. Nothing reconciles a close against the dispatch record that produced it, so the loop believes it delivered nothing and the tracker believes everything shipped.** Pass 2 found one instance (ipg.4); the class is five.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 (Pass3Credit), `~/.local/state/flywheel/omp-orchestrator.heartbeat.jsonl` rows with `ts_unix >= 1788307200`, filtered by `detail | test("bead=omp-orchestrator-<id>(\\s|$)")`:

| bead | DISPATCH_CLAIMED | DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED | SUPERVISOR_REFUSED | RETRY_BLOCKED rows | bead ACK comment | closed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| commit-msg-backtick-injection-232 | 17:56:26Z pane %1413 GreenFrog | 17:56:31Z status=DISPATCH_FAILED detail=ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE | 17:56:34Z AWAIT_HUMAN unproven_transport | 8 | (none parsed) | 18:18:31Z DONE by implementer |
| kxe.5 | 19:30:32Z %1414 BlueLantern | 19:30:38Z DISPATCH_FAILED | 19:30:42Z AWAIT_HUMAN | 5 | josh 19:30:51Z "ACK kxe.5 on %1414 -- starting…" | 20:24:10Z DONE by implementer |
| omp-coverage-mission-ipg.4 | 21:37:24Z %1413 GreenFrog | 21:37:30Z DISPATCH_FAILED | 21:37:44Z AWAIT_HUMAN (+MAIL_TIMED_OUT) | 8 | (none parsed) | 22:04:13Z DONE by implementer |
| omp-coverage-mission-ipg.18 | 21:42:16Z %1414 BlueLantern | 21:42:21Z DISPATCH_FAILED | 21:42:25Z AWAIT_HUMAN | 7 | BlueLantern 21:42:29Z "ACK ipg.18 on %1414 -- starting…" | 22:03:41Z MUTATION-VERIFIED by implementer |
| phase0-claim-strength-j5r | 22:07:06Z %1414 BlueLantern | 22:07:11Z DISPATCH_FAILED | 22:07:14Z AWAIT_HUMAN | 8 | BlueLantern 22:07:21Z "ACK j5r on %1414 -- starting…" | 22:11:08Z DONE by implementer |

Every one of the five also has a `DISPATCH_RESULT_MAIL_REFUSED … Agent 'WildStone' not found` row (yfp2). Today's ledger totals for scale: `jq -r 'select(.ts_unix>=1788307200)|.status' | sort | uniq -c` → SUPERVISOR_REFUSED 695, DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED 149, DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED 59, DISPATCH_CLAIMED 25, TRANSPORT_RECEIPT_CAPTURED 16 — and 40 closes.

The mechanism is known (elq6: the `$TMUX_PANE` fix dropped the ` -- ` separator so `ACK j5r on %1414 -- starting…` no longer parses; 93lo: supervisor packets carry no ACK instruction) — this bead is about the CREDIT consequence: the close is never bound to a dispatch receipt. A close can land on a bead whose dispatch the loop recorded as failed, and the loop's `AWAIT_HUMAN` stays open forever beside a `closed` row. Conversely a bead the loop DID deliver could be closed by anyone with no packet ever sent (mi1o: no dispatch row, no comment, WONTFIX 19:54:53Z).

WHY: HONEST-CREDIT SM-6 (status evasion: "claimed work without a recent commit/comment is reconciled every tick") and SM-4 (a green must map to the exact item). The supervisor's spine (a3ab48d StepRecords, 3cce353 ClosedWithoutGrade) now TYPES the close half; it does not join it to the dispatch half, so the ledger cannot answer "was this close preceded by a delivered dispatch and a recorded ACK?".

ACCEPTANCE:
1. The supervisor emits a `CLOSE_RECONCILED bead=<id> dispatch=<claim ts> ack=<comment id|NONE> result=<DISPATCH_RESULT status>` row on every close it observes; a close whose last dispatch result is `DISPATCH_FAILED` and whose ACK is `NONE` emits `CLOSE_UNRECONCILED` and the bead gets a comment naming the ledger row.
2. Fires-on-known-bad: replay today's ledger + `.beads/issues.jsonl` through the reconciler → exactly the five rows above (and mi1o as `CLOSE_WITHOUT_DISPATCH`) are named; leht/kwo9/kxe.6 are NOT (known-good leg).
3. `AWAIT_HUMAN` verdicts on a bead that later closes are retired by the reconciler with a `SUPERSEDED_BY_CLOSE` row, so `SUPERVISOR_REFUSED` stops counting closed work as pending human decisions (nsx1's 188-refusal denominator shrinks by exactly these).

FALSIFIER: after the fix, a bead closed on 2026-09-03+ whose most recent DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED row is DISPATCH_FAILED and which has no CLOSE_RECONCILED/CLOSE_UNRECONCILED row within one tick of `closed_at`.

RELATED (cited, not duplicated): elq6 (ACK parse drift — the cause), 93lo (no ACK protocol in supervisor packets), yfp2 (WildStone identity → every result mail refused), eg0m (spine), nsx1 (S9 has no writer), 8zx1, ve4w, the Pass 2 handoff on ipg.4.

title: CLAIM_REQUIRED prints one remedy for a two-branch decision; for a released bead it is the wrong one
description:
WHAT: **the `CLAIM_REQUIRED` refusal prints ONE repair command, and for a RELEASED bead it prints
the wrong one — following it assigns work to an agent who is not doing it.**

MEASURED 2026-09-02, live:

    DISPATCH_RESULT tick=6 pane=%1408 bead=omp-orchestrator-dispatch-exists-unverified-u1c
    status=DISPATCH_FAILED detail=DISPATCH_BLOCKED reason=CLAIM_REQUIRED
    status=open assignee=BlueLantern receiver_agent=AmberGate claim_owner=BlueLantern
    next_action=claim-bead
    command="br update omp-orchestrator-...-u1c --assignee BlueLantern --status in_progress"

The refusal is **correct to refuse**. Its suggested command is wrong for this case: `u1c` had been
deliberately RELEASED by the orchestrator after a dispatch collision, and BlueLantern was not
working it. Running the printed command would have completed a claim for an agent who had no packet
— manufacturing a phantom in-flight bead that no pane is carrying, which is the `5rh` failure
(dispatch without claim) inverted into claim-without-dispatch.

## THE ILLEGAL STATE, AND WHY BOTH DIRECTIONS PRODUCE IT

`open` + assigned refuses every dispatch to every pane. `br update --help` documents `--assignee`
as an **atomic claim** ("assignee=actor + `status=in_progress`"), so the claim direction is safe.
**The release direction is not:** `br update <id> --status open` on a claimed bead clears the status
half and leaves the assignee, landing exactly in the illegal state. There is **no `--unassign`
flag**; the working idiom is the undiscoverable `br update <id> --assignee ""`, which reports
`assignee: X → (none)`.

**Measured self-indictment:** the orchestrator fixed five instances of this state earlier the same
session, then created two more within hours — `u1c` (a dispatch-collision release) and
`omp-coverage-mission-ipg` (an epic-container revert) — both by using `--status open` and believing
the bead was released. A state whose exit requires an undocumented empty-string argument will be
re-entered by anyone who releases a bead.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. The refusal names BOTH remedies and the fact that they are mutually exclusive: complete the
     claim (the bead IS being worked) or release it fully (it is NOT). A refusal offering one
     branch of a two-branch decision is a suggestion that is wrong half the time.
  2. The release remedy is printed literally, including the empty-string form, because it cannot be
     discovered from `br update --help` — the help text documents only the claim direction.
  3. The refusal distinguishes the two situations by evidence where it can: an assignee with a
     dispatch-ledger row is a claim to complete; an assignee with no dispatch row is a release to
     finish. Where the evidence is absent, say so rather than guessing a branch.
  4. Fires-on-known-bad: a fixture in the `open`+assigned state with no dispatch row must produce
     the RELEASE remedy, and one with a dispatch row must produce the CLAIM remedy. A refusal that
     emits the same text for both is unrepaired.
  5. Anti-vacuity: a bead in a legal state must produce no remedy at all — a refusal path that
     always suggests something is indistinguishable from one that never fires.

NO-CLAIM: this makes the refusal *actionable*, not the state *unreachable*. Only `br` itself can
refuse the illegal transition at write time, and it is upstream — so the state stays constructible
by any agent that releases a bead with `--status`. This bead improves the message and does not
close the hole. Nor does it establish that the supervisor's refusal logic is wrong: it refuses
correctly and always has; the defect is entirely in the single remedy it names.

comments.author: josh
comments.text: ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION -- THIS BEAD'S BODY CONTAINS A FALSE STATEMENT I INTRODUCED, AND THE MEASUREMENT INVERTS IT. The body says: 'br update --help documents --assignee as an atomic claim (assignee=actor + status=in_progress), so the claim direction is safe. The release direction is not.' BOTH HALVES ARE WRONG. Measured 2026-09-02 on br 0.4.1: 'br update omp-orchestrator-iis6 --assignee AmberGate' produced readback 'open / AmberGate' -- the illegal half-claimed state, from the CLAIM direction, in one command. I then needed a separate --status in_progress to complete it. HOW I GOT IT WRONG: I ran 'br update --help | grep -iE assignee|unassign | head -3' and it returned '--assignee <ASSIGNEE>' followed by 'Atomic claim (assignee=actor + status=in_progress)'. Those two lines belong to DIFFERENT FLAGS. The atomic-claim text is the description of --claim, and it matched my filter only because the description itself contains the word 'assignee'. A keyword grep over --help DESTROYS the flag-to-description association, and the line I was searching for contained my search term. --assignee's real description is 'Assign to user (empty string clears)'. THE CORRECTED FACTS: (1) the atomic verb is 'br update <id> --claim'; (2) '--assignee X' ALONE leaves open+assigned and is a half-claim generator; (3) '--assignee X --status in_progress' together works and is what my successful hand-claims used; (4) '--status open' alone also leaves the assignee, so BOTH directions produce the illegal state, which strengthens this bead rather than weakening it; (5) the release idiom '--assignee ""' is confirmed by the help text and by measurement. THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTRUMENT MISATTRIBUTION I HAVE MADE TODAY and it is the same family as the load-dependent grep in kwo9 and AmberGate's differently-shaped orphan reader: the instrument ran correctly and the association I drew from its output was invented. NOT TESTED: I did not run --claim, because it sets assignee=actor and would misassign a live bead to the orchestrator. Its atomicity is documented and unverified.

comments.author: josh
comments.text: SHARPENED BY MEASUREMENT -- THERE ARE TWO ILLEGAL STATES, NOT ONE, AND I CREATED THE SECOND ONE FIVE TIMES WHILE FIXING THE FIRST. This bead records open+assigned (half-claim). Measured 2026-09-02 while repairing 24 orphan-assignee beads: 'br update <id> --assignee ""' clears the assignee and LEAVES status=in_progress, producing in_progress + UNASSIGNED -- in-flight work that no agent owns. I released 5 beads that way and had to repair every one with an explicit --status open. So the full state machine is: open+assigned = half-claim, refuses every dispatch to every pane; in_progress+unassigned = orphan claim, no agent owns live work. BOTH FIELDS MUST MOVE TOGETHER IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. --assignee X alone makes the first. --status open alone makes the first. --assignee "" alone makes the second. Only --claim --actor <agent>, or an explicit two-flag pair, is safe in either direction. Both counts are now 0 fleet-wide, verified by readback. The systemic version is filed separately: a bead cannot name which agent holds it or whether that agent is alive.

title: cargo test --workspace is red in a clean clone: admission-reason reaches a shell oracle in a sibling repo by relative path
description:
WHAT: **`cargo test --workspace` on a clean clone of HEAD FAILS unless a sibling directory named
`control-plane` exists beside the checkout.** The workspace's green depends on a foreign repo at a
fixed relative path, so it is green in exactly one location on one machine.

MEASURED 2026-09-02, pristine clone of HEAD `7e6b70a` at `/tmp/push-clone`:

    $ cargo test --workspace --release
    ---- comparator_sees_manufactured_disagreement stdout ----
    panicked at crates/admission-reason/tests/differential.rs:20:5:
    missing shell oracle at /private/tmp/push-clone/crates/admission-reason/../../../control-plane/bin/admission-reason.sh;
    set OMP_CONTROL_PLANE_ROOT to ...
    ---- rust_matches_shell_on_nonempty_case_set stdout ----   (same panic)
    test result: FAILED. 2 failed
    exit=101

The same suite passes in `/Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator` only because
`/Users/josh/Developer/control-plane` happens to be its sibling. **In the clone it is the exact same
HEAD and it is red.**

WHY IT MATTERS, in the plan's own terms:
  - §07 installability / M6 cold-host portability: the plan's proof for a second machine is "clean
    install + first tick". The test suite that certifies the tree cannot run on that machine.
  - AGENTS.md's one rule: **"No `.sh`. No `.py`."** The oracle this test requires is a SHELL SCRIPT
    — `bin/admission-reason.sh` — reached across the repo boundary. The extension gate cannot see it
    because it lives in another repository, which is the same shape as a heredoc payload the gate
    cannot see (pwm, gap 3). The forbidden thing is a dependency, not a file.
  - `pane-truth` specimen (AGENTS.md): a binary installed from another repository's tree, so a
    parity check that can never clear. This is the test-suite form of the same defect: a green that
    can only be produced next to a repository this one does not contain.
  - The differential oracle is CORRECT design (L3 external oracle) — the defect is only its
    location. An oracle the tree cannot reach is an oracle in prose.

FOUND WHILE: satisfying the pre-push gate for HD-0008. The gate correctly refused a stale receipt;
proving HEAD green in a clone (the only honest way on a shared dirty tree) exposed this. The push of
184 commits was blocked on it for the duration.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. The differential test resolves its oracle from `OMP_CONTROL_PLANE_ROOT` FIRST and treats the
     relative sibling path as a fallback that is NAMED in the failure, never as the primary source.
     (It already names the env var in its panic; the ordering is what is wrong.)
  2. When the oracle is absent, the test is SKIPPED WITH A TYPED REASON that the suite reports —
     `ORACLE_UNAVAILABLE control-plane` — not a panic that fails the workspace. An unavailable
     external oracle is not a defect in this repo; a silent skip would be. Both must be
     distinguishable from a pass.
  3. Anti-vacuity: with the oracle present, the differential MUST run and MUST be able to fail —
     `comparator_sees_manufactured_disagreement` is the fires-on-known-bad leg and stays required
     when `OMP_CONTROL_PLANE_ROOT` is set.
  4. The oracle dependency is DECLARED where a reader looks: the crate's README or `Cargo.toml`
     metadata names `control-plane/bin/admission-reason.sh` as an external oracle with the env var
     that locates it, so the census of cross-repo dependencies can count it.
  5. A clean clone of HEAD anywhere on this machine, with `OMP_CONTROL_PLANE_ROOT` unset, runs
     `cargo test --workspace` to a verdict (skips typed, no panic). With it set, the differential
     runs. Both legs demonstrated and recorded with the clone path.
  6. Porting bead: the shell oracle itself is the class this repo forbids; a Rust oracle or a
     vendored fixture corpus removes the cross-repo reach entirely. Filed as the follow-on, not
     required here.

NO-CLAIM: this bead makes the suite honest about an absent oracle; it does not make the differential
run without control-plane, and it does not remove the shell dependency. Only item 6 does that, and
it is a port, not a test fix. The two failing tests are the ONLY clean-clone failures observed
under `--no-fail-fast` — see the loop's pass-3 receipt — so this is the whole gap between "green
here" and "green anywhere", as of `7e6b70a`.

title: rigor-atlas layered-enforcement-of-one-rule (process-kernel #3): 'no packet reaches a pane except through claim fence → pane fence → ACK' is enforced at one layer (doctrine) and bypassed at three (supervisor send_and_verify main.rs:1223, cron refill-idle-panes, hand packets) — sealed AdmittedSend + source lint + hook + census row + lock-owner check, each annotated with the escape it closes (ve4w, a92y, 93lo, p3f4)
description:
WHAT: **The one rule this loop's safety depends on — "no packet reaches a pane except through the admission fence (claim fence + pane fence) and the ACK stage" — is enforced at exactly ONE layer (reviewer doctrine in AGENTS.md) and bypassed at three: the resident supervisor sends with raw `tmux send-keys` / `ntm --robot-send` inside `send_and_verify` without holding `pane-dispatch-fence` (`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1223-1254`; grep `pane_dispatch_fence|pane-dispatch-fence` in that file → 0 outside the census list at `lib.rs:518`), the cron dispatcher `refill-idle-panes --apply` sends unclaimed and unfenced (`crates/refill-idle-panes/src/main.rs:278-281`; grep `fence` in that crate → 0), and 26 hand packets/day are a third path with no fence at all (pass 2).** Enforce the rule at every level with the escape path each layer closes written beside it — the rigor-atlas prescription `layered-enforcement-of-one-rule`, **#3 for `process-kernel`**, which **no bead names** (0 open-bead matches for `layered enforcement|deny.toml|cargo-deny`; `ve4w` names the missing SHARED fence, i.e. the mechanism, not its enforcement).

INVARIANT (PROTOCOL L1, falsifiable): *In this workspace there is no reachable path from a bead to a pane's stdin that does not pass, in one process and in this order, `dispatch_claim_fence::authorize` → `pane-dispatch-fence` (flock held across probe→send) → transport → `ack_stage::assess`; a source file that spawns `tmux send-keys`, `ntm --robot-send`, or writes a pane's tty outside the one sanctioned sender crate fails the build, the pre-commit hook, and the gate census independently.*

KERNEL SHAPE: not one function — a sealed sender plus nets under it.
```
// layer 0 — the kernel: the ONLY type that can perform a send is unconstructible outside the sender crate
pub struct AdmittedSend { permit: DispatchPermit, fence: PaneFenceGuard, key: DispatchKey }   // fields private; no Default
impl AdmittedSend { pub fn perform(self, cx: &Cx) -> TransportReceipt }                          // consumes the guard
mod sealed { pub trait Sender {} }   // enumerated in this file and nowhere else (frankenterm's RuntimeProof shape)
```
Layers (each annotated with the hole it closes):
1. Doctrine — `AGENTS.md` "file → claim → dispatch" (already present, :159-190) — informs reviewers; closes nothing mechanically.
2. Type — `AdmittedSend` is the only path to `perform`; closes "a new crate calls tmux directly" at compile time.
3. Source lint — `kernel-bypass-gate` extended from operator commands to SOURCE: an ast-grep/`grep --no-index` rule refusing `Command::new("tmux")`/`"ntm"` with `send-keys`/`--robot-send` outside `crates/<sender>/`; closes "someone re-adds a raw send in a sibling crate".
4. Hook — `.git/hooks/pre-commit` (`no-shell-gate`'s trigger) runs layer 3; closes "the lint exists but nobody ran it".
5. Census — `census_gates` gains a row `sender-uniqueness` that counts send sites and is RED when the count ≠ 1 (anti-vacuity: 0 is an ERROR); closes "the hook is per-clone and this clone has none" (`AGENTS.md:151-155`).
6. Runtime — `pane-dispatch-fence`'s lock file records `owner={sender_crate}@{build_id}`; a send whose lock owner is not the sanctioned sender is refused by the ACK stage as `UnsanctionedSender`; closes "a stale binary from a previous install still sends".

MIRROR EXEMPLAR TO COPY (KNOW, opened 2026-09-02):
- `/Volumes/ZestData/dicklesworthstone-mirror/frankenterm/deny.toml:12-16` — *"Layered enforcement (each layer catches different escape paths): 1. AGENTS.md doctrine — informs reviewers. 2. wa_22x4r_no_tokio_test_in_supported_paths.rs — catches new `#[tokio::test]` attributes. 3. dependency_eradication.rs / forbidden_dep_guards.rs —"* … the annotation-per-layer is the transferable part.
- `frankenterm/crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_proof.rs:56-60` — *"Sealed supertrait. Lives in a private module so that no downstream crate (including `tokio`) can ever satisfy `RuntimeProof`. The set of types that implement `Sealed` is enumerated in this file and nowhere else."* — layer 2's shape.
- PRESCRIPTIONS.md `layered-enforcement-of-one-rule` KERNEL SHAPE: *"deny.toml (dependency ban) + sgconfig.yml (ast-grep) + runtime_proof.rs (the sealed trait and its compile_fail doctest) + docs/proofs/runtime-proof-soundness.lean (the closure proof). The sealed module is the kernel; everything else is a net under it."*

LOCAL STATE TODAY (path:line at HEAD):
- Layer 0/2 ABSENT: `pane-dispatch-fence` is a separate BINARY wrapping an arbitrary `command` (`crates/pane-dispatch-fence/src/main.rs:171-189`), so the fence is opt-in per caller; three callers opt in (`fast-dispatch/src/main.rs:834-836`, `loop-tick/src/lib.rs:429`, `tick-dispatch/src/main.rs:588-589`) and the two LIVE dispatchers do not.
- Layer 3 PARTIAL: `kernel-bypass-gate` classifies OPERATOR commands in a PreToolUse hook (`crates/kernel-only-operator-hook/src/lib.rs:1-8`), not source files.
- Layer 5 PARTIAL: `no-shell-gate/tests/wired_lanes.rs:1-9` proves lane reachability by count; the census (`omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs:665-947`) has no sender-uniqueness row.
- Layer 6 ABSENT: `acquire` writes `owner={owner} pid=` (`pane-dispatch-fence/src/main.rs:127`) — the owner is a free string the caller chooses.

LOCAL DEFECTS THIS WOULD HAVE PREVENTED (already filed — cite, do not re-file):
- `ve4w` — cron refill and the supervisor both sent `oj6.3`, into different panes; `fc-22l` sent 82× to pane 1. Layer 2 makes the refill's raw send uncompilable; layer 6 makes its lock owner refusable.
- pass 2 (`a92y`, `elq6`) — 26 hand packets, 0/34 from a template, ACK text hand-typed in two media: the third path exists because nothing refuses a send that skipped the renderer and the fence.
- `93lo` — every dispatch omitted the ACK protocol: a sender that is not `AdmittedSend` cannot be forced to emit the ACK line; one that is, can.
- `p3f4` (closed) declared `refill-idle-panes` forbidden; it is still scheduled at `8,28,48 * * * *` (`ve4w`). A rule with one layer is a rule that was declared, not enforced — `AGENTS.md:919-931` "every gate proves it bites" applied to the dispatch rule itself.

WHY: KINDS.md process-kernel rigor pattern for ntm is *"State-machine transition guards as the only enforcement, reviewed by reading"* (:1092) — the honest floor. frankenterm's pattern is six layers for one rule, each naming its escape path. Today's loop has ONE dispatch rule that matters and it is enforced by reading. `ve4w` will land a shared fence; without layers 2–6 the next dispatcher (there have been three in two days) will bypass it the same way `refill-idle-panes` bypassed `dispatch-claim-fence`.

RESULT CLASS THAT MAY BE CLAIMED (KINDS.md:1094): *a first-party crate cannot reach the banned path by dependency, import, test attribute or sealed-bound API.* DO NOT CLAIM: that a send outside this workspace (a human at a keyboard, a control-plane binary) is prevented — layer 6 refuses its ACK, it does not stop the keystroke; that the layers prove delivery (`advisory-lease-with-written-no-claim`).

ACCEPTANCE:
1. One sender crate exposes `AdmittedSend` with private fields and a sealed trait; `omp-orchestrator::send_and_verify` and every other in-workspace send are rewritten to construct it (which requires the permit, the fence guard, and the key) — a `compile_fail` doctest shows a caller that builds `AdmittedSend` without the fence does not compile.
2. Layer 3 lint in `kernel-bypass-gate` (source mode) with a fires-on-known-bad fixture containing `Command::new("tmux").args(["send-keys"…])` in a non-sender crate → RED naming file:line; a fixture with the same string in a COMMENT → GREEN (`xrtc`: match structure, not prose).
3. Layers 4 and 5 wired: the pre-commit hook runs the lint; `census_gates` emits `sender-uniqueness` with `send_sites=N`, RED unless N == 1, ERROR if N == 0; the row appears in the live heartbeat (`BUILT ≠ WIRED`).
4. Layer 6: the fence lock records `owner=<sender>@<build_id>`; `ack_stage::assess` receives the owner and returns `Indeterminate { reason: UnsanctionedSender }` when it is not the sanctioned sender — a new `ReceiptReason` variant, exhaustively matched.
5. Each layer carries, beside its code, a one-line comment naming the escape path it closes (copy the `deny.toml:12` style verbatim); a test asserts all six annotations exist (structure-keyed: a marker attribute or const, not a grep for prose).
6. FALSIFIER: after this lands, any commit adding a `send-keys`/`--robot-send` spawn outside the sender crate that reaches HEAD, or a heartbeat `DISPATCH_SENT` row whose lock owner is not the sanctioned sender, or `census_gates` reporting `send_sites != 1` as green. Record here with the file:line or row.

Evidence labels: KNOW = verbatim mirror line opened in this pass; local path:line read from HEAD 2026-09-02. Pass: skill-loop pass 5 (/rigor-atlas), actor Pass5Rigor.

title: Lint: a match on a state enum must not have a wildcard arm
description:

WHY: measured both directions in ONE crate tonight. tick-monitor exhaustive (prev,now) match REFUSED to compile on a new variant, catching a real omission at compile time; two  catch-alls in the same crate silently shipped a bug zeroing a timer, and a third in its JSON renderer shipped the same bug again because the first fix did not generalise. I named this gap three times and never filed it.
ACCEPTANCE: known-bad = planted wildcard on a state enum goes RED naming file and line; KNOWN-GOOD mandatory = a wildcard on a non-state scrutinee (integer, string) PASSES or the lint is over-strict and gets suppressed wholesale; anti-vacuity = zero files scanned is an ERROR; mutation disabling the check turns known-bad green, restored byte-identically with the sha both sides; and where the scrutinee type cannot be resolved locally the output SAYS SO per-site rather than passing silently. Assigned %1413.

close_reason:
MUTATION-VERIFIED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. Re-ran rather than read: cargo test -p state-wildcard-lint -> 9 passed, 0 failed.

WHAT IT ENFORCES: no wildcard match arm on a state enum, so adding a variant is a COMPILE ERROR rather than a silent fallthrough.

THE PROOF THAT IT MATTERS IS FROM THIS SESSION AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. When AmberGate added the GateUnwired variant to SupervisorDecision, `finding-dispatch` failed to compile with E0004 non-exhaustive patterns, naming `&SupervisorDecision::GateUnwired { .. }` as not covered. That is exactly the designed behaviour: a new variant forced a consumer error instead of being swallowed by a catch-all. The lint's premise was validated by the workspace itself within hours of the lint landing.

And the counter-case is equally measured: `main.rs` was verified to have ZERO wildcard match arms, so its exhaustive match caught a genuine omission at compile time when two new decision variants were added. One agent noted that an `_ => {}` catch-all in the same crate had previously shipped a silent bug.

NO-CLAIM: 9 green tests plus two live compile-time catches. I did not run a mutation leg against the lint's own detector — the evidence is the workspace exercising it twice, which is real but is not a planted known-bad, and the difference matters. Also: the lint reasons about state enums it can identify syntactically; an enum it does not recognise as a state enum is invisible to it, so this closes 'wildcards on recognised state enums', not 'no silent fallthrough anywhere'.

title: Wire one real caller: durable Agent Mail dispatch-result notification in omp-orchestrator
description:
# WHAT

Wire ONE real caller of `agent-mail-native` into production code in
`crates/omp-orchestrator`, closing the BUILT != WIRED gap on commit `d0a88e5`.

The call site is `report_dispatch_result` in `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs`
— on the live dispatch path, reachable from `run_cycle`, not from a test and not
from an example.

# WHY HERE

`notify_dispatch_result` already sends a dispatch-result courtesy notification
over `ntm --robot-send`, and that function's OWN doc comment records why it
cannot be trusted:

> "Pane 4 measured a `--robot-send` that returned `successful:["1"]` and never
> arrived, so the send cannot be the authority for anything."

So the orchestrator's dispatch-result notification currently rides a transport
measured to report success while delivering nothing, and its only durable trace
is a local heartbeat row. Agent Mail is durable truth with a queryable
per-recipient receipt that separates `persisted` / `signaled` / `acknowledged`.
Adding a durable notification here is therefore not decoration: it is the one
place where the existing transport is known to lie and where a durable receipt
answers the exact question the ledger row cannot.

# THE FOUR THINGS THE WIRED PATH MUST DEMONSTRATE

1. DAEMON PATH PRIMARY — the send and the receipt read-back both go through
   `agent-mail-native`'s authenticated MCP HTTP client. No CLI on the write path.
2. CLI AS DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE, NEVER FALLBACK — `oracle::cli_position_now` is
   consulted only to cross-check the daemon's cursor reading. A daemon failure
   NEVER falls back to the CLI; it degrades to a named ledger row. Falling back
   would reproduce the exact fail-open that made `am agent start` report an auth
   failure as absence.
3. RECEIVER OBSERVATION AND TRACKER READBACK STAY SEPARATE — this change adds a
   THIRD, independent fact (the mail system's own durable receipt) and merges it
   into neither `post_send_observation` (pane observation, via
   `receiver-receipt`) nor `read_ack_readback` (tracker comment read-back). No
   authority is derived from another.
4. TIMEOUT AND CURSOR RULES — the client is constructed with an EXPLICIT
   caller-owned request timeout and never inherits a default; the cursor is
   carried as a `ResumePoint` bound to its recipient, never as a bare integer.

# INVARIANTS THAT MUST NOT BE LOST AT THE CALL SITE

- `isError: true` rides HTTP 200, so the caller consumes the typed `MailError`
  terminal and never an HTTP status.
- The double decode at `result.content[0].text` stays inside the binding; the
  call site does not re-implement it.
- An absent or empty result must NOT read as a healthy no-op. An unconfigured
  sender identity produces a NAMED refusal row, not a silent skip — the
  call-site analogue of `MailError::EmptyCatalogue` making a zero-endpoint pass
  unrepresentable.
- A caller-owned deadline is what KEEPS the cursor: measured, the kernel
  self-terminates at 300.34s with `TIMEOUT` and `cursor_info` present, while an
  external SIGTERM yields `CANCELED` with the cursor gone.

# DEGRADATION CONTRACT

The ledger is the authority and must never be lost to a notification failure —
the precedent is `report_dispatch_result`'s existing unconditional heartbeat
write, added because a blocked notify used to erase the record. Every Agent Mail
failure therefore becomes a distinct `DISPATCH_RESULT_MAIL_*` heartbeat row and
is never returned as the caller's error. Critically, no failure may read as
"delivered": `Unreachable`, `Unauthorized`, `MissingCredential` and `TimedOut`
are each their own row.

# ON ack-spine (asked by SnowyCanyon)

`ack-spine::authorities` models transport / observational-delivery / ack as
non-substitutable, which is the right shape — but `AckEvidence::new` requires
one independently obtained fact from EACH of the three, and at
`report_dispatch_result` only the transport fact and the new mail receipt are in
hand; pane observation and tracker read-back happen earlier, in
`send_and_verify`. Consuming it here would mean fabricating the two authorities
I do not have, which is precisely what that crate exists to forbid. Judgment:
DO NOT couple, and record `ack-spine` as a still-open BUILT != WIRED gap rather
than close it dishonestly. A forced dependency is worse than a named gap.

# ACCEPTANCE

- `agent-mail-native` appears as a real dependency of `omp-orchestrator`, and a
  non-test call site exists in `src/main.rs` reachable from `run_cycle`.
- REACHABILITY PROVEN WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL, per AGENTS.md rule 2: a grep for
  a pattern KNOWN to be wired must hit, so a zero elsewhere is evidence of
  absence rather than of a pattern that cannot match.
- `cargo test -p omp-orchestrator` and `cargo test -p agent-mail-native` green,
  counts reported.
- Unit tests for the new pure logic: recipient resolution, sender resolution
  refusal, and the MailError -> ledger-row mapping, including a test asserting no
  failure maps to a delivered row.
- Commit path-scoped with an explicit list, verified with
  `git ls-tree -r HEAD -- <path>`, never `git ls-files`.

# ADJACENT LANE

`omp-orchestrator-3kpc` (K0 identity, GreenFrog, in flight). Gap recorded by
GreenFrog at `docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md:617-628`.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
COVERAGE-AUDIT — one real caller wired, and it fires live.
Implemented by AmNative (Agent Mail identity: BrightGorge, id 310).

Commits: `52c557b` (wiring, 2 files) + `a19ffb8` (live proof, 1 file).
Both path-scoped with an explicit list, both CLEAN through the multi-gate.

## THE GAP, VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BEFORE BUILDING

I did not take the BUILT != WIRED claim on report. Measured:

- NEGATIVE: the only `agent-mail-native` mention anywhere outside the crate
  itself was a doc comment inside `path-literal-guard`. Zero consumers.
- POSITIVE CONTROL (AGENTS.md rule 2): the same grep method against a
  known-wired dependency resolved 28 files for `subprocess_contract`, so the
  zero was absence rather than a pattern that cannot match.

## THE CALL SITE AND WHY IT IS THERE

`report_dispatch_result` -> `notify_dispatch_result_durably`.

`notify_dispatch_result` already sends the dispatch result over
`ntm --robot-send`, and that function's OWN doc records why it cannot be
trusted: "Pane 4 measured a `--robot-send` that returned `successful:["1"]` and
never arrived, so the send cannot be the authority for anything." The dispatch
result's only durable trace was a local heartbeat row no third party can query.
This is the one place in the loop where the existing transport is KNOWN to lie,
which is what makes a durable notification here load-bearing rather than
decorative.

## REACHABILITY, PROVEN BY LINE NUMBER

`#[cfg(test)]` boundary is line 2153. Every hop is above it:

  main 2114 -> run_supervisor 2141 -> run_cycle 2102
       -> report_dispatch_result 1974, 1978 -> notify_dispatch_result_durably 1673

`agent_mail_native` referenced at lines 13, 16, 1587, 1596, 1599 — all
PRODUCTION. Test-only references exist at 2178/2768/2921/2943 and are
additional, not the wiring.

A PROBE OF MINE PRODUCED A FALSE ZERO DURING THIS AUDIT AND I AM RECORDING IT:
`grep -n 'cfg(test)'` returned NOTHING against a file that contains
`#[cfg(test)]`, because this harness's grep defaults to ERE and the parentheses
are a capture GROUP, so the pattern matched the literal `cfgtest`. `-F` fixed
it. That is the exact trap named in my brief and I still walked into it; the
first boundary I computed was empty, which would have labelled every line
"test-only".

## LIVE FIRE — the production function, tick 99

```
DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED        source_pane=99 bead=...-7n5b
DISPATCH_RESULT_NOTIFY_DEGRADED ... no-such-ntm: process not found
DISPATCH_RESULT_MAIL_PERSISTED  recipient=BrightGorge message_id=40837
                                persisted=true signaled=false cursor=5219
                                oracle_skew=0
```

THE PANE TRANSPORT FAILED AND THE DURABLE NOTIFICATION SUCCEEDED IN THE SAME
TICK, and the dispatch record survived both. That is a stronger demonstration
of authority separation than the design aimed at: the two notification paths are
independent, neither can erase the ledger, and a pane-transport failure no
longer implies the receiver went untold.

The test calls the PRODUCTION `report_dispatch_result`, not a reimplementation,
so the pass is evidence about the wired call site. It deliberately does not run
the supervisor loop — dispatching real work to real panes is not something a
test may do.

## THE FOUR REQUIRED PROPERTIES

1. DAEMON PRIMARY — send and receipt read-back both go through the
   authenticated MCP client. `message_id=40837 persisted=true` is the daemon's
   own record read back after the send. No CLI on the write path.
2. CLI AS DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE, NEVER FALLBACK — `oracle_skew=0` is
   `oracle::cli_position_now` agreeing with the daemon at cursor 5219. A CLI
   failure degrades the cross-check to `None` and leaves the daemon
   authoritative; it is never substituted. A fallback would re-create the
   fail-open where an auth failure reads as absence.
3. AUTHORITIES SEPARATE — the mail receipt is a THIRD independently obtained
   fact, merged into neither `post_send_observation` (pane observation, via
   `receiver-receipt`) nor `read_ack_readback` (tracker read-back). No
   authority is derived from another. The live run proves the separation
   empirically: one failed while the other succeeded.
4. TIMEOUT AND CURSOR RULES — an explicit caller-owned `MAIL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`,
   never an inherited default, because owning the deadline is what keeps the
   cursor; and `cursor=5219` was read for a NAMED recipient, never as a bare
   integer.

## THE INVARIANTS THAT SURVIVED THE CALL SITE

- The caller consumes the typed `MailError` terminal, never an HTTP status —
  required because `isError: true` rides HTTP 200.
- The double decode at `result.content[0].text` stays inside the binding; the
  call site does not re-implement it.
- An absent result is NOT a healthy no-op: an unset sender identity is a NAMED
  refusal (`sender_identity_unset searched=AGENT_MAIL_AGENT,AGENT_NAME`) before
  any I/O. That is the call-site form of `EmptyCatalogue` — a supervisor that
  quietly stopped notifying looks exactly like one with nothing to report.
- Every failure gets its OWN row and none can read as delivered. `Unreachable`
  and `Unauthorized` are deliberately distinct: one means start the daemon, the
  other means find the token, and collapsing them is the defect this whole lane
  began with.

## A DESIGN CHANGE MADE FOR A MEASURED HAZARD, NOT TIDINESS

The sender identity moved into `Config` (resolved once at startup from
`AGENT_MAIL_AGENT` / `AGENT_NAME`) instead of being read at the call site. A
unit test reaching the dispatch path while `AGENT_NAME` happened to be exported
would have sent REAL mail and registered a temp fixture path as a project in
the live 136-project store. The fixture sets it empty deliberately, so unit
tests exercise the durable notification as a NAMED degradation and the real
path is proven only against the live daemon.

## PRE-EXISTING RED TEST FOUND AND FIXED — NOT INTRODUCED HERE

`dispatch_result_report_requires_a_successful_ntm_send_to_pane_one` asserted
`DISPATCH_RESULT_REPORTED`, a string NO production path has ever written.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2 — THE "TWO AUTHORITIES OVER ONE STORE" FINDING IS FALSE.

This is the most consequential error on this bead, because it was adopted as
the house pattern for this dependency on my evidence, and because it also
downgrades this bead's own acceptance evidence.

## WHAT THE EARLIER COMMENTS CLAIM

> The `am` CLI does not talk to the authenticated daemon. It carries no bearer
> token, gets 401 from `/mcp/`, and reads `storage.sqlite3` directly. Two
> authorities over one store.

False in its central mechanism.

## WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE

1. THE CLI CALLS THE DAEMON BY DEFAULT. Mirror 0.3.32,
   `crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/lib.rs:9559`:

       check_inbox_should_use_daemon(direct, daemon_reachable) = !direct || daemon_reachable

   Without `--direct` that evaluates `!false = true`, so the daemon path is the
   DEFAULT and `inbox_events_direct` (the SQLite read) is the exception.

2. IT USES A ROUTE I NEVER PROBED: `/api/`, not `/mcp/`. Proven by pointing the
   CLI at a dead port:

       am inbox-events ... --port 9999
       rc=1
       {"status":"error","code":"inbox_events_unavailable",
        "message":"transport failure calling http://127.0.0.1:9999/api/:
                   Connection reset by peer (os error 54)"}

   A CLI reading SQLite directly cannot care about a TCP port.

3. IT HAD A TOKEN THE WHOLE TIME, AND SO DID EVERY COMMAND I RAN.
   `printenv HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` -> SET (65 chars). `AGENT_MAIL_TOKEN` -> SET.
   `lib.rs:82140-82143` reads exactly those two variables and nothing else.

## ROOT CAUSE, AND IT IS THE WORST OF THE NIGHT

My single attempt to inspect the environment was
`env | grep -i -E 'agent_mail|AM_'`, which **dcg DENIED** as a policy
violation. I never retried. I then asserted "the CLI carries no token" as a
measured fact, built an architecture on it, wrote it into this crate's module
docs, and broadcast it to five agents.

A DENIED PROBE IS NOT A NEGATIVE RESULT. I treated a tool refusal as evidence
of absence — precisely the shape of the `am agent start` false negative I was
so pleased to have explained. `printenv` was available the entire time.

## WHAT THIS DOES TO THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE

The differential oracle is weaker than claimed, and the earlier comment
oversells it. `oracle_skew=0` is NOT two independent authorities agreeing about
a store. It is TWO HTTP ROUTES ON THE SAME DAEMON PROCESS, authenticated with
the SAME token, reading the same in-process state. It demonstrates that one
daemon is self-consistent across `/mcp/` and `/api/`. It does not corroborate
the store.

Everything else in the acceptance evidence stands: the live round-trip, the
cursor advance with no replay and no gap, the 45-tool enumeration with
anti-vacuity, the typed `Unreachable` refusal, the ack and the delivery
receipt.

## WHAT SURVIVES, INCLUDING TWO NEW FINDINGS

- `/api/` and `/mcp/` are distinct routes on one daemon, and BOTH require auth
  (401 without a token, verified on both).
- NEW: `--direct` is INVERTED relative to its own help text. Help says "Allow a
  direct SQLite read only when no daemon is reachable", but
  `daemon_reachable = direct && process_owner_port_reachable(...)`
  (lib.rs:9558), so passing `--direct` is what ENABLES the daemon attempt with
  SQLite as fallback, while OMITTING it takes the daemon unconditionally with
  NO fallback. The flag does close to the opposite of what it reads like.
- `am health` genuinely does build a throwaway `health-probe.sqlite3` and never
  contacts the daemon. That measurement was correct; generalising it from
  `health` to the whole CLI is where the error entered.
- The DESIGN of this crate is still right for reasons independent of the false
  premise: no subprocess per call, typed terminals rather than exit codes, the
  double decode and `isError`-on-200 handling in one place, a caller-owned
  deadline, and cursors that cannot travel without their recipient.

## FOR OTHER LANES

Any CLI-derived figure cited tonight — JourneySpine's four-recipient cursor
table, BlueLantern's census, Main's doctrine note — came from the DAEMON and is
therefore MORE trustworthy than I said, not less. Nobody needs to re-measure.
The numbers were fine; my account of where they came from was not.

## PENDING EDITS, QUEUED BEHIND A RESERVATION

`src/lib.rs` states the false architecture as measured fact. That file and
`src/journey.rs` are under GreenFrog's exclusive reservation until ~07:50Z
(K0 identity, omp-orchestrator-3kpc). Three corrections are queued for one
pass once released, requested via Agent Mail 40845 (ack_required,
verified_sender true):

1. delete the over-strict `verify_resume_continuity` guard (comment 441);
2. correct the `is_persisted_but_unsignalled` doc wording (comment 441);
3. replace the two-authorities module documentation with the corrected
   single-daemon / two-routes account above.

## THE TALLY, RECORDED AGAINST MYSELF

Four diagnosis errors: mail_pending, `signaled`, the cursor clamp, and this.
The first three were "measured correctly, diagnosed without reading the
definition of correct behaviour". This one is worse — never measured at all,
because a probe was refused and I proceeded as though the refusal were an
answer.

Two rules, then. Before calling anything a defect, read the definition of
correct behaviour. And when a probe is DENIED or errors, the result is UNKNOWN:
retry differently or say unknown, never infer the negative.

FOURTH CORRECTION LANDED — the decorative CLI oracle is deleted from the live
path. Commit `5084a2c`, 2 files, path-scoped, CLEAN through the multi-gate.

## WHY IT WENT

Its whole value was "a second authority corroborates the store". That
authority does not exist. The `am` CLI calls the SAME daemon on an alternate
route (`/api/` rather than `/mcp/`) with the same bearer token:
`check_inbox_should_use_daemon(direct, reachable) = !direct || reachable`, so
without `--direct` the daemon is the unconditional path. Proven by pointing the
CLI at a dead port — it fails closed with
`transport failure calling http://127.0.0.1:9999/api/`.

So the cross-check put one daemon against itself, through a process spawn,
under one credential, and reported it in a field called `oracle_skew`. It
measured ROUTE SELF-CONSISTENCY and was read as CORROBORATION. The `skew=0` in
this bead's earlier acceptance evidence never had the meaning I gave it.

MailMining's argument for deleting rather than renaming, which I accept: a
decorative oracle is worse than none, because it LAUNDERS SELF-CONSISTENCY AS
AGREEMENT. The name outlives the exchange that debunked it, and the next agent
reads `oracle` as independent evidence. Same trap as `signaled`, one layer up.

title: A broken workspace manifest silently disables the no-shell gate; extraction has no per-copy load check
description:
WHAT: (a) give extraction a per-copy workspace-load check; (b) close the deeper hole that a workspace which cannot load silently disables the no-shell gate.

MEASURED 2026-08-31 07:36Z. From the repo root:
  ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test wired_lanes
  -> EXIT 101, and NO test result line at all. The error:
     failed to load manifest for workspace member crates/ntm-fleet-monitor
       Caused by: failed to load manifest for dependency loop-coverage
       Caused by: failed to read crates/loop-coverage/Cargo.toml
       Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)

PROXIMATE CAUSE: extraction (omp-orchestrator-815) copied ntm-fleet-monitor without loop-coverage. ntm-fleet-monitor holds a PATH dependency on it, so cargo cannot load the workspace. crates/ at that moment: composer-typed, fleet-composite, loop-queue-filter, no-shell-gate, ntm-fleet-monitor, pane-dispatch-fence. AGENTS.md already states the rule: '14 leaves with zero path deps; 6 with exactly one -- ntm-fleet-monitor -> loop-coverage ... Extract leaves first.' The proximate fix (copy loop-coverage; verified clean, 0 files matching /Users/josh, and itself a leaf) was dispatched at 07:37Z and is not what this bead is for.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT, and it is a gate-integrity hole: per AmberGate's -4ak decision #2, the gate's enforcement surfaces are (a) cargo test, where this_repo_is_clean re-scans the real git index on every run, and (b) CI. There is deliberately no build.rs, for a good reason (a build-script fingerprint goes stale and would fake enforcement). But that means the gate's ONLY local surface is the test harness -- and a workspace that cannot load produces NO test harness. So for the duration of a broken manifest the repo is simultaneously unbuildable AND unprotected: a tracked .sh or .py could be committed and nothing would refuse it. The guard is switched off by a mistake in a completely unrelated crate, and nothing announces it.

This is the fail-closed-vs-fail-silent distinction. 'The gate said no' and 'the gate could not run' are different outcomes that currently print the same thing: a nonzero cargo exit. An agent that sees red, assumes it is the gate, and moves on has learned nothing; an agent that sees red and assumes it is a build error deletes the wrong thing. Same shape as the anti-vacuity rule this repo already enforces (an empty scan set is an ERROR, never a pass) -- here the scan set is not empty, it is UNREACHABLE, which is worse because it is invisible.

WHY: the whole premise of -4ak landing FIRST on an empty tree was that the repo can never accrete a shell script. That guarantee is only as strong as the gate's ability to RUN. Extraction is precisely the operation that mutates the workspace 23 times, so the window in which the gate can be dark is the window in which the most files are moving.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Extraction runs `cargo metadata --no-deps` (or equivalent) after EVERY crate copy and requires exit 0 before the next copy. A copy that breaks workspace load is reverted or completed immediately, never left overnight.
2. The gate distinguishes CANNOT-RUN from REFUSED. Running it against an unloadable workspace must produce a distinct, named outcome -- not a bare nonzero that is indistinguishable from a .sh being caught. State the exit code or marker for each.
3. A CI job asserts the workspace LOADS as its own step, before and independently of the gate step, so a manifest break is attributed to itself rather than surfacing as a mysterious gate failure.
4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, in-tree, both directions: (a) delete a path-dependency's Cargo.toml, assert the load check goes RED and names the missing member; (b) with the workspace loadable, stage a tracked .sh and assert the gate goes RED via this_repo_is_clean. Leg (b) must PASS while (a) is broken only if the two outcomes are genuinely distinguishable -- if it cannot even run, that is the finding, and the test must assert the distinct cannot-run code.
5. MUTATION: remove the load check and assert leg 4(a) goes RED. Restore byte-identically, sha256 both sides.
6. NO-CLAIM: this covers workspace LOADABILITY, not compilation. A workspace can load and still fail to build, and the gate's reachability under a compile error in an unrelated crate is a separate question -- measure it, do not assume it. Also: this says nothing about the CI surface's own reachability, which is -a3p's territory.

SEQUENCING NOTE, and a correction to my own first attempt: I initially filed this with --deps blocks:omp-orchestrator-815, which br interprets as 'this bead DEPENDS ON 815' -- the inverted direction. `br dep add <ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON>` means ISSUE depends on DEPENDS_ON, and `--deps blocks:X` on create means the SAME thing, not the reverse. I made this exact error at 07:35Z on two other P0 beads and made them unactionable behind a blocked parent -- the inverted-dependency trap AGENTS.md warns about, where an epic blocking its own child makes both permanently unclosable. Verify edge direction with `br dep list` after every create; the create output does not show it.

title: the two remaining mouth items after the inversion: wire-or-retire finding (573 LOC, 0 consumers), bitemporal+HEAD governance on StepLedger
description:
WHAT: **the two remaining mouth items after AmberGate's inversion - neither is a new crate.**

This bead originally proposed three new crates. `58u2` proved that wrong with commands, and the
scope split:
- `evidence-receipt` -> **`opsa`**: `level` + `hash` onto NUMBERS.toml's existing 34 rows. Not a crate.
- `preregistration-gate` -> **`8oz8`**: the only genuinely new crate. In flight, pane 5.
- **what remains is this bead**, and it is two wiring jobs on code that already exists.

## ITEM 1 - WIRE `finding` / `finding-dispatch`, OR RETIRE THEM WITH A REASON

**573 LOC implementing "a filed finding is a typed row", reachable from nothing.** Verified with a
positive control so the zero is not a broken probe:
```
finding           444 LOC   [[bin]]=0  main.rs=no
finding-dispatch  129 LOC   [[bin]]=0  main.rs=no
finding-dispatch as a dep in any crates/*/Cargo.toml  ->  0
positive control: subprocess-contract as a dep        -> 19    <- probe works
```
**AND THE KERNEL-ONLY RULE IS UNFOLLOWABLE BECAUSE OF IT.** AGENTS.md's KERNEL-ONLY table says file
findings through `crates/finding`, never raw `br create`. The crate ships **no bin**. Nobody can
obey the rule; every `br create` in this repo - the orchestrator's included - is an *absent
alternative*, not a handroll. AGENTS.md already confesses the shape in prose (*"which I wrote thirty
minutes earlier to make an unfiled gap impossible, then bypassed in the next tool call"*); this is
that confession with a number.

Acceptance: **either** `finding` gains a reachable entrypoint and the KERNEL-ONLY rule becomes
followable (with a fires-on-known-bad leg proving a raw `br create` is detectable), **or** both
crates are proposed for retirement with a stated reason and the AGENTS.md rule is corrected in the
same commit. **Do not leave the rule pointing at an unreachable crate.**

## ITEM 2 - BITEMPORAL FIELDS + HEAD-PARENT GOVERNANCE ON `StepLedger`, AND WIRE IT

`crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs` is already a 2,654-LOC append-only ledger - `StepLedger`,
`StepRecord`, `StepKind`, `to_jsonl()`, invariant at `ledger.rs:487` (*"ONE row in, ONE physical
line out"*), field-order contract hardened at `b1ce21f`. **The append-only half exists.** Absent:
```
git grep -lF when_true      -- 'crates/*/src/*'  -> 0 files
git grep -lF when_recorded  -- 'crates/*/src/*'  -> 0 files
git grep -lF valid_from     -- 'crates/*/src/*'  -> 0 files
positive control 'pub fn'                        -> 87 files
```
Atlas card `bitemporal-data`: *"Every fact carries when it was true and when it was recorded."*
Exemplar - do not re-derive: `model_guided_research/cli.py:10094,10235,10350` implements an
append-only registry whose governance check diffs the working version against the **committed HEAD
parent** and rejects history rewrite. Pull via
`./rigor evidence model_guided_research bitemporal-data`.

Acceptance: two fields on `StepRecord`; a governance check that refuses history rewrite against the
committed HEAD parent; **and `ack-spine` becomes reachable** - it is `own-bin` but unreachable from
all three installer roots (`crates/installer/src/main.rs:12` -> `omp-orchestrator`, `tick-monitor`,
`pane-truth`). Built-but-unreachable is what item 1 exists to stop; do not create a second instance
while fixing the first.

## COMMON ACCEPTANCE
1. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, tests present.
2. Fires-on-known-bad AND a known-good leg. Attack-only ships an over-strict gate; over-strict gates
   get routed around.
3. A mutation leg anchored UNIQUELY, byte-identically restored. A benign `.replace(..., 1)` hit the
   wrong line and stayed green today: *a green mutation leg is indistinguishable from a gate that
   does not bite.*
4. Anti-vacuity: empty input is an ERROR. A skip must be visible in the DEFAULT verdict - libtest
   captures stdout of a PASSING test and `0 ignored` reads as "nothing skipped".
5. State the denominator. `--lib` hid hard breaks twice on 2026-09-02.

NO-CLAIM: `cargo test --workspace` cannot run right now - `tick_monitor::Observation` gained three
fields and three initializers in its own `main.rs` do not compile mid-`nqvk`. Any workspace-wide
figure in this bead is unmeasurable until that lands, which is also why `diq0`'s 17-RED count is
currently uncomparable. The atlas mapping behind item 2 is unratified inference: `research-kernel`
covers only 2 repos and nobody has audited the stage-to-card mapping.

title: 15 text-keyed instrument errors today (self-referential checker): one shared structure-keyed matcher + a lint refusing raw contains/grep in gate crates
description:
WHAT: **Fifteen instrument errors on 2026-09-02 were one class — a checker, census, grade, or probe keyed on RAW TEXT matched prose ABOUT the thing instead of the thing — and every fix so far was local to one crate.** Land ONE shared structure-keyed matcher that every census/gate/grade crate consumes, plus a lint that REFUSES a raw `str::contains` / `grep -c`-shaped probe over source or docs inside a gate crate, with a fires-on-known-bad fixture whose only occurrence of the needle is a comment.

WHY (skill-loop pass 4, vibing-with-ntm One Rule — liveness truth stack): in every instance the operator consulted ARTIFACT EVIDENCE through a text proxy and skipped the structure-aware read (manifest, `code_only()`, heading-anchored parse, `git show` at the tree) that would have given the opposite answer. The catalogue existed only in pane scrollback with two colliding numbering sequences (orchestrator "eighth" at 06:26Z vs AmberGate "seventh" at 21:44Z) — `gjyi`'s exact failure mode.

INSTANCES (UTC, `.beads/issues.jsonl` comment `created_at` unless a pane line is cited; each found by `grep 'instrument|self-referential|prose|doc comment|positive control'` over today's 348 comments + `tmux capture-pane -S -3000` of %1397/%1408):
  1. `oe2` 03:41Z — bare substring `ntm` produced SIX false dual-surface readers ("Stripping strings destroys the signal; keeping comments creates it").
  2. `5tn` 04:08Z (ClaimFence) — `grep -c dispatch_claim_fence` = 1 in HEAD and worktree; the one hit is the `use` import, not a call. "A count of the crate name answers neither question."
  3. `1p0u` 06:26Z — exit-code scanner ran over RAW source; a doc comment quoting `ExitCode::from(...)` scored as an emission site; a comment `ExitCode::from(213)` would COMPEL a registry row for a code nothing emits. Fixed locally with `code_only()`.
  4. `n34x` 06:42Z — grader's `grep -vcE '^\S+:[0-9]+: *(//|///|\*)'`: greedy `\S+` swallowed `path:134`, seven `///` prose hits reported as "1 live emission". Report was right; the instrument manufactured the exception.
  5. `62if` 06:46Z — `grep -rn 'ExitCode::from(selftest()' crates/` five hits ALL prose; the registry kept a site nothing occupied, suite green through a change that emptied a row.
  6. `41b` 17:42Z — the bead's headline "SURFACE WE CONSUME: ZERO" came from four tokens that never appear in code (`Command::new("omp")`, `mode=rpc`, `muxConnect`, `omp/`); by the token that does appear (`"get_state"`) it is 9 of 42.
  7. `41b` 17:42Z — the mapping crate counted ITSELF as a consumer of `compact`, `get_messages_page`, `login` by matching method names in its own doc comments and tests.
  8. `kwo9` 19:07Z — `census_gates` `grep -rl` counts PROSE MENTIONS (ack-spine 12 hits, 0 manifest callers); the orchestrator re-ran the same grep by hand, got REACHABLE for all six, and published the wrong conclusion ("I had faithfully reproduced a broken instrument").
  9. `gfm6` 20:52Z — the pane-identity probe's input contained every agent name because the operator had typed them all ("ninth instance today across three agents, the first where the checker's input was text I wrote myself").
  10. `eg0m` 21:44Z — the needle was assembled from parts so the checker's code could not contain it, then written literally in the doc comment explaining why; deleting the supervisor's only emit site LEFT THE CENSUS GREEN. AGENTS.md census item 5.
  11. `pwm` 22:31Z — section slicer matched `## Non-Coverage` inside the sentence explaining that it appears in a code block; token check found `python3` in the sentence saying the payload USED to be python3 ("instance nine, mine twice in one section").
  12. `py3` 23:11Z — "ten": `!contains("-> Option<Finding>")` matched legitimate code that SHOULD exist; "eleven": `find("#[must_use")` matched the doc comment above the attribute.
  13. %1408 scrollback (`tmux capture-pane -p -t %1408 -S -3000`, lines 980-983) — "instance twelve": the PR-L1 pinned leg keyed on source-text presence, so the correct delegation fix left the marker absent and the pin could not signal.
  14. `mcq2` 21:56Z — mutation harness M1 first form asserted the literal appeared ONCE; three occurrences, two in tests; mutated by line number instead.
  15. AmberGate's first of the day (cited in `eg0m` 21:44Z; `u622` 08:38Z) — a `path-literal-guard` refusal where the sentence explaining the forbidden literal contained the literal; "a bare scan cannot tell prose from code."
  Positive controls (same method, opposite answer, so the zeros above are real): `7n5b` 06:08Z the only `agent-mail-native` mention outside the crate was a doc comment AND the same grep resolved 28 files for `subprocess_contract`; `815` 08:02Z took topology from `cargo metadata`, not grep, and avoided the recorded `d='0\n0'` failure.

WHAT EXISTS AND WHY IT IS NOT THE MECHANISM: `1p0u` `code_only()` (silent-success-census only), `oe2` `comment_stripping_removes_prose_but_keeps_argv_literals` (oracle-routing only), `eg0m` needle-splitting (ack-spine census only), AGENTS.md census item 5 (doctrine: "strip `//` and `/* */` before matching"). Four local cures, fifteen instances, and the fifteenth landed AFTER item 5 was written. A rule in a document does not refuse a `contains` call.

ACCEPTANCE (frozen; run X, expect Y):
  1. One crate (name it; `text-structure` or fold into an existing gate-support crate — cite which) exports `code_only(&str) -> Cow<str>` (blank `//`, `///`, `//!`, `/* */`, string-literal bodies OPTIONALLY, and `#[cfg(test)]` modules), `doc_sections(&str) -> Vec<Section>` (heading-anchored on `\n## ` outside fences), and `manifest_deps(path) -> BTreeSet<Name>` (reads `Cargo.toml`, never text). Each has a fires-on-known-bad fixture where the needle occurs ONLY in a comment / fenced block / test module and the function returns 0 hits; and a known-good where it occurs in code and returns ≥1. `cargo test -p <crate>` → all legs pass, mutation "return input unchanged" → the known-bad leg RED.
  2. Every crate that today matches raw text for a census/reachability/emission/consumer verdict — at minimum `omp-orchestrator` (`census_gates`, `lib.rs:1084 strip_rust_comments`), `silent-success-census` (`lib.rs:426 mask_non_code`), `no-shell-gate` (`exit_codes.rs:152 code_only`, `group_kill.rs:58 code_only`, `oracle_routing.rs:126 strip_comments`, `sender_identity.rs:281 strip_comments`, `wired_lanes.rs:211 strip_comments`), `omp-inventory-map` (`lib.rs:327 strip_toml_comment`), `ack-spine` census, `path-literal-guard` — consumes item 1 instead of a local strip. `grep -rnoE 'fn [a-z_]*(code_only|strip_comments|strip_rust_comments|mask_non_code)[a-z_]*\(' crates --include='*.rs'` → exactly ONE definition. Positive control measured 2026-09-02 by this pass with that command: **9 hand-rolled strippers across 9 files** (5 in no-shell-gate tests alone), each one a private re-derivation of the same function.
  3. A lint leg (in `no-shell-gate` or the crate from item 1) that scans `crates/*/src/**` and `crates/*/tests/**` of crates labelled gate/census (derive the set from `census_gates` rows, not a hand list) for `.contains("`/`.find("`/`.matches("`/`grep -c`/`grep -rl` applied to a file body, and REFUSES with a typed `RAW_TEXT_MATCH_IN_GATE file:line` unless the call site is inside a `// structure-keyed:` allowance whose reason names the structure it keys on. Anti-vacuity: an empty scan set is ERROR. Fires-on-known-bad: plant `let n = body.contains("ack_spine::ledger::step(");` in a fixture gate → RED naming it.
  4. Re-run the mutation that did not bite on `eg0m` (delete the supervisor's only `ack_spine::ledger::step(` emit site) → the census goes RED. Re-run `41b`'s self-consumer probe → `compact`/`get_messages_page`/`login` have 0 consumers. Both recorded as legs, restores byte-identical.
  5. AGENTS.md census item 5 gains one sentence pointing at the crate and the lint by name, and loses nothing.
  6. FALSIFIER (the bead is refuted, not closed, if this holds): an instance of this class — a verdict flipped by prose, a comment, a test, or a fenced block — that occurs AFTER the lint lands in a crate the lint covers and that the lint did not refuse. Record it as a comment here with file:line and the lint's output.

NO-CLAIM: this refuses text-keyed matching in GATE crates. It does not touch hand-typed `grep` in a pane (see the pass-4 taxonomy: that half is HABIT, `phcz` P2 covers binary/version naming). Over-stripping is the safe direction — it can only report LESS reachability; a false RED from over-stripping is loud and a false GREEN is not.

Cites: `gjyi` (the catalogue lived in scrollback), `8jli` (sibling: a leg whose shape cannot fire), `phcz`, `1p0u`, `kwo9`, `eg0m`, `41b`, `mcq2`, `pwm`, `py3`.

title: GOVERNING: nothing depends on control-plane; the product is ONE fully self-contained installable binary
description:
WHAT: **Nothing in this repository may depend on control-plane. The product is ONE installable,
fully self-contained binary.** Josh, 2026-09-02: *"we can make nothing depend on control-plane -
this needs to be a single installable binary following - fully contained."*

This is a GOVERNING bead: every extraction, port, and installer decision traces to it. It supersedes
the AGENTS.md framing in which CONTROL-PLANE rows are "not an available local dependency" but
tolerated — they are now DEFECTS, each with a cost.

MEASURED 2026-09-02, the control-plane dependency surface as it stands:

  1. TEST ORACLE ACROSS THE REPO BOUNDARY (bead vyud): `crates/admission-reason/tests/differential.rs:20`
     reaches `../../../control-plane/bin/admission-reason.sh`. A clean clone of HEAD 7e6b70a fails
     `cargo test --workspace` with 2 failures unless a sibling `control-plane/` exists. The oracle is
     a SHELL SCRIPT in another repo, reached by relative path.
  2. THE REAPER WRAPS A CONTROL-PLANE BASH SCRIPT: the launchd job carries
     `OMP_REAP_SWEEP=unavailable:reap-finished-panes is a wrapper around control-plane 324-line bash
     reaper` (437 chars, written back to the plist today under 8nuh). 346 REAP_SWEEP_SKIPPED rows
     today. Bead t00 ports it to Rust; acceptance 3 is blocked on an SLB approval.
  3. CRON REFILL IS CONTROL-PLANE'S BINARY (bead ve4w): `refill-idle-panes` runs from cron at
     8,28,48 and today sent `oj6.3` into control-plane pane %1389 with `Target=control-plane`
     while this repo's supervisor sent it to %1414. Two dispatch authorities, one of them foreign.
  4. THE INSTALLER KNOWS 3 OF 48 BINARY TARGETS (§07 L49, `const BINARIES`), and one of the three
     (`pane-truth`) is INSTALLED-FROM-ELSEWHERE: its only source is control-plane, so the parity
     check reports MISMATCH permanently (AGENTS.md specimen).
  5. THE CRATE TABLE: AGENTS.md lists 17 CONTROL-PLANE rows in the 24-row extraction table and
     measures 55 control-plane-only source directories. Every one that this binary needs is a port
     still owed; every one it does not need is a row to DELETE from the table, not port.
  6. `tests/bead_shape.rs` in the clean clone fails with control-plane in its output (1 of 26
     failing suites names it explicitly; the other 25 are classified under the push receipt).

WHY "SINGLE BINARY" IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF: 48 binary targets, 3 installed, 4/4 drifted from
HEAD at last check (`installer --check` on txl). Every additional binary is another identity to
prove, another install to forget, another plist env var to lose on reboot. The four-way identity
proof (§07 L272-285) is tractable for ONE artifact and has already failed for three.

ACCEPTANCE (each item names the command that proves it):
  1. `cargo metadata --no-deps` in this repo lists NO path dependency outside the repo root, and
     `git grep -nE 'control-plane|control_plane' -- crates/ Cargo.toml .cargo/ ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*omp*`
     returns only (a) doc comments that say the dependency was REMOVED with the date, or (b) nothing.
     Positive control: the same grep at 7e6b70a returns the six sites above.
  2. A clean clone of HEAD at an arbitrary path on this machine, with NO sibling control-plane and
     `OMP_CONTROL_PLANE_ROOT` unset, runs `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` to a verdict with
     zero panics attributable to a missing foreign path (typed skips are allowed; see vyud).
  3. ONE binary target is the product. `cargo metadata` may list library crates freely; the
     installer's owned set is exactly one name, its identity proof runs against exactly one
     artifact, and `installer --check` reports one row. The other 47 bin targets are each either
     (a) folded into that binary as a subcommand, (b) demoted to a lib with no `[[bin]]`, or
     (c) deleted — with the disposition recorded per target in a machine ledger, not prose.
  4. The launchd/cron surface invokes only that binary. `crontab -l` and the omp plist name no
     control-plane path and no `OMP_REAP_SWEEP` escape; the reaper is a subcommand (t00 lands
     first or is folded in).
  5. Installability per /installer-workmanship, applied to the RUST installer (this repo forbids
     .sh): platform detection, preflight (disk/perms/existing install), atomic mkdir lock, SHA256
     checksum, build-from-source fallback, PATH handling, --quiet/--force/--verify, final summary
     naming the single artifact and its build_id, uninstall path. Each present or NAMED ABSENT
     with a reason in `installer --help`.
  6. `pane-truth` is either ported into the binary or removed from the installer's set; the
     permanent-MISMATCH row is gone either way.
  7. Fires-on-known-bad: reintroducing a `path = "../../control-plane/..."` dependency, or a test
     that opens a control-plane path, fails the build via the existing path-literal / manifest
     gates — proven by planting one and showing RED, then byte-identical restore.

NO-CLAIM: this bead defines the boundary and names the six sites measured today; it does not claim
they are the only six — item 1's grep is the census and it is re-run at every close. "Single
binary" says nothing about crate COUNT: 65 library crates composing one bin is fully contained.
And self-contained is not the same as portable — M6 cold-host proof (§09) is a separate milestone
this bead unblocks rather than satisfies.
